title: Highlights from the 5th Epic Leadership Summit
text:
The University of Texas System convened a two-day (January 23 - 24) Epic - UT System Leadership Summit at the UT Health San Antonio, bringing together representatives from all eight health-related institutions (HRIs). The summit provided a platform to discuss the research and development of the Epic electronic health record (EHR) system, review progress on collaborative projects, and explore future opportunities to advance the One UT Health Strategic Framework. Attendees included executive leaders from UT MD Anderson Cancer Center, UT Health Science Center at Houston, UT Medical Branch at Galveston (UTMB), UT Southwestern Medical Center, UT Rio Grande Valley, UT Tyler, Dell Medical School at UT Austin, UT Health San Antonio, and the UT System administration.
Edward Sankary, MD, UT Health San Antonio’s chief health information and value officer, emphasized the value of this gathering. “This engagement provided an exceptional opportunity to enhance collaboration with our sister institution HRIs, aligning our efforts where it makes the most sense,” he said. During the summit, updates on future development were shared alongside discussions led by UT System and Epic executives. Topics included elevating infrastructure and technology, improving patient access, optimizing revenue cycles, enhancing pharmacy services and advancing population health initiatives. Additionally, there was a strong focus on the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and unified collaboration. Sankary highlighted the collaborative framework initiated by John Zerwas, MD, FASA, executive vice chancellor for health affairs at UT System. “When I think of the One UT Health Strategic Framework, Epic comes to mind,” Zerwas said.

title: Highlights from the 5th Epic Leadership Summit
text:
Each participating workgroup (see below) was encouraged to explore unique opportunities for collaboration, fostering a more integrated approach to achieving shared objectives. A notable takeaway from the summit was the increasing significance of AI in operations, particularly related to Epic.
Throughout the summit, participants engaged in workgroup breakout sessions focused on a variety of crucial topics aimed at improving patient care and operations:
Clinical Highlights:
- A workshop on Bedside TV was conducted remotely, highlighting innovative engagement tools for patients.
- An important Epic summary addressed FDA regulations surrounding Operational Performance Assessments and responses to the HHS proposed rule on health IT standards.
- Discussions on the plan for 2025 clinical sessions included insights into ambient listening technology and its integration with outside vendors.
- An opportunity for leveraging multiple Epic AI applications
- The "Level Up Scheduling Optimization" combined session provided tools for better collaboration in e-visits through MyChart messaging and innovations in managing patient charges.
Patient Access Innovations:
- Epic presented recommendations for enhancing system-wide collaboration in patient access.
- Sessions focused on relaunching the Cheers initiative and integrating phone systems.
Text-based communication strategies to reduce no-shows and same-day cancellations were explored, alongside collaborative sessions with clinical focused on optimizing scheduling and E-visit integration.
Infrastructure and Technology Developments:
- Recommendations from Epic regarding infrastructure and technology collaboration emphasized cyber resiliency and business continuity to ensure institutions can care for critical patients effectively.
- Updates on HIPAA Security Rule compliance and innovations in operational capabilities were also addressed.
Revenue Cycle Strategies:
- Epic outlined system-wide collaboration plans for the revenue cycle, including updates on payer platforms and applications of AI in clinical appeals.

title: Highlights from the 5th Epic Leadership Summit
text:
- Updates on HIPAA Security Rule compliance and innovations in operational capabilities were also addressed.
Revenue Cycle Strategies:
- Epic outlined system-wide collaboration plans for the revenue cycle, including updates on payer platforms and applications of AI in clinical appeals.
- Predictive analytics on payment recovery likelihood and discussions on business continuity planning highlighted crucial financial strategies moving forward.
Pharmacy Updates:
- The summit also focused on UT System pharmacy priorities, with updates on pharmacy collaboration across institutions.
Innovations included the WAM across institutions, implementation of home infusion modules, and Epic’s roadmap for monitoring pharmacy contracts and cycle tools.
"As we leverage the right technologies and carefully monitor performance, we can not only keep costs down but also ensure that our processes are both more effective and efficient," said Sankary.
The leadership summit exemplified the commitment to continuous improvement and collaboration. Stay tuned for more updates on the advancements and initiatives stemming from this productive gathering.

title: Interdisciplinary Advisory Committee (IAC)
text: The Integrated Advisory Council (IAC) provides governance for Epic-related projects across the organization. It is composed of 16 operational voting streams, each represented by members appointed by the Epic Enterprise Collaborative. This structure ensures broad organizational representation while maintaining a focused, efficient decision‑making body.

title: Interdisciplinary Advisory Committee (IAC)
text:
The IAC meets monthly to review and score all items in the Epic project intake queue. Each project is evaluated using a standardized scoring model designed to measure impact, feasibility, and resource needs.
Scoring Criteria & Weights
Clinical Impact — 15%
- Strategic Impact — 10%
- Regulatory / Patient Safety — 15%
- Revenue Impact — 10%
- Risk — 10%
- Training — 5%
- Scope — 10%
- Project Planning — 5%
- Resource Effort — 20%
To ensure fair evaluation and accurate resource planning, each project request must include clear, complete information for every scoring category.

title: Interdisciplinary Advisory Committee (IAC)
text:
Across the organization, the Epic team is currently managing:
- ~80 active projects
- 47 additional requests in the intake queue
After the IAC completes its monthly prioritization, Health IT reviews the highest‑scoring projects and determines which can move forward based on available resources. Because resource availability varies, not all approved projects begin immediately.

title: Interdisciplinary Advisory Committee (IAC)
text:
Project size and complexity vary widely. On average:
3 to 6 projects are selected for kickoff each month
Projects not selected remain in the intake queue and are re‑evaluated the following month alongside new submissions.
To ensure older requests continue to receive consideration, the IAC applies a two‑point score increase for every month a project remains in the queue without advancing.

title: Introducing the NEW Epic Referral Order System
text:
BetterCare is excited to introduce our new Epic Referral Order System, a game-changer in how we handle patient referrals. This system is designed to boost efficiency utilizing Transcribe Orders and Appointment Request WQs features.
Here's why you should be thrilled about this innovative system:

- Enhanced Communication: Say goodbye to communication gaps! Our system ensures seamless communication between referring providers, specialists and other health care stakeholders. You'll stay informed every step, ensuring optimal patient care.
- Improved Efficiency: Automation is the name of the game. Our system eliminates administrative hassles by automating various aspects of the referral workflow, such as scheduling appointments and sending reminders. It reduces patient delays, allowing you to focus on what matters most—patient care.
- Comprehensive Tracking: Knowledge is power. With real-time updates on the status of your referrals, you'll have complete visibility into the process. Monitor progress, identify bottlenecks, and take timely action to ensure a smooth patient referral experience.

title: Journey to Level 7: UT Health San Antonio Achieves Epic’s Gold Stars Level 7
text:
We are thrilled to announce that UT Health San Antonio has just advanced again from Epic’s Gold Stars Level 6 to Level 7. This impressive achievement reflects the relentless dedication and hard work of our Information Technology team in enhancing our electronic health record (EHR) solutions. By adopting 75% of the Epic Gold Stars features, we have now integrated more advanced capabilities, enabling us to reach Level 7.
Epic Refuel Program
The primary driver of our advancement has been the robust Epic Refuel program that launched last year. This initiative was aimed at:
- Modernizing the Epic System: Introducing new modules and features.
- Increasing Efficiency and Usability: Enhancing the overall user experience with the system.
- Reducing System Failure Risk: Ensuring a stable and reliable EHR system.
- Expediting Quarterly Upgrades: Keeping our system up-to-date with the latest improvements.
Boosting User Satisfaction: Enhancing the daily experience for our users.
Current Progress
- 12 of 38 Applications: Already at Gold Stars Level 10.
- Next Refuel Package: Set to go live on October 15, 2024, at 9 PM, including several new upgrades, features, and Gold Stars items.
Our Gold Star Level 7 achievement is a testament to our commitment to being at the forefront of EHR innovation. We are not stopping here; our ultimate goal is to reach Level 10, the highest rating, symbolizing our commitment to excellence and providing an improved, safer, and more efficient user/patient experience.

title: Journey to Level 7: UT Health San Antonio Achieves Epic’s Gold Stars Level 7
text: A big thank you to the IT team for your unwavering dedication. Your efforts are instrumental in maximizing our Epic EHR system to its fullest potential. Congratulations to everyone involved for this significant milestone. Let’s keep up the momentum as we move forward!

title: Kyle Seale Parkway Opening Signals a BetterCare Milestone
text:
UT Health San Antonio's new outpatient and surgery center at Kyle Seale Parkway (KSP) opens Tuesday, March 19; the opening signals our first BetterCare milestone of 2024 as we introduce our updated Epic platform to all clinic specialties at KSP Clin…
UT Health San Antonio's new outpatient and surgery center at Kyle Seale Parkway (KSP) opens Tuesday, March 19; the opening signals our first BetterCare milestone of 2024 as we introduce our updated Epic platform to all clinic specialties at KSP Clinic. On February 26, a collective of operations, IT, and Epic met to conduct their 30-Day Go-live Readiness Assessment (GLRA) of the KSP Clinic and reported that all systems are "go" for the March 19th opening!
The teams are actively conducting Technical Dress Rehearsal (TDR), ensuring all hardware and devices are ready for operations. End users will conduct Workflow Dress Rehearsals the week of March 11 with BetterCare leadership available to help guide them. Super users will also be available onsite the week of go-live to support operations and ensure a seamless technical transition to their new facility. A remote team will be available to field help desk calls and service request tickets.
BetterCare is a Health IT program committed to making lives better for both our patients and clinicians. Together with our Epic partner, we are taking advantage of clinical support and automation, streamlining workflows, improving access to patient health information, and elevating our patient's health care experience.

Ensure compliance with IRUSP Standard 22, which outlines requirements for vendor and third-party controls and compliance.
UT Health San Antonio recognizes that Vendors and other contractors serve an important function in the development and/or support of services, hardware, and software and, in some cases, the operation of computer networks, Servers, and/or applications. This standard applies to contracts entered into by UT Health San Antonio that involves third-party access to or creation of Information Resources or University Data by a third-party.
22.1 Contracts. Contracts of any kind, including purchase orders, memoranda of understanding (MOU), letters of agreement, or any other type of legally binding agreement, that involve current or future third-party access to or creation of Information Resources and/or Data must include terms determined by the Office of General Counsel as sufficient to ensure that Vendors and any subcontractors or other third-parties that maintain, create, or access University Data as the result of the contract comply with all applicable Federal and State security and privacy laws, U. T. System 165, this Information Resources and Use Policy, and any applicable U. T. System and University Policies or Standards, and must contain terms that ensure that all University Data affected by the contract is maintained in accordance with those standards at all times, including post-termination of the contract. All contracts must be reviewed and executed by the UT Business Contracts Office.

title: Governance
text:
22.2 The Data Owner, UT Health San Antonio procurement officers and staff, and the UT Health San Antonio Chief Information Security Officer are jointly and separately responsible for ensuring that all contracts are reviewed to determine whether the contract involves third-party access to, outsourcing, maintenance, or creation of University Data; and that all such access, outsourcing, or maintenance fully complies with this Standard at all times.
22.3 Any contract involving third-party access to, creation, or maintenance of Protected Health Information (PHI) as defined in 45 C.F.R. § 164.501, must include a Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) business associate agreement in a form approved by UT Health San Antonio counsel or the U. T. System Office of General Counsel.
22.4 Any contract involving third-party-provided credit card services must require that the Contractor provides assurances that all subcontractors who provide credit card services pursuant to the contract will comply with the requirements of the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) in the provision of the services.
22.5 Vendor or other Third-Party Assessment. Prior to access, maintenance, or creation of University Data by a Vendor or any other third-party, the Institution must perform an assessment to ensure that:
22.5.2 any subcontractor or other third-party that will access, maintain, or create Data pursuant to the contract will also ensure the confidentiality, security, and Integrity of such Data while it is at rest and during any transmission or transfer.
22.6 As part of the Institution’s assessment of a Vendor or other third-party, the Institution will request copies of any self-assessments or third-party assessments that the Vendor or third-party has access to.

title: Clinical IT Hub Multispecialty and Research Hospital (MSRH)
text:
OpTime
This application is used to prepare, schedule, and document all information related to surgery and the operating room. It is used in the Operating Room, Endoscopy room, Pre-Admission Testing clinics. This application is used to by PAT staff, Surgical nurses, Surgeons, Preference card builders, Schedulers, Billers. Key words include, surgeon, greaseboards, operating room, implant, supplies, preference cards, status boards, snapboard.
Anesthesia
Application used for any patients receiving anesthesia. Can be used in the operating room, Interventional Radiology, Special Procedure Rooms, PAT clinics, Pain Management. Key words include, anesthesiologist, CRNA documentation, preprocedure, postproced, intraprocedure, sedation
Inpatient Willow
This application is used for the ordering, verifying, preparing, dispensing, and charging for medications in the hospital setting (admitted patients). Pharmacy dispenses to inpatient units and outpatient units that are administering medications on site. This application does not support the take home prescriptions, this would be handled by a different application. This application is used by inpatient pharmacists, pharmacy technicians. Key words include pharmacy, pharmacist, pharmacy tech, dispense, hospital medications, compound and repackaging.
Cupid
This application is used to order and document cardiology procedures and cases. Includes invasive (eventually) and non-invasive procedures such as echo. This application is used by cardiologists, imaging techs, cardiovascular nurses. Key words include cardiologists, cardiac, echo, EKG.
Lumens

title: Clinical IT Hub Multispecialty and Research Hospital (MSRH)
text:
Cupid
This application is used to order and document cardiology procedures and cases. Includes invasive (eventually) and non-invasive procedures such as echo. This application is used by cardiologists, imaging techs, cardiovascular nurses. Key words include cardiologists, cardiac, echo, EKG.
Lumens
This application supports endoscopy workflows. Endoscopists use this to document their findings, automatically create an anatomical summary, and review and incorporate images from procedures with Lumens. When they have finished documenting procedure details and findings, endoscopists can pull nursing information, images taken during the procedure, and information documented on the anatomical diagram into a professional procedure report. Procedures supported include colonoscopy, EGD, Bronchoscopy and a few others. This application is used by endoscopists, Gastroenterologists, Endoscopy nurses, Pulmonologists. Key words include, endoscopy, gastroenterology, GI, bronchoscopy.
ASAP
Used by Acute Care Clinical staff to document clinical care in the ACC. Called ASAP because of the fast paced nature of the area. Key words for this application include, emergency, ACC, triage, trackboard, ED narrator
Inpatient Clinical Documentation
Used for documentation on admitted patients (inpatient), usually in hospitals. Primary purpose is to ensure inpatient patient information is documented appropriately in the chart. This application supports notes, assessments, flowsheets, medication administration, plan of care, the brain, virtual nursing, remote sitters, patient education. Key words for this application include, MAR, flowsheets, worklist, brain, medication administration, rehab, wound care, IV.
Inpatient Orders

title: Clinical IT Hub Multispecialty and Research Hospital (MSRH)
text:
Inpatient Orders
Used to assist in providers’ orders for admitted patients, Examples of orders include labs, imaging, medications, nutrition, consults. Areas to commonly assist in include finding orders, placing orders, editing order details, cosigning or signing orders. Used primarily by physicians nurses, midlevel providers, Residents. Key words include orders, admitted patients, cosign orders, verbal order, patient lists, system lists.
Bugsy
This application is used for infection control to monitor and report certain types of infections (like MRSA, sepsis) in inpatient settings. Data can be abstracted in order to research patients with potential infections, and confirmed cases can then be sent to infection control agencies. Used by Infection Preventionists, Infection Control Agencies. Key words include, infection control, infection preventionist, infection control agency, antimicrobial stewardship, Hospital Associated Infection (HAI).
Clinical Case Management
This application is used to identify patients in need of ongoing assistance, conduct utilization review to ensure payers will cover the cost of the patients' hospital stays. Coordinate the care that patients receive post-discharge, such as contacting long-term care facilities and arranging physical therapy. This application is used within the inpatient setting only. This is used by inpatient case managers, social workers. Key words include, case manager, payer communication, utilization review, discharge planning.

title: Meet Art, Penny, and Emmie
text: Strategic investments are centered on three core audiences: clinicians, revenue cycle teams, and patients. AI-enabled Epic tools help reduce burden, improve operational performance, and expand access—creating measurable value across care delivery, financial operations, and patient engagement. Meet Art, Penny, and Emmie.

title: Meet Art, Penny, and Emmie
headingPath: Epic Art: Smarter Documentation, Happier Clinicians
text:
Epic Art is a clinician-facing AI assistant built directly into Epic workflows. It helps with chart review, documentation summarization, and order placement—quietly reducing the time and mental effort required to get through the day.
By easing documentation burden and supporting consistent, accurate charting, Art gives clinicians back something precious: time. Time to focus on patients, not paperwork. As staffing struggles persist across healthcare, Art offers a scalable way to support provider efficiency while helping combat burnout and improve retention.

title: Meet Art, Penny, and Emmie
headingPath: Epic Penny: AI Where Revenue Really Counts
text:
Epic Penny focuses on one of the highest-effort areas in healthcare operations: the revenue cycle. Designed to support billing review, follow-up, and insurance appeals, Penny helps teams work faster and more accurately.
In an environment of ongoing financial pressure, Penny provides targeted AI support that strengthens billing performance while reducing manual workload and burnout. It’s a smart investment in financial resilience with minimal operational risk.

title: Meet Art, Penny, and Emmie
headingPath: Epic Emmie: Always-On Support for Patients
text:
Epic Emmie is a patient-facing virtual assistant embedded within Epic platforms. From scheduling help to billing questions and general inquiries, Emmie gives patients quick, consistent answers—when they need them.
As expectations for digital access continue to rise, Emmie expands self-service options while easing the load on call centers and frontline staff. The result? Better access, faster support, and more staff capacity for complex, high-touch interactions.

title: Meet Art, Penny, and Emmie
text: Together, Art, Penny, and Emmie represent a practical, people-centered approach to AI—one that scales support without sacrificing quality, safety, or experience. They don’t replace expertise; they amplify it—helping clinicians, staff, and patients each get what they need most.

title: NEW Epic Modules are Transforming Health Care at KSP and across UTHSA
text:
UT Health San Antonio and our new Kyle Seal Parkway (KSP) facility continue to make significant strides with the recent go-lives of numerous Epic BetterCare modules and enhancements. The latest implementations are pivotal in our commitment to providing top-notch patient care and streamlining operations.
The KSP Ambulatory Surgical Center (ASC) celebrated its launch on April 15, introducing cutting-edge Epic modules like OpTime for Surgery and Anesthesia tailored to enhance surgical procedures. With OpTime for Surgery and Anesthesia modules, our teams have advanced tools to optimize surgical workflows, ensuring precision and efficiency at every step. Lumens for GI and Endoscopy is another Epic module that went live on April 25, solidifying our dedication to comprehensive patient care across all specialties.
On April 19, Refuel Phase 2h went live, bringing a wave of enhancements and new Epic modules. Notably, KSP stands as a beacon of innovation as the first in the world to implement Gallery for Document Management. Other additions, including Bones for Orthopedics, Hello World for Patient SMS Messaging, Mosaiq for Radiation Oncology, and a comprehensive Referrals Overhaul, exemplify our relentless pursuit of excellence in patient management and communication. In addition to these groundbreaking launches, we underwent a successful Epic Upgrade to Version Nov2023 on April 9, ensuring our systems remain at the forefront of technological advancement.

title: NEW Epic Modules are Transforming Health Care at KSP and across UTHSA
text: These milestones underscore UT Health San Antonio’s unwavering commitment to revolutionizing health care delivery through Epic BetterCare. With each implementation, we reaffirm our dedication to providing patients with the highest quality of care while equipping our health care professionals with the tools they need to excel in their roles. As we continue this journey of innovation, KSP remains steadfast in our mission to redefine health care standards for the betterment of our community.

title: New IT Features To Elevate Your Precision, Speed & Insights
headingPath: 🗣️Abridge Verbatim Mode: Precision Documentation, Made Effortless
text:
Capture every word, every nuance—Verbatim Mode blends summarized notes with verbatim detail, giving you a complete, accurate clinical record without extra clicks.
➡ Exact transcription for crystal-clear documentation.
➡ Context preserved so nothing is lost in translation.
➡ Intuitive design for fast, easy access to what matters most.
Learn more about Verbatim >

title: New IT Features To Elevate Your Precision, Speed & Insights
text:
With Aura, Epic brings specialty lab integration into the fast lane. Say goodbye to time-consuming configuration—connect once to labs like Natera, Caris, and Guardant, and download ready-to-go packages to activate in your Epic build. Orders and results flow through your existing workflows—no more scanned PDFs or disjointed processes. Oncology teams, this is a game-changer.
➡ Seamlessly send orders and receive discrete results from specialty labs using workflows you already know.
➡ Streamline patient result delivery through MyChart—no extra steps needed.
Learn more about Aura >

title: New IT Features To Elevate Your Precision, Speed & Insights
headingPath: 📝 ProcDoc for Dermatology: Document Procedures in Seconds
text:
Derm providers, meet your new favorite shortcut. Just type “.procdoc” and watch your note write itself. Standardize mole removals, skin excisions, and more with procedure-specific smart forms. You’ll save time, reduce errors, and ensure consistent documentation—all while orders, charges, and notes are placed in one go.
➡ Faster notes. Cleaner documentation. Fewer clicks. Learn more about ProcDoc >

title: New IT Features To Elevate Your Precision, Speed & Insights
headingPath: 🗺️ SlicerDicer Geovisualization: See Your Data on a Map
text:
Data just got visual. Now, researchers, physicians, and schedulers can view patient trends by ZIP code. Discover geographic patterns and visualize population health insights with geocoded data and interactive maps—all within SlicerDicer.
➡ Where are your patients coming from? Where should outreach go next? Now you’ll know. Learn more about Geovisualization>

title: New IT Features To Elevate Your Precision, Speed & Insights

Epic is now connected through Trusted Exchange Framework (TEFCA), the federal initiative supporting seamless EHI exchange across the U.S. This expands your access to patient data—safely, securely, and instantly—across health systems and networks.
➡ No matter where your patient has been, you’ll have their records right when you need them. Learn more about TEFCA >

text:
The Registration and Eligibility workflow has been enhanced with Experian’s Patient Access Curator. Working in conjunction with Real-Time Eligibility, the Patient Access Curator accurately identifies patient insurance coverage and eligible benefits.…
The Registration and Eligibility workflow has been enhanced with Experian’s Patient Access Curator. Working in conjunction with Real-Time Eligibility, the Patient Access Curator accurately identifies patient insurance coverage and eligible benefits. This behind-the-scenes enhancement reduces the need for staff to contact multiple insurance agencies and manually verify coverage, saving time and improving efficiency.
The Patient Access Scheduling Optimization Project is in full swing. The project includes a review of each specialty offered at UT Health and their scheduling workflows before the end of Fiscal Year 2026.
The primary objectives of this initiative are to:
Integrate Scheduling Criteria:
Transition all scheduling criteria currently documented into Epic's electronic scheduling system.
Improve Scheduling Efficiency:
Increase Accuracy: Enhance the precision of staff scheduling.
Reduce Appointment Scheduling Time: Minimize the time required to schedule appointments across specialty areas.
Implement Patient Self-Scheduling:
Introduce self-scheduling options for patients through MyChart, allowing them to book appointments independently.

title: Patient Access Scheduling, Registration, Admissions & Referrals
text:
Transitioning to a self-scheduling model will significantly decrease the need for staff involvement in the scheduling process, streamlining operations and improving the overall patient experience.
Historically, patients who schedule their own appointments have demonstrated lower no-show rates compared to those scheduled through other methods.
Gastroenterology, Ophthalmology, and Orthopedics completed scheduling optimization and went live in March 2026, with the following services:
Guided Patient Scheduling: Decision Trees (electronic algorithms) will be added to the scheduling workflows to walk the scheduling staff through gathering pertinent information that is required to schedule the patient’s appointment. The decision trees will assure that the patient is scheduled with the appropriate provider and department.
Ticket Scheduling: Order based scheduling that is initiated by the provider through a referral or follow-up appointment. A scheduling ticket is sent to the patient to allow the patient to schedule the appointment. The ticket will include the visit type, provider, department and time frame in which the appointment will be scheduled.
Direct or Self-Scheduling: Patient initiated scheduling of routine visits such as follow-up and annual examinations. The patient will be able to schedule visits with providers and in departments in which they have an established relationship.

title: Patient Access Scheduling, Registration, Admissions & Referrals
text:
System Guided Scheduling automatically finds the best appointment options to ensure patients see the right provider, at the right location, and at the right time, while following organizational rules. This approach improves patient service and helps reduce operational costs.
During your department's Guided Scheduling optimization engagement, the following Epic functionality will be reviewed:
Fast Pass - Use of the Wait List to send patients available appointments through MyChart messaging that meet the criteria. This is used to provide earlier appointments for patients.
Ticket Scheduling - The patient is sent an order-based scheduling ticket to schedule their appointment (e.g., visits, labs, radiology, colonoscopy, etc.). The ticket will include the department, provider, visit type and timeframe in which the appointment can be scheduled. Epic will use the criteria within the ticket to provide the patient with solutions for scheduling.
Direct Scheduling - The ability for a patient to schedule an established or follow-up visit with an existing provider.
Scheduled for go live in June 2026.

title: Recap: UT Health San Antonio's Inaugural AI Symposium in Clinical Healthcare
text:
- Share the healthcare innovation happening at UT Health San Antonio >
UT Health San Antonio’s Clinical IT Department recently hosted the university’s inaugural AI Symposium in Clinical Healthcare, bringing together over 200 physicians, nurses, faculty, executive and clinical leaders alongside national experts to explore how artificial intelligence is being applied across clinical care, education and operations.
Throughout the day, speakers from leading organizations including Microsoft, Epic Systems, Abridge and Qualified Health shared insights on how AI is transforming healthcare delivery today and what comes next.
Across each session, a consistent theme emerged: AI is not a future concept, but a present-day tool being actively integrated into care delivery.
Presentations explored how AI tools can be used today and, in the future, to streamline workflows, surface critical insights and better support both patients and clinicians.
Just as important as the breadth and depth of expertise in the room were the big questions being answered:
How do we reduce clinician burden, not add to it?
How do we identify patients who need care and reach them sooner?
How do we scale this responsibly across a complex health system?

title: Recap: UT Health San Antonio's Inaugural AI Symposium in Clinical Healthcare
text:
INTRODUCTION: INAUGURAL 2026 AI SYMPOSIUM IN CLINICAL HEALTHCARE | Watch the video
Robert Leverence, MD, Senior Vice President of Clinical Affairs, UT San Antonio
Rob Hromas, MD, Dean, Long School of Medicine, UT San Antonio
Edward Sankary, MD, Vice President and Chief Health Information and Value Officer, UT Health San Antonio
OVERVIEW OF AI IN EPIC | Watch the video
Christopher Alban, MD, MBA, VO, Clinical Informatics | Epic Systems
AI tools are embedded directly into the Epic electronic health record to support clinicians, care teams and patient care. From ambient listening that captures conversations during visits to intelligent medical record summaries that highlight the most relevant information in a patient’s chart, these tools are designed to reduce documentation burden, enhance care and improve efficiency.
Key takeaway: AI works best when it is built into existing workflows, helping clinicians act more quickly and confidently.
UT Health San Antonio impact: Integrating AI into Epic enables our clinicians to spend less time documenting and more time delivering high-quality, patient-centered care.
NOT ALL AI IS EQUAL: MATCHING LLM CAPABILITIES TO CLINICAL, ACADEMIC AND OPERATIONAL NEEDS | Watch the video
Susan Fenton, PhD, RHIA ACHIO FAMIA, Vice Dean of Education D. Bradley McWilliams School of Biomedical Informatics | UT Health Houston
AI applications span clinical care, education and operations, but not all tools are created equal. Successful adoption depends on aligning the right AI capabilities to the right use cases, from evidence-based clinical decision support to educational content development and administrative efficiency.
Key takeaway: AI delivers the most value when it is applied intentionally to specific needs, not broadly across all functions.

title: Recap: UT Health San Antonio's Inaugural AI Symposium in Clinical Healthcare
text:
Key takeaway: AI delivers the most value when it is applied intentionally to specific needs, not broadly across all functions.
UT Health San Antonio Impact: Thoughtful adoption and target use of different AI tools helps ensures AI is responsibly applied where it drives the greatest impact across patient care, education and operations.
POWER YOUR AI TRANSFORMATION WITH MICROSOFT CLOUD FOR HEALTHCARE | Watch the video
Charles Uche Emenugha, Cloud Solutions Architect | Microsoft
Scalable AI adoption requires more than tools. It depends on a strong digital foundation that integrates data, analytics and workflows. Platforms like Microsoft Azure and tools like Copilot enable organizations to operationalize AI across teams, streamline communications and improve productivity.
Key takeaway: AI transformation is driven by strategy, infrastructure and alignment around intentional outcomes.
UT Health San Antonio Impact: Continuous strengthening our data and cloud infrastructure will allow us to scale our AI solutions across the university and accelerate innovation.
CLINICAL INTELLIGENCE IN ACTION: OPTIMIZING CARDIOVASCULAR CARE FOR MILLIONS | Watch the video
Keval Desai, MD, MBA | Qualified Health
AI can analyze large volumes of patient data to identify individuals who may benefit from additional care, screenings or treatment adjustments. By surfacing care gaps and recommending next steps, these tools enable care teams to intervene earlier and more effectively.
Key takeaway: AI enables a shift from reactive care to proactive, data-driven interventions.
UT Health San Antonio Impact: Using AI tools, like Qualified Health to proactively identify care gaps can help us reach patients sooner, improve their outcomes and expand access to our life-saving care.
ABRIDGE: BUILDING HEALTHCARE'S FIRST UNIFIED INTELLIGENCE PLATFORM
Redi Conant, MD, Sr. Physician Executive | Abridge

title: Recap: UT Health San Antonio's Inaugural AI Symposium in Clinical Healthcare
text:
ABRIDGE: BUILDING HEALTHCARE'S FIRST UNIFIED INTELLIGENCE PLATFORM
Redi Conant, MD, Sr. Physician Executive | Abridge
Conversational AI is transforming clinical documentation by converting patient visits into structured notes in real time. These tools reduce administrative workload and support more accurate, efficient documentation and follow-up while enabling clinicians to stay focused on patient interactions.
Key takeaway: Reducing documentation burden improves both clinician experience and patient engagement.
UT Health San Antonio Impact: Reducing administrative burden during and after appointments reduces burnout and allows our clinicians to deliver a more informed, complete and connected care experience.
EFFICIENCY WITHOUT SACRIFICING TRANSPARENCY: BRINGING AI TO THE BEDSIDE | Watch the video
Leslie Schatz, Head of Innovation and Product Marketing | UpToDate, Wolters Kluwer Health
As AI adoption accelerates, transparency and evidence-based design are critical to building trust. Clinicians must understand how AI-generated insights are developed and how they align with real clinical decision-making.
Key takeaway: Trust and transparency are essential for safe and effective AI use in healthcare.
UT Health San Antonio Impact: Prioritizing transparency and evidence-based decision making helps ensure the AI tools we use support safe, high-quality care and maintain the trust of our patients and care teams.
BUILDING THE AI IMAGING FACTORY: FROM DATA RETRIEVAL TO AUTONOMOUS AGENTS AND CLOSED-LOOP INNOVATION | Watch the video
Kal Clark, MD Associate Professor/Clinical | UT Health San Antonio Department of Radiology
Instead of fearing its impact, UT Health San Antonio is leveraging AI’s integrated data and large-scale clinical insights to develop and evaluate AI models in radiology and imaging practice. These efforts aim to improve efficiency, accuracy and scalability while contributing to the advancement of AI in medicine.

title: Recap: UT Health San Antonio's Inaugural AI Symposium in Clinical Healthcare
text:
Key takeaway: Access to comprehensive data and clinical expertise positions UT Health San Antonio to be an Academic Health Center leading in AI innovation.
UT Health San Antonio Impact: Our ability to use full care spectrum data to develop and validate our own AI models strengthens our leadership in advanced diagnostics and research-driven care.
PROTECTING THE DIGITAL HEALTH ENTERPRISE: CYBERSECURITY AND GOVERNANCE IN AI-ENABLED CARE AND RESEARCH | Watch the video
Michael Schnabel, MBA, Senior Vice President and Chief Information Officer | UT Health San Antonio
As AI capabilities expand, so does our responsibility to protect against cybersecurity risks and implement solid governance requirements. The university, state and federal government have regulations in place to protect patient data, enforce compliance and maintain accountability.
Key takeaway: Strong governance, user awareness and compliance are critical to safe and secure AI adoption.
UT Health San Antonio Impact: Creating, maintaining and training on our strong AI governance structure helps ensure we all adopt, deploy and advance digital technology innovation while protecting patient data, protected information, institutional integrity and trust.

title: School of Dentistry adopts Epic Wisdom to better serve patients
text:
By Kristin Zapata, Communications Specialist Senior The UT Health San Antonio School of Dentistry has integrated Epic Wisdom, a leading electronic health record (EHR) system, into its UT Dentistry clinics, advancing patient care by combining dental …
By Kristin Zapata, Communications Specialist Senior
The UT Health San Antonio School of Dentistry has integrated Epic Wisdom, a leading electronic health record (EHR) system, into its UT Dentistry clinics, advancing patient care by combining dental and medical health records. In a recent Health Innovations’ article, Lawrence Tabak, DDS, PhD, principal deputy director of the National Institutes of Health, stressed the importance of merging health records to provide more holistic, effective care.
“Somewhere along the way, the head was somehow dissociated from the rest of the body,” Tabak said. “What we really want to do here is put the head back on the rest of the body, both figuratively and of course metaphorically.” The move to Epic Wisdom replaces the previous dental-focused system, axiUm, and aligns with these national efforts to integrate medical and dental care. “With Epic Wisdom, our students, residents and faculty are better equipped to address the complex health care needs of patients,” said Peter M. Loomer, DDS, PhD, MBA, dean of the UT Health San Antonio School of Dentistry. “This transition reflects the growing recognition of the impact of oral health on overall health and the significant role dentists and dental hygienists play in patient care and well-being.”

Peter M. Loomer, DDS, PhD, MBA

title: School of Dentistry adopts Epic Wisdom to better serve patients
text: Epic Wisdom promises to better streamline care by offering dental providers access to patients’ medical histories, enabling more informed treatment decisions and coordinated care. Patients are now able to view all their medical and dental records, appointments and test results in one place through Epic’s MyChart platform, improving their overall health care experience. The system’s user-friendly design and advanced capabilities support digital workflows in dental clinics, enhancing efficiency and patient outcomes.

title: School of Dentistry adopts Epic Wisdom to better serve patients
text:
The transition to Epic Wisdom culminated on Dec. 10 after months of preparation, including transferring five years of patient records and radiology data, customizing the system and conducting training workshops for faculty, staff, residents and students. “The workgroups from clinical, administrative and service departments worked side by side with the Epic Wisdom implementation team” said Gary F. Guest, DDS, the school’s chief information officer. “We had one of Epic’s most extensive transfers of dental data from the legacy system to Epic, which facilitated the immediate use of the system for patients on the first day of deployment.”
The integration of Epic Wisdom aims to strengthen patient care and prepare dental students for real-world practice in an increasingly connected health care environment. Faculty and staff continue refining workflows and training processes to maximize the system’s benefits. This latest milestone reinforces the School of Dentistry’s commitment to deliver patient-centered, high-quality care while supporting its mission of education, research and community outreach.

title: Stephanie Johnson honored with 2023-2024 Non-Clinical Gold Shield Award for Epic Care Team excellence
text:
Stephanie Johnson, a key member of the Epic Care Team at UT Health San Antonio, has been awarded the 2023-2024 Non-Clinical Gold Shield Award for her exceptional contributions to patient safety. Johnson's ability to retain information with an unparalleled level of detail has significantly impacted patient safety and outcomes. Her knowledge and expertise have made her an invaluable asset in streamlining the process of creating, reviewing and finalizing treatment plans.
One of Johnson's standout achievements is her role in developing comprehensive order sets for Mays Cancer Center, home to the UT Health San Antonio MD Anderson Cancer Center. By identifying and addressing key safety concerns for various treatments, she has helped enhance patient experience at every step. Her work has ensured that new and updated treatment plans are implemented efficiently, prioritizing the well-being of patients.
Johnson's innovative approach to maintaining the treatment plan library is another example of her outstanding work. By creating treatment groups, she can make single changes that update numerous plans simultaneously. This method improved patient safety and generated significant cost savings. For instance, when literature showed that lower doses of anti-nausea medication reduced side effects, Johnson swiftly updated all treatment plans to reflect this, ensuring better patient outcomes.
Her quick response in addressing potential safety risks, such as identifying errors in how Epic was interpreting home medications, further demonstrates her dedication. Consistently approachable and committed, Johnson embodies the values of UT Health San Antonio, earning her the prestigious Gold Shield award.

The Epic Thrive Workshop is essential for ordering providers seeking to maximize their efficiency and enhance patient care through effective use of the Epic electronic health record (EHR) system. The Epic Thrive Workshop not only equips ordering providers with vital skills but also significantly saves time, allowing them to focus more on their patients and less on navigating the EHR system.
Read the Continuing Education Statements section for more information.
- Watch Video (1:52 min)
- Why you should enroll in Epic Thrive
Epic currently offers Thrive sessions for outpatient, inpatient, surgical, dentistry, anesthesia, and ASAP providers. In these 2-3-hour workshops, an Epic trainer demonstrates and assists attendees as they adjust key user settings in their production environments. All Epic-led Thrive sessions have small class sizes to enable trainers to assist with individual questions as attendees practice.
According to the KLAS Arch Collaborative, clinicians who spend 3-5 hours a year on ongoing training are 2-3 times more satisfied with their EHR.1.
Thrive training helps clinicians establish good efficiency habits and tailor their workspaces to support their personal workflows. Users can apply the knowledge from Thrive training to their own work or use it to help educate others. Thrive training is hands-on and moves at a pace that encourages questions and participation, allowing clinicians to walk away from class ready to use what they learned the next time they log in to the system for patient care.

title: Transforming Health Care with AI: Insights from the 2025 UT System AI Symposium
text:
Enjoy this brief recap of the inspiring two-day symposium.
The 2025 UT System AI Symposium in Healthcare, held May 15–16 in Houston, Texas at the Helix Park TMC3 Collaborative Building, brought together leading voices in academic medicine, technology, and industry to explore the transformative potential of artificial intelligence in healthcare. Spanning two days of keynotes, panels, research showcases and student presentations, the event demonstrated the University of Texas System's commitment to advancing AI-driven innovation across its institutions.
Enjoy this brief recap of the inspiring two-day symposium.

links.text: 2025 UT System AI Symposium in Healthcare

title: Transforming Health Care with AI: Insights from the 2025 UT System AI Symposium
headingPath: A Visionary Start: Opening Remarks and Welcome
text: The symposium opened with remarks from Dr. John Zerwas of the UT System Office of Health Affairs, followed by institutional welcomes from Dr. Peter Pisters (UT MD Anderson), Dr. Peter McCaffrey (UTMB), and Dr. Jiajie Zhang (UTHealth Houston). Together, they set the tone for the summit, emphasizing collaboration, shared infrastructure and the strategic importance of AI across the UT health ecosystem.

title: Transforming Health Care with AI: Insights from the 2025 UT System AI Symposium
headingPath: Keynote Highlights: Academic and Clinical Perspectives
text:
Dr. Peter Embi, Chair of Biomedical Informatics at Vanderbilt University Medical Center, delivered the academic keynote, addressing the future of AI in academic medicine. He emphasized the need for ethical, scalable and collaborative approaches to integrating AI into research and clinical workflows.
Dr. Jochen Reiser, President and CEO of UTMB Health, delivered the afternoon keynote on Day 1, offering a Texas-based perspective on the institutional leadership and infrastructure required to make AI impactful at the bedside.

title: Transforming Health Care with AI: Insights from the 2025 UT System AI Symposium
text:
Panels throughout the symposium addressed the implementation of AI strategies at both system-wide and national levels. Notable sessions included:
One UT Health System AI Collaboration Strategy, moderated by Zain Kazmi (UT System), featuring insights from leaders across UT institutions, including our Dr. Edward Sankary, Chair of the UT-HIP AI in Healthcare Collaborative, on shared governance and data infrastructure.
Nationwide AI Collaboratives, featuring speakers from Vanderbilt, Microsoft, and the Coalition for Health AI, discussing national standards, interoperability and partnerships.
The Future of AI in Healthcare – Industry, Entrepreneur, & VC Perspectives, bringing together investors and startup founders to examine the commercialization and clinical scalability of AI technologies.
Fireside Chat: Brining AI from Innovation to Bedside which featured leaders from the HRIs, including Dr. Edward Sankary from UT Health San Antonio, discussing how to deploy AI in clinical practice.

headingPath: Breakout Sessions Tracks on highly Relevant AI Topics
text:
AI Governance and Regulation
AI in Clinical Trials & Drug Discovery
AI in Medical Imaging & Diagnostics

title: Transforming Health Care with AI: Insights from the 2025 UT System AI Symposium
headingPath: Innovation on Display: Showcases and Lightning Talks
text:
Day 1 included the UT Health Enterprise Innovation Show & Tell, moderated by Dr. Susan Fenton (UTHealth Houston), where researchers presented operational and clinical AI solutions in development across campuses.
Day 2 featured Industry Lightning Talks with speakers from Microsoft, AWS, Meta, Palantir, Hippocratic AI, and Epic, offering a fast-paced overview of how leading tech firms are approaching healthcare data challenges.
The Future of AI in Healthcare – Industry, Entrepreneur and Venture Capitalist Perspective, with speakers from Microsoft and startups, including Qualified Health which is providing a trial of a secure chatbot to UT Health San Antonio.
The Student Lightning Talks showcased emerging talent from across the UT System, with six finalists presenting projects in clinical decision support, imaging, and digital health.

title: Transforming Health Care with AI: Insights from the 2025 UT System AI Symposium
headingPath: Closing the Loop: Strategic Reflections and a Call to Action
text:
The symposium concluded with a closing panel moderated by Dr. Jiajie Zhang, featuring academic leaders from UT Austin, UT MD Anderson, UTHealth Houston, UTMB and UT Southwestern. The discussion focused on moving from aspiration to execution and ensuring AI initiatives remain grounded in academic rigor and clinical relevance.
Final remarks by Nyma Shah (UT MD Anderson), Dr. Peter McCaffrey, and Dr. Xiaoqian Jiang (UTHealth Houston) underscored the value of continued collaboration and the importance of sustaining the momentum built during the symposium.

title: UT Health's 90-Day Go Live Risk Assessment: Preparing for December 10th Epic Go-Lives
text:
As we gear up for the December 10th Epic go-lives, we want to share some valuable information about our 90-Day Go-Live Readiness Assessment (GLRA). On September 11, we will conduct a brief (one and a half hours) assessment of our new systems across the Multispecialty and Research Hospital, the School of Dentistry and Refuel Phase 4. The GLRA will provide numerous opportunities for both our workforce and the institution including:
Ensuring a Smooth Transition
The GLRA helps us spot and tackle any potential bumps in the road before we go live. This way, our everyday operations will experience less disruption, allowing you to continue providing outstanding service to our patients and clients.
Enhanced Training and Support
We are rolling out comprehensive training and support that will help you feel confident and ready to use the new system. We're investing in your success, ensuring you feel equipped with all the skills you need! Visit our BetterCare training site for more information.
Operational Readiness
We’ll be checking in on the readiness of our clinical workflows and financial operations to make sure everything is on track. This means you're free to focus on what you do best.
Open Communication and Collaboration
The GLRA encourages open discussions about any challenges we might face. Sharing our thoughts helps everyone feel involved and appreciated, making our team stronger!
Identifying and Mitigating Risks
By identifying any risks in advance, we can work together to tackle them. This proactive approach ensures that your day-to-day activities run smoothly.
Clear Next Steps and Responsibilities
The GLRA will map out clear responsibilities and next steps for all team members! This clarity will help us reduce confusion and while generating efficiencies.

title: UT Health San Antonio Achieves Epic’s Gold Stars Level 6
text:
Congratulations to our UT Health San Antonio Information Technology team on reaching Epic’s Gold Stars Level 6. This recognition is a testament to your hard work and dedication in implementing our institution’s focused electronic health record (EHR)…
Congratulations to our UT Health San Antonio Information Technology team on reaching Epic’s Gold Stars Level 6. This recognition is a testament to your hard work and dedication in implementing our institution’s focused electronic health record (EHR) solutions. By adopting at least 65% of the Epic Gold Stars features, you have positioned UT Health San Antonio as a cutting-edge organization and a leader in EHR use.
The primary driver of UT Health San Antonio’s Epic Gold Stars advancement has been our Epic Refuel program which launched last year to achieve greater efficiency, usability, and integration. Refuel will help modernize our Epic system, increase adoption of features and modules, reduce the risk of system failure, expedite quarterly upgrades, and increase user satisfaction, efficiency, and usability.
The Information Technology team continues to march forward with 12 of 38 Applications already at Gold Stars Level 10. The next Refuel package with several new upgrades, features, and Gold Stars items will go live on October 15, 2024, at 9 PM.
Thank you, team, for your dedication to maximizing our Epic EHR system to provide an improved, safer, and more efficient user/patient experience.

UT Health San Antonio leaders joined colleagues from health institutions across The University of Texas System for the 9th Biannual Epic/UT Leadership Summit to collaborate on advancing digital health innovation that supports providers, care teams and patients.

title: Highlights from the 9th Biannual Epic/UT Leadership Summit
text:
Nearly 80 leaders from UT System and Epic recently gathered at the 2026 Epic UT System Leadership Summit in Verona, Wisconsin to focus on strengthening collaboration, aligning strategic priorities and accelerating digital health innovation across institutions.
A new UT System initiative emerged from the summit's Cross-Institution Governance Panel, where Ed Sankary, MD, Vice President and Chief Health Information and Value Officer, and Julie Wingate, MSN, RN-NI, AVP, Clinical Information Systems, shared perspectives on navigating different governance structures while advancing systemwide progress.
“This initiative will give UT System institutions, including UT Health San Antonio, a more efficient way to evaluate Epic AI features, understand how they can support patient care and move the right solutions toward implementation,” Sankary said.
Artificial intelligence (AI) and analytics were major themes throughout the summit. Sessions explored how UT Health San Antonio and UT institutions can move beyond pilot programs by using advanced analytics to support decision-making and adopt emerging technologies such as ambient listening and other AI tools designed to support patient care.
Important infrastructure topics surrounded cloud migration, downtime preparedness, digital accessibility and login delays, all critical components for maintaining reliability and readiness across health systems. Epic Cogito Cloud (cloud migration) offers new business intelligence capabilities, including the ability to use natural-language chat to query Epic on financial and clinical questions. Agent Factory, is an emerging Epic feature that allows health systems to create customized AI agents that can perform tasks tailored to a health system's specific protocols, workflows and guidelines.

title: Highlights from the 9th Biannual Epic/UT Leadership Summit
text:
Breakout sessions brought UT System teams together to collaborate on initiatives impacting clinical care, infrastructure, revenue cycle, patient access and pharmacy. During the Clinical Breakout Session, Sankary guided discussions on clinical optimization, AI reporting metrics, clinician wellbeing and operational continuity. For the Patient Access Breakout Session, Chatchawin Assanasen, MD, Associate Chief Medical Officer for UT Health San Antonio focused the group on initiatives aimed at improving patient flow and access across UT health institutions, including scheduling modernization, Emmie readiness and referral automation.
Additional breakout topics aligned UT System priorities with digital health innovation including research modernization, clinical trial matching, Gold Stars adoption and Epic Willow for pharmacy operations.
The summit concluded with leadership commitments to continue advancing this work, reinforcing a shared vision for coordinated progress across the UT System. Through continued cross-institutional collaboration, the focus is on improving efficiency, accelerating technology adoption and enhancing patient care at UT Health San Antonio and across all UT System health institutions.

title: UTHSA2026AISymposium
text:
“Not All AI Is Equal: Matching LLM Capabilities to Clinical, Academic, and Operational Needs”
Susan H. Fenton, PhD, RHIA, ACHIP, FAMIA
Dr. Fenton is a professor and the first McWilliams Vice Dean for Education. In addition, she directs the Center for Quality Health IT Improvement. Fenton's research focus areas include workforce development, ICD-11, and the optimal use of health information technology for chronic and preventive care in low-resource settings. In 2019, Dr. Fenton received the UT System Regent’s Outstanding Teaching Award. The next year, she was named as a member of The University of Texas Kenneth I. Shine, MD Academy of Health Science Education and awarded the title of UT System Distinguished Teaching Professor. Fenton later earned the UTHealth Houston President’s Scholar Award for Teaching for 2021. During her time at the school, Dr. Fenton has led the creation of the school’s newest degree, the Doctorate in Health Informatics, and directed the effort to make updates to the Master’s program so it could earn CAHIIM accreditation.

title: UTHSA2026AISymposium
text:
“Building the AI Imaging Factory: From Data Retrieval to Autonomous Agents and Closed-Loop Innovation”
Kal L. Clark, MD, Assoc. Professor/Clinical, Vice Chair for Informatics
Dr. Clark is the Vice-Chair of Informatics and an Associate Professor of Radiology. His primary clinical expertise is emergency and trauma radiology in the Division of Emergency Radiology. Academic interests include artificial intelligence as it relates to error mitigation, disease classification, disease diagnosis, radiation safety, and general quality improvement. He is a member of the UTSA MATRIX AI Consortium for Human Well-Being and the UT System CAID (Consortium for AI in Diagnostics). Dr. Clark is fellowship-trained in neuroradiology. He completed his medical training at the Washington University in St Louis School of Medicine and completed his radiology residency and neuroradiology fellowship at Duke University in Durham, North Carolina.

title: UTHSA2026AISymposium
text:
"Efficiency without Sacrificing Transparency: Bringing AI to the Bedside"
Leslie Schatz, Head of Innovation & Product Marketing
Leslie has dedicated her entire career to delivering better healthcare through technology. She plays a strategic role in launching new products and capabilities within the Clinical Effectiveness business, including several flagship product launches for UpToDate®. She is most interested in the intersection of how access to data and clinicogenomics will lead to decreased clinical trial phase durations. She is also watching the practical application of value-based care and the regulatory environment that may enable it.
Before joining Wolters Kluwer, Leslie served as the Chief Product Officer for Analytics at Optum, where she built new products within the Life Sciences space, launched new Payer offerings, ran a data-enabled healthcare digital marketing business, and collaborated to make an Analytics Center of Excellence a reality for Optum’s healthcare customers. Leslie came to Optum via the acquisition of the Advisory Board Company, where she spent 16+ years in a variety of roles. Most notably, Leslie served as General Manager of several of the former Crimson technology products, which served providers in helping them make operational, financial, clinical, and purchasing decisions with analytics. Prior to that, she held account management, national accounts, product management, customer success, and consulting roles across a variety of provider-centric disciplines in the analytics space.
Leslie enjoys public speaking and has spoken about analytics, technology, and healthcare data at numerous conferences, podcasts, web conferences, and summits including Scottsdale Institute, Becker's webinars, multiple Advisory Boards, and Optum conferences.

He holds three patents contributing to Epic’s ongoing innovation and has presented internationally on interoperability, EHR usage, and physician well-being.

Michael Schnabel, MBA, Vice President and Chief Information Officer
Michael Schnabel is the Vice President and Chief Information Officer at UT San Antonio, overseeing the university’s technology environment, including research and teaching support, administrative systems, information security, and technical services.
He previously spent more than a decade at UT Health San Antonio as chief information security officer and assistant vice president for information security and operations, where he modernized cybersecurity and network infrastructure and led major initiatives across academic, research, and clinical domains. Earlier roles include information security officer at City of Hope National Medical Center and senior vice president/CIO at Gateway Business Bank. He holds an MBA in Information Technology Management and a Bachelor of Science in Cybersecurity and Information Assurance from Western Governors University.

title: UTHSA2026AISymposium

“Clinical Intelligence in Action: Optimizing Cardiovascular Care for Millions of Texans”
Keval Desai, MD, MBA, AI and Data Science Lead, Qualified Health
Keval Desai, MD, MBA, is an Internal Medicine Physician at Stanford University and the Clinical Lead for Care Delivery at Qualified Health AI. He earned his medical degree from Yale University along with a business degree from the Yale School of Management, completed his internal medicine residency at Yale New Haven Hospital, and received specialized primary care training at the West Haven VA Center of Excellence. He has held leadership roles at Oak Street Health and CVS Health, and has prior experience with the North Carolina state health department. His work sits at the intersection of care delivery, AI transformation, value-based care, and population health. He is focused on leveraging technology and systems design to improve patient outcomes at scale while making it easier for physicians and healthcare team members to do their best work.

Reid Conant, MD, Sr. Physician Executive, Abridge
As Sr. Physician Executive at Abridge, Dr. Reid Conant brings extensive experience as a Physician Executive and Innovator, dedicated to leveraging AI to transform healthcare delivery. As a leader in the speech and ambient fields for more than a decade, Reid brings cross-functional perspective and drives innovation through teamwork with the Product, Engineering, Implementation, Strategy and Business Development teams at Abridge. He focuses on building and bringing technologies to market that enhance provider workflows, reduce burnout, improve patient care, and improve productivity and profitability. Previously, Dr. Conant founded Conant and Associates, Inc., guiding it through its acquisition by Nuance Communications (later acquired by Microsoft). As CMIO, he led initiatives in Virtual Assistant, Ambient Clinical Intelligence, and other cutting-edge AI-based technologies. He is passionate about driving AI-powered innovation to create a more efficient, high-quality healthcare system. Dr. Conant is board certified in both Emergency Medicine and Clinical Informatics.

title: UTHSA2026AISymposium

Charles Emenugha, Cloud Solutions Architect, Microsoft
Charles Emenugha is a Cloud Solution Architect at Microsoft, specializing in Microsoft 365 Copilot, AI adoption, enterprise mobility, and modern workforce transformation. Based in the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area, Charles serves within Microsoft's US SLED (State, Local, Education & Defense) Customer Success Unit, where he partners with higher education institutions, academic medical centers, and public sector organizations to accelerate their AI and cloud journeys. With deep expertise in Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, Copilot Studio, Azure AI, and enterprise security platforms, Charles has led large-scale AI adoption programs, executive briefings, and end-user enablement sessions for some of the nation's leading institutions — including universities, health systems, and government agencies. He is a recognized trusted advisor in the areas of AI strategy, cloud governance, prompt engineering, and Copilot extensibility.
Charles holds a Bachelor of Technology in Project Management, a Special Executive Master's Program in Information Technology, and is a Doctor of Business Administration candidate, with a focus on Cybersecurity Management. He is also a certified Microsoft trainer and accredited technical educator.
Outside of work, Charles enjoys chess, scrabble, karate, and exploring mountains, historical landmarks, and scenic destinations around the world.

title: Understanding Verbatim Mode in Abridge
text: Verbatim Mode is a feature in the Abridge Clinician App that helps providers create accurate medical notes by mixing summarized content with word-for-word recordings, including pauses, stutters, coughing, etc. It’s designed to make documenting visits easier, faster, and more precise.

title: Understanding Verbatim Mode in Abridge
text: Verbatim Mode lets clinicians record parts of a visit exactly as spoken. While the app normally creates a summarized “ambient” note, Verbatim Mode captures detailed sections—like imaging reads or important discussions—that must be kept word-for-word. This content appears as polished text in the final note, with grammar and spelling corrected.

title: Understanding Verbatim Mode in Abridge
text:
To start, clinicians tap “+ Verbatim Content.” The app shows real-time transcription while recording. After recording, they can choose which section of the note to add it to—like Results, HPI, or Assessment and Plan. These snippets show up in blue in the final note and can be edited or copied.
Users can also create a verbatim only note, which is built entirely from recorded verbatim content instead of summarized audio. These notes don’t include transcripts or Patient Visit Summaries.

title: Understanding Verbatim Mode in Abridge
text: Before finalizing, clinicians can preview their notes and add more verbatim snippets if needed. For integrated systems, notes can be sent directly to the electronic health record (EHR), like Epic, without extra steps.

title: Understanding Verbatim Mode in Abridge
headingPath: When Verbatim Mode Is Most Helpful
text:
The guide recommends using Verbatim Mode when accuracy matters most, such as:
Pre-charting summaries
Independent interpretations of imaging
Hospital follow-ups
Risks and benefits discussions
Attestations
Simple checkups or brief visit notes
Telephone encounters or Inbasket messages
Snippets can be recorded before or after the ambient note is created, making the process flexible.

title: Understanding Verbatim Mode in Abridge
text: The feature works only on the mobile app version 3.6 or later and currently supports English. Verbatim snippets can be edited in the web editor but not on the mobile app. If internet connection is lost, real-time transcription stops until the device reconnects.

title: Virtual nursing enhances patient care through Epic technology at UT Health San Antonio’s MSRH
text:
In a cutting-edge initiative, UT Health San Antonio’s Multispecialty and Research Hospital (MSRH) has integrated virtual nursing into its patient care model, leveraging Epic technology to elevate the quality of care provided to patients. This innovative approach introduces a new layer of support for both patients and nursing staff, enhancing quality, efficiency and communication within health care teams.
At the heart of this transformation are virtual nurses, who serve as an extension of the bedside nursing team. Assigned to specific units, these skilled professionals support the admission and discharge processes, streamline operations, and ensure that patients receive timely and effective care. By utilizing Epic's tools, virtual nurses manage tasks such as admission navigators and after-visit summaries while also providing vital patient education.
“One of the most critical responsibilities of virtual nurses is conducting continuous quality surveillance,” explained Nancy Doolittle, Chief Nursing Officer at MSRH. “The virtual nurses monitor patients remotely, watch for signs of condition deterioration and new orders, and allow bedside nurses to focus on hands-on patient care. This real-time support maximizes the bedside nurse's ability to engage directly with patients, ultimately improving patient satisfaction and outcomes,” added Doolittle.
Lindsey Greene, director of acute care nursing at MSRH, says, “Patients also benefit from this dual-nurse model, as they have 24/7 access to both their bedside nurse and a virtual nurse.” Greene added that the virtual nurse is just a call light away, ready to address any immediate concerns and ensure that the patient's needs are met promptly. This approach fosters a more connected and responsive care environment.

title: Virtual nursing enhances patient care through Epic technology at UT Health San Antonio’s MSRH
text:
Moreover, the virtual nurses actively participate in multidisciplinary rounds, collaborating with health care providers, patients and family members to enhance discharge planning and improve overall patient flow. This collaboration not only elevates the patient’s experience but also ensures that the health care team functions as a cohesive unit, with seamless, collaborative communication.
"The Epic virtual nursing platform offers a multitude of features and analytical tools that are crucial for patient care. It was specifically designed with input from virtual nurses to ensure they have access to vital data. This allows them to monitor patients closely and identify issues that might not be visible to bedside nurses, ultimately enhancing the overall quality of care," said Jason Harrington, information services administrator for UT Health Physicians.
As a pioneering model in San Antonio, this virtual nursing model is already demonstrating its impact, with positive feedback from staff members who express newfound appreciation for the additional support. The benefits of virtual nursing are tremendous:
- Improved staff satisfaction, mentorship for new nurses, and enhanced retention
- Increased patient and family satisfaction
- Optimized throughput with support for admissions, transfers, discharge planning, and coordination
- Augmented skill mix of the care team at the bedside
- Future-proofing for additional surges, disasters, and workforce shifts
- Promotion of patient safety, quality and enhancement of clinical outcomes

title: Virtual nursing enhances patient care through Epic technology at UT Health San Antonio’s MSRH
text:
- Augmented skill mix of the care team at the bedside
- Future-proofing for additional surges, disasters, and workforce shifts
- Promotion of patient safety, quality and enhancement of clinical outcomes
The virtual nursing team is currently operating with seven virtual nurses, with plans to expand to over 20, allowing for comprehensive coverage across various floors of the hospital. Doolittle says, “The integration of virtual nursing is a significant step forward in health care delivery, combining advanced technology with compassionate care. As our virtual nursing program continues to evolve, UT Health San Antonio is setting a new standard for patient care, demonstrating that even in a rapidly changing landscape the focus remains on providing exceptional relationship-based patient experiences.”
For more information about the virtual nursing initiative and the technology behind it, please watch our Virtual Video or listen to our Virtual Nursing Podcast.

title: WhatsNew
text:
The Pro Workflow
Access the Abridge tab:
Right-click within your Abridge text in your note (or tap the circle with ellipses ...) and select Linked Evidence to open the Abridge activity panel.
Request: Enter your instruction (e.g., "Add more family history into the HPI") in the Abridge Assist tab.
Note: Processing may take 30-60 seconds for complex requests.
Review (The "Diff" View): Use the blue/red highlights to see exactly what changed.
Accept & Finalize
Scroll down in the Assist panel to find and hit Accept.
Sequential Edits: You must Accept your current change before submitting a new prompt.
Deliver: Once satisfied, select Send to EHR.
Save Your Favorites
Instead of re-typing the same instructions, you can build your own library of go-to prompts to speed up your workflow:
Manual Save: Type a prompt directly into the "Saved Prompts" section for future use.
One-Click Save: Simply click the blue flag next to any submitted prompt to add it to your favorites.
Important Guardrails (Keys to Success)
Transcript-Only: Assist can only refine what was discussed; it cannot "invent" details missing from the transcript.
Plain Text Only: Epic does not support bolding/italics so your final note will be plain text.
One-Way Sync: Finalize edits before hitting "Send to EHR." Further changes must be made in Epic.
Rejecting Edits: Not what you wanted? Hit Reject to return to your original note instantly.

Epic is one of the most widely used electronic health record (EHR) systems in the healthcare industry. Epic is also a clinic information system (CIS) that includes scheduling, revenue cycle, patient communications and data analytics functionality. Epic supports both in-Patient and Outpatient patient care. Epic clinical functionality is developed in modules for services like Cardiology, Orthopedics and Radiology. The Epic module that supports Dentistry is called Wisdom. Epic provides the foundation of comprehensive patient record system for UT Health San Antonio. In 2024, The School of Dentistry began efforts to transition from axiUm (est. 2008), a Dental Health Record System, to Epic.

links.text: Casey Cloud: Patient Education Resource (Print, Videos, and Animations for Dental Patient Education)

title: Epic Wisdom
text: The School of Dentistry has a significant strategic plan initiative in progress for transitioning our electronic patient record system and clinical information system from axiUm to a comprehensive health care information system, Epic. This transition for the School of Dentistry will become an integral part of the UT Health San Antonio comprehensive health care system. All UT Health clinical enterprises will use one electronic patient record system (EHR). As a reminder, the Dental School’s EHR migration is part of a larger BetterCare digital transformation that includes the upgrade of the Epic Ambulatory (Outpatient System) for medical the practice plan, the new Kyle Sealy facility that includes an Ambulatory Surgical Center (ASC) and the UT Health Multispecialty and Research Hospital (MSRH) (Epic Inpatient Component). For the School of Dentistry, the primary utilization will be Epic Ambulatory and the Dental Module, called Wisdom.

title: Epic Wisdom
text: The Wisdom module of Epic enhances dental care within integrated health systems. As a component of the Epic integrated clinical information system, Wisdom seamlessly integrates with other care management and documentation tools across the continuum of care. This Wisdom module includes a tooth chart for documenting specific findings and displaying related oral health management, hard and soft tissue findings with graphical representation for documentation, the periodontal chart for recording and tracking patient’s periodontal conditions. Dental team members can document treatment plans for oral issues and manage preventive care, interface the plan to patient scheduling and then record and track the execution of the plan down to the procedure level. Wisdom leverages the tools in all Epic instances with such features that are part of the Epic system such as the interface to registration, scheduling, professional billing and revenue cycle, and analytics.
