text:
The Epic Snapboard (see screen image*) is the equivalent of axiUm Appointment Books. Note the columns will be shown by either the Provider names (such as individual students or residents) or resource name such as Operatory room number or equivalent designation. Some clinics may have both. Similar to the axiom appointment books patients can be scheduled in these blocks. Most Snapboards have 15 minute blocks. You can also drag and drop appointments using the snap board tools.
The Snapboard is part of the Epic scheduling module known as Cadence.

title: Epic Wisdom
headingPath: Rooming – Reason for visit, Patient History Review, and Vitals
text:
Rooming (see screen image*) is the equivalent of the axiUm initial activities when a patient's starts their appointment with the medical and dental history review, vital signs, review of medications and allergies. The expectation is this information is reviewed prior to starting the diagnostic or intervention care.
Note as we are now in the patient record for an individual patient, specific patient information appears on the left-hand pane that includes their record number age date of birth, and other key medical information.

title: Epic Wisdom
text:
The Tooth Chart tab is selected, and the “Hard Tissue” button is on. Epic has an axiUm equivalent Odontogram (hard tissue, see screen image*) with representation of the teeth and surfaces. With icons circled above, just like axiUm, a primary or permanent dentition is selected. Categories for notating on the odontogram include findings (red icons), completed and existing treatments (blue) and planned items (green). Once planned procedure are completed, the color will switch from green to purple.
Periodontal Charting
The Tooth Chart tab is selected, and the “Periodontal” button is selected. Epic Periodontal Charting (see screen image*) is very similar to axiUm with pocket depth, bleeding, suppuration and gingival margin, and calculates the Clinical Attachment level (CAL). You can also document furcations and mobility. One can also see changes in these values as future periodontal exams are added.

title: Work Just Got Simpler: Referral Authorizations Made Easy
text:
Our Epic team has been working continuously behind the scenes to revamp our patient health record platform and implement new systems to streamline workloads— letting Epic do the work . For instance, our benefit and referral coordinators can expect t…
Our Epic team has been working continuously behind the scenes to revamp our patient health record platform and implement new systems to streamline workloads—letting Epic do the work. For instance, our benefit and referral coordinators can expect to see fewer authorizations in their work queue due to the retooling of “referral authorizations.”
Our Epic team members have done a rebuild within Epic to the Auto Status Assignment (ASA) table; this new ASA table allows our system to authorize basic consultation referrals automatically. Coordinators will no longer see these basic referral requests in their work queue. Specialty referrals like radiology, genetics, and infertility will still require prior authorization and will continue to appear in their Authorization work queues. The automation of authorizations is user-friendly and positively impacts our coordinator’s workload, allowing our team coordinators to invest their time in other areas and let the Epic system do the work.
BetterCare is an IT program committed to elevating our patient’s health care experience through improved access to their health information, streamlined appointments and visits, better coordination of care, and reduced medical errors. Visit https://uthealthsa.sharepoint.com/sites/BetterCare to learn more about our BetterCare initiative.

title: What is Epic Haiku?
text:
What is Epic Haiku?

Epic Haiku is a mobile application designed for healthcare providers, allowing them to access the Epic electronic health record (EHR) system from their smartphones or tablets. It enables convenient access to patient information, messaging, and schedule management on the go.

title: How do I download and install Epic Haiku?
text:
How do I download and install Epic Haiku?

Epic Haiku can be downloaded from the Apple App Store or Google Play Store. After installation, you'll need to configure the app with your organization's server settings, which can be obtained from your IT department.

title: What can I do with Epic Haiku?
text:
What can I do with Epic Haiku?

With Epic Haiku, you can:

- View patient charts, including lab results, medications, and medical history.

- Manage your schedule and review upcoming appointments.

- Communicate securely with other providers or care team members.

- Capture clinical photos and securely upload them to the patient’s record.

title: Is Epic Haiku secure?
text:
Is Epic Haiku secure?

Yes, Epic Haiku uses secure, encrypted connections to ensure that patient data is protected. It complies with HIPAA regulations to safeguard patient privacy.

title: Can I use Epic Haiku to prescribe medications?
text:
Can I use Epic Haiku to prescribe medications?

Epic Haiku allows you to view patient medications and make medication-related notes, but prescribing capabilities may vary depending on your organization's configuration. Check with your IT department for specific features available in your setup.

title: What devices are compatible with Epic Haiku?
text:
What devices are compatible with Epic Haiku?

Epic Haiku is compatible with iOS and Android devices. Ensure that your device is running a supported version of the operating system as specified in the app's requirements on the App Store or Google Play.

title: How do I troubleshoot issues with Epic Haiku?
text:
How do I troubleshoot issues with Epic Haiku?

If you encounter issues, first ensure that your app and device are updated to the latest versions. If problems persist, contact your IT support team for assistance with configuration or connectivity issues.

title: How do I log in to Epic Haiku?
text:
How do I log in to Epic Haiku?

You can log in to Epic Haiku using your standard Epic credentials. Ensure that your device is connected to the internet and that you have the necessary server information configured in the app.

title: Who should I contact for help with Epic Haiku?
text:
Who should I contact for help with Epic Haiku?

For any issues or questions related to Epic Haiku, contact your organization's IT support team. They can assist with installation, configuration, and troubleshooting.

title: Can I access Epic Haiku outside of my healthcare facility?
text:
Can I access Epic Haiku outside of my healthcare facility?

Yes, as long as you have an internet connection and the necessary security configurations in place, you can access Epic Haiku from anywhere.

title: Why did we change from aXium and what is Epic?
text:
Why did we change from aXium and what is Epic?

The change from aXium to Epic Wisdom was made to provide UT
Dentistry with a more secure, integrated and efficient electronic health record
system. Epic Wisdom offers a powerful and comprehensive platform that provides a
full health history for patients with existing medical records in Epic through
other care providers.

Epic is a leading provider of electronic health record
solutions used by healthcare organizations to manage patient information,
streamline workflows and improve outcomes. More information on Epic can be
found on their website.

title: Why is Thrive training important?
text:
Why is Thrive training important?

According to the KLAS Arch Collaborative, clinicians who spend 3-5 hours a year on ongoing training are 2-3 times more satisfied with their EHR.1.
Thrive training helps clinicians establish good efficiency habits and tailor their workspaces to support their personal workflows. Users can apply the knowledge from Thrive training to their own work or use it to help educate others. Thrive training is hands-on and moves at a pace that encourages questions and participation, allowing clinicians to walk away from class ready to use what they learned the next time they log in to the system for patient care.

title: Who is the intended audience for Thrive training?
text:
Who is the intended audience for Thrive training?

Thrive classes are designed for clinicians who are using Epic in their day to day job. Thrive training is particularly impactful for clinicians who understand their core workflows but would like to increase their efficiency in the system. These users can be identified through self-selection or through efficiency data provided by tools like Signal, ASAP PEP, and NEAT.
Epic-led Thrive training is open to existing End-User Training Services (EUTS) organizations, as well as organizations who haven't yet used EUTS. If you are not already participating in EUTS, talk to your Epic representative to get started.

title: AI Text Assistant
text:
AI Text Assistant

Is currently being piloted by specific departments (will be available to all in the next upgrade, August 2026).
To more quickly write notes, patient instructions, letters, and In Basket messages, clinicians can use AI-powered text action tools to:
- Summarize a piece of text that the clinician wrote to make it shorter or update the formatting, such as turning a paragraph into a list.
- Update the text to make sense to a specific audience, such as translating clinical jargon into wording that a patient can more easily understand.

title: Abridge Dictation
text:
Abridge Dictation

Is currently being piloted by specific departments. Verbatim Mode allows clinicians to more easily create their ideal clinical note through any combination of summarized and verbatim, word-for-word content—captured before or after note generation.

title: Dashboard Insights
text:
Dashboard Insights

Sometimes it would be nice to have an assistant to help walk you through what all that data on your dashboard means. Generative AI tools summarize reporting content, suggest possible conclusions, and identify key insights.

title: Draft Hospital Course in Discharge Summary
text:
Draft Hospital Course in Discharge Summary

Reduce physicians' documentation load by using generative AI to draft a hospital course note using data already available in the patient's chart.

title: Inpatient Insights
text:
Inpatient Insights

Rounding clinicians see a complex mix of patients, ranging from those they've been checking in with every day to those they've never met before. To help them quickly prepare for each of those patients, they can use generative AI to create three types of insights to fit the type of information and level of detail that would be most helpful: 

- Patient Story insights are designed to familiarize clinicians with a patient they have not previously encountered. These summaries include history from notes and chart data, recent events, and other details related to the current admission, helping them prioritize and plan their care efficiently. Patient Story summaries are organized into three sections: history, events during admission, and recent events. The recent events section includes similar information to the freestanding Recent Events summary described below.

- Notes summaries focus on summarizing relevant details from recent notes on the patient, helping clinicians quickly get up to speed on recent observations and developments or see highlights from the rest of the treatment team. 

- Recent Events summaries provide an overview of recently documented information on the patient, including intake/output, medications, results, orders, the problem list, notes, vitals, nursing assessments, and code events, ensuring that clinicians are aware of significant recent changes in a patient's condition since the last time they rounded.

title: PB Coding Assistant
text:
PB Coding Assistant

Save coders time so they can process more sessions and focus on those that require more expertise, helping maximize reimbursements. The Coding Assistant shows coders a list of potential diagnosis and procedure codes they might want to add based on notes that are relevant to a particular charge session, helping them review charge sessions efficiently and avoid jumping between many activities in search of relevant information.

Qualifying notes are automatically processed behind the scenes before a coder reviews the session, and they can jump to the source of supporting documentation when they need additional context. Cited text is highlighted in the note so they can decide whether the suggestion makes sense, all without needing to access Chart Review. When they decide to use a potential code, they can quickly add, swap, or remove codes from the charge session directly.

title: InBasket Categorization
text:
InBasket Categorization

Is currently being piloted by specific departments. In Basket automatically categorizes patient-initiated messages into subjects like Clinical Advice, Paperwork, or Scheduling, using a predictive model to help care teams triage and prioritize incoming requests. This allows staff to filter messages based on their roles, reducing response times and improving efficiency in handling patient communications.

title: InBasket Urgency
text:
InBasket Urgency

Is currently being piloted by specific departments. The Potentially Urgent predictive model automatically assigns urgency levels to patient messages, helping clinicians prioritize responses to potentially urgent communications while managing increasing message volumes. Currently, it categorizes messages as urgent, routine, or low (for FYI messages), with the option for users to manually select high urgency when needed.

title: Outpatient Insights
text: Outpatient Insights leverages generative AI to create patient visit summaries 36 hours prior to appointments, allowing clinicians to save time on preparation and stay informed about past visits, including external notes from Care Everywhere. The system automatically updates summaries if there are changes to the patient's record and generates new ones for walk-in appointments. Clinicians can personalize their summaries by selecting specific notes or topics of focus and have access to citations for each point, enabling them to quickly reference relevant context.

title: ART: Augmented Response Technology
text:
ART: Augmented Response Technology

Is currently being piloted by specific departments. Draft by Art streamlines communication for clinicians and staff by leveraging generative AI to create draft responses to patient messages. The system analyzes incoming messages from patients along with pertinent patient information to anticipate how a clinician or staff member might reply. It then generates a draft response that can be easily modified before being sent to the patient.

title: Ambient Orders
text:
Ambient Orders

Ambient AI tools utilize passive listening technology to capture clinical encounters through discreet devices, employing natural language processing and machine learning to structure, code, and stage draft orders directly in the clinician's EHR system. This automation enhances efficiency, boosts patient engagement, reduces clinician burnout, and improves accuracy by minimizing manual data entry errors.

title: Abridge tab in Hypersapce
text:
Abridge tab in Hypersapce

Clinicians can access Abridge features directly within the Epic Hyperspace interface, enabling them to summarize clinical documentation in brief sentences or short paragraphs. This integration aims to alleviate the documentation burden and reduce clinician burnout, allowing healthcare providers to concentrate more on patient care.

title: Improve Cancer Staging Compliance
text:
Improve Cancer Staging Compliance

The current rate of discrete cancer staging documentation is ~7% of all eligible cancer problems are staged when a Beacon plan is applied. The vast majority of cancer staging is being documented as free text in notes.
cancer staging compliance by expanding security and adjusting workflows for tumor registrars and/or oncology support staff to take over as data entry for discrete staging data that is then routed to the provider to review and sign. Monitor and track compliance through the use of close encounter decision support to match your workflows.
In the Foundation system we've built out a rule-based cancer staging BPA that warns clinicians upon interacting with the patient's chart or orders that they have a cancer diagnosis that does not have staging complete.

title: Cancer Staging Optimization
text:
Cancer Staging Optimization

With the launch of Epic's Beaker Anatomic Pathology staging module, lab results from Beaker can now be seamlessly imported into staging forms. This will save oncologists time and ensure consistent cancer staging information across the system.

Additionally, soft stop reminders for encounter closure will enhance compliance with discrete staging, addressing the current challenge of free-text documentation in notes.

title: Specialty Content Review – Neurology (RW4) (new)
text:
Specialty Content Review – Neurology (RW4) (new)

We are excited to announce several enhancements in Epic designed specifically for the Neurology Clinic. These improvements aim to streamline workflows and enhance patient care. Here’s what you can expect:
Refreshed Neurology-Specific Snapshot and Sidebar Reports: A more intuitive and organized view tailored to neurology needs, providing easier access to critical information.
New Pediatric Epilepsy Learning Health System (PELHS) SmartForm: A specialized SmartForm to support the management of pediatric epilepsy patients, enabling efficient documentation and tracking.
Seizure Action Plan: A dedicated feature to help clinicians quickly document and manage seizure action plans for patients.

Procedure Documentation: Improved tools for documenting neurology-specific procedures with precision and ease.
Neuro Exam SmartForm: A new form designed to simplify the documentation of neurological exams, ensuring comprehensive and standardized entry of clinical data.
Refreshed Navigator Layout: The navigator has been restructured to be more user-friendly and better aligned with clinical workflows in neurology.

title: Cash Management
text: Cash Management allows cash reconciliation with the customer's bank to happen within Epic rather than being external. With this functionality, individual checks within an 835 file are checked against a list of 'Cash Records' that correspond to specific deposits made by payers into the customer's account. This way, we can ensure that payments are only posted in Epic after the money hits the account.

We are excited to inform you about upcoming updates to Epic that will improve the efficiency and clarity of workflows related to hypertension and heart failure management. Here is a summary of the new features and enhancements:

title: Hello World Billing Notifications
text:
Hello World Billing Notifications

For Hello World Billing's SMS notifications, it’s important to clarify the key information typically communicated to end users. Here’s a general overview:
Account Balance Information: SMS notifications can inform users about current balances, overdue amounts, or successful payments.
Due Date Reminders: Friendly reminders a few days before payment due dates to help users avoid late fees.
Payment Confirmation: Users receive confirmations for successful payments, providing assurance and record of the transaction.
Dispute Notifications: For any billing disputes or adjustments, an SMS may inform users of resolution statuses.
Support and Contact Information: SMS notifications often include details on how users can contact support for billing questions.
Opt-in/Opt-out Options: Users should have the ability to manage their SMS notifications preferences for billing information.

title: Trusted Exchange Framework (TEFCA)
text:
Trusted Exchange Framework (TEFCA)

The Trusted Exchange Framework and Common Agreement™, also known as TEFCA™, outlines a common set of principles, terms, and conditions to support the development of a Common Agreement that helps enable the nationwide exchange of electronic health information (EHI) across disparate health information networks (HINs). The TEFCA is designed to scale EHI exchange nationwide and help ensure that HINs, health care providers, health plans, individuals, and many more stakeholders have secure access to their electronic health information when and where it is needed.

title: Extract Sciences - Aura Integration
text:
Extract Sciences - Aura Integration

Aura brings the promise of precision medicine within reach for the entire Epic community. With Aura, you can collaborate with specialty diagnostic labs in a fraction of the time necessary to configure traditional interfaces. Connect to a single compendium of tests from each participating lab, then download purpose-built configuration packages to update your local Epic build. After that, providers can use their existing Epic workflows to send orders to and receive discrete results from any lab on the network.
Today, oncology end users noted that Natera, Caris, and Gaurdant were the most common specialty diagnostic labs being used. The core workflows for these tests are managed outside of Epic with results scanned and separate processes to share with patients via MyChart.

title: RefuelProjList
text:
Feature/Project | Application | Affected Applications | Category | Description

text:

Getting Started
Welcome to Haiku, Epic's mobile app for Android smartphones.
Download Haiku
On your device, tap to open the Google Play store and search the Apps section for "Epic Haiku". In the
search results, tap and install the Haiku for Android app.
Log in
On your device, tap the app's icon and enter your user ID and password in the login fields. Tap the label at the
top of the login screen to connect to a different organization or instance.
Tap and hold an item on the screen to see a tooltip with more information on patients,
appointments, In Basket messages, and more.
What is an activity?
Each activity supports a specific task, such as reviewing the chart or e-prescribing medications. You can access
startup activities when you open Haiku, and you can access chart activities from the springboard, which
appears when you first open a chart or when you tap Back from any chart activity.
Log out
When you leave Haiku to go to your device home screen or switch to another app, Haiku continues to run in
the background. For security reasons, Haiku automatically logs you out after a period of inactivity. However,
you can also log out yourself if you know you won't need to use the app for a while.
To do so, tap (the More menu button), and tap Logout. Note that you can't see the More menu from
within a patient's chart.

Find Your Patients
Find admitted patients
Tap to open your patient lists You can set a default list in Hyperspace by right-clicking the list and clicking
Default List. To open a different patient list, you can tap Change List.
The following icons indicate that a patient has new information to review.
 indicates new abnormal results.
 indicates new critical results.
 indicates an isolation or infection.
 indicates new notes.
You can tap to sort the current list.
Note that you can only remove these icons in Hyperspace by clicking Time Mark in the
Notes activity or the Results Review activity.
Find clinical appointments and surgical cases
Tap to open your schedule. Select a date on the calendar view to see your schedule for that day.
To see schedules for other groups, departments, or colleagues, tap .
The schedule shows each patient's age and sex, as well the appointment type. Appointments are color-coded
and marked (with a dot) using the same colors as in Hyperspace. The rings that appear around the
appointment time indicate the appointment's time and length. For example, a 15-minute appointment in the
future appears like this:
Surgical cases appear like this:
To filter the schedule to only appointments with a certain status, tap and select the statuses you want to
see.
Edit Schedule and Patient List columns
The Schedule and Patient List in Haiku and Canto can be edited to show additional information using the same
text-based columns in Schedule and Patient List views in Hyperspace. Only one additional column can be
added at a time in the mobile apps.

1. Tap the three-dot menu in the top right corner of the Patient List or Schedule.
2. Tap Settings.
 If needed, turn Show additional column to on.
3. Search or scroll available columns and select your desired column.
Find patients in the emergency department
When you log in to Haiku in the ED, the Track Board appears, and you're in the My Pts (My Patients) list.
My Pts shows patients assigned to you with acuity level (by color), location, chief complaint, lab and imaging
status, and wait time. To see more details, such as which labs were done, tap and hold a patient's name.
To see patients who are waiting and assign yourself to a patient:
1. At the top of the list, tap My Pts.
2. From the menu, select Next to See.
3. Swipe left on a patient's name and tap Assign Me.
Find other patients
To find a patient who isn't on your patient list or schedule, tap Search for a patient, and enter a patient's
name or MRN. Fields for sex or date of birth appear when you start typing. The results appear with more
patient details, such as address. Tap to sort the list of patients that were found.
If you select a patient from a search, any documentation you do in Haiku is linked to the most recent available
encounter. If Haiku can't find a recent encounter for the patient, a new encounter is created to store your
documentation when you start entering orders or writing a note.

text:
6
Manage In Basket Messages
In the In Basket activity, you can read and respond to many types of messages, including:
 Staff Message
 Results
 Coding and CDI Queries
 Cosign - Clinic Orders
 Rx Request
 Pt Advice Request
 Patient Call
 Procedure Prep
You can also create new Staff Messages.
The In Basket folder appears with the number of unread messages. The number appears in red if any of the
unread messages are high priority. If you don't have any unread messages, no number appears. If you don't
have any messages in that folder, the folder appears in gray.
Prioritize messages
The following icons appear next to messages in a folder to help you prioritize them:
High priority
Low priority
Unread message
Pended message
A message is pended if you’ve opened it and taken an action but haven’t marked the message done
yet.
Overdue message
In Hyperspace, when sending a message, the sender can include an action, such as "Call patient".
The action can also be flagged with a due date and time. If that due date and time has passed, the
message appears as overdue in Hyperspace and the app.
You are responsible for the message.
Messages with responsibility help recipients track whether someone has started working on a task.
Only the person who has responsibility for a message can mark it as done.
Swipe left on an In Basket message and tap Defer to remove the message from your mobile In Basket.
Messages you defer appear in your Hyperspace In Basket, but are hidden from your mobile In Basket.

Work with Staff Messages
1. To create a new Staff Message, from the In Basket activity, tap .
2. Select Compose Staff Message.
3. Write your message and, optionally, tap to add the following flags to your message before sending
it:
 Call Me flags the recipient to call you.
 Set Priority flags the message as high, routine, or low priority.
4. Tap to send the message.
When you receive a Staff Message, tap to reply or tap to forward the message.
Review results
Tap a result to open it.
The following icons can appear next to Results messages:
The patient has abnormal results.
The patient has critical results.
The green circle indicates that all the patient's orders have been resulted. A number
indicates the total number of resulted orders that you haven't yet reviewed.
Not all orders for this patient have been resulted. A number indicates the total number of
orders that have been resulted that you haven't yet reviewed.
Send a reminder to follow up on a result
If you see a result in a Results message that you want to investigate further, you can send yourself a reminder
to do so. The reminder is sent as a Patient Reminder message with the original Results message attached to it.
Note that you can only access the reminder message in your Hyperspace In Basket.
1. In a Results message, tap .
2. Enter any additional text you want to add and tap to send the reminder to yourself.
Create a result note
1. In a Results message, tap .

Respond to patient advice requests
1. In a Pt Advice Request message, tap View to see any attachments.
 If you need to review the full chart, tap the patient's name.
2. Act on the request:
 Tap to reply to the patient by email.
 Tap to forward the message to another provider.
 Tap to indicate that you have responded by calling the patient. The message is removed
from your In Basket.
 Tap to see other options, like No Action.
Manage E-Visit messages
1. Tap the E-Visits folder in your In Basket and select the message you want to review.
2. Review the information in the patient's E-Visit message, including self-triage or questionnaire
responses.
3. If you don't want to take responsibility for the E-Visit message, tap Put Back to return the message to

4. To reply to the message or route it to another provider, tap .
5. To go to the patient's chart, tap either the patient's name or picture in the message header. From the
chart, you can complete many of the same tasks you would in a normal office visit, including reviewing
the patient's allergies and medications, documenting a visit diagnosis, writing progress notes, and
placing orders.
Review patient escalations
When an escalation is sent for a patient who uses MyChart Care Companion (for example, because they report
concerning symptoms on a daily check-in questionnaire), you'll receive a push notification. You can view
details of the escalation and follow up from the new Patient Escalation folder in In Basket.

Review a snapshot of medical information

Long-term medication
Patient-reported medication
If the patient is on any opioids, to see Morphine Equivalent Daily Dosing (MEDD) information, tap the link

Mark information as reviewed

Review past encounters

Review documents from outside organizations
Information about external encounters and results appears throughout Haiku. The icon indicates

To see complete documents for encounters and results performed at other organizations, from a patient's

 Tap Summaries to review a patient's clinical summaries.
 Tap Documents to review a patient's clinical documents.

Update a patient's photo

Capture clinical images

text:
12
Review Results
Review results
From the springboard, tap Results to see a list of recent results for the patient. Tap a result to see details.
 For lab tests, a table of lab results appears. Swipe left to see past values for the same lab. Tap Report
to see the report view.
 For imaging or ECG results, a narrative report appears.
Tap and hold on a result to see the reference range for that component.
Review a patient's new or abnormal results
An icon appears in the patient list for patients with any new results. These same icons appear in the Results
activity.
Abnormal result
Critical result
View a graph of results
Review discrete lab results in a graph. While reviewing a table in the Results activity, turn your device
horizontally.
Each result component appears on the graph in a unique color. To help you match the line color to a particular
result component, a key appears at the top of the graph.
Focus on one type of result
Tap the colored circle on the left side of the screen that corresponds to that component's color. The line that
represents that component appears brighter than the other lines. Slide your finger up and down in order to
choose the component you want to bring to the front of the graph.
Focus on one result value
Each white data point on the graph represents a specific result value for a component. Tap and hold near a
data point to view more information about that value, including the actual result value, the reference range,
the result date, and the result time.

text:
13
View and Create Notes and Letters
From the springboard, tap Notes to view and create notes and letters. If your organization is licensed for
Nuance or 3M M*Modal speech recognition software, you can dictate your notes and letters with speech-to-
text. The Notes activity shows you all of a patient's encounter notes in one location.
From the list, tap a note you want to review. Tap Back to return to the list.
Use filters to narrow down the list of notes
To filter the notes you see in the activity, tap and choose a filter category. For example, you might filter by
note type and show only progress notes. Tap to apply the filters you've selected. You can clear your filters
by tapping and then Clear All.
Create a new note or letter
Notes and letters you create are automatically associated with an encounter in the patient's chart so you can
find them later.
1. Tap to create a new note or letter. The encounter associated with the note appears in a gray
banner beneath the patient header.
a. To change the note type, tap .
b. Tap Note Info.
c. Choose a note type from the Type menu.
d. Tap OK to accept the changes.
2. Enter text or tap the microphone button to use Nuance or Fluency speech-to-text.
3. Tap Sign at Close Encounter, or tap to Sign, Pend, or Discard your note.
 You can edit pended notes later from the Notes activity. Signed notes are filed to the chart.
 Note that you can't use Haiku to edit pended notes that were created in Hyperspace.

text:
14
View Information in a Push Notification
Open an activity from a push notification
When you're already logged in to Haiku, you can open an activity directly from a push notification.
Simply tap the notification to open the related activity. For example, a critical result notification opens the
related message in the In Basket activity.
Review recent notifications
Tap to open the Notifications activity.
Choose which push notifications appear
1. In the Notifications activity, tap and select Notification Settings.
2. To turn off a certain type of notification, select the notification type, then slide the button next to that
notification type to the left.
 For example, to turn off push notifications for staff messages, slide the button next to "Staff
messages" to the left. When you turn off a notification type, the notification still appears in the
Notifications activity, but no alert or banner appears when you receive the notification.
3. To turn off all push notifications, slide the button next to "Push notifications" to the left.
Allow critical notifications
To let certain very important alerts related to patient safety to break through your phone's settings and arrive
with a loud volume, when prompted, allow urgent notifications to bypass Do Not Disturb settings.
To manually allow critical notifications, if you denied them at the prompts, from your device home screen,
open the Settings app and navigate to your Notifications settings. Tap Haiku. Enable Set as priority. Only
device alerts, such as patient heart rate, are sent as priority alerts by the app.

E-Prescribe Medications
Note that you can only order medications, not procedures. Tap Orders from the springboard to open E-
Prescribing.
You can write most outpatient and inpatient orders from Haiku, but note these limitations:
 For non-medication orders and inpatient orders, you can only edit indications of
use and answer questions.
 You can't manage your preference list.
If you can't sign an order because details are missing, tap Pend or Save Work and finish
entering the order from a workstation.
Review medication information
The Active Meds tab shows a list of the patient's current outpatient prescriptions.
 Tap the allergies information bar to review the patient's allergies.
 Inpatient medications appear only in the patient summary.
Search for a medication
Tap to see your Haiku preference list and open search to find medications that aren't in your preference
list. Medications included in Haiku and other preference lists are elevated in the search results.
The following icons appear in the search results:
Medications that the system has added to your preference list
Medications you have added to your Haiku preference list
When a patient is admitted, disappears, and you cannot prescribe medications for the patient.
Use Hyperspace to manage your preference list.
Write a prescription
1. In the E-Prescribing activity, review any current prescriptions or facility-administered medications and
tap the allergies information bar to review allergy information.
2. Tap to search for a medication. Matching medications on your preference list appear at the top of
the search results.
3. Select a medication and tap each field to enter specific order information. When you are finished filling
out the medication details, tap Accept.

E-prescribe controlled medications
E-prescribing controlled substances from mobile devices is not available at all organizations.

Contact previous care team members

Message Colleagues with Secure Chat
Read and reply to new messages
When you receive a new Secure Chat message, you get a notification on your device. Tap the notification to
open the conversation and type your reply in the field at the bottom of the screen.
Review all conversations and start new ones
1. Tap to open the Secure Chat activity and see a list of all your conversations.
 The icons next to each message indicate who is participating in the conversation.

title: Abridge Inside Support Guide
text:
Common Support Issues
Epic’s IT Support team should be able to resolve most common support issues without
needing assistance from the Abridge team. Below is a list of commonly asked questions
and suggested responses.
1. Hardware, WiFi, and Connectivity
Which devices do I need to use Abridge?
● All you need is a phone and computer to get started. For best results, ensure that
your phone’s microphone is not obstructed (e.g., by being in a pocket or a bag).
● Recording should not be a significant drain on your baery, but if you’re worried
about baery life, feel free to turn o your screen display while recording or use a
wireless charger.
● Abridge will work on Haiku version 10.9+ and Canto version 10.9+
What versions/devices are required?
The ambient module has the following requirements:
● Hyperspace: May ‘23+ (May ‘23 - Feb ‘24 will require SUs)
● Hyperdrive is required
● Haiku: 10.9+ and/or Canto: 10.9+
● iOS versions: Epic mobile apps are released monthly and tested against the current iOS
+ one prior version. So 10.9+ versions that are released in May of 2024 are available for
iOS 17 + iOS 16 compatible devices.
What do I do if I’m having problems with my Wi-Fi connectivity?
● First, verify whether other network applications, such as a web browser, work on
the same device.
● If your phone cannot connect to a wireless or mobile network, you cannot record
conversations with Abridge.
4

title: Abridge Inside Support Guide
text:
● If you are having intermient connectivity issues but can navigate to Abridge
within Haiku/Canto, you can continue recording without any data loss. However,
your recording will not be processed until your internet connection returns.
● If you continue to have network connectivity issues, you should contact your IT
department to troubleshoot your phone’s Wi-Fi connection.
How does oine mode work?
If your phone cannot connect to a wireless or mobile network, you cannot record
conversations with Abridge.
Abridge can only be opened inside of Haiku while a user is online. We require an internet
connection to check permissions before beginning each new patient recording.
Once users have opened the Abridge-branded recording buon inside of Haiku, the entire
conversation can be conducted while oine. The conversation can be ended while oine.
Audio uploading and processing will not work while a user is oine. Once a user is online
again, Abridge can process audio and begin generating a note.
2. Geing Started
How to check if Abridge Inside is enabled?
IT answer: Check that the security points and profile build have been configured.
User answer: You will know you have an Abridge account if you can see the ambient menu
option within Haiku.
1. Go to Haiku
2. Open a patient from the schedule
3. Look for the “Ambient” tab: this tab is displayed if– and only if– Abridge Inside is set up
correctly
5

title: Abridge Inside Support Guide
text:
Who can use Abridge Inside for recording?
Anyone with view access to a patient on a schedule can use Abridge Inside, if given the
appropriate security points and profiles. This means that fellows, residents, or other sta
who support clinic schedules of clinicians can use Abridge!
Abridge Inside is ambulatory only. Inpatient and ED patient lists will not be shown.
Abridge Inside recording only functions on iOS devices. See the device/version section
above for more details.
3. Uploading
My recording isn’t uploading from the mobile app.
When upload issues arise, Abridge will automatically make several aempts to retry a
conversation upload. If your conversation doesn’t properly upload (and the ‘Note
Status’ is “uploading”), please take the following steps:
1. Keep the app open in the foreground until the entire recording has uploaded.
2. Try closing other apps that might compete for uploading connectivity bandwidth
3. Make sure that you’re connected to a Wi-Fi network. If the app is already open, it
will automatically aempt to upload the conversation once a network is detected.
4. Close and re-open Haiku.
5. Check other Internet-connected apps on the same phone to see if they are
working.
If other apps work, but your conversation does not upload, or if you continue to
encounter problems, please contact the Abridge team.
4. Recording
My recording is incomplete.
Please forward any truncated recording issues to the Abridge team so they can
investigate the issue further.
6

title: Abridge Inside Support Guide
text:
It is possible that the app was closed during an upload aempt., Picking up incoming
calls may also interrupt the Abridge recording. See below for more details on
interruptions.
Can I use Abridge for telehealth appointments?
Abridge supports telehealth appointments. Do not wear headphones; your phone needs
to pick up the audio from your computer's speakers for Abridge to capture the visit.
5. Interruptions
My phone baery died while recording a visit. What should I do?
Any recording up to the point of your phone baery dying will be saved locally on your phone.
When your phone is powered up again and connected to the Internet, the file will be uploaded
to the cloud as usual.
Someone called me while using Abridge. What should I do?
If you answer a phone call while recording, Abridge will automatically pause the
recording. After you end the call, tap on the Haiku app to bring it back into the
foreground, where you will need to tap the play buon to resume the recording.
● Phone call: recording will pause if the phone call is answered.
● Phone dies: Any recording up to the point of your phone baery dying will be saved
locally on your phone. When your phone is powered up again and connected to the
Internet, the file will be uploaded to the cloud as usual.
● Telehealth call started on the same phone as Abridge: The case of using the phone for
telehealth and Abridge at the same time is not supported. In this case, the Abridge
recording will pause. Your telehealth app will start using the microphone.
● Phone Alarm: This uses the speaker

title: Abridge Inside Support Guide
text:
telehealth and Abridge at the same time is not supported. In this case, the Abridge
recording will pause. Your telehealth app will start using the microphone.
● Phone Alarm: This uses the speaker
● Voice memo: This uses the phone microphone.
7

title: Abridge Inside Support Guide
text:
6. Abridge-Generated Notes
My clinical note isn’t appearing in Epic. What should I do?
First, check the Note Status in Haiku or Hyperspace to understand if the note is still
“Recording” “Uploading” “Processing” “Ready” or “Reviewed”. Also, check your Internet
connection.
If…
● Recording = you are still actively recording. You’ll need to pause the recording and
generate the note before it can appear in Hyperspace.
● Uploading = if your audio has not been fully uploaded to Abridge, Abridge cannot begin
the note-generating process. See “Quick Uploading Best Practices”
● Processing = Two things could be true
8

title: Abridge Inside Support Guide
text:
○ You never hit the “Create Note” buon. Therefore, Abridge has not begun to
generate the note. Return to Haiku to press this buon.
○ If Haiku displays the “Recording Completed” screen on the Abridge tab, then
your note is currently being processed by Abridge’s machine learning. If this
takes more than a few minutes, reach out to Abridge Support.
● Ready = Your note was processed by Abridge.
○ Check the Abridge tab to see if the note content appears.
○ Check that the user has pulled in dotphrases / templates that leverage
Abridge’s dotphrases (no dotphrases = no note).
● Find the dotphrases below:
Abridge Note Section Epic SmartLink
History of Present Illness .HPISEC
Results .RESULTSEC
Physical Exam .PESEC
Assessment and Plan .APSEC
My note is totally empty. What should I do?
First, check if the note was processed successfully:
● Method 1: Look for “Ready” note status.
● Method 2: Check if the user can open the Abridge Activity Tab from the ambient
SmartSection headers; from here, the user may check information about the recording
duration and transcript.
If the Abridge note content is empty, it is likely that Abridge could not find enough medical
information in the recording to generate a note. This can occur if the audio file is very short,
the microphone was too obstructed to capture any dialogue, or if there was no medical
discussion.
9

7. Data and Privacy
Is Abridge HIPAA-compliant?
Yes, Abridge’s enterprise-grade technology is 100% HIPAA-compliant and uses
industry-best practices to protect patient information.
How does Abridge ensure data privacy and security?
Data is always stored via secure channels. Abridge stores and processes all data within
HIPAA-secure US-based data centers to meet security and availability requirements.

title: Look-Alikes Quick Start Guide
text: With the power of Cosmos, a clinician's network is now a lot bigger. You can search the Look-Alikes network right from your patient’s chart to find other clinicians across the community who have experience caring for patients similar to the one you're seeing. You can then reach out and collaborate with those colleagues to get the clinical insights you need to care for your patients.

title: Look-Alikes Quick Start Guide
headingPath: Search for Patients with Known Rare Conditions
text:
When you see a patient with a condition that’s a good fit for Look-Alikes, you’ll see in the problem list and in the Storyboard.
The conditions that make the Look-Alikes activity appear automatically are a group of diagnoses that have been deemed rare based on research and clinician feedback.
- Click to open the Look-Alikes activity. This will start a Look-Alikes search.
If the patient has more than one rare disease condition, the search will not start automatically.
- When the search is complete, you will see a list of clinicians who have seen similar patients.
- The results are sorted by how many patients like yours that they have seen, with local clinicians moved to the top of the list.
- Reach out to those clinicians using the contact information provided.
- Search results are also sent to your In Basket, so you can reference these results again later.
- Click Modify Criteria if there are other unique factors about the patient that should be included in the search.

title: Look-Alikes Quick Start Guide
headingPath: Searching for a Look-Alike for Patients with Unknown Rare Conditions
text:
You can also use Look-Alikes for patients whose condition is not known or is not on the list of conditions that will flag a patient for the Look-Alikes search. Enter relevant symptoms, diagnoses, demographics, or allergies to find patients similar to yours.
- Open Look-Alikes.
- To open Look-Alikes for patients when you do not see the icon, search for "look-alike".
- You can also find the Look-Alikes activity in the more activities dropdown menu.
- Use the Search Conditions field to add your patient's clinically relevant diagnoses.
These conditions come from the Problem List. If a relevant diagnosis is not available, first update the patient's problem list and then return to this activity.
- Use the Search Signs and Symptoms field to add your patient's relevant symptoms, related to their diagnosis or otherwise.
Only symptoms documented using NoteWriter forms will appear here.
- Use the Demographics section as needed to narrow the criteria further.
- Use the Allergies section to add the patient's allergies if needed.
- Click Reset Criteria to start over, if needed.
- Click Find Providers when you're ready to see results for clinicians with patients like yours.
- By default, this search only includes physicians.
- To expand the search to include advanced practice providers, click next to Find Providers and select Find Physicians and APPs.
This search may take a few minutes. All results will be sent to your In Basket; you can leave the activity after you start the search and come back to the results in your In Basket later.

title: Look-Alikes Quick Start Guide
text:
After you decide which clinician to reach out to about the patient, you can call their office or send an In Basket message.
- The phone numbers are listed in the clinician's contact information card, or you can click Send an In Basket message below their name.
- If you send an In Basket message, there is a prepopulated template you can use to start the conversation. Edit this message as needed, and then click Send.

title: Look-Alikes Quick Start Guide
text:
Being part of the Look-Alikes network is always your choice. As part of the network, you can reach out to your colleagues, and, if you’ve cared for rare patients, your colleagues can reach out to you. You can update your participation preferences at any time.
- Click in the upper right-hand corner of the Look-Alikes activity.
- Click Participate in the Look-Alikes Community in the About Me tab that opens to leave or join the Look-Alikes network.
You can also access these settings from anywhere in Epic using the About Me activity.
- Click your user icon in the top-right corner of the screen.
- Click About Me.
- In the Look-Alikes Communication section, select Participate in the Look-Alikes Community to opt in or out of the network at any time.

title: Look-Alikes Quick Start Guide
text:
- Click your user icon in the top-right corner of the screen.
- Click About Me.
- In the Look-Alikes Communication section, select Participate in the Look-Alikes Community to opt in or out of the network at any time.

title: UTHSCA specialties (1)
text:
/* Copyright (C) 2022 Epic Systems Corporation
********************************************************************************
TITLE: Haiku - Logins by User
PURPOSE: Review Haiku and Canto logins for a date range, including user information
AUTHOR: Zachary Hacklander
REVISION HISTORY:
ZAKH 11/29 819798 - Created
*******************************************************************************/
SELECT haiku.ID AS [User ID]
,haiku.Name AS [User]
,haiku.Email AS [Email]
,haiku.[Specialty Name]
,haiku.[Provider Type]
,haiku.[Device ID]
,haiku.[App Version]
,haiku.[Device OS]
,haiku.[Device OS Version]
,MAX(haiku.[Access Time]) AS [Most Recent Access]
FROM (
SELECT DISTINCT
CLARITY_EMP.USER_ID as 'ID'
,MAX(CLARITY_EMP.USER_NAME_EXT) as 'Name'
,MAX(CLARITY_EMP_DEMO.EMAIL) AS 'Email'
,MAX(CLARITY_DEP.DEPARTMENT_ID) as 'Department'
,MAX(D_PROV_PRIMARY_HIERARCHY.SPECIALTY_NAME) AS 'Specialty Name'
,MAX(D_PROV_PRIMARY_HIERARCHY.PROVIDER_TYPE) AS 'Provider Type'
,MAX(CLARITY_DEP.REV_LOC_ID) as 'Revenue Location'
,MAX(CLARITY_DEP.SERV_AREA_ID) as 'Service Area'
,MAX(CASE WHEN ACCESS_LOG.METRIC_ID = 94200 OR ACCESS_LOG.METRIC_ID = 94210 then 'Haiku'
WHEN ACCESS_LOG.METRIC_ID=94300 OR ACCESS_LOG.METRIC_ID = 94310 THEN 'Canto' END) as 'Application'
,MAX(CASE WHEN ACCESS_LOG.METRIC_ID = 94200 OR ACCESS_LOG.METRIC_ID = 94300 then 'Successful Login'
WHEN ACCESS_LOG.METRIC_ID=94210 OR ACCESS_LOG.METRIC_ID = 94310 THEN 'Failed Login' END) as 'Login Status'
,MAX(ACCESS_LOG.ACCESS_TIME) as 'Access Time'
,MAX(CASE WHEN acl2.DATA_MNEMONIC_ID = 'HKUDVCID' then acl2.STRING_VALUE ELSE '' END) as 'Device ID'
,MAX(CASE WHEN acl2.DATA_MNEMONIC_ID = 'HKUAPVER' then acl2.STRING_VALUE ELSE '' END) as 'App Version'
,MAX(CASE WHEN acl2.DATA_MNEMONIC_ID = 'HKUOSNAM' then acl2.STRING_VALUE ELSE '' END) as 'Device OS'
,MAX(CASE WHEN acl2.DATA_MNEMONIC_ID = 'HKUOSVER' then acl2.STRING_VALUE ELSE '' END) as 'Device OS Version'
,ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY CLARITY_EMP.USER_ID ORDER BY ACCESS_LOG.ACCESS_TIME DESC) AS RN
--,MAX(ACC_LOG_DTL_NI.STRING_VALUE) as 'Login Error'
FROM ACCESS_LOG
INNER JOIN CLARITY_EMP ON ACCESS_LOG.USER_ID=CLARITY_EMP.USER_ID
LEFT OUTER JOIN ACC_LOG_DTL_IX ON (ACCESS_LOG.PROCESS_ID=ACC_LOG_DTL_IX.PROCESS_ID) AND (ACCESS_LOG.ACCESS_INSTANT=ACC_LOG_DTL_IX.ACCESS_INSTANT) and ACC_LOG_DTL_IX.DATA_MNEMONIC_ID = 'DEP'
LEFT OUTER JOIN CLARITY_DEP on STRING_VALUE=CLARITY_DEP.DEPARTMENT_ID
LEFT OUTER JOIN ACC_LOG_DTL_IX acl2 ON (ACCESS_LOG.PROCESS_ID=acl2.PROCESS_ID) AND (ACCESS_LOG.ACCESS_INSTANT=acl2.ACCESS_INSTANT) and acl2.DATA_MNEMONIC_ID in
('HKUDVCID','HKUAPVER','HKUOSNAM','HKUOSVER')
LEFT OUTER JOIN ACC_LOG_DTL_NI ON (ACCESS_LOG.PROCESS_ID=ACC_LOG_DTL_NI.PROCESS_ID) AND (ACCESS_LOG.ACCESS_INSTANT=ACC_LOG_DTL_NI.ACCESS_INSTANT) and ACC_LOG_DTL_NI.DATA_MNEMONIC_ID = 'LOGINERROR'
LEFT JOIN CLARITY_EMP_DEMO ON CLARITY_EMP_DEMO.USER_ID = CLARITY_EMP.USER_ID

title: UTHSCA specialties (1)
text:
LEFT OUTER JOIN CLARITY_DEP on STRING_VALUE=CLARITY_DEP.DEPARTMENT_ID
LEFT OUTER JOIN ACC_LOG_DTL_IX acl2 ON (ACCESS_LOG.PROCESS_ID=acl2.PROCESS_ID) AND (ACCESS_LOG.ACCESS_INSTANT=acl2.ACCESS_INSTANT) and acl2.DATA_MNEMONIC_ID in
('HKUDVCID','HKUAPVER','HKUOSNAM','HKUOSVER')
LEFT OUTER JOIN ACC_LOG_DTL_NI ON (ACCESS_LOG.PROCESS_ID=ACC_LOG_DTL_NI.PROCESS_ID) AND (ACCESS_LOG.ACCESS_INSTANT=ACC_LOG_DTL_NI.ACCESS_INSTANT) and ACC_LOG_DTL_NI.DATA_MNEMONIC_ID = 'LOGINERROR'
LEFT JOIN CLARITY_EMP_DEMO ON CLARITY_EMP_DEMO.USER_ID = CLARITY_EMP.USER_ID
LEFT JOIN CLARITY_SER ON CLARITY_SER.PROV_ID = CLARITY_EMP.PROV_ID
LEFT JOIN D_PROV_PRIMARY_HIERARCHY ON D_PROV_PRIMARY_HIERARCHY.PROV_ID = CLARITY_SER.PROV_ID
WHERE ("ACCESS_LOG"."METRIC_ID"=94200 OR "ACCESS_LOG"."METRIC_ID"=94210 OR "ACCESS_LOG"."METRIC_ID"=94300 OR "ACCESS_LOG"."METRIC_ID"=94310)
AND ACCESS_LOG.ACCESS_TIME >= '20230801'
--AND ACCESS_LOG.ACCESS_TIME >= {{REPORT_START_DT}}
--AND ACCESS_LOG.ACCESS_TIME < {{REPORT_END_DT}}
--AND (NULLIF(COALESCE({{E_DEPARTMENT}},N''), N'') IS NULL OR (CLARITY_DEP.DEPARTMENT_ID in ({{E_DEPARTMENT}})))
--AND (NULLIF(COALESCE({{E_REVENUE_LOCATION}},N''), N'') IS NULL OR (CLARITY_DEP.REV_LOC_ID in ({{E_REVENUE_LOCATION}})))
--AND (NULLIF(COALESCE({{E_SERVICE_AREA}},N''), N'') IS NULL OR (CLARITY_DEP.SERV_AREA_ID in ({{E_SERVICE_AREA}})))
--AND (NULLIF(COALESCE({{E_USER}},N''), N'') IS NULL OR (CLARITY_EMP.USER_ID in ({{E_USER}})))
--AND (NULLIF(COALESCE({{E_LOGIN_STATUS}},N''), N'') IS NULL OR (ACCESS_LOG.METRIC_ID in ({{E_LOGIN_STATUS}})))
GROUP BY acl2.PROCESS_ID,acl2.ACCESS_INSTANT,CLARITY_EMP.USER_ID,ACCESS_LOG.ACCESS_TIME
#ERROR!
) haiku
WHERE haiku.RN = 1
GROUP BY haiku.ID
,haiku.Name
,haiku.Email
,haiku.[Specialty Name]
,haiku.[Provider Type]
,haiku.[Device ID]
,haiku.[App Version]
,haiku.[Device OS]
,haiku.[Device OS Version]
ORDER BY haiku.ID
