text:
Each activity supports a specific task, such as reviewing the chart or e-prescribing medications. You can access activities from the tabs on the bottom of the screen or by tapping a patient's name from the schedule or patient list.
When you have a patient chart open, tap and drag the activity bar at the bottom of the screen to the left to see more activities.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#5
text: When you leave Haiku, the app continues to run in the background. For security reasons, Haiku automatically logs you out after a period of inactivity. However, you can also manually log out. To do so, tap , Options, and then Log Out.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#6
text:
Tap Patients to open your patient lists. You can set a default list back in Hyperspace by right-clicking the list and clicking Default List. To open a different patient list, tap .
The following icons indicate that a patient has new information to review.
- indicates new abnormal results.
- indicates new critical results.
- indicates an isolation or infection.
- indicates new notes.
To edit a patient list, open the list and tap Edit. To remove a patient from the list, tap the icon and then tap Delete. To add a patient, tap the + button, search for a patient, and then select the patient. When you are finished editing the patient list, tap Done.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#7
headingPath: Find clinical appointments and surgical cases
text:
Tap Schedule to open your schedule. Select a date on the calendar view to see your schedule for that day. To see schedules for other groups, departments, or colleagues, tap .
The schedule shows each patient's age and sex, as well the appointment type. Appointments are color-coded and marked (with a dot) using the same colors as in Hyperspace. The rings that appear around the appointment time indicate the appointment's time and length.
For example, a 15-minute appointment appears like this:
If you're a surgeon and your cases are scheduled in Epic, they also appear on your schedule. Surgical cases appear like this:
To filter the schedule to only appointments with a certain status, tap and select the statuses you want to see.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#8
headingPath: Edit Schedule and Patient List columns
text:
The Schedule and Patient List in Haiku and Canto can be edited to show additional information using the same text-based columns in Schedule and Patient List views in Hyperspace. Only one additional column can be added at a time in the mobile apps.
To add an additional column in the mobile apps:
- Tap the three-dot menu in the top right corner of the Patient List or Schedule.
- Tap Settings.
- If needed, turn Show additional column to on.
- Search or scroll available columns and select your desired column.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#9
headingPath: Find patients in the emergency department
text:
When you log in to Haiku in the ED, the Track Board appears, and you're in the My Pts list.
My Pts shows patients assigned to you with acuity level (by color), location, chief complaint, lab and imaging status, and wait time. To see more details, such as which labs were done, tap and hold a patient's row.
To see patients who are waiting and assign yourself to a patient:
- At the top of the list, tap My Pts.
- From the menu, select Next to See.
- Swipe left on a patient's name and tap Assign Me.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#10
text:
To find a patient who isn't on your patient list or schedule, tap More in the activity tabs and Search to open the Patient Search activity. Then search as you normally do in Hyperspace, using the patient's name or MRN, as well as sex or date of birth, and the results appear with more patient details, such as address.
When you select a patient from a search, any documentation you do in Haiku is linked to the most recent available encounter. If an encounter is found when you select a patient from a search, a banner appears to let you know what encounter you’re in. If Haiku can't find a recent encounter for the patient, a new encounter is created to store your documentation when you start entering orders or writing a note, and you see a notification that an encounter was created.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#11
text: An encounter is automatically selected in Haiku if you select a patient appointment from the schedule or select an admitted patient from a patient list. To help make sure you’re documenting in the encounter you expect, such as when entering charges for an office visit or writing a note for the current admission, tap on the left side of the activity tabs to see what encounter you’re in.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#12
text:
To create a new patient record:
- Search for a patient in one of the following places:
- From Patient Lists, tap Edit, and tap +.
- Tap More, and select Search.
- Enter the patient's name.
- If you don't find the patient's record, tap .
- Select one of the following ways to enter information:
- Tap Demographics, and enter a sex, date of birth and social security number (or note an unknown SSN).
- Tap Face Sheet, and take a picture of a face sheet document.
- Tap Done.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#13
text:
In the In Basket activity, you can read and respond to many types of messages, including:
- CC'd Charts
- Chart Completion (Cosign Notes and Cosign Orders only)
- Coding and CDI Queries
- Cosign - Clinic Orders
- CRM (Customer Relationship Management)
- Dictate Later
- E-Visit/Video Visit
- Patient Call
- Pt MedAdvc Rq (Patient Medical Advice Request)
- Patient Escalation
- Procedure Prep
- Results
- Rx Request
- Staff Message
You can also create new Staff Messages and MyChart messages to patients and proxies. MyChart messages are sent as Patient Medical Advice Request messages.
The In Basket folder appears with the number of unread messages. The number is red if any of the unread messages are high priority. If you don't have any unread messages, no number appears. If you don't have any messages in that folder at all, the folder is gray.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#14
text:
The following icons appear next to messages in a folder to help you prioritize them:
High priority
Low priority
Unread message
Pended message
A message is pended if you’ve opened it and taken an action but haven’t marked the message done yet.
Overdue message
In Hyperspace, when sending a message, the sender can include an action, such as "Call patient". The action can also be flagged with a due date and time. If that due date and time has passed, the message appears as overdue in Hyperspace and the app.
You are responsible for the message.
Messages with responsibility help recipients track whether someone has started working on a task. Only the person who has responsibility for a message can mark it as done.
Swipe left on an In Basket message and tap Defer to Workstation to remove the message from your mobile In Basket. Messages you defer appear in your Hyperspace In Basket, but are hidden from your mobile In Basket.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#15
text:
- To create a new Staff Message, from your dashboard or the In Basket activity, tap .
- Select Compose Staff Message.
- Write your message and, optionally, add the following flags to your message before sending it:
- flags the recipient to call you.
- flags the message as high priority.
- Tap Send to send the message.
When you receive a Staff Message, tap to reply or forward the message.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#16
text:
Tap a result to open it.
The following icons can appear next to Results messages:
The patient has abnormal results.
The patient has critical results.
The green circle indicates that all the patient's orders have been resulted. A number indicates the total number of resulted orders that you haven't yet reviewed.
Not all orders for this patient have been resulted. A number indicates the total number of orders that have been resulted that you haven't yet reviewed.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#17
text:
- In a Results message, tap .
- Select the results you want to release.
- Select Note options.
- Select File to Chart.
- To add a comment for the patient, tap Compose Note.
- On the Results Release screen, tap Share Note and Release Results to release the results to MyChart.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#18
headingPath: Send a reminder to follow up on a result
text:
If you see a result in a Results message that you want to investigate further, you can send yourself a reminder to do so. The reminder is sent as a Patient Reminder message with the original Results message attached to it. Note that you can only access the reminder message in your Hyperspace In Basket.
- In a Results message, tap .
- Enter any additional text you want to add and tap Send to send the reminder to yourself.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#19
text:
- In a Results message, tap .
- Tap the Compose Note field and enter a note for the result.
- Optionally tap Note Options for the following options:
- If you want to mark the note as Important, select the Important option
- If you want to file your note, select the File to Chart option.
- Tap Send to send the note.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#20
text:
- In an Rx Request message, tap a pending medication to review the order details. Tap Rx Request to return to the message.
- If you need to review the full chart, tap the patient's name.
- Act on the request:
- Tap Approve to approve all pending medications.
- Edit the order details as needed, and then tap Accept.
- Tap Edit to selectively approve and refuse pending medications or edit the order details.
- Tap a medication to edit the order details and, when you are finished, tap Accept.
- Tap Refuse to refuse a pending medication.
- Tap Sign, select a reason for refusal for the medication, and then tap Accept.
- To change pharmacies or split up prescriptions between multiple pharmacies, tap Associate Pharmacies.
- Tap Sign to sign any approved refill requests. If you have addressed all the requests in the message, it is removed from your In Basket.
- If you aren't ready to close the encounter, toggle Sign encounter off.
- Tap Accept.
You can also swipe up on the Patient Info tab to see more about the patient.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#21
text:
- In a Cosign - Clinic Orders message, tap an order to review the order details.
- If you need to review the full chart, tap the patient's name.
- Act on the request to complete the message and remove it from your In Basket:
- Tap Sign to cosign the orders.
- Tap Decline to decline to provide your cosignature.
- Tap Select to sign or decline individual orders in a single message.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#22
text:
You can act on the following Chart Completion messages in Haiku or Canto:
- In a Cosign Note message, tap Sign to either sign or attest the note. If you need to attest the note, a field appears to enter your part with the keyboard or speech-to-text.
- In a Cosign Order message for inpatient orders, tap Sign or Decline to take the same action for all orders, or tap Select to choose which ones you want to sign.
- In a Coding Query message, tap New Note to create a note to respond to the coder's questions. Complete the note and tap Sign to complete the message.
- Tap Request Clarification to reply to the coder with a question. Tap Send to complete the message.
You can review other types of deficiencies but not act on them. To clear a message that you can't complete right now, tap and then tap Defer to Workstation.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#23
text:
- In a Patient Advice Request message:
- If you need to review the full chart, tap the patient's name.
- To open an attachment, tap the file name.
- Act on the request:
- Tap to reply to the patient by email.
- Tap to forward the message to another provider.
- Tap the phone number at the top of the message to call the patient.
- Tap Done to remove the message from your In Basket.
- Tap to mark the message as New or defer it to your workstation to read later.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#24
text:
- Tap the E-Visits folder in your In Basket and select the message you want to review.
- Review the information in the patient's E-Visit message, including self-triage or questionnaire responses.
- If you don't want to take responsibility for the E-Visit message, tap Put Back to return the message to the folder.
- To reply to the message or route it to another provider, tap .
- To go to the patient's chart, tap either the patient's name or picture in the message header. From the chart, you can complete many of the same tasks you would in a normal office visit, including reviewing the patient's allergies and medications, documenting a visit diagnosis, writing progress notes, and placing orders.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#25
text: When an escalation is sent for a patient who uses MyChart Care Companion (for example, because they report concerning symptoms on a daily check-in questionnaire), you'll receive a push notification. You can view details of the escalation and follow up from the new Patient Escalation folder in In Basket.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#26
text:
While writing a note, you can type .dictatelater to add a placeholder that you can fill in later from Haiku. You complete these placeholders from your In Basket.
- In the Dictate Later folder, open a note and go to a placeholder text box.
- Tap to begin dictating.
- Tap Save in the upper right corner to save your changes.
- If you have to stop dictating a note partway through, your changes are saved in Haiku, but aren't visible to other clinicians until you're done.
- Tap Done to complete the placeholders and finalize the note.
- Any unfinished .dictatelater links are deleted when you mark a note as done.
- If you accidentally delete a placeholder for which you already dictated text, that text is sent to your In Basket as a Staff Message so you don't lose your work.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#27
headingPath: Read and reply to new messages
text: When you receive a new Secure Chat message, you get a notification on your device. Tap the notification to open the conversation and type your reply in the field at the bottom of the screen.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#28
headingPath: Review all conversations and start new ones
text:
- Tap Secure Chat to open the Secure Chat activity and see a list of all your conversations.
- The icons next to each message indicate who is participating in the conversation.
- If a conversation is about a patient, that patient's name and, if they're admitted, their location, appear above the message.
- Tap to start a new conversation.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#29
headingPath: See who has read a message
text: Tap a message bubble to see the full list of users who have read it.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#30
headingPath: Review a snapshot of medical information
text:
You can see an overview of the patient's current medical information from the Summary activity, which appears when you open a patient's chart.
The Current Medications section shows all the patient's outpatient and hospital medications. The following icons appear in this section:
Long-term medication
Patient-reported medication
If the patient is on any opioids, to see Morphine Equivalent Daily Dosing (MEDD) information, tap the link below the medication’s name.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#31
text: From the Encounters activity, you can review information about previous encounters. Tap an encounter to review it.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#32
text:
Information about external encounters and results appears throughout Haiku. The icon indicates information from another organization
To see complete documents for encounters and results performed at other organizations, from a patient's chart, tap Care Everywhere to open the Care Everywhere activity.
- Tap Summaries to review a patient's clinical summary.
- Tap Documents to review a patient's clinical documents.
Documents listed in black text are available to view, while documents listed in gray text must be requested from Hyperspace before you can view them.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#33
text: In the Patient Summary activity, tap Mark as Reviewed to record that you've reviewed the patient information.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#34
text:
- In the patient's chart, tap the patient photo or camera icon in the upper-left corner of the screen.
- Tap Capture ID Photo and use the camera on your device to take a picture.
- Tap Use Photo to save the photo to the Demographics activity in the chart.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#35
text:
- Tap the camera icon next to the patient’s photo to open the Media Capture activity.
- In the Media Capture activity, tap Capture Clinical Image and use the camera on your device to take a picture.
- Tap Use Photo, select a document type, enter a description, and rotate the picture if necessary.
- Tap Save and enter a document type and comment if required to save the media to the chart. You can review media captures in the Media Manager or the Chart Review activity in Hyperspace.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#36
text:
- In the patient's chart, tap Media to go to the Media activity.
- Scroll through the list of media files or, to find a specific media file, search using information such as:
- Document type
- The user who imported the file
- Keywords from the image's description
- The date the file was imported
- Tap a photo or document to see a full-screen view, where you can zoom in and out or pan around the image.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#37
text:
After you open the patient's chart, tap Results to go to the Results activity. This activity shows a list of recent results for the patient. Tap a result to see details.
- For lab tests, a table of lab results appears. Swipe left to see past values for the same lab. You can tap to see the report view.
- For imaging or EKG results, a narrative report appears.
Tap and hold on a result to see the reference range for that component.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#38
headingPath: Review a patient's critical or abnormal results
text:
An icon appears in the patient list for patients with any new results. These same icons appear in the Results activity.
Abnormal result
Critical result

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#39
text:
Review discrete lab results in a graph. While reviewing a table in the Results activity, turn your device horizontally.
Each result component appears on the graph in a unique color. To help you match the line color to a particular result component, a key appears at the top of the graph.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#40
headingPath: Focus on one type of result
text: Tap the colored circle on the left side of the screen that corresponds to that component's color. The line that represents that component appears brighter than the other lines. Slide your finger up and down in order to choose the component you want to bring to the front of the graph.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#41
text: Each white data point on the graph represents a specific result value for a component. Tap and hold near a data point to view more information about that value, including the actual result value, the reference range, the result date, and the result time.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#42
headingPath: View and Create Notes and Letters
text: Tap Notes to see a list of encounter notes. From the list, tap a note you want to review.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#43
headingPath: Use filters to narrow down the list of notes
text: To filter the notes you see in the activity, tap Filter and choose a filter category. For example, you might filter by note type and show only progress notes. Tap Done to apply the filters you've selected.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#44
headingPath: Create a new note or letter
text:
To write a note or letter, go to Notes Entry. A new note opens automatically. Notes and letters you create are automatically associated with an encounter in the patient's chart. The encounter associated with the note appears in gray below the patient header.
- If there are already notes, tap to start a new one.
- Start entering text with the keyboard or tap the microphone on the Nuance or Fluency toolbar to dictate with speech-to-text.
- To change the note type, tap and then Note Info.
- When you've made your selection, tap Note Details and then Done to return to the note.
- When you're done, tap Sign on Sign Visit. Or, tap to sign or pend the note.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#45
headingPath: Attach an image to a note
text: To attach an image while you're writing a note, tap and then tap Add image. After you take the photo, you can tap Annotate to draw annotations on the image. Tap Save and enter a document type and description if required to insert the image and return to your note.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#46
text:
To begin, tap to open the Orders activity.
A list of active orders appears. In outpatient visits, the list shows medications. If the patient is admitted or in the ED, it shows both medications and procedures. If you use a Quick List, tap the list title to switch between active orders and your Quick List.
You can write most outpatient and inpatient orders from Haiku, but note these limitations:
- For non-medication orders and inpatient orders, you can only edit indications of use and answer questions.
- You can't manage your preference list.
If you can't sign an order because details are missing, tap Pend or Save Work and finish entering the order from a workstation.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx
title: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users

meta.file: Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx

id: file:Shared Documents/Haiku Quick Start Guide for iOS Users.docx#47
text:
- To enter an order in Haiku:
- Search for an order or browse your preference list by tapping .
- Tap to write a new order for one of the patient's current orders.
- Tap the orders you want to select and tap Done.
- To review and sign, tap . In the list of selected orders:
- To print or call in a medication that can't be e-prescribed, select the appropriate Class in the order details. You'll see a list of orders to call in to the pharmacy after you sign.
- To get a notification when results for an inpatient lab are ready, tap .
- To change pharmacies for a prescription, tap the pharmacy name. You can split prescriptions between multiple pharmacies if needed.
- To verify the patient's coverage information or associated an order with a diagnosis, tap .

About Abridge
Abridge was founded in 2018 with the mission of powering deeper understanding in healthcare. Its
AI-powered platform is purpose-built for medical conversations, drastically reducing the burden of
clinical documentation while enabling clinicians to focus on what maers most—their patients.
Abridge’s participation in Epic’s recently launched Workshop program unlocks the collaborative
power of co-development between Epic and Abridge to tackle health systems’ most pressing
issues.
From Haiku to Hyperspace, clinicians can harness the power of Abridge from start to finish without
ever leaving Epic. Capture patient conversations in Haiku or Canto. Use the Abridge activity tab in
Hyperspace to trust and verify AI-generated note drafts quickly. Abridge is the only company that
maps AI-generated summaries to ground truth, helping clinicians quickly trust and verify the
output.
Visit hp://www.abridge.com to learn more.

title: Abridge Inside User Guide
text:
Geing Started
Welcome to Abridge! We're excited to help you onboard and simplify your documentation. In this
section, we’ll review some of the basics of how to get started and access Abridge.
In this guide:
● Haiku refers to Epic's iPhone app
○ Note: Abridge Inside is only compatible with iOS devices and is not currently
supported on Haiku for Android
● Canto refers to Epic's iPad app
● Hyperspace refers to Epic’s desktop/laptop application
Abridge recording can be made from your iOS Haiku or Canto app using the latest version. For
simplicity, we will only reference “Haiku” in this guide.
Required hardware, Wi-Fi, and baery
You only need your iPhone (or iPad) and workstation to get started. You don’t need any additional
hardware to use Abridge.
You need an Internet connection to begin recording. A fast WiFi connection will give you the best
results.
Recording should not be a significant drain on your baery, but if you’re worried about baery life,
feel free to turn o your screen display while recording or use a wireless charger.
Accessing your Abridge account
Your organization’s IT will enable you to access Abridge Inside. Simply start the workflow from
Haiku to begin using Abridge.

text:
In-person and virtual care
Abridge Inside supports in-person and telehealth patient visits that take place outside of Haiku.
For telehealth, skip headphones and use a dierent device than your phone to conduct the virtual
visit. Your phone must record the audio from your computer's speakers during the visit.
HIPAA compliance
Abridge is fully HIPAA compliant. Read more here.

Managing multiple patients at the same time
Seamlessly pre-chart, post-chart, or switch between patients by pausing recordings. Here are
some examples of when you might use this feature:
● Resuming a recording to add more medical terminology post-visit.
● Recording a resident’s patient presentation, pausing before entering the patient's room,

Pause: Tap the pause buon to pause your current recording.

title: Abridge Inside User Guide
text:
Recording Tips
General Tips
Let’s review some tips for ensuring the best audio quality, processing speed, and note accuracy
while recording.
● Record using a high-speed Wi-Fi connection for the fastest note-generation and smooth
uploads.
● Abridge needs your phone’s microphone. Make sure that you’re not using other apps that
are using your device’s microphone at the same time as recording with Abridge.
● Place your phone in between you and your patient without any obstructions.
● Converse instead of dictate. Abridge processes natural clinician-patient conversation, so
talk to your patient like you normally would.
● Verbally share findings and plans throughout the visit, including during the physical exam.
Be sure to vocalize non-verbal cues such as shrugs and nods.
● Use the pause and resume functionality to include medical terminology before or after a
visit. The more details you can provide, the higher quality note will be produced.
● If you answer a phone call while recording, Abridge will automatically pause the recording.
After you end the call, tap on the Haiku app to bring it back into the foreground, where you
will need to tap the play buon to resume the recording.
● Don’t use headphones. For telehealth visits, your phone needs to pick up the audio from
your computer's speakers to capture the visit.

title: Abridge Inside User Guide
text:
Verbalizing your Physical Exam
Abridge automatically generates a dedicated Physical Exam section in your clinical note.
How it works
Clinicians across all healthcare specialties can capture positive and negative findings from key
systems by verbalizing each system during the patient visit.
- HEENT
- Neck
- Chest
- Cardiovascular
- Breast
- Abdomen
- Vitals
- Rectal
- Extremities
- Musculoskeletal
- Neurological
- Skin
- Genitourinary
Physical Exam Best Practices
1. Introduce the exam “Moving on to the physical exam…” or “Let’s take a look…”
2. Tie findings to a location on
the body
Recommended: “Both ears are clear of blockages
Avoid: “All clear over here.”
3. Use specific sensory words Recommended: “I am palpating your neck, and I feel a
swollen lymph node.”
Avoid: “There’s swelling in your neck.”
4. Expect Abridge to reflect
your words as spoken
Saying “Heart exam is normal” will output “Heart exam is
normal,” not a list of templated findings such as “Heart
has regular rate and rhythm.”

Results
Abridge automatically generates a dedicated Results section in your clinical note. This section is
enabled and shown by default.
How it works
Your note will automatically capture spoken objective findings related to results, such as labs,
pathology, diagnostic tests, imaging findings, and notes about in-oice procedures.
The subsections include:
- Labs
- Pathology
- Diagnostic
- Radiology
- Procedure
(e.g., laryngoscopy, injections)

Completing Your Abridge Note
Once you’ve initiated note creation from Haiku, you can review and verify your note in Hyperspace.
The steps appear below.
Note Statuses
Use the “Note Status” field to check if your note is ready
1. Haiku: Take a look at the “Note Status” column within your patient list inside Haiku..
2. Hyperspace: Similar to Haiku, you will have a “Note Status” column within your patient list.
In addition, a pop-up will appear on the upper right-hand corner of your screen, leing you
know that your note is ready. Click “Go to Note” to begin reviewing your note.

title: Abridge Inside User Guide
text:
There are 5 dierent Note Statuses within Abridge that will keep you informed about how your
note is processing:
1. Recording: You are actively recording
2. Uploading: Abridge is gathering the audio file from your device
3. Processing: Abridge has received the audio file and is beginning to process
a.
Key troubleshooting tip: If you paused the recording and did not tap “Create Note,”
your Note Status will remain as “Processing.” In order to resolve this, navigate to your
patient in Haiku and tap “Create Note.”
4. Ready: The Abridge AI note is available within Epic
5. Reviewed: You have reviewed and signed the note
Epic will provide a cue to you when the note is ready for review.

title: Abridge Inside User Guide
text:
Adding Abridge note sections to your note
SmartSections are used to pull in the Abridge content as soon as the note has been generated
and note content is available. You never need to “refresh” to pull in Abridge content.
You can easily add ambient SmartSections to your patient’s note within their chart by leveraging
templates or dotphrases. The workflow described below is compatible with:
● Standard template: If you have a standard note template that you use within your
department, your project team can update it to incorporate the ambient SmartSections into
your note
● Personalized template: If you have personalized note templates, you can modify that
template and incorporate the ambient SmartSections
Return to TOC 18
© 2024 Epic Systems Corporation

title: Abridge Inside User Guide
text:
● No templates: If you do not use templates, you can always pull these SmartSections into
new notes that you are creating.
When using templates:
1. Open your desired note template (this template should already be set up to leverage
ambient SmartSections)
2. View and edit the AI content in the ambient SmartSections

Editing your note
SmartSections are a specific category of dotphrases or SmartLinks, and are editable. They allow
Abridge Note Sections to be pulled into your patient’s clinical note, including any edits you make.
When you make edits within a SmartSection, your edits will be sent directly to Abridge upon
signing your final note. SmartSections areas are clearly marked by the vertical shaded bars directly
to the left of your Abridge note content.
Accessing the Abridge tab
Abridge oers built-in auditability to ensure trust and verification with our Linked Evidence
feature. Linked Evidence helps you view the origin of particular AI summaries so you can see the

Summary will reflect Abridge’s first draft of the conversation. Your note and PVS will not be
editable but can be edited within the patient chart directly.
Linked Evidence
Abridge oers built-in auditability to ensure trust and verification via our Linked Evidence feature.
Linked Evidence helps you view the origin of AI summaries so that you can see the source of truth.

Every Abridge-generated clinical note includes a “Patient Visit Summary” with a plan and
instructions in patient-friendly language. This can be copied into your Patient Instructions from
the visit.
How it works
1. Click the “Patient Visit Summary” tab to view the summary draft.
2. When finished, in order to retain formaing, click "Copy All" to copy/paste the summary into
the patient record.

Providing feedback to Abridge

title: Abridge Inside User Guide
text:
Advanced Features
Now that we’ve covered the basics of recording, let’s review some of our advanced features.
Pre-chart in Epic with Abridge
You have the flexibility to start your documentation in Epic before you record with Abridge:
1. Start your note
a. Add SmartSections
b. Add any content to your note
2. Record with Abridge from Haiku
3. Press the “Create Note” buon in Haiku
4. Edit your note in Hyperspace.
a. Your Abridge content will flow into the pre-created SmartSections.
b. Your Abridge AI content will be appended to any prior content that you have created
Language, accents, and dialect interpretations
Abridge uses proprietary automatic speech recognition �ASR� to process audio, and our AI
performs well across diverse accents, languages, and dialects.
Today, Abridge supports medical conversations in 14 languages including English, Spanish,
Chinese (Mandarin), Chinese (Cantonese), Tagalog, Vietnamese, Arabic, French, Korean, Russian,
Haitian Creole, German, Japanese, Italian, and more, generating a note in English after the visit.

title: Abridge Inside User Guide
text:
In the example below, the patient and clinician spoke German during the visit.
Multiple speakers per patient visit
Abridge’s AI can predict the speaker, whether it’s a patient, caregiver, or doctor. Abridge works well
in seings for multiple participants, especially with interpreters and caregivers. Everything
captured in the recorded conversation will contribute to the Abridge-generated clinical note.
Updating patient pronouns
You can always update or change a patient’s gender pronoun to accurately reflect and respect
patient identities by choosing from she/her, he/him, or they/them pronouns when disclosed.
Return to TOC 29

title: Abridge Inside User Guide
text:
You can update patient pronouns during the recording process, before tapping “Create Note.”
Abridge will auto-populate your patient’s pronouns from your patient’s record. If you want to
update or change your patient’s pronoun in your Abridge note, you can do so by selecting a
dierent pronoun from the recording or pause screen within Haiku. Please note, if you update your
patient’s pronouns within the Abridge note it will not be updated in your patient’s record.
If no pronoun is ingested from the chart and no manual pronoun is selected, Abridge’s technology
will try to predict patient pronouns based on the context from the conversation.

title: Abridge Inside User Guide
text:
Editing your seings
The first time you record in Haiku, you will be asked to select your “Note Seings.” These enable
you to set up new notes that fit your preferences. These seings will impact all future clinical
notes that are generated. You can always update your seings within the Abridge tab if you’d like
to adjust them.
In the Abridge tab in Hyperspace, you can edit your “Note Seings” by navigating to the gear icon
at the top of your note panel.

Customize which note sections appear in your note and Abridge tab by selecting from the menu.
● The core sections �HPI, PE, Results, and A&P) will appear in your clinical note.
● The additional sections �PMH, Meds, SH, and FH� will be shown in the Abridge tab and can
be copied into the final note.
Customize your “History of Present Illness” section by choosing between two formaing options:
“Concise” or “Comprehensive.”
“Concise” is recommended for best results. “Comprehensive” captures more details for clinicians
who prefer more context.

title: Abridge Inside User Guide
text:
Example of a “Concise” note:
History of Present Illness
The patient, with a history of diabetes and recent vision loss, presents for follow-up. They report no nausea with weekly
Trulicity injections and are familiar with the pen. They have not experienced the common side eect of weight loss with
Trulicity, and aribute their recent weight gain to decreased mobility due to vision loss. They underwent an operation for
their vision last week, but report no improvement and are unable to drive. They continue to work, with transportation
provided by their husband.
They are also taking metformin and insulin, but no Farxiga. They administer 20�25 units of insulin at bedtime and report no
hypoglycemic episodes. Their morning blood sugars are around 140. They recall a previous medication, possibly an
injectable, that maintained their blood sugars in the 90s, but cannot remember the name. They have one more box of
insulin vials left from a previous prescription.
In addition to their diabetes and vision loss, they have been dealing with the stress of decreased independence and
increased reliance on their husband for transportation.
Example of a “Comprehensive” note:
History of Present Illness
The patient, with a history of diabetes, has been managing their condition with Trulicity, metformin, and insulin. They have
not experienced any side eects such as nausea or pancreatitis from the Trulicity. However, they have not noticed any
weight loss, a common side eect of the medication. They have been taking insulin at a dosage of between 20 and 25 units,
with no episodes of hypoglycemia. Their blood sugar control has been satisfactory, with an A1c close to 7, but there is a

title: Abridge Inside User Guide
text:
with no episodes of hypoglycemia. Their blood sugar control has been satisfactory, with an A1c close to 7, but there is a
desire to lower it further due to their eye problems.
The patient recently underwent an operation for their vision, which has been significantly impaired. They report a distinct
blur in their right eye and the presence of a floater. They are unable to drive due to their vision problems and have been
staying at home since the operation. They are scheduled for a follow-up appointment next week.
The patient has also been experiencing high morning blood sugar levels, around 140. They recall a previous medication,
possibly an injectable, that kept their levels consistently in the 90s, but they cannot remember the name. They have been
using an Accu Chek meter to monitor their blood sugar levels.
The patient has been taking their insulin at bedtime, but there is a plan to change this to taking it with breakfast and dinner.
The patient has been struggling with weight gain, which they aribute to their limited mobility due to their vision problems.
They acknowledge the impact of weight gain on their blood sugar control and overall health. They also express the
emotional toll of their vision problems and the resulting changes in their lifestyle.
Return to TOC 34
© 2024 Epic Systems Corporation

title: Abridge Inside User Guide
text:
Customize your “Assessment & Plan” section by choosing between two formaing options:
“Bulleted” or “Paragraph.”
“Bulleted” (recommended) lists out elements of the plan under each problem as separate bullets,
and “Paragraph” is a descriptive blurb of the problem and associated plan.
Example of a “Bulleted” note:
Assessment & Plan
Possible Ischemic Heart Disease: New onset exertional chest pain and shortness of breath with radiation to the arm and
associated lightheadedness. High risk given history of diabetes, hypertension, and family history of heart disease.
- Perform EKG and echocardiogram today.
Poorly Controlled Diabetes: Hemoglobin A1C of 9 in January. Admied to inconsistent use of Metformin.
- Encourage consistent use of Metformin 500mg twice daily.
- Review diabetes medications with nurse during today's visit.
Uncontrolled Hypertension: Blood pressure of 180/80 today.
- Start Hydrochlorothiazide 25mg daily.
- Refer to nutritionist for low salt, heart healthy diet education. Nutritionist to call next week.
Example of a “Paragraph” note:
Assessment & Plan
Possible Ischemic Heart Disease: She presents with new onset exertional chest pain, shortness of breath, and
lightheadedness, compounded by multiple cardiovascular risk factors including hypertension, diabetes, and a
family history of heart disease. We will perform an EKG and echocardiogram this afternoon.
Poorly Controlled Diabetes: Her last A1C in January was 9, indicating poorly controlled diabetes, exacerbated by
inconsistent adherence to metformin. We will continue Metformin 500mg twice daily and review diabetes
medications with a nurse this afternoon.
Uncontrolled Hypertension: Her blood pressure today is 180/80, indicating uncontrolled hypertension. We will start
Hydrochlorothiazide 25mg daily and refer her to a nutritionist for low salt, heart-healthy diet counseling.

title: Abridge Inside User Guide

Feedback
You’re now ready to begin using Abridge! Feedback is our lifeblood. As you start to use Abridge,
we’d love to hear your feedback and thoughts. We use your comments to improve our technology
and the output of your note drafts—and we want you to get the best note possible!
There are two main ways you can provide feedback:
● Note star rating: Within the Abridge tab there is a star rating buon and an opportunity to
leave comments about how we can improve the quality of your note. Our team reads
through all feedback to beer understand how we can improve.
● Email: Share your experiences with us by emailing help@abridge.com.

UT Health San Antonio IT Partner Team
UT Health San Antonio
Information Technology
ISSUE ALERT
**Description:**
We are currently experiencing an issue where Appointment Request and Referral Authorization work queues are displaying with zero items, despite pending requests and authorizations being present in the system. This issue may affect operational workflows and patient care processes.
**What to expect:**
Appointment Request and Referral Authorization work queues are displaying with zero items despite pending requests and authorizations being present in the system.
**Impact:**
- Teams reliant on these work queues for processing appointment requests and authorizations are unable to view or action their tasks.
- Delays in appointment scheduling and referral authorization approvals may occur, leading to potential impacts on patient care timelines.
**Current Status:**
- The issue has been identified and is under active investigation by our technical teams.
- We are working closely with our Epic teams to resolve the problem as quickly as possible.
**What you need to do:**
**Next Steps:**
- We will provide regular updates as we work towards a resolution.
- A follow-up communication will be sent once the issue has been resolved or if further actions are needed.
- Please inform your teams who work with appointment requests and referral authorizations.
Thank you for your patience and cooperation as we work to resolve this issue. Please contact the Epic Help Desk if you experience any other related problems or require additional support.
Need Help? Contact Us @

title: IssueAlertUpdate
text:

Folder: Shared Documents/Site Report

Issue alert update notice from the UT Health San Antonio IT Partner Team about Appointment Request and Referral Authorization work queues displaying zero items.
MESSAGE FROM THE
UT Health San Antonio IT Partner Team
UT Health San Antonio
Information Technology
**ISSUE ALERT UPDATE**
**Description:**
We are providing an important update regarding the recent issue where Appointment Request and Referral Authorization work queues were displaying zero items.
**What to expect:**
Please review the current Update and Impact.
**Update:**
- A utility has been successfully run to repopulate the affected work queues.
- All referral statuses have been set to **"Pending"** with a reason of **"System Automatically Pend."**
- A **secondary utility** is currently in progress to restore referrals to their appropriate statuses. We will notify you once this process has been completed.
- **Previous documentation** related to referrals and appointment requests remains available for review and has **not been impacted** by this issue.
- Referrals entered with today's date are not impacted and can continue to be worked as normal.
**Impact:**
- While work queues are now populated, the "Pending" status may cause temporary delays as manual reviews are needed until the secondary utility completes its work.
- Teams are encouraged to review and action the items in their work queues, while awaiting updates from the secondary utility.
**What you need to do:**
**Next Steps:**
- Continue to monitor and process items in the repopulated work queues as appropriate.
- Referral statuses will be automatically updated once the secondary utility completes, and we will send a follow-up communication at that time.

title: Abridge Integrated User Guide
text:
Feedback 39
About Abridge
Abridge was founded in 2018 with the vision of empowering more understanding in healthcare. We
aim to help people feel taken care of by eliminating the need for burdensome clerical work, which
aords clinicians the time and energy to connect with their patients. Our software captures
details directly from recorded patient encounters and helps you eiciently draft your clinical
documentation within seconds.
Powered by Linked Evidence, Abridge is the only company that maps AI-generated summaries to
the source audio and transcript, helping providers quickly trust and verify the summary. Visit
hp://www.abridge.com to learn more.
Return to TOC 3

title: Abridge Integrated User Guide
text:
Geing Started
Welcome to Abridge! We're excited to help you onboard and simplify your documentation. In this
section, we will walk you through signing into Abridge on your computer and downloading
the Abridge for Clinicians mobile app.
You will record patient conversations using the mobile app or web (if enabled), and you will edit
and complete clinical notes on your laptop/desktop at notes.abridge.com.
Sign in
1. Visit notes.abridge.com to sign into your account.
2. Sign in using your work email and authenticate via SSO if SSO is supported by your
health system.
Return to TOC 4

title: Abridge Integrated User Guide
text:
Editing your seings
As a part of the sign-in process, you will be asked to update your “Note Seings.” These seings
enable you to set up new notes that fit your preferences. You’ll want to customize your seings
before recording your patient conversations. These seings will impact all future clinical notes
that are generated, and you can always update your seings if you’d like to adjust them.
You can also edit your “Note Seings” by navigating to the menu bar at the top left corner of your
screen and clicking “Note Seings.”
Return to TOC 5

title: Abridge Integrated User Guide
text:
Customize your “History of Present Illness” section by choosing between two formaing options:
“Concise or Comprehensive.”
Example of a “Concise” note:
History of Present Illness
The patient, with a history of diabetes and recent vision loss, presents for follow-up. They report no nausea with
weekly Trulicity injections and are familiar with the pen. They have not experienced the common side eect of
weight loss with Trulicity, and aribute their recent weight gain to decreased mobility due to vision loss. They
underwent an operation for their vision last week, but report no improvement and are unable to drive. They
continue to work, with transportation provided by their husband.
They are also taking metformin and insulin, but no Farxiga. They administer 20�25 units of insulin at bedtime and
report no hypoglycemic episodes. Their morning blood sugars are around 140. They recall a previous medication,
possibly an injectable, that maintained their blood sugars in the 90s, but cannot remember the name. They have
one more box of insulin vials left from a previous prescription.
In addition to their diabetes and vision loss, they have been dealing with the stress of decreased independence
and increased reliance on their husband for transportation.
Example of a “Comprehensive” note:
History of Present Illness
The patient, with a history of diabetes, has been managing their condition with Trulicity, metformin, and insulin.
They have not experienced any side eects such as nausea or pancreatitis from the Trulicity. However, they have
not noticed any weight loss, a common side eect of the medication. They have been taking insulin at a dosage of
between 20 and 25 units, with no episodes of hypoglycemia. Their blood sugar control has been satisfactory, with

title: Abridge Integrated User Guide
text:
not noticed any weight loss, a common side eect of the medication. They have been taking insulin at a dosage of
between 20 and 25 units, with no episodes of hypoglycemia. Their blood sugar control has been satisfactory, with
an A1c close to 7, but there is a desire to lower it further due to their eye problems.
The patient recently underwent an operation for their vision, which has been significantly impaired. They report a
distinct blur in their right eye and the presence of a floater. They are unable to drive due to their vision problems
and have been staying at home since the operation. They are scheduled for a follow-up appointment next week.
Return to TOC 6

title: Abridge Integrated User Guide
text:
The patient has also been experiencing high morning blood sugar levels, around 140. They recall a previous
medication, possibly an injectable, that kept their levels consistently in the 90s, but they cannot remember the
name. They have been using an Accu Chek meter to monitor their blood sugar levels.
The patient has been taking their insulin at bedtime, but there is a plan to change this to taking it with breakfast
and dinner.
The patient has been struggling with weight gain, which they aribute to their limited mobility due to their vision
problems. They acknowledge the impact of weight gain on their blood sugar control and overall health. They also
express the emotional toll of their vision problems and the resulting changes in their lifestyle.
Next, customize your “Assessment & Plan” section by choosing between two formaing options:
“Bulleted” or “Paragraph.”
“Bulleted” lists out elements of the plan under each problem as separate bullets, and “Paragraph”
is a descriptive blurb of the problem and associated plan.
Example of a “Bulleted” note:
Assessment & Plan
Possible Ischemic Heart Disease: New onset exertional chest pain and shortness of breath with radiation to the arm
and associated lightheadedness. High risk given history of diabetes, hypertension, and family history of heart disease.
- Perform EKG and echocardiogram today.
Poorly Controlled Diabetes: Hemoglobin A1C of 9 in January. Admied to inconsistent use of Metformin.
- Encourage consistent use of Metformin 500mg twice daily.
- Review diabetes medications with nurse during today's visit.
Uncontrolled Hypertension: Blood pressure of 180/80 today.
- Start Hydrochlorothiazide 25mg daily.
- Refer to nutritionist for low salt, heart healthy diet education. Nutritionist to call next week.
Return to TOC 7

title: Abridge Integrated User Guide
text:
Example of a “Paragraph” note:
Assessment & Plan
Possible Ischemic Heart Disease: She presents with new onset exertional chest pain, shortness of breath, and
lightheadedness, compounded by multiple cardiovascular risk factors including hypertension, diabetes, and a family
history of heart disease. We will perform an EKG and echocardiogram this afternoon.
Poorly Controlled Diabetes: Her last A1C in January was 9, indicating poorly controlled diabetes, exacerbated by
inconsistent adherence to metformin. We will continue Metformin 500mg twice daily and review diabetes
medications with a nurse this afternoon.
Uncontrolled Hypertension: Her blood pressure today is 180/80, indicating uncontrolled hypertension. We will start
Hydrochlorothiazide 25mg daily and refer her to a nutritionist for low salt, heart-healthy diet counseling.
Optional sections
Optional sections include: Past Medical History, Medications, Social History, and Family History
Each of these sections will be hidden by default. To enable these sections, click the sections so
that the checkmark appears.
Return to TOC 8

title: Abridge Integrated User Guide
text:
Once you’ve customized your notes, you can also choose to hide or show dierent note sections.
Click the check mark to select which sections you would like to show or hide by default.
Return to TOC 9

title: Abridge Integrated User Guide
text:
Download and setup
You must log in to notes.abridge.com first to avoid receiving an error message when signing in to
the mobile app.
1. Download the Abridge For Clinicians mobile app from the Apple App Store or the Google Play
Store.
2. Sign in using your work email and authenticate via SSO if SSO is supported by your health
system.
Return to TOC 10

title: Abridge Integrated User Guide
text:
Logging in and out
● Each time you open the Abridge mobile app on your phone or log on via your laptop/desktop,
use your SSO credentials.
○ Tip: We recommend you bookmark notes.abridge.com in your web browser.
● To log out of the Abridge mobile app, navigate to the seings icon at the top left corner of
your screen and click “Logout.” To log out of the web editor, navigate to the menu bar on the
top left corner of your screen and click “Logout.”
● For security purposes, you will be automatically logged out from the Abridge mobile app
every 21 days and every 12 hours from the web editor, or in alignment with the security
parameters set up by your organization
Return to TOC 11

title: Abridge Integrated User Guide
text:
Updating the Abridge for Clinicians mobile app
Abridge is always making continuous improvements to our software, including new or improved
functionality, bug fixes, and security enhancements. We recommend that you turn on automatic
updates to ensure that you have access to the latest version of our mobile app, inclusive of the
latest enhancements in our AI. Abridge supports iPhones with iOS 15 software or later and Android
devices with Android 10 or later.
In-person and virtual care
Abridge supports in-person and telehealth patient visits. For telehealth, remember not to wear
headphones; your phone needs to pick up the audio from your computer’s speakers to capture the
visit.
HIPAA compliance
Abridge is fully HIPAA compliant. Read more here.
Return to TOC 12

title: Abridge Integrated User Guide
text:
The Basics—Recording Patient Visits
This section reviews the basics of how to record with Abridge and how to introduce this new
technology to your patients.
Required hardware, Wi-Fi, and baery
All you need is your phone and computer to get started. You don’t need any additional hardware to
use Abridge. For best results, ensure that your phone’s microphones are not obstructed (e.g. by
being in a pocket or a bag).
You can record conversations without Wi-Fi or in airplane mode. However, you will need an Internet
connection to upload your conversations and receive your AI-generated note draft.
Recording should not be a significant drain on your baery, but if you’re worried about baery life,
feel free to turn o your screen display while recording or use a wireless charger.
Abridge supports iPhones with iOS 15 software or later and Android devices with Android 10 or
later.
Introducing Abridge to your patients
Ensure you follow your organization’s recommended guidelines for patient consent.
Return to TOC 13

title: Abridge Integrated User Guide
text:
Recording patient visits
1. Ensure you follow your organization’s recommended guidelines for collecting patient
consent to be recorded.
2. Open the Abridge for Clinicians mobile app.
3. Select your patient in the “Worklist” view. If your patient does not appear on your worklist,
tap the “+” buon and label the recording using the patient’s first and last name.
4. Tap the red record buon to start recording.
5. When finished recording, tap “Create Note.”
Managing multiple patients at the same time
Seamlessly pre-chart, post-chart, or switch between patients by pausing recordings. Here are
some examples of when you might use this feature:
Return to TOC 14

title: Abridge Integrated User Guide
text:
● Resuming a recording to add more medical terminology post-visit.
● Recording a resident’s patient presentation, pausing before entering the patient's room,
and resuming the recording when you round on the patient.
Deleting recordings
If you want to delete a recording, go to the specific recording you want to delete and click the
garbage can icon in the top right corner of the screen. You’ll need to confirm you’d like to delete
the recording. You can delete recordings during a live session or after a recording has been
completed.
Return to TOC 15

title: Abridge Integrated User Guide
text:
Recording Tips
Let’s review some tips for how to ensure the best audio quality, processing speed, and note
accuracy while recording.
● Never log out of or delete the app. If you’re experiencing an issue with recording or
uploading, reach out to our Support team at help@abridge.com
● Record using a high-speed Wi-Fi connection for the fastest note-generation and smooth
uploads.
● Abridge needs your phone’s microphone. Make sure that you’re not using other apps that
are using your device’s microphone at the same time as recording with Abridge.
● Place your phone in between you and your patient without any obstructions.
● Converse instead of dictate. Abridge processes natural clinician-patient conversation, so
talk to your patient like you normally would.
● Verbally share findings and plans throughout the visit, including during the physical exam.
Be sure to vocalize non-verbal cues such as shrugs and nods.
● Use the pause and resume functionality to include medical terminology before or after a
visit. The more details you can provide, the higher quality note will be produced.
● If you answer a phone call while recording, Abridge will automatically pause the recording.
After you end the call, we recommend that you tap on the Abridge app to bring it back into
the foreground, where you should see the recording resume.
● Don’t use headphones. For telehealth visits, your phone needs to pick up the audio from
your computer's speakers to capture the visit.
Return to TOC 16

title: Abridge Integrated User Guide
text:
Completing Your Abridge Note
With Abridge Integrated, you can seamlessly send your note directly into Epic with just the click of
a buon. Once you complete a patient recording, you can begin verifying your Abridge-generated
note on web.
Follow these simple steps:
1. Navigate to notes.abridge.com on web.
2. Click the patient visit in the sidebar to review the generated clinical note draft. Your most
recent note will always appear at the boom of the list.
3. When finished, click “Send Note” to send your note directly to Epic.
Return to TOC 17

title: Abridge Integrated User Guide
text:
Verifying your note
When verifying your note in the Abridge web editor, you will see 3 main sections:
● Worklist: The left-hand panel is a list of all the conversations you recorded. Your most
recent note will appear at the boom of the list.
● Note Editor: In the center panel, you can view and edit the Abridge-generated note. Edit
your note like a text document.
● Transcript and Linked Evidence: In the right-hand panel, you’ll find the full transcript from
your conversation. Highlight text for corresponding evidence in the transcript.
Return to TOC 18

title: Abridge Integrated User Guide
text:
Linked Evidence
Abridge oers built-in auditability to ensure trust and verification via our Linked Evidence feature.
Linked Evidence helps you view the origin of particular AI summaries so you can see the source of
truth. You can view the corresponding evidence from the transcripts when you highlight text in
your Abridge clinical note.
Return to TOC 19

title: Abridge Integrated User Guide
text:
Patient Visit Summary
Every Abridge-generated clinical note automatically includes a “Patient Visit Summary” with a plan
and instructions for your patient in patient-friendly language.
How it works:
● Click the “Patient Visit Summary” buon to view the summary draft.
● You can verify and edit the summary like a text document.
● When finished, print or copy/paste the summary to share with your patient.

title: Abridge Integrated User Guide
text:
Viewing Your Note Inside Epic
Once you send your note into Epic, you can easily pull the content from Abridge into your patients’
notes in Epic.
Use dotphrases to pull in your Abridge note
Abridge content is pulled into the patient’s note in Epic through Epic SmartLinks. There is one
SmartLink for each note section generated in Abridge. These SmartLinks work the same as other
SmartLinks that you already use in Epic today.
There are dierent ways your Epic templates can be designed:
● If you have a standard template that you use within your department, your project team can
update it to incorporate the Abridge SmartLinks in the correct sections.
● If you have a template that you have personalized for yourself, you can modify that template
and incorporate the Abridge SmartLinks as you please.
● If you do not use templates, you can always pull these SmartLinks in as a one-o to new
notes that you are writing.

text:
Pre-chart in Epic with Abridge
You have the flexibility to start your documentation in Epic before you record with Abridge. Here’s
how:
1. Complete your note in the web editor and click “Send Note” to send it into Epic.
2. Select the “Refresh” icon in the Epic Notes Activity section to pull in the Abridge-generated
content to the appropriate SmartLinks in your template.
Note: Refresh won’t be needed if your template or SmartLinks are inserted after the Abridge note
has been pushed to Epic.

title: Abridge Integrated User Guide
text:
Advanced Recording Features
Now that we’ve covered the basics of recording, let’s review some of our advanced features.
Language, accents, and dialect interpretations
Abridge uses proprietary automatic speech recognition �ASR� to process audio and our AI
performs well across diverse accents, languages, and dialects.
Today, Abridge supports medical conversations in English, Spanish, Chinese (Mandarin), Chinese
(Cantonese), Tagalog, Vietnamese, Arabic, French, Korean, Russian, Haitian Creole, German,
Japanese, Italian, and more, outpuing a fully English note at the end.
In the event that audio has been mistranscribed, the ground truth audio is available for you to refer
back to and ensure that your note captures all critical details.

Multiple speakers per patient visit
Abridge’s AI can predict the speaker, whether it’s a patient, caregiver, or doctor. Abridge works well
in seings for multiple participants, especially with interpreters and caregivers. Everything that’s
captured in the recorded conversation will contribute to the Abridge-generated clinical note.

text:
Feedback
You’re now ready to begin using Abridge! Feedback is our lifeblood. As you start to use Abridge,
we’d love to hear your feedback and thoughts. We use your comments to improve our technology
and the output of your note drafts—and we want you to get the best note possible! There are two

MESSAGE FROM THE

UT Health San Antonio
Information Technology
INFORMATIONAL MESSAGE
**Description:**
Coming Wednesday, October 30 there will be an update to Epic Security for Physicians and Midlevel Providers
**What to expect:**
IT teams at UTHSA are laying the groundwork in UT Epic to facilitate a smoother opening of MSRH. As part of this groundwork, we are standardizing provider security templates that will make inpatient tools more readily accessible come December. This change will also better align individual providers with their specific role and scope of practice.

text:
2
Getting Started
Welcome to Haiku, Epic's mobile app for iPhones and iPod Touch.
Download Haiku
On your device, tap to open the App Store and search for "Epic Haiku". Next to the Epic Haiku app in the
search results, tap and then tap . When prompted, enter the password for your Apple ID.
Log in
On your device, tap the app's icon and enter your user ID and password in the login fields. Tap the label at the
top of the login screen to connect to a different organization or instance.
Tap and hold an item on the screen to see a tooltip with more information on patients,
appointments, In Basket messages, and more.
What is an activity?
Each activity supports a specific task, such as reviewing the chart or e-prescribing medications. You can access
activities from the tabs on the bottom of the screen or by tapping a patient's name from the schedule or
patient list.
When you have a patient chart open, tap and drag the activity bar at the bottom of the
screen to the left to see more activities.
Log out
When you leave Haiku, the app continues to run in the background. For security reasons, Haiku automatically
logs you out after a period of inactivity. However, you can also manually log out. To do so, tap , Options,
and then Log Out.

Find your patients
Find admitted patients
Tap Patients to open your patient lists. You can set a default list back in Hyperspace by right-clicking the list
and clicking Default List. To open a different patient list, tap .
The following icons indicate that a patient has new information to review.
 indicates new abnormal results.
 indicates new critical results.
 indicates an isolation or infection.
 indicates new notes.
To edit a patient list, open the list and tap Edit. To remove a patient from the list, tap the icon and then tap
Delete. To add a patient, tap the + button, search for a patient, and then select the patient. When you are
finished editing the patient list, tap Done.
Find clinical appointments and surgical cases
Tap Schedule to open your schedule. Select a date on the calendar view to see your schedule for that day. To
see schedules for other groups, departments, or colleagues, tap .
The schedule shows each patient's age and sex, as well the appointment type. Appointments are color-coded
and marked (with a dot) using the same colors as in Hyperspace. The rings that appear around the
appointment time indicate the appointment's time and length.
For example, a 15-minute appointment appears like this:
If you're a surgeon and your cases are scheduled in Epic, they also appear on your schedule. Surgical cases
appear like this:
To filter the schedule to only appointments with a certain status, tap and select the statuses you want to
see.

text:

1. Tap the three-dot menu in the top right corner of the Patient List or Schedule.
2. Tap Settings.
 If needed, turn Show additional column to on.
3. Search or scroll available columns and select your desired column.
Find patients in the emergency department
When you log in to Haiku in the ED, the Track Board appears, and you're in the My Pts list.
My Pts shows patients assigned to you with acuity level (by color), location, chief complaint, lab and imaging
status, and wait time. To see more details, such as which labs were done, tap and hold a patient's row.
To see patients who are waiting and assign yourself to a patient:
1. At the top of the list, tap My Pts.
2. From the menu, select Next to See.
3. Swipe left on a patient's name and tap Assign Me.
Find other patients
To find a patient who isn't on your patient list or schedule, tap More in the activity tabs and Search to open
the Patient Search activity. Then search as you normally do in Hyperspace, using the patient's name or MRN,
as well as sex or date of birth, and the results appear with more patient details, such as address.
When you select a patient from a search, any documentation you do in Haiku is linked to the most recent
available encounter. If an encounter is found when you select a patient from a search, a banner appears to let
you know what encounter you’re in. If Haiku can't find a recent encounter for the patient, a new encounter is

text:
available encounter. If an encounter is found when you select a patient from a search, a banner appears to let
you know what encounter you’re in. If Haiku can't find a recent encounter for the patient, a new encounter is
created to store your documentation when you start entering orders or writing a note, and you see a
notification that an encounter was created.
What encounter am I in?
An encounter is automatically selected in Haiku if you select a patient appointment from the schedule or
select an admitted patient from a patient list. To help make sure you’re documenting in the encounter you
expect, such as when entering charges for an office visit or writing a note for the current admission, tap on
the left side of the activity tabs to see what encounter you’re in.
Create a new patient record
To create a new patient record:
1. Search for a patient in one of the following places:
 From Patient Lists, tap Edit, and tap +.
 Tap More, and select Search.

text:
6
Manage In Basket Messages
In the In Basket activity, you can read and respond to many types of messages, including:
 CC'd Charts
 Chart Completion (Cosign Notes and Cosign Orders only)
 Coding and CDI Queries
 Cosign - Clinic Orders
 CRM (Customer Relationship Management)
 Dictate Later
 E-Visit/Video Visit
 Patient Call
 Pt MedAdvc Rq (Patient Medical Advice Request)
 Patient Escalation
 Procedure Prep
 Results
 Rx Request
 Staff Message
You can also create new Staff Messages and MyChart messages to patients and proxies. MyChart
messages are sent as Patient Medical Advice Request messages.
The In Basket folder appears with the number of unread messages. The number is red if any of the unread
messages are high priority. If you don't have any unread messages, no number appears. If you don't have any
messages in that folder at all, the folder is gray.
Prioritize messages
The following icons appear next to messages in a folder to help you prioritize them:
High priority
Low priority
Unread message
Pended message
A message is pended if you’ve opened it and taken an action but haven’t marked the message done
yet.
Overdue message
In Hyperspace, when sending a message, the sender can include an action, such as "Call patient".
The action can also be flagged with a due date and time. If that due date and time has passed, the
message appears as overdue in Hyperspace and the app.
