You are responsible for the message.
Messages with responsibility help recipients track whether someone has started working on a task.
Only the person who has responsibility for a message can mark it as done.
Swipe left on an In Basket message and tap Defer to Workstation to remove the message from your mobile In
Basket. Messages you defer appear in your Hyperspace In Basket, but are hidden from your mobile In Basket.
Work with Staff Messages
1. To create a new Staff Message, from your dashboard or the In Basket activity, tap .
2. Select Compose Staff Message.
3. Write your message and, optionally, add the following flags to your message before sending it:
 flags the recipient to call you.
 flags the message as high priority.
4. Tap Send to send the message.
When you receive a Staff Message, tap to reply or forward the message.
Review results
Tap a result to open it.
The following icons can appear next to Results messages:
The patient has abnormal results.
The patient has critical results.
The green circle indicates that all the patient's orders have been resulted. A number
indicates the total number of resulted orders that you haven't yet reviewed.
Not all orders for this patient have been resulted. A number indicates the total number of
orders that have been resulted that you haven't yet reviewed.
Release results to MyChart
1. In a Results message, tap .
2. Select the results you want to release.
3. Select Note options.
4. Select File to Chart.
5. To add a comment for the patient, tap Compose Note.

Send a reminder to follow up on a result
If you see a result in a Results message that you want to investigate further, you can send yourself a reminder
to do so. The reminder is sent as a Patient Reminder message with the original Results message attached to it.
Note that you can only access the reminder message in your Hyperspace In Basket.
1. In a Results message, tap .
2. Enter any additional text you want to add and tap Send to send the reminder to yourself.
Create a result note
1. In a Results message, tap .
2. Tap the Compose Note field and enter a note for the result.
3. Optionally tap Note Options for the following options:
 If you want to mark the note as Important, select the Important option
 If you want to file your note, select the File to Chart option.
4. Tap Send to send the note.
Refill prescriptions
1. In an Rx Request message, tap a pending medication to review the order details. Tap Rx Request to
return to the message.
 If you need to review the full chart, tap the patient's name.
2. Act on the request:
 Tap Approve to approve all pending medications.
 Edit the order details as needed, and then tap Accept.
 Tap Edit to selectively approve and refuse pending medications or edit the order details.
 Tap a medication to edit the order details and, when you are finished, tap Accept.
 Tap Refuse to refuse a pending medication.

Cosign clinic orders
1. In a Cosign - Clinic Orders message, tap an order to review the order details.
 If you need to review the full chart, tap the patient's name.
2. Act on the request to complete the message and remove it from your In Basket:
 Tap Sign to cosign the orders.
 Tap Decline to decline to provide your cosignature.
 Tap Select to sign or decline individual orders in a single message.
Address Chart Completion tasks
You can act on the following Chart Completion messages in Haiku or Canto:
 In a Cosign Note message, tap Sign to either sign or attest the note. If you need to attest the note, a
field appears to enter your part with the keyboard or speech-to-text.
 In a Cosign Order message for inpatient orders, tap Sign or Decline to take the same action for all

 In a Coding Query message, tap New Note to create a note to respond to the coder's questions.
Complete the note and tap Sign to complete the message.
 Tap Request Clarification to reply to the coder with a question. Tap Send to complete the message.
You can review other types of deficiencies but not act on them. To clear a message that you can't complete
right now, tap and then tap Defer to Workstation.
Respond to patient advice requests

 If you need to review the full chart, tap the patient's name.

 Tap the phone number at the top of the message to call the patient.
 Tap Done to remove the message from your In Basket.
 Tap to mark the message as New or defer it to your workstation to read later.
Manage E-Visit messages
1. Tap the E-Visits folder in your In Basket and select the message you want to review.
2. Review the information in the patient's E-Visit message, including self-triage or questionnaire
responses.
3. If you don't want to take responsibility for the E-Visit message, tap Put Back to return the message to

the patient's allergies and medications, documenting a visit diagnosis, writing progress notes, and

Review patient escalations
When an escalation is sent for a patient who uses MyChart Care Companion (for example, because they report

Message Colleagues with Secure Chat
Read and reply to new messages
When you receive a new Secure Chat message, you get a notification on your device. Tap the notification to
open the conversation and type your reply in the field at the bottom of the screen.
Review all conversations and start new ones
1. Tap Secure Chat to open the Secure Chat activity and see a list of all your conversations.
 The icons next to each message indicate who is participating in the conversation.
 If a conversation is about a patient, that patient's name and, if they're admitted, their location,

Tap a message bubble to see the full list of users who have read it.

Review Patient Information
Review a snapshot of medical information
You can see an overview of the patient's current medical information from the Summary activity, which
appears when you open a patient's chart.
The Current Medications section shows all the patient's outpatient and hospital medications. The following
icons appear in this section:
Long-term medication
Patient-reported medication
If the patient is on any opioids, to see Morphine Equivalent Daily Dosing (MEDD) information, tap the link
below the medication’s name.
Review past encounters
From the Encounters activity, you can review information about previous encounters. Tap an encounter to
review it.
Review documents from outside organizations
Information about external encounters and results appears throughout Haiku. The icon indicates
information from another organization
To see complete documents for encounters and results performed at other organizations, from a patient's
chart, tap Care Everywhere to open the Care Everywhere activity.
 Tap Summaries to review a patient's clinical summary.
 Tap Documents to review a patient's clinical documents.
Documents listed in black text are available to view, while documents listed in gray text
must be requested from Hyperspace before you can view them.
Mark information as reviewed
In the Patient Summary activity, tap Mark as Reviewed to record that you've reviewed the patient
information.

Capture and Review Patient Photos and Media
Update a patient's photo
1. In the patient's chart, tap the patient photo or camera icon in the upper-left corner of the screen.
2. Tap Capture ID Photo and use the camera on your device to take a picture.
3. Tap Use Photo to save the photo to the Demographics activity in the chart.
Capture clinical images
1. Tap the camera icon next to the patient’s photo to open the Media Capture activity.
2. In the Media Capture activity, tap Capture Clinical Image and use the camera on your device to take a
picture.
3. Tap Use Photo, select a document type, enter a description, and rotate the picture if necessary.
4. Tap Save and enter a document type and comment if required to save the media to the chart. You can
review media captures in the Media Manager or the Chart Review activity in Hyperspace.
Review clinical images and media
1. In the patient's chart, tap Media to go to the Media activity.
2. Scroll through the list of media files or, to find a specific media file, search using information such as:
 Document type
 The user who imported the file
 Keywords from the image's description
 The date the file was imported
3. Tap a photo or document to see a full-screen view, where you can zoom in and out or pan around the
image.

Review Results
Review results
After you open the patient's chart, tap Results to go to the Results activity. This activity shows a list of recent
results for the patient. Tap a result to see details.
 For lab tests, a table of lab results appears. Swipe left to see past values for the same lab. You can tap
to see the report view.
 For imaging or EKG results, a narrative report appears.
Tap and hold on a result to see the reference range for that component.

Abnormal result

horizontally.
Each result component appears on the graph in a unique color. To help you match the line color to a particular

Tap the colored circle on the left side of the screen that corresponds to that component's color. The line that
represents that component appears brighter than the other lines. Slide your finger up and down in order to
choose the component you want to bring to the front of the graph.
Focus on one result value

data point to view more information about that value, including the actual result value, the reference range,

15
View and Create Notes and Letters
Tap Notes to see a list of encounter notes. From the list, tap a note you want to review.
Use filters to narrow down the list of notes
To filter the notes you see in the activity, tap Filter and choose a filter category. For example, you might filter
by note type and show only progress notes. Tap Done to apply the filters you've selected.
Create a new note or letter
To write a note or letter, go to Notes Entry. A new note opens automatically. Notes and letters you create are
automatically associated with an encounter in the patient's chart. The encounter associated with the note
appears in gray below the patient header.
 If there are already notes, tap to start a new one.
 Start entering text with the keyboard or tap the microphone on the Nuance or Fluency toolbar to
dictate with speech-to-text.
 To change the note type, tap and then Note Info.
 When you've made your selection, tap Note Details and then Done to return to the note.
 When you're done, tap Sign on Sign Visit. Or, tap to sign or pend the note.
Attach an image to a note
To attach an image while you're writing a note, tap and then tap Add image. After you take the photo, you
can tap Annotate to draw annotations on the image. Tap Save and enter a document type
and description if required to insert the image and return to your note.

Write Orders
To begin, tap to open the Orders activity.
A list of active orders appears. In outpatient visits, the list shows medications. If the patient is admitted or in
the ED, it shows both medications and procedures. If you use a Quick List, tap the list title to switch between
active orders and your Quick List.
You can write most outpatient and inpatient orders from Haiku, but note these
limitations:
 For non-medication orders and inpatient orders, you can only edit indications of
use and answer questions.
 You can't manage your preference list.
If you can't sign an order because details are missing, tap Pend or Save Work and finish
entering the order from a workstation.
Write new orders
1. To enter an order in Haiku:
 Search for an order or browse your preference list by tapping .
 Tap to write a new order for one of the patient's current orders.
2. Tap the orders you want to select and tap Done.

 To print or call in a medication that can't be e-prescribed, select the appropriate Class in the order
details. You'll see a list of orders to call in to the pharmacy after you sign.
 To get a notification when results for an inpatient lab are ready, tap .
 To change pharmacies for a prescription, tap the pharmacy name. You can split prescriptions
between multiple pharmacies if needed.
4. To verify the patient's coverage information or associated an order with a diagnosis, tap .

18
Record a Dictation
Haiku provides a dictation activity for you to record and file dictations to your server, from which they can
later be transcribed. The note is then entered in the patient's chart for you to read in Haiku or Hyperspace.
Record a new dictation
From the patient's chart, tap Dictation.
1. Start a new dictation by tapping the red record button. A graph indicates the volume of your voice as
you record.
2. Tap Pend to save the dictation.
 Tap OK to return to the recording screen in the patient's chart.
 Tap Manage to go to the Dictations activity.
If you access another activity while recording, the dictation pauses. When you return to
the recording screen, you can continue your dictation where you left off.
Open pended dictations
1. From the home screen, tap Dictation. (You might need to tap More to see this button.)
2. Tap on the dictation you want to open.
Edit a dictation
If you are interrupted while recording a dictation or want to re-record some information, you can edit the
dictation.
1. Open the dictation you want to edit. Then, tap and hold the upper-left or upper-right corner of the
recording.
2. Slide the line to the section you want to trim. The section to be removed appears dark green.
3. Tap Trim to remove the dark green section from the recording.
Note that you cannot edit filed dictations.
File or delete a dictation
1. Select the radio button next to any dictations you want to delete or send.
2. Tap Delete or Send. Alternatively, tap Send All to send all pended dictations. The word Sent appears

Document Professional Charges
File a new charge
1. In a patient's chart, tap Charges to open the charge calendar.
2. Select a date for which to file charges and tap Add.
3. On the Add Charges screen, select a charge.
 To use the same details for all the charges you add in this session, tap Defaults.
 Tap Done to select the charge.
4. Tap each charge to add associated diagnoses and enter comments.
 You can select a diagnosis from the patient's problem list, a list of recently used diagnoses, or a
database search that includes your preference list.
 The primary diagnosis has a small blue diamond next to it.
5. Swipe a charge to the left and tap Remove to delete it.
6. Tap File to file the charges. If any charges are missing details, you can complete them before filing.
You can leave the activity at any point to pend the charges you're working on. A reminder
to finish the charges is sent to your in Basket. Pended charges that you enter in Haiku or
Canto are filed automatically 30 days after the service date, even if there are errors.
Copy a charge
1. In a patient's chart, tap Charges to open the charge calendar.
2. Select a date for which to file charges and tap Add.
3. Tap and select a charge from the list.
4. Tap Done. If you need to make small changes, tap to edit the charge.
5. Tap File to file the charge.

Contact Care Team Members
Tap Care Team to see other providers who work with the patient.
Contact previous care team members
1. Tap one of the listed phone numbers to place a call to the care team member directly from your
iPhone. (The phone also appears if you are using an iPod touch, but the button is not active.)
2. Tap the care team member’s address to open a map showing that location.
Note that your phone number will appear on calls you make from your iPhone. The

Conduct a Video Visit
Connect with colleagues
1. Open a patient's chart to the same encounter as the colleague with whom you want to connect and
then tap to open the Telehealth activity.
2. If you are the first one to join the call, tap Start Video Call to begin the video visit. If your colleague has
already joined the call, tap Join Video Call.
While you're on a video call, the Telemed activity takes up the full screen. If you navigate
to a different activity, your video is paused and the patient sees your initials in a circle
instead of a video image until you return to the video visit.
Connect with patients
In the Schedule activity, a video camera icon appears next to the name of a patient who has been scheduled
for a Telehealth visit.
1. Open the patient's chart and tap Telemed to open the Telemed activity
2. To join the call, tap Connect to Video.
While you're on a video call, the Telemed activity takes up the full screen. If you navigate
to a different activity, your video is paused and the patient sees your initials in a circle
instead of a video image until you return to the video visit.

text:
22
View Information in a Push Notification
Open an activity from a push notification
When you're already logged in to Haiku, you can open an activity directly from a notification.
Simply tap the notification to open the related activity. For example, a critical result notification opens the
related message in the In Basket activity.
Review recent notifications
1. Tap More at the bottom of the screen.
2. Tap Notifications to open the Notifications activity.
Choose which push notifications appear
1. In the Notifications activity, tap .
2. To turn off a certain type of notification, slide the button next to that notification type to the left. For
example, to turn off push notifications for staff messages, slide the button next to "Staff messages" to
the left. When you turn off a notification type, the notification still appears in the Notifications activity,
but no alert or banner appears when you receive the notification.
3. To turn off all push notifications, slide the button next to "Push notifications" to the left. This setting
overrides any individual notification settings.
Allow critical notifications
To let certain very important alerts related to patient safety to break through your phone's settings and arrive
with a loud volume, when prompted, accept both prompts to allow urgent notifications to bypass Do Not
Disturb settings.
To manually allow critical notifications, if you denied them at the prompts, from your device home screen,
open the Settings app. Select Haiku and then select Notifications. Enable Allow Critical Alerts. Only device
alerts, such as patient heart rate, are sent as urgent alerts by the app.

title: Look-Alikes Quick Start Guide
text:
2
Overview of Look-Alikes
With the power of Cosmos, a clinician's network is now a lot bigger. You can search the Look-Alikes network
right from your patient’s chart to find other clinicians across the community who have experience caring for
patients similar to the one you're seeing. You can then reach out and collaborate with those colleagues to get
the clinical insights you need to care for your patients.

title: Look-Alikes Quick Start Guide
text:
3
Search for Patients with Known Rare
Conditions
When you see a patient with a condition that’s a good fit for Look-Alikes, you’ll see in the problem list and
in the Storyboard.
The conditions that make the Look-Alikes activity appear automatically are a group of
diagnoses that have been deemed rare based on research and clinician feedback.
1. Click to open the Look-Alikes activity. This will start a Look-Alikes search.
If the patient has more than one rare disease condition, the search will not start
automatically.
2. When the search is complete, you will see a list of clinicians who have seen similar patients.
 The results are sorted by how many patients like yours that they have seen, with local clinicians
moved to the top of the list.
3. Reach out to those clinicians using the contact information provided.
 Search results are also sent to your In Basket, so you can reference these results again later.
4. Click Modify Criteria if there are other unique factors about the patient that should be included in
the search.

title: Look-Alikes Quick Start Guide
text:
4
Searching for a Look-Alike for Patients with
Unknown Rare Conditions
You can also use Look-Alikes for patients whose condition is not known or is not on the list of conditions that
will flag a patient for the Look-Alikes search. Enter relevant symptoms, diagnoses, demographics, or allergies
to find patients similar to yours.
1. Open Look-Alikes.
 To open Look-Alikes for patients when you do not see the icon, search for "look-alike".
 You can also find the Look-Alikes activity in the more activities dropdown menu.
2. Use the Search Conditions field to add your patient's clinically relevant diagnoses.
These conditions come from the Problem List. If a relevant diagnosis is not available, first
update the patient's problem list and then return to this activity.
3. Use the Search Signs and Symptoms field to add your patient's relevant symptoms, related to their
diagnosis or otherwise.
Only symptoms documented using NoteWriter forms will appear here.
4. Use the Demographics section as needed to narrow the criteria further.
5. Use the Allergies section to add the patient's allergies if needed.
6. Click Reset Criteria to start over, if needed.
7. Click Find Providers when you're ready to see results for clinicians with patients like yours.
 By default, this search only includes physicians.
 To expand the search to include advanced practice providers, click next to Find Providers and
select Find Physicians and APPs.
This search may take a few minutes. All results will be sent to your In Basket; you can leave
the activity after you start the search and come back to the results in your In Basket later.

title: Look-Alikes Quick Start Guide
text:
5
Contact Other Clinicians
After you decide which clinician to reach out to about the patient, you can call their office or send an In Basket
message.
1. The phone numbers are listed in the clinician's contact information card, or you can click Send an In
Basket message below their name.
2. If you send an In Basket message, there is a prepopulated template you can use to start the
conversation. Edit this message as needed, and then click Send.

title: Look-Alikes Quick Start Guide
text:
6
Configure Participation Settings
Being part of the Look-Alikes network is always your choice. As part of the network, you can reach out to your
colleagues, and, if you’ve cared for rare patients, your colleagues can reach out to you. You can update your
participation preferences at any time.
1. Click in the upper right-hand corner of the Look-Alikes activity.
2. Click Participate in the Look-Alikes Community in the About Me tab that opens to leave or join the
Look-Alikes network.
You can also access these settings from anywhere in Epic using the About Me activity.
3. Click your user icon in the top-right corner of the screen.
4. Click About Me.
5. In the Look-Alikes Communication section, select Participate in the Look-Alikes Community to opt in
or out of the network at any time.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Overview of Haiku and Canto.pdf
title: Overview of Haiku and Canto
id: file:Shared Documents/Overview of Haiku and Canto.pdf#0
text:
EpicUUID: 3F044700-E43D-4ECE-9C5D-A70874781820Overview of Haiku and Canto
Haiku and Canto, Epic's mobile applications, give clinicians EMR access wherever they are. Clinicians can use
these applications to perform many of the same workflows they also handle in Hyperspace: review a patient's
chart, respond to In Basket messages, prescribe medications, take clinical photos, capture professional charges,
and more. Documentation in these applications is part of the patient's record, so clinicians can switch between
their mobile device and a workstation at their convenience. Haiku runs on iOS and Android smartphones. Canto
runs on iPads.
Limerick, Epic’s Apple Watch application, is an extension of Haiku on iOS. Clinicians who connect their Apple
Watch to their Haiku iPhone can use Limerick to view their schedule, default patient list, an In Basket
overview, and brief patient summaries.
Convenient access to patient information
Patient lists and schedules
In Haiku and Canto, clinicians can access the same schedules and patient lists they see in Hyperspace and search
for patients that don’t appear in these lists. Surgeons can also mark their readiness to begin a procedure and
document case tracking events to update a patient’s status.© 2024 Epic Systems Corporation 1

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Overview of Haiku and Canto.pdf
title: Overview of Haiku and Canto
id: file:Shared Documents/Overview of Haiku and Canto.pdf#1
text:
EpicUUID: 3F044700-E43D-4ECE-9C5D-A70874781820From the Schedule activity, clinicians can see their appointments for the day as well as review schedules for past
and future days, with the same layout they’re familiar with from Hyperspace. From the schedule, they can tap a
patient's name to access that patient's chart and review pertinent information for their visit.
Results Review
To help clinicians stay up to date on a patient’s lab tests and procedures, Haiku and Canto offer quick access to
the Results Review activity, which shows results for EKG, imaging, cultures, and microbiology sorted by their
individual components. Results appear in the app as soon as they’re available, so the clinician doesn’t need to
log in to a workstation to find the latest updates. Abnormal results are highlighted to draw the clinician’s
attention.
In Result Management, clinicians can compose, route, and file result notes in addition to adding patient-facing
comments and releasing results to patients through MyChart.
Care Everywhere reports
Care Everywhere supports sharing patient data between healthcare organizations, including organizations that
use another EHR, to ensure clinicians have access to all relevant details when making decisions about the
patient’s care. If a clinician has previously loaded a document or clinical summary through Care Everywhere in
Hyperspace, they can also access that information through Haiku and Canto.
Media Viewer© 2024 Epic Systems Corporation 2

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Overview of Haiku and Canto.pdf
title: Overview of Haiku and Canto
id: file:Shared Documents/Overview of Haiku and Canto.pdf#2
text:
EpicUUID: 3F044700-E43D-4ECE-9C5D-A70874781820Clinicians can capture and review clinical images and documents, like snapping a photo of a wound or scanning
an insurance card, using their mobile device. The Media Viewer activity supports documents in JPEG, PNG,
TIFF, and PDF formats stored on Epic’s Web BLOB Service (WBS) and in third-party document management
systems.
Epic Monitor
Epic Monitor's Patient Dashboard on mobile devices provides clinicians with an at-a-glance view of a patient's
vitals, recent lab results, current medications, and other important information. The Epic Monitor is typically
shown on a screen mounted beside a patient’s bed, but the portability of Haiku and Canto allows clinicians to
check this information from elsewhere. When treating patients with infectious conditions, they can access the
Patient Dashboard without entering the patient’s room and risking exposure.
Compose notes and update documentation on the go
Notes entry
In Haiku and Canto, clinicians can create notes and letters either by entering them with the keyboard or with
dictation through their device’s built-in microphone. They can work from the same note templates they’re
accustomed to using in Hyperspace and use the same SmartTools. The Dictate Later feature allows linking to an
in-progress note in Hyperspace during a visit or pre-charting, then completing the note later with easy speech-
to-text dictation. After a note is complete, the clinician can share it with the patient through MyChart.© 2024 Epic Systems Corporation 3

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Overview of Haiku and Canto.pdf
title: Overview of Haiku and Canto
id: file:Shared Documents/Overview of Haiku and Canto.pdf#3
text:
EpicUUID: 3F044700-E43D-4ECE-9C5D-A70874781820Chart completion
Working from a mobile device to complete outstanding documentation can be more convenient than using
Hyperspace if a workstation isn’t immediately available. From the In Basket Chart Completion folder, which is
available in both Haiku and Canto, physicians can see all of their Chart Completion messages and act on most of
them, including signing, cosigning, attesting, or declining. Each message shows whether it can be acted upon
from mobile, and clinicians can easily defer those that cannot to a workstation to complete later.
Jot and annotate
Clinicians can use Jot on Canto to create freehand notes or messages to follow up on later, without the need for
pen or paper. Jots are intended to capture thoughts and observations in the moment; they aren’t part of the legal
medical record and are automatically deleted 30 days after their last view or edit.
Communicate with patients and colleagues
Push notifications
Clinicians can see when they receive In Basket messages, new results, and other real-time updates on their
mobile devices and follow up without needing to find a workstation.
Secure Chat© 2024 Epic Systems Corporation 4

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Overview of Haiku and Canto.pdf
title: Overview of Haiku and Canto
id: file:Shared Documents/Overview of Haiku and Canto.pdf#4
text:
EpicUUID: 3F044700-E43D-4ECE-9C5D-A70874781820In Haiku and Canto on iOS, clinicians can use Secure Chat to communicate about patients and share signed
orders or saved work with colleagues. It provides a familiar texting experience for clinicians—including
forwarding messages and using emojis to react—while maintaining the security of patient information, and
doesn’t require opening a separate app.
Epic Voice Assistant
With the help of Hey Epic!, the Epic Voice Assistant, clinicians can quickly retrieve specific pieces of
information that they need before they see a patient. Without touching a screen, mouse, or keyboard, they can
dig into details like the patient’s recent lab results or current medications. Hey Epic! also supports ambient note
writing on iOS so that, with a third-party natural language processing service, physicians can document notes
for an entire visit by simply recording their conversation with the patient.
In Basket and MyChart
Clinicians can manage their In Basket while they’re away from their desk or outside of the clinic using Haiku
and Canto. They can access commonly used folders such as Staff Message, Refill Request, and Cosign Clinic
Orders, and take follow-up actions in addition to composing new messages to colleagues or to patients through
MyChart. For situations that require complex actions, such as making updates in a Hyperspace-only activity,
they can defer a message from their mobile device to follow up later when they have access to a workstation.
Staff Directory
The Staff Directory helps clinicians find any colleague at your organization and see their name, specialties, and© 2024 Epic Systems Corporation 5

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Overview of Haiku and Canto.pdf
title: Overview of Haiku and Canto
id: file:Shared Documents/Overview of Haiku and Canto.pdf#5
text:
EpicUUID: 3F044700-E43D-4ECE-9C5D-A70874781820contact information. Clinicians can use it to call, message, or email colleagues and create an easily accessible
list of favorite contacts.
Third party dialer/VoIP integration
Voice over IP (VoIP) enhances communication workflows by making it easy to place secure phone calls across
your organization even without a cellular plan. Haiku and Canto integrate with third-party VoIP vendors' apps
so that the clinician can tap a colleague’s phone number in Epic to launch the VoIP app and place a call without
using their personal device's cellular data, even if they are in an area with poor cellular service.
Complete simple visits without a workstation
Ordering
Physicians can place and manage orders, panels, and Order Sets using Haiku and Canto. In inpatient contexts,
they have the option to order from their existing preference lists and preconfigured Quick Lists. In outpatient
contexts, they can document clinic-administered and patient-reported medications and can e-prescribe
controlled substances. Physicians can specify an order class and pharmacy to determine how medications are
prescribed.
Express Lanes (Canto only)© 2024 Epic Systems Corporation 6

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Overview of Haiku and Canto.pdf
title: Overview of Haiku and Canto
id: file:Shared Documents/Overview of Haiku and Canto.pdf#6
text:
EpicUUID: 3F044700-E43D-4ECE-9C5D-A70874781820To complete a full visit including diagnoses and patient follow-ups with just a few taps, clinicians can open an
Express Lane in Canto. They can print the After Visit Summary using their iPad without the need for a
workstation or help from front desk staff.
Level of service
To ensure accurate coding, clinicians completing simple visits in Canto can also select an appropriate level of
service from within the app.
Future plans
For more information about current features and future plans, review the Haiku and Canto Upgrade Overview.© 2024 Epic Systems Corporation 7

WHY IS PATIENT
PRIVACY IMPORTANT?
Maintaining privacy and confidentiality
creates a safe space for patients to speak
freely with their healthcare providers; and
can lead to better interactions and
higher-quality care.
Accessing electronic patient information
beyond what is required or permitted for
work-related purposes is unethical and
violates the HIPAA Privacy Rule.
OUR COMMITMENT
UT Health San Antonio will maintain the
privacy and confidentiality of electronic
patient information by monitoring and
auditing electronic health record access as
required by federal law.

Epic users are subject to monitoring
and will be held accountable for any

text:
The Institutional Compliance &
Privacy Office has implemented
a Patient Privacy Monitoring
Program in Epic Accessing PHI in Epic for
Personal Use is Prohibited
Privacy violation examples include:
The following examples of inappropriate Epic
access will be audited and monitored daily:
You access and view your personal lab
results in Epic instead of using MyChart.
You review your parents’ medical records
from their most recent visits in Epic instead
of the MyChart Proxy.
You schedule appointments in Epic for
family members and friends even if it is not
part of your job.
You access Epic because your co-worker’s
birthday is coming up, but you can’t
remember the exact date and want to
send out a card.
You had the same procedure as a friend in
another department and want to compare
your doctor’s notes.
TREATMENT
Access a patient’s record for a treatment-related
purpose. This means that you have a business
purpose relating to the treatment of this patient.
PAYMENT
Access a patient’s record for payment-related
activities like obtaining reimbursement for
treatment that has been provided, determining
eligibility for coverage, or some similar payment
activity.
HEALTH CARE OPERATIONS
You are performing a business function as part
of your job that requires access to patient
information, such as: legal, audit, compliance,
business analytics, quality improvement, quality
assessment, or some similar business activity.
EDUCATION
You supervise UT Health San Antonio students
or residents, and it is your job to identify patient
cases for review by your students.
RESEARCH
You have an IRB-approved study, and your
approved study protocol specifically permits you
to use/access this patient information.
UT HEALTH SAN ANTONIO
EMPLOYEES MAY ACCESS
PATIENT INFORMATION FOR
BUSINESS PURPOSES ONLY.

How to Create an Epic Support Service Request in My Service Center
FOR IMMEDIATE/EMERGENCY ASSISTANCE: Contact the Service Desk at 210-450-4800

1. There are various ways to enter a support ticket.
You can call the help desk at 210-450-4800 or
enter a ticket online via Team Dynamix
N/A

with My Service Center, so when you first navigate
to the page you will need to confirm whether or

If you see “Sign In” as shown to the right, you will
need to click “Sign In” and you will either be
automatically signed in or you will need to
complete the 2 Factor Authentication as shown in
steps 3 and 4 below.
However, if you see “your name” as shown in
figure 2 to the right then you are already signed in
to My Service Center and may skip steps 3 and 4
below.
3. Once you click on “Sign In”, you will be presented
with a standard Office 365 window and you select
your UTHSCSA account.

Request Title: Short description of the issue

title: UTHSCSA Wisdom Abstraction Guide
text:
Login information:
1. Environment: PRD Hyperspace
2. Login credentials: Log in with your UTHSA username and password
3. Additional details: <Enter the department for which you will be abstracting patient information>
Create an Abstract Encounter
1. In the menu at the top of the screen, click Encounter.
2. Type the MRN of the patient you are abstracting in the patient look up screen. You may need to use
First Name, Last Name, DOB if referencing Axium MRNs as they are different from Epic’s.
3. Click Create an Encounter.
4. Enter the following information:
• Type: Abstract
• Provider: Provider, Historical
• Department: Enter the Department for which the abstraction applies or Abstraction
(Today).

title: UTHSCSA Wisdom Abstraction Guide
text:
5. Click Accept. This will open the patient’s chart to the Chart Review activity.
• notice that any past encounters for the patient within the last 5 years will appear.
6. Click the Rooming navigator tab to begin abstraction
Abstract Allergies
1. Open the Allergies/Contraindications section
2. If the patient has no allergies, select the No Known Allergies check box.
3. To add an allergy, click on the pink Allergies/Contraindications header.
4. Type in the allergy and press Enter or click Add.

title: UTHSCSA Wisdom Abstraction Guide
text:
5. Select the appropriate allergy from the list and click Accept.
6. Enter a Reaction and a Severity if you have this information.
7. Click Accept.
• If severity is not entered, a warning of Not Specified will appear for the allergy. This is okay.
Abstract Medications
1. Find the Medication Review section. Click the purple banner if you see the pencil as seen in the
screenshot.
2. Search for the medication you are looking for.
3. Edit the Medication details from the details in your legacy system.

title: UTHSCSA Wisdom Abstraction Guide
text:
4. Click Accept when complete.
Abstract History
All history can be added or modified from the History navigator section. The section is broken into
subsections based on the type of history you’re editing. Common historical items are listed based on the
specialty you’re logged into.
Medical History
1. Dental History is the first subsection within the History navigator. Mark pertinent positives or
negatives using the +/- buttons next to the item.

title: UTHSCSA Wisdom Abstraction Guide
text:
2. Medical History is the second subsection within the History navigator. Mark pertinent positives or
negatives using the +/- buttons next to the item.
2. To add additional details, under Past Medical History, double click a diagnosis to add a comment or
date.
Surgical History
Surgical History appears next and functions the same way as Medical History.
Family History
Family History is set up in a grid format to more easily document history across patient relationships.

title: UTHSCSA Wisdom Abstraction Guide
text:
1. To add a problem that is listed, click the cell that corresponds the correct problem to the
appropriate relative.
a. EXAMPLE: In the example below, we’re adding a Problem of Asthma for the patient’s Father.
2. To add a Problem that isn’t listed, single click on the icon for any listed relative.
3. You can also indicate ‘No Known Problems’ for a given relationship if appropriate.

title: UTHSCSA Wisdom Abstraction Guide
text:
4. To indicate negative Family History for a given problem across all relationships, use the Negative
History line at the very bottom of the Relationships.
5. Note: you can switch between formats by clicking one of the options on the top right side of the
activity.
(If Needed) Update the Patient’s PCP and Care Team
1. In Search bar at the top of the chart search for Care Teams.
2. Search for the patient’s PCP
3. Alternatively, Free Text the external provider PCP name if you cannot find it in Epic.
4. Use Add Team Member to add any specialists to the patient’s Care Team

title: UTHSCSA Wisdom Abstraction Guide
text:

1. Click Sign Visit in the Visit Taskbar (lower right) to close the encounter.

title: Specimen Processing - Receive Specimens
text:
2
Record that a specimen has arrived at the lab
1. Open the Receiving activity.
2. Scan the label for each specimen you are receiving into the lab.
 The collection information entered by other staff appears, and the specimen is automatically
marked as received.
 The tests for the specimens you received now appear on the Outstanding List.
Update collection information
1. Scan the specimen and review the collection details.
2. Enter the missing information.
 You can use the speed buttons on the right to quickly enter missing information where appropriate.
Fields that are required are marked with a .
3. Click Receive.
See expected and recently received specimens
1. In the Receiving activity, select the view you want to open: Recent or Expected.
a. The Recent view shows all specimens received in the last hour.
b. The Expected view shows all collected specimens that are accessioned into your lab.
2. Click a column header to sort the specimens as appropriate. For example, clicking the Patient column
header will sort specimens in your view by the patient's name.
Cancel or redraw a specimen
1. In the Receiving activity, find and select the specimen that needs to be cancelled or redrawn.
2. Click to see the actions you can take on this specimen.
3. Click Cancel or Redraw as appropriate.
a. Cancel a test if it is no longer needed or was entered in error. For example, this may be the case if
the wrong order was released.
b. Redraw a specimen if the original is unusable. For example, this may be the case if the specimen
was contaminated or spilled in transit.

summary link or Collect All to enter collection information manually instead.

Update Collection Information During
Specimen Collection
Follow these steps to update collection information, such as the container type while collecting a specimen:
1. Use the Collection activity to print specimen labels and click Collect All.
2. Click the specimen ID above the collection date and time to launch Specimen Update.
3. From here, you can review and update collection information, including but not limited to the
collection date and time, the specimen type, and the container type.
4. Click the magnifying glass for the field you need to update, and select the appropriate option.
5. When you are ready to move on, click Accept.
 When you click Accept, the Specimen Update activity closes and you return to
the Collection activity.
6. Complete the collection workflow as usual.
This workflow is primarily intended for specimens collected for walk-in patients.

Follow these steps to update specimen collection, such as the container type after completing specimen
collection:
1. Use the button on your toolbar or the Epic menu search to launch Specimen Update.

 Click Expanded Search to use additional criteria for your search, including patient name, order
number, submitter information, and more.

collection date and time, the specimen type, and the container type.
5. Click the magnifying glass for the field you need to update, and select the appropriate option.
6. Click Accept.

Take responsibility for a patient
Taking responsibility for a patient means that you are assigned to the patient and plan to perform the draw.
Patients you take responsibility for do not appear on the draw lists of other phlebotomists.
To take responsibility for a patient, follow these steps:
1. Select the appropriate draw list.
2. Find the patient and tap the circle next to their name.
You can see patients that other users are responsible for by selecting Show Taken.
Print labels and collect a specimen
1. Right before you enter the patient's room to collect the specimen(s), tap the patient's name on the
draw list to open their chart.
2. Review the tubes needed and any active allergies, isolations, infections, and more.
3. Enter the room.
4. Tap Collection Sequence to view details about the order(s) that need(s) to be collected.
5. Answer collection questions, if any.
6. Scan the patient's wristband label to print labels and complete the first step of positive patient
identification (PPID).
7. If needed, you can:
a. Tap Skip to skip collecting an order at this time. You can tap Collect to bring the order back to
collection.

Create and accession a case from Order Inquiry
1. In Order Inquiry, select the order(s) to include in the case.

 If a case already exists, you can instead add the specimen to it by selecting Existing Case and
entering the case number.

Create and accession a case for an OR or radiology
specimen
1. In Case Receiving, scan the specimen barcode. Then, click Case Builder on the Case Receiving
toolbar.
 A case type and ID are assigned automatically.
 Collection information that was entered during surgery appears in the Specimen table, including
whether the specimen is frozen.
To increase the case ID number, click next to the Case number field. The ID advances
to the next available number. To return to the original number, click .
2. Review the default specimen protocols and tasks. Add any additional protocols if necessary.
3. When you are done, click Accept to accession the case and close the Case Builder activity.
Add specimen and task protocols to a case
To add tasks to multiple blocks, click the blocks icons and search for the task in the Add
Tasks to... field.

If the case hasn't yet been accepted, deleting an item completely removes it from the case.
If the case has already been accepted, the deleted item appears with a line through it to indicate that it

To see deleted tasks, click Show Deleted. If you deleted an item in error, select it and
click Restore.
 To delete an entire specimen, along with all of its blocks and tasks, select the specimen and click
Delete.
 To delete a block and all tasks on the block, click X to the right of the block you'd like to delete.
 To delete a task, click X to the right of the task you would like to delete.
Document an intraoperative consultation

Enter results for an abnormal Pap smear
1. In the Outstanding List, select the case you'd like to result and click in the resulting pane.

Sign out a normal Pap smear
Verifying results releases the results to the patient's chart and sends the results to the provider.
There are several verification options available when you click the arrow next to Verify:
Final Verify Releases results to the patient's chart and sends the results to the patient's
primary care provider.
Prelim Verify Sends results to the patient's chart with a preliminary status.
Pend Final Indicates to a supervisor that final results are ready to be reviewed.

If you click the Verify button directly, the system assumes you want to final verify the case. To sign out the
case, you must final verify it.
If you attempt to verify a case that requires review from a pathologist or has been selected
for rescreening, a verification failure message appears. Click OK. The case advances
automatically to the next status and is removed from your work list.

If the case hasn't yet been accepted, deleting an item completely removes it from the case.
If the case has already been accepted, the deleted item appears with a line through it to indicate that it
doesn't need to be processed or performed and that charges won't be filed for it.
To see deleted tasks, click Show Deleted. If you deleted an item in error, select it and
click Restore.
 To delete an entire specimen, along with all of its blocks and tasks, select the specimen and click
Delete.
 To delete a block and all tasks on the block, click X to the right of the block you'd like to delete.
 To delete a task, click X to the right of the task you would like to delete.

1. In Case Builder, click the Grossing tab.
2. Scan the specimen label to load the blocks.
When you add a block to a specimen, the newly created block has the same tasks as the
most recently created block.
3. Scan the specimen label again or click Print New to print labels for any blocks that need them.
4. Scan each block to mark it as confirmed.
 After a block is scanned for confirmation, if necessary, continue to scan the block to record the
piece count.
 For example, if you need to increase the piece count for block A1 by two, scan A1's label two times.

text:
4
Copy a provider on the patient's results
Use the CC List window to specify result recipients for all of the orders associated with a specimen. You can
specify individuals, or use the modifiers at the bottom of the window to include specific types of recipients,
such as pools, classes, or submitters.
Pools and classes are used to send messages to groups of people. A class message is just
an individual message that is sent to the group. Each class member receives their own
copy. A pool message is a single message that is shared by everyone in the group.
Essentially, it is a task message. When a pool member acts on the message, it is marked
as Done and is removed from the pool members' In Baskets.
1. In the Case Builder, click CC Results on the activity toolbar or in the actions menu.
2. Choose to whom to send the results.
 To send results to a specific submitter, click Submitter and use the search field to search by name.
 To send results to a specific group, click In Basket Class and enter the team, pool, etc.
 To send results to a specific user, click Free Text Recipient and enter that person's contact
information.
3. Click Accept. The recipients you entered receive an In Basket message with a copy of the results
from that case.

text:
2
Create requisitions for paper orders from a submitter
1. Open Requisition Entry.
2. In the Submitter field, enter the organization submitting the specimens.
3. Search for and select your patient, and confirm their demographics information.
a. If you need to update a patient's demographic information, click Edit.
b. When you are ready to save your changes, click Update and then select Update
Selected Demographics to confirm.
4. Enter the authorizing and ordering provider.
a. If the order was authorized and placed by two different providers, click Split to create
two separate provider fields.
b. If a provider is not in the system, click and search for the provider. If the provider is
not found, enter their information and click New.
5. In the Orders section, enter the diagnosis code in the Add a diagnosis field.
a. If the requisition is from a toxicology submitter, enter a Reason instead of a diagnosis.
6. Enter the procedure(s) being performed.
a. Depending on the procedure, you may be prompted to enter more information, such as specimen
type and specimen source, and answer any required questions.
7. When the form is filled out, click Create Specimens.
8. Enter collection information.
9. When you are ready to receive the specimen(s) in to your lab, click Receive All.
10. If you need to add a recipient to the CC List for this order, click CC Results and add the
recipient.
11. To save your work and create a new requisition, click Accept & New. To save your work and close
Requisition Entry, click Accept.

a. To receive the specimen(s), accept the requisition and start creating a new requisition all in one
click, click Receive, Accept, & New.
b. Note: You must accept the requisition in order to transmit the results.
If you have several requisitions with similar information to enter from the same submitter,
you can set up default values that will carry over from one requisition to the next.
After you fill out the first requisition, click Set Defaults and select the values you want
to carry over. When you're done selecting the default values, click Accept. When you
click Accept & New to save the current requisition and create a new one, the newly
defined default values will automatically be applied to the new requisition.
Create a follow-up task for a requisition
1. In Requisition Entry, click > Add Follow-up Task.
2. In the window that appears, click Add and select the Follow-up Type.
3. Enter the following information:
a. Start and due date/times
b. User assigned to the task (Click Self to assign the task to yourself).
c. Comments explaining the follow-up needed, if appropriate.
4. Click Accept.
Assign a requisition with missing information for
follow-up
1. Open the Follow-up Work List.
2. Go to Views > Missing Requisition Items.
3. Select a requisition to assign.
Use Ctrl+click to select multiple requisitions.
4. Assign the requisition to yourself or to another person.
 To assign the requisition to yourself, click .
 To assign the requisition to another user, click the field next to and enter the person's name.
 If applicable, enter when the assignment starts and when the task is due.

Complete other requisition follow-ups
You can complete requisition follow-ups that do not pertain to missing requisition information directly from
the Follow-up Work List:
1. Open the Follow-up Work List.
2. If applicable, go to Views and select the view that matches your needs.
3. Select the requisition you are looking to complete.
4. Select an appropriate event and enter a comment to explain the resolution of this follow-up.
5. Click Complete.
Create a requisition batch
Use Express Requisition Entry to create a number of requisitions with common information at once. You can
print labels and begin testing before entering any requisition information. You might do this, for example, if
you are preparing for a health fair.
1. Open Express Requisition Entry.
2. Enter the number of requisitions you want to create.
3. Add the submitter as well as the authorizing and ordering provider(s).
4. Add a diagnosis.
5. Enter the procedure being performed, if applicable.
a. Depending on the procedure, you may be prompted to enter more information, such as specimen
type and specimen source.
6. Enter collection information and details about the order, as appropriate.
7. When the form is filled out, choose one of the following options:
a. Click Create Requisitions.
 Requisitions are created.
b. Click Create Specimens
 Requisitions are created and the labels for your specimens print.

Note the Batch ID at the bottom of the screen. You may need this information to enter patient information
after the specimens are collected.
Enter patient information in a requisition batch
1. Open the Requisition Entry Work List.
2. If applicable, go to Views and select the view that matches your needs.
3. Select the batch for which you need to enter patient information and click Req Entry.
4. Enter the patient's name, the specimen source, and the time the specimen was collected.
5. Click Next to accept the current requisition and move to the next requisition in the batch.
6. Enter information for the remaining patients.
7. When you are done, receive the specimens, if appropriate, and accept the requisitions.
Create a requisition for an unregistered patient
1. In Requisition Entry, enter the submitter and the patient's name.
2. Use the Patient Lookup window to enter patient information.
3. Click Find.
4. Click Create & Reg to create the patient record and open the Registration activity.
5. Complete the patient's registration information, including demographics, guarantor accounts, and
coverages, and then click Finish.
6. Enter requisition and collection information, and create the specimen as usual.

Introduction
To help with billing accuracy, laboratory charges are split into two categories:
 Draw charges: The charges for collecting a specimen.
 Draw charges can be shared across multiple specimens and cannot be voided from the lab.
 Test charges: The charges for performing a test.
 Test charges are associated with one individual test and can include multiple chargeable
components.
While draw charges are usually triggered when a specimen is accessioned, test charges can be triggered when
any of the following events occur:
 Specimens are accessioned
 Specimen are received into the lab
 Results are entered
 Results are final verified
The event associated with charge triggering can depend on the test type and whether the
test is sent out or performed in house.

Review and Update Individual Charges
Review charges for a test
1. Use Specimen Inquiry (by Patient) to search for and select a patient.
2. Click the specimen ID for the test you need to review.
 The specimen ID is a hyperlink listed in the Specimens section of Specimen Inquiry.
3. Review the Specimen Tracking section to determine if charges have been triggered for this test.
 From here, you can review when, where and by whom charges were triggered.
4. Review charge details in the Charge Summary section.
5. Click to expand charge details.
 From here, you can review proposed charges, billed charges, charge quantities, the date of service,
and more.
Void charges
From the lab, you can void charges up to 5 days after initial submission or patient discharge. After that, you
must contact your billing department to credit a charge.
Follow these steps to void a charge:
1. Open Specimen Inquiry for the specimen used for the affected test.
2. Review the Charge Summary section.
3. Select the charge to void and click .
4. Enter a reason for voiding the charge.
 Optional: Add a comment to provide additional information.
5. Click Accept to confirm voiding the charge.
6. Confirm that the charge status updated accordingly.
Draw charges cannot be voided from the lab. Contact your billing department if you need
to cancel a draw charge.

Overview of dashboards
Dashboards centralize information you need throughout your day, and are the primary method of reporting
content distribution. Instead of going to multiple screens to run reports, monitor turnaround times and review
lab charges, you can see all this information on your collection of dashboards.
Your default favorite dashboard appears when you log in and toggle to the My Dashboards activity.
You can access other available dashboards by clicking the name of the dashboard, such as Lab Manager -
Home, and selecting another favorited dashboard. If you want to search for additional dashboards, type the
name of the dashboard in the search bar or click Show Catalog to browse the full list.
Favorite dashboards for easy access later. To make a favorited dashboard your default
dashboard, drag it to the top of the list.
Overview of reporting content
Your reports and other reporting content can be accessed through your available dashboards or the Analytics
Catalog.
When you a run a report from a dashboard component, the results are shown directly in that component. You
can take additional action on the results, which is covered in another section of this guide.
The Analytics Catalog is a database of available reports and dashboards that links directly from your
dashboards. You can quickly access your favorite content and search for new content. Run a report from the
Catalog to see the results.
Find and run reports from the Catalog
1. Use the Epic menu search to open the Analytics Catalog.
2. Search for the topic of the report. For example, if you want a report to find lab tests without charges,
type "tests without charges".

Tests Without Charges - All Labs
Summary: Identify gaps in lab charging to ensure your organization receives the lab income it is due. The
report is particularly useful for identifying gaps in charging during go-live. Additionally, a report built from the
same template (Lab Missing Charges Report Template) can generate a Tests Without Charges report for one
lab in particular.
This report shows tests that were verified and do not have associated charges. Tests that frequently appear in

 The test that is missing charges and the associated testing lab

 The requisition ID and hospital account (HAR) ID
Use the lower detail view for the highlighted specimen's Charge Summary to review the missing charges.

Summary: Create a report from this template to help prevent workqueues from being neglected or otherwise

For example, you can see:
 Ignored or neglected workqueues that haven't been accessed or haven't had activities recently.
