title: Lab Supervisor - SlicerDicer
text:
2
Self-Service Reporting
Self-Service Reporting with SlicerDicer
Use SlicerDicer to find data you need to investigate a hunch. You can refine your searches on the fly to better
understand the data. Right in Hyperspace, examine trends, drill down to line-level details, and jump to related
records to follow up.
Access SlicerDicer
1. Chart Search for SlicerDicer.
2. Select a data model.
 If you're unsure which model to select, click for more details.
 If you only have access to one data model, that model will open automatically.
3. If you select the wrong data model, click Start Over in the toolbar to clear the graph and select a new
data model.
SlicerDicer is a great tool but is not the best choice for all reporting needs. SlicerDicer draws
from data that is at least a day old, so you can't use it for real-time reporting, such as acute
care monitoring. In addition, most of the time SlicerDicer can search only discrete data. For
example, SlicerDicer doesn't know a patient has a particular diagnosis if the only place the
diagnosis is documented is in a free text note.
As always, handle patient data with care.
Create a starting population
Every data model has a default base population that you can see in the population section. Use criteria to
further narrow your starting population, filtering on items such as diagnoses, weight, or lab components. You
can add multiple criteria, add sequential or overlapping criteria, and use additional advanced logic on criteria
to get to the data you need.
1. Click Browse to search available criteria.
2. Select a criterion. If you want to learn more about a criterion, click .

title: Lab Supervisor - SlicerDicer
text:
to get to the data you need.
1. Click Browse to search available criteria.
2. Select a criterion. If you want to learn more about a criterion, click .
3. After selecting a criterion, you may need to provide additional details:
 For criteria based on lists of records or category values, like Diagnosis, you need to select a
particular option, like Hypertension. If you don't select an option, the criteria isn't active and
doesn't affect your results.
 For numeric criteria, like patient Weight, you need to choose a range on a slider bar. By default,
SlicerDicer shows patients with any value documented, even beyond the range on the slider bar. If
you click the less than and greater than buttons at the end of the slider bar, SlicerDicer limits the
range to the bar's end points. You can move the stops on the slider bar to further narrow the
range.
 For criteria with no options, like Pregnant?, SlicerDicer automatically finds records that match the
criteria.

title: Lab Supervisor - SlicerDicer
text:
3
 For free text criteria, like Component Result Text in the Lab Specimens and Tests data model, you
need to enter a keyword or phrase for SlicerDicer to search for.
4. To exclude records that match the selected criterion, click and select Exclude.
Remove a criterion by hovering and clicking X.
Click Undo, Redo, or Start Over in the toolbar to fix any mistakes.
Add sequential criteria
This section applies only to some data model. Suppose you're investigating root causes of opioid addictions
and wondering whether having surgery within the last year could be a factor. SlicerDicer can show you the
patients who had a surgery and were subsequently diagnosed with opioid dependence.
1. Add a criterion for the event that occurred first. In this example, filter results by an encounter type of
surgery.
2. Right-click the criterion and select Add Sequential Criterion > Add New Criteria.
3. Select the criterion for the event that occurred second. In this example, select the Diagnosis criterion
and enter opioid dependence.
4. Update the Within field for your use case. In this example, enter 12 months.
If you want to see sequential rates, the workflow for adding the criteria is slightly different than adding
sequential criteria in your main population. For example, suppose you want to see the percentage of patients
who were discharged and had an admission within 30 days.
1. Add a criterion for the event that occurred first. In this example, add the Discharged? criterion.
2. Add a measure for the event you want to see the rate of and verify the Percentage calculation is
selected. In this example, add the Admitted? measure.

title: Lab Supervisor - SlicerDicer
text:
2. Add a measure for the event you want to see the rate of and verify the Percentage calculation is
selected. In this example, add the Admitted? measure.
3. In the right pane, click Make Rate Sequential.
4. In the First section, choose the event that occurred first, which is the Discharged? criterion in this
example.
5. In the And Then section, update the Within options to match the time frame for your use case. In this
example, you would enter 30 and select Days.
Not all criteria track data over time. If a criterion has (Current) at the end of its name, that means it uses only
the most recent value. This has the following implications for SlicerDicer:
 The query date range doesn't apply to these criteria. For example, suppose your session includes only
the MyChart Status (Current) criterion. If you try to use the line graph to see how the number of
patients with an activated MyChart account has changed over time, the line will always be flat because
SlicerDicer uses only patients' current MyChart status.
 Specifying sequential or overlapping criteria doesn't apply to these criteria.
 Using a different date range than the range on the graph doesn't apply to these criteria.
Modify criteria relationships
Use filter linking, overlapping date ranges, and advanced logic to create your report population exactly as you
need to.

title: Lab Supervisor - SlicerDicer
text:
4
 Filter linking requires two or more criteria to be associated with the same event. For example, suppose
you're using the Patients data model and you add the Department criterion for the North Department
and the Encounter Type criterion for office visits.
 If the criteria are linked together, as shown by the , SlicerDicer returns patients who had an
office visit in the North Department.
 If you unlink the criteria, as shown by the , SlicerDicer returns patients who had any type of
encounter in the North Department if they also had an office visit in any department.
 Overlapping date ranges require two criteria to have occurred simultaneously. For example, suppose
you want to find pregnant patients who had a specific procedure. For this report, right-click the
Procedures criterion, select Add Overlapping Criterion > Add New Criteria, and select the Pregnant?
filter. If you don't specify the criteria as overlapping, SlicerDicer returns patients who were pregnant
and had the specified procedure at any time during the query date range, even if, for example, the
pregnancy didn't begin until after the procedure occurred.
Focus on recent data
Suppose you want to find patients who were diagnosed with a condition for the first time in the last year. You
can't simply add a diagnosis criterion and change the date range to be the last year, because that population
would include any patients who had the diagnosis in the last year, regardless of when they were first
diagnosed.
To create a report like this one, use two criteria. In this example, one criterion finds patients who had the

title: Lab Supervisor - SlicerDicer
text:
would include any patients who had the diagnosis in the last year, regardless of when they were first
diagnosed.
To create a report like this one, use two criteria. In this example, one criterion finds patients who had the
diagnosis in the last year, and the other criterion excludes patients diagnosed prior to the last year.
These steps describe this setup in more detail:
1. Click the Dates section. Change the start date to y-1.
2. Add the Diagnosis criterion and select the condition you're interested in.
3. Add a second Diagnosis criterion with the same condition.
4. Right-click the second criterion and select Specify Date Range > Other Range.
5. Change the date range to be between the earliest date you have data and y-1. To find out the earliest
date you have data, enter a very early date, like y-100. SlicerDicer automatically updates the date to
the earliest possible date.
6. Click OK.
7. Right-click the second criterion and select Exclude.
Slice a population to make comparisons
Use slices to split up your population to compare results among subgroups. For example, suppose you use
criteria to narrow your starting population to patients with an active MyChart account. You could then slice
this population by county to see which counties have the most MyChart users.
When you add slices, you can grab the top or bottom slices, such as the 10 counties with the most MyChart
users. You can also enter specific slices, such as to compare the number of users in Dane, Jefferson, and Dodge
counties.
1. Click next to Slices to add a slice.
2. Select the appropriate filter.

title: Lab Supervisor - SlicerDicer
text:
users. You can also enter specific slices, such as to compare the number of users in Dane, Jefferson, and Dodge
counties.
1. Click next to Slices to add a slice.
2. Select the appropriate filter.
3. Click the magnifying glass to select specific slices. Alternatively, click to select the top or bottom
slices.

title: Lab Supervisor - SlicerDicer
text:
5
4. If you have similar slices you want to group together, select the check boxes next to those slices and
click Group.
Add a measure
Use measures to change how you're measuring your population. By default, SlicerDicer shows the number of
records that match the criteria you've specified. You can use measures to change this to show rates or other
metrics. Not all filters have the same measures available.
1. Click next to Measures.
2. Select a measure. Using patient weight as an example, these measures have the following definitions:
 Percentage: The percentage of patients who are the specified weight and match the other criteria.
If a measure has multiple values documented during the query date range, the percentage
calculation uses all values documented instead of only the most recent.
 Maximum: The greatest weight of any patient who matches the other criteria.
 Minimum: The lowest weight of any patient who matches the other criteria.
 Average: The mean weight of the patients who match the other criteria.
 Deviation: The standard deviation from the mean weight of the patients who match the other
criteria.
 Variance: The deviation squared, which is also equal to the total difference between each patient's
most recent weight and the average weight of the patients who match the other criteria.
 Median: The midpoint weight of the patients who match the other criteria.
 Percentile: The weight for which a specified percentage of the patients who match the other
criteria is below.
3. Select a criterion.
4. Hover over results on the graph to view values for any measures you've added.

title: Lab Supervisor - SlicerDicer
text:
 Percentile: The weight for which a specified percentage of the patients who match the other
criteria is below.
3. Select a criterion.
4. Hover over results on the graph to view values for any measures you've added.
If a filter doesn't contain the measure you need, click Create New Formula to create a
new measure on the fly.
Change visualization options
Visual Options control how your data is represented. Change elements like the graph type, measures, or colors
to aid your analysis of the data.
1. In the Visual Options section, choose a visualization type.
a. See Change the graph type for an explanation of the different types.
2. Configure additional display options, such as measure used for bar heights, measure used for y-axis on
a line graph, and colors.
Pick the right visualization for your analysis
You can change the graph type to better suit your data visualization. For example, click to view a line
graph. Available graphs are listed under Visual Options.
If you're not sure which graph type is best for your data, use this section as a quick reference:
 Vertical bar graph

title: Lab Supervisor - SlicerDicer
text:
6
 Compare different values and see differences at a glance.
 Horizontal bar graph
 Shows the same information as the vertical bar graph.
 Shows crowded axis labels more clearly.
 Line graph
 See how results change over time.
 Remember to change the date summary level by clicking the Dates section.
 Tree map
 Group hierarchical data together.
 Use the whole area of the graph to show shapes more clearly than bar graphs, such as when you
have multiple levels of slices.
 Note that it's harder to compare area than it is to compare height and length, so it can be more
difficult to spot differences between two values than when using a bar graph.
 Map visualization
 Break down results by patient ZIP Code. The map always uses the patient's address, not other
addresses like clinic location.
 See if geographic area is correlated with your results.
 Note that maps aren't available for every data model or at every organization.
 Detail table
 View summarized details about your results.
 View line-level details for records associated with your account.
 View line-level details for all records if you have proper security.
 Export results to Excel for further analysis.
 In some data models, you can take actions like opening a patient chart or surgery preference card.
Take action on line-level detail
1. In the Visual Options section, select the detail table. The table includes some basic information about
each record in your population, as well as the measures you added. If you have the right security, click
a header to expand it to see line-level details.

title: Lab Supervisor - SlicerDicer
text:
each record in your population, as well as the measures you added. If you have the right security, click
a header to expand it to see line-level details.
2. From this view, you can also:
 Add additional columns after you expand a header. Click at the top of the table.
 Remove columns. Right-click the column header and select Remove.
 Rearrange columns. Click and drag a column to move it.
 Sort results by clicking a column header.
 Export the details to Excel for further analysis. Right-click and select Export Patients to Excel.
See populations on a map
Use the geographic visualization to investigate whether patient data correlates geographically by ZIP Code.
Darker areas on the map have a greater number of patients who meet the criteria you specify (or a higher
amount of whatever metric you're measuring). Just like with any SlicerDicer population, keep in mind that the
map shows data only for patients seen by your organization.

title: Lab Supervisor - SlicerDicer
text:
7
The map in SlicerDicer is always based on patient ZIP Code, regardless of what data model you're using. For
example, in the ED Encounters data model, the colors on the map correspond to where patients live, not to
where the ED visits occurred.
1. Click the globe to open the map.
2. Hover over a ZIP Code to see more details about the population, like the raw count or percentage of
patients in that ZIP Code who meet the criteria you specified.
3. To analyze data on the map:
 Pan around the map or zoom in or out to see if there are similar patterns in other areas.
 Click the magnifying glass and then enter a ZIP Code to center the map on that ZIP Code.
Change the active date range
Some data models have more than one relevant date for the query date range. For example, the ED
Encounters data model can show results based on the ED encounter date, arrival date, or departure date. To
change the date range used for your session:
1. Click the Dates section.
2. Select a new Based On option.
Save and share populations
You can save a population if you use it frequently and might want to revisit it later.
1. On the toolbar, click Save As and give the session a name.
2. Review and change additional information as needed, such as the date range, and click Create Session.
You can add the session to a group to organize your Load screen.
See and edit saved populations
1. On the toolbar, click Load and select the desired population.
2. Modify the population as needed and save changes.

title: Lab Supervisor - SlicerDicer
text:
You can add the session to a group to organize your Load screen.
See and edit saved populations
1. On the toolbar, click Load and select the desired population.
2. Modify the population as needed and save changes.
Share a population
1. On the toolbar, click Share. Note that sharing automatically saves your session.
2. Enter a name and select whether you want to share the session with everyone or specific people. If you
choose to share with specific people, enter each user you want to give access to the session.
3. Review and change additional information as needed, and then click Save and Share.

title: Lab Supervisor - SlicerDicer
text:
8
Explore Beaker Data with Slicer Dicer
Use SlicerDicer to create reports about Lab Data. You don't need to understand the underlying data structures
or work with your reporting team to create the report. Instead, you can build a report from scratch in minutes
in SlicerDicer.
The most important thing to remember about SlicerDicer is that the data is at least a day old. SlicerDicer isn't
an appropriate tool for reports that require real-time data.
This section walks you through creating an example report in SlicerDicer. It covers some of the key features
you'll use to create reports. Keep in mind that the data at your organization won't match the data in this
example.
In this example, imagine you're a pathologist. You're working on a case and want to identify past cases that
share similar specimens and patient demographics. You decide to use SlicerDicer to identify a group of these
cases to investigate further.
Create Your Base Population
First, select a data model and add filters so that SlicerDicer includes only the cases that meet your criteria. In
this scenario, you want to see cases with similar specimens and observations.
1. Open SlicerDicer and select the Lab Specimens and Tests data model.
2. Check the default date range. By default, the last 6 months of specimens are included, which is a good
sample size for this report. If you needed to adjust the date range, look at the Dates section to explore
your options.
3. Narrow the population by adding a criterion to your population.
 You want to investigate all specimens from cases that led to a final diagnosis containing the word
"malignant".

title: Lab Supervisor - SlicerDicer
text:
your options.
3. Narrow the population by adding a criterion to your population.
 You want to investigate all specimens from cases that led to a final diagnosis containing the word
"malignant".
 The criterion looking for a specific word, such as malignant, within a certain component, such as
the final diagnosis, is called Component Result Text.
 If you prefer to browse for criteria instead of typing what you're looking for, you can click Browse
and select Component Result Text.
4. Enter the keyword you want to search for in the field. For example, to find specimens that include the
word "malignant" in their results, type malignant.
 You can also search for a phrase by enclosing it in quotation marks.
5. Next, select a component to limit your search to. Since you want to focus on specimens containing the
keyword in the final diagnosis text, search "final diagnosis" or click to select it from a list of
components.

title: Lab Supervisor - SlicerDicer
text:
9
Add a slice
Next, break up your population into different slices to hone in on related cases. In this scenario, you want see
what specimen sources are most common for specimens with results including your keyword.
1. Add a slice and click Specimen, and then select the Specimen Source criterion.
2. Click Grab Top 10, which breaks up the population by the ten most common sources.
 You could also type a specimen source to return only specimens with sources that exactly match
your patient's.
 If you have similar sources that you want to consider together, select the check boxes next to those
procedures and click Group. Enter a name for the group to help you remember what it includes.
For example, you might group specimen sources of Breast, Left and Breast, Right into one source
and name it Breast.
 If there are slices you don't want to include on the graph, click next to the slice you want to
remove.
3. In the Visual Options section, select the Tree Map, which is helpful for visualizing volume.
4. Suppose you want to further investigate specimens from the same source as your patient, whose
specimen was collected from the cervix. Right-click the Cervix specimen source and choose Slice to add
another slice.
5. Click Patient or Testing Source and then Age at Collection to divide the specimens by patient age.
Choose a measure
Add measures to your data help make more meaningful comparisons. In this example, measures can show
general trends for the kinds of specimens you're looking at, helping you determine whether your patient
might be an outlier.

title: Lab Supervisor - SlicerDicer
text:
Choose a measure
Add measures to your data help make more meaningful comparisons. In this example, measures can show
general trends for the kinds of specimens you're looking at, helping you determine whether your patient
might be an outlier.
If you want to see a count of tests and cases, similar to what appears on the lab Outstanding List, you can add
a count measure for your data:
1. Click the purple plus sign in the Measures section and search for Distinct Count of Cases and Tests.
 If you want to learn more about a filter, slice, or measure, click the information button.
2. Select the calculation method that best matches your needs.
3. A green Update top slices? bar appears in the Slices section under the header, because the top ten
results have now changed to reflect your new measure. Click this bar to show the updated top ten
results.
Take Action on Line-Level Detail
Now that you've narrowed your population down to the specimens most similar to those in the case you are
investigating, you can use your report as a jumping-off point to dive deeper into past cases.

title: Lab Supervisor - SlicerDicer
text:
10
1. In the Visual Options section, select the detail table. The table includes some basic information about
each specimen, broken down into the age slices you added earlier.
2. Expand the Age at Collection category your patient fits into to see all the specimens that share a result
keyword and age of collection with your patient's.
3. Right-click a specimen. From the menu, you can jump into Inquiry to learn more about the specimen or
jump to the patient chart to see additional background information about a case, which might give you
insight into your current patient.
4. From this view, you can also:
 Add additional columns. Click the at the top of the table.
 Remove columns. Right-click a column header and select Remove.
 Rearrange columns. Click and drag a column to move it.
 Sort results by clicking a column header.
 Export the details to Excel for further analysis. Right-click and select Export to Excel.

Add a setup task to the list
1. Open the Setup Bench. Select a test in the left table to see the setup tasks associated with it.

Document your plating tasks
When all your setup tasks are done, you need to confirm that you completed them. The growth timer starts
when you confirm your tasks.
After you click Confirm, you cannot undo it.
1. With your test selected in the Setup Bench, verify that you've completed all of the tasks listed. Add any
additional tasks to the list, if necessary.
2. Select the tests you completed and confirm them. The test falls off the work list and labels print.
a. If you completed all of the tasks, click Select All & Confirm. The Date and Time fields automatically
populate with "Today" and "Now".
b. If you completed some default tasks but not others, select tasks you completed and then click
Confirm. "Today" and "Now" are applied to the tasks you confirmed.
c. If you need to edit the date and time for a task, select it, edit the dates and times as necessary, and
then click Confirm. The updated time and date are applied to the tasks you confirmed.
Report the results of a Gram stain
1. From your Outstanding List, find the specimen on which you are performing the Gram stain.
Click CTRL+F to search the Outstanding List.
2. Bring the test into Edit Mode.
3. Use the Quantity and Description fields to record the results of the Gram stain.

Results Entered in Error
Update non-verified results
Follow these steps to remove results that were entered in error and have not been verified yet.
1. Use the button on your toolbar or the Epic menu search to launch the Outstanding List.
2. Search for and select the affected patient’s test.
3. Click to open the case in Edit Mode.
4. Delete the incorrect results.
 Optionally, leave a comment that the original information was entered in error.
5. Click to save the results.
Update verified results
Follow these steps to remove results that were entered in error and have been verified.
1. Open the Outstanding List, search for and select the affected patient’s case.
2. From the resulting pane, click the Amendment button.
3. Enter an amendment reason, such as Corrected result due to user error, and click Confirm
Amendment.
4. Click to open the case in edit mode.
5. Update the incorrect results.
6. In the Correction History component, enter a comment identifying the change that you made, such as,
“Corrected the Final Diagnosis, which previously said liver cancer was present.”
7. If results were entered on the wrong patient, be sure to do the following:
a. Delete all result component values.
b. In the Correction History component, enter a comment such as, “Removing results that were
entered on the wrong patient.”
c. Cancel the test if it was ordered on the wrong patient.
8. Click to save the results.
9. Click Verify.
10. Click Confirm Final. The system automatically retriggers Beaker results routing to send an updated
result report to all recipients of the earlier, incorrect report.

title: Pathologist - Manual Chart Correction
text:
4
Scan on Incorrect Patient or Test
Update non-verified scan
Follow these steps to update a scan that was entered in error and has not been verified yet.
1. Use the button on your toolbar or the Epic menu search to launch the Outstanding List.
2. Search for and select the affected patient’s test.
3. Click to open the case in Edit Mode.
4. In the Attached Documents section of the resulting pane, click the delete icon next to the image that
you want to remove. The scan is permanently removed from the case.
5. Click to save.
Update verified scan
Follow these steps to update a scan that was entered in error and has been verified.
1. Open the Outstanding List, search for and select the affected patient’s case.
2. From the resulting pane, click the Amendment button.
3. Enter an amendment reason, such as Other with a comment explaining that the wrong scan was
reported to the chart, and click Confirm Amendment.
4. Click to open the case in edit mode.
5. In the Attached Documents section of the result pane, click Internal.
6. In the Correction History component, enter a comment explaining the change, such as, "Removed a
scan that was incorrectly reported." Click the save icon.
7. Click Verify.
8. Click Confirm Final. The system automatically retriggers Beaker results routing to send an updated
result report to all recipients of the earlier, incorrect report.
Note that you can't remove a previously verified scan from an order. You can only suppress the scan at
verification. This behavior ensures that the scan is always available for selection during a future verification.

title: Pathologist - Manual Chart Correction
text:
5
Report Chart Errors and Duplicate Patients
Alert data integrity staff to potential chart errors
When you notice inconsistencies or potential errors in a patient's chart that you can't fix by yourself, create a
Help Desk ticket to report the charting error. This request helps the data integrity team promptly respond to
potential patient care concerns.
If you are able to correct the error, you should perform the correction yourself without
filling out the request form.
1. Click the Help Desk icon ( ) in the upper-right corner of the screen next to the Log out button.
2. Choose a type of Chart Correction Request.
3. Fill out the fields with the appropriate information:
 Subject: Chart Correction
 Priority: High
 Phone number: A number where you can be reached
 Patient: The patient affected by the error
 Type of problem: The type of chart correction issue found
4. In the comment field, explain the nature of the charting error and what needs to be resolved.
5. Click Send. An In Basket message is sent to the data integrity analysts, notifying them of the charting
error. An analyst will follow up with you for more information if necessary.
Alert data integrity staff that patients need to be
merged
There might be times when you suspect a patient has a duplicate record in the system. For example, if you find
two patients with the same name and birthdate, with similar Social Security numbers, it's possible that
hospital staff accidentally created a new record when the patient already had a record. By marking the two

title: Pathologist - Manual Chart Correction
text:
two patients with the same name and birthdate, with similar Social Security numbers, it's possible that
hospital staff accidentally created a new record when the patient already had a record. By marking the two
records for a patient merge, you can report this information to the HIM department and let them know they
should investigate whether to combine the records.
1. Search for "Mark Patients for Merge" in Chart Search.
2. Enter the name of one of the patients whose record you think is duplicated.
3. Click Find Patient and select the patient's name in the search results.
4. Enter the name of the other patient whose record you think is duplicated.
5. Select the values in either patient column that you think are likely to be correct.
6. In the Reason field, select the reason that you think the two patient records should be merged.
7. To send more detailed information to HIM staff, enter any additional information in the Comment
field.
8. Click Mark for Merge to send the patient information to HIM Staff.

Report Chart Errors and Duplicate Patients
Alert data integrity staff to potential chart errors
When you notice inconsistencies or potential errors in a patient's chart that you can't fix by yourself, create a
Help Desk ticket to report the charting error. This request helps the data integrity team promptly respond to
potential patient care concerns.
If you are able to correct the error, you should perform the correction yourself without
filling out the request form.
1. Click the Help Desk icon ( ) in the upper-right corner of the screen next to the Log out button.
2. Choose a type of Chart Correction Request.
3. Fill out the fields with the appropriate information:
 Subject: Chart Correction
 Priority: High
 Phone number: A number where you can be reached
 Patient: The patient affected by the error
 Type of problem: The type of chart correction issue found
4. In the comment field, explain the nature of the charting error and what needs to be resolved.
5. Click Send. An In Basket message is sent to the data integrity analysts, notifying them of the charting
error. An analyst will follow up with you for more information if necessary.
Alert data integrity staff that patients need to be
merged
There might be times when you suspect a patient has a duplicate record in the system. For example, if you find
two patients with the same name and birthdate, with similar Social Security numbers, it's possible that
hospital staff accidentally created a new record when the patient already had a record. By marking the two

title: Pathologist - User Settings
text:
2
User Settings Checklist
Use this guide as a companion during User Settings Labs and beyond. User settings allow you to configure the
system to work for you. For example, you can change the way information appears, create custom Smart
Phrases, and make it easier to find commonly-used activities. The end goal is to allow you to spend less time in
the system and more time working. Work through this document and consult the user settings lab facilitator if
you get stuck.
Personalization will continue after go-live, as you identify trends in the tools you use most often.
User Settings Priorities
During User Settings Labs, start with the Pre-Live section. Focus first on:
 Setting default activity views
 Creating and customizing SmartPhrases
If you have additional time, complete the rest of your pre-live user settings topics.

title: Pathologist - User Settings
text:
3
Pre-Live
Set default activity views
Customize your default view for the activities listed below so that you always see the information that's most
important to you first. For example, you might have one Outstanding List view showing cytology orders and
another Outstanding List showing only cases assigned to you. You can choose which view you'll see when you
access the Outstanding List, and the same applies to each of your activities.
1. When you open the activity for the first time, the Report Setting window opens.
 Note: If you already have a default report set, you can find Report Settings by clicking Views
> Settings.
2. Choose the report you want to have as your default and select the My Default report check box.
3. Click Save.
4. Click Run to open the activity and see your new default report.
Create new Outstanding Lists
Create new Outstanding Lists to organize and quickly find your cases. Check with your organization to see if
there's an Outstanding List view that they recommend.
1. From your Outstanding List, click Views > Settings.
2. Select an existing list and click Save as.
3. Name your list. We recommend prefacing the list name with your initials.
4. Click Display to configure which columns appear in your report and where.
a. Click and to rearrange the order of the columns.
b. Select a column from the Selected Columns list and click to remove it from your report.
c. Select a column from the Available Columns list and click to add it to your report.

title: Pathologist - User Settings
text:
b. Select a column from the Selected Columns list and click to remove it from your report.
c. Select a column from the Available Columns list and click to add it to your report.
5. If you want to set your new list as your default you may do so by checking the My Default box in the
bottom left.

title: Pathologist - User Settings
text:
5
SmartTools
Types of SmartTools
SmartTools help you quickly document information. There are four types of SmartTools. Use each one to pull
different information into your document.
SmartTool Use to pull in
SmartTexts Templates or blocks of text
SmartPhrases Long words, phrases, or paragraphs
SmartLists A predefined list of choices
SmartLinks Information from another part of the chart
You can use SmartTools in many places throughout Epic. If you see these buttons, the
field is SmartTool-enabled:
Create a SmartPhrase to reuse text you commonly type
Create a SmartPhrase from text you type
1. While charting, type the text you want to save as a SmartPhrase. Make sure the text doesn't include
any patient-specific information, so you can reuse it for other patients.
 You can create a SmartPhrase anywhere you see this toolbar:
2. Select the text and click .
3. In the SmartPhrase Editor, enter a short, intuitive name for your SmartPhrase. This is the name you'll
type to insert the SmartPhrase in a note.
 You can't include spaces or symbols in the name.
 Tip: Preface the name with your initials so you can find it easily.

title: Pathologist - User Settings

4. Enter a summary of your SmartPhrase in the Description field.
 When you search for your SmartPhrase, this description appears in the results after the
SmartPhrase name.
5. Click Accept to save and close your new SmartPhrase.
6. To use your SmartPhrase in a note or letter, type a period immediately followed by the SmartPhrase
name. Press the Spacebar to insert your SmartPhrase in the note.
Add synonyms in the Synonym field to make your SmartPhrase easier to find. To see how,
refer to Add synonyms to quickly find your SmartPhrases.
Share SmartPhrases
In the SmartPhrase Editor, go to the Sharing field and enter the names of any colleagues who should have
access to your phrase. You can choose to make them Owners by selecting the Can Edit? box
 Owners can use and modify your SmartPhrase.
 Users can use your SmartPhrase, but not modify it.
You can copy the Owners & Users list from one phrase to another. In the Sharing field, click
Copy Users. In the Phrase field, enter the name of a SmartPhrase in which you've already
listed owners or users and click Accept.
Create a SmartPhrase from a SmartText
If you frequently make the same changes to a certain SmartText, save your edited version of the text as a
SmartPhrase.
1. In a note, click to open the SmartPhrase Editor.
2. In the Insert SmartText field, search for the SmartText you want to edit.
3. Edit the text to reflect your preferences.
4. Name your new SmartPhrase and click Accept.

templates

Add a SmartLink to your SmartPhrase to pull in patient-specific information
1. In the location where you want the SmartLink to appear, enter a period followed by the first few letters

STOMACHPAIN.

Add a SmartList to your SmartPhrase
Use SmartLists to select from a list of common choices when writing your note.

1. Click > Personalize Toolbar.
2. In the window that appears, add or remove buttons based on your preferences and click Accept.
Click Restore Defaults to reset your changes.

title: Pathologist - User Settings
text:
10
Post-Live
Run Reports from a Dashboard
Overview of dashboards
Dashboards centralize information you need throughout your day, and are the primary method of reporting
content distribution. Instead of going to multiple screens to run reports, view your schedule, and access your
In Basket messages, you can see all this information on your collection of dashboards.
Your default favorite dashboard appears when you log in and toggle to the My Dashboards activity.
You can access other available dashboards by clicking the name of the dashboard, such as Pathologist
Dashboard, and selecting another favorited dashboard. If you want to search for additional dashboards, type
the name of the dashboard in the search bar or click Show Catalog to browse the full list.
Favorite dashboards for easy access later. To make a favorited dashboard your default
dashboard, drag it to the top of the list.
Toggle between dashboards
The first dashboard you see when you open My Dashboards is your primary dashboard. Depending on your
reporting needs, there might be several dashboards you need to regularly access.
To open a different dashboard, simply click on the current dashboard name and select a new dashboard.
Switch to a favorited dashboard
Your commonly used dashboards should be favorited for easy access. You can favorite individual dashboards
or a group of related dashboards, called redirectors, by clicking the star next to the name.
Search for and switch to a new dashboard
If you need a dashboard that isn't favorited, or simply want to browse the available reporting content, you can
search for dashboards in the Analytics Catalog.
1. Click on the current dashboard name and then Show Catalog.

title: Pathologist - User Settings
text:
If you need a dashboard that isn't favorited, or simply want to browse the available reporting content, you can
search for dashboards in the Analytics Catalog.
1. Click on the current dashboard name and then Show Catalog.
 You may also use Chart Search to open the Analytics Catalog at anytime in your workflow.
2. Enter a search term. Filter results by a content type of Dashboards.
3. Hover over a dashboard and click to view more details about the record.
4. If appropriate, click Open.
 You can also hover over a dashboard and click without viewing the record details.
Plan on needing this dashboard again in the future? Hover and click to favorite a
dashboard for easy access later.

text:
11
Add a report to your dashboard
Your dashboard should give you quick access to all of the reports you commonly run. If a report you run
frequently isn't on your dashboard, you can add it to a Link component.
Add a report to your favorites
1. In the Analytics Catalog, search for the report you want to add to your dashboard.
2. Click next to the report.
3. Return to your dashboard and click > Refresh in the report listing component. The report now
appears in the list.
Add a report to a link component
1. Click and select Component Display.
2. Select Report in the Add item field.
3. Search for a report by topic.
4. Select a report and add the report to the component.
 Drag and drop to move the report to where you want it to appear in the list.
5. Accept again to save your changes.
Modify a report to meet your needs
Before you run a report from your dashboard or from the Catalog, you can modify its existing search criteria,
add new criteria, change its search time frame, and add or remove columns from its results display. You can
then save your changes for future use and make your modified reports available to others.
Modify a report's search criteria
1. To edit a report, open the Report Settings window:
a. Hover over a report on your dashboard, then hover over Ready to run, click the arrow next to
Ready to run, and then click .
b. In the Catalog, hover over a report's name and click Edit.
2. On the Criteria tab, click any criterion to change the search value.

b. In the Catalog, hover over a report's name and click Edit.

3. If you change a report, you can save a private copy so you don't have to make changes each time you
run the report. The copy of the report is available to view and run only by you. Click Save As if you
want to save your changes in a new version of the report. Give your report a name and click Accept.
Then click Run.
If you want to run the report on someone else's patients, click Choose Criteria and

Add criteria to a report's search

3. Click Save As and enter a new name if you want to create a new version of the report, and then click
Run. The report runs and the results include records based on the new criteria.
4. Look for the new report on the Report Listing component of your dashboard.
Search a different range of dates
In some reports, you can set a date range to control the time frame the report searches. Setting a date range
helps limit the number of results.
The date range applies only to criteria that change over time (these criteria are identified by the icon). For
example, if you're searching for your male patients between January 1 and March 1, the date range is ignored
because a patient's sex rarely changes. All of your patients appear in the results. If you add the criterion BMI >
30, the report uses the date range because BMI can change over time. The search results include only male
patients that had a BMI greater than 30 between January 1 and March 1.
1. From the Catalog, hover over a report and click in the upper right.
2. Click the pencil to specify the date range and, in certain reports, the time range.
a. Enter a relative date using one of the following shortcuts: w=week, m=month, mb=beginning of the
month, me=end of the month, or y=year. You can also use an absolute date.

title: Pathologist - User Settings
text:
a. Enter a relative date using one of the following shortcuts: w=week, m=month, mb=beginning of the

full months.

4. Save your changes and return to the report.
Understanding report expiration
After a report has successfully run, users can view the results in the Results Viewer.
You can view the report, but you are unable to re-run the report (refreshing it with updated data) until the
"Valid until" time has been reached.
 When the "Valid until" time has been reached, the results of the report will be considered obsolete, or
expired, and will fall off the list.
 The only time a user can re-run a report before the "Valid until" time has been reached is when the
report is modified so that the current results may no longer be considered valid. This usually means a
change to the report's filters or to the columns being displayed.
Expired results usually cannot be viewed, but you can see a list of your recently expired results by selecting
Expired.

Add specimens to a storage rack
1. Use the Epic menu search to open the Container Storage activity.
2. Select a rack and click Accept to open it.
3. Select the slot where you would like to place your specimen.
4. Scan the barcode of your specimen or manually enter the specimen ID. The specimen appears in the
corresponding line in the list on the left.
5. Repeat steps 3-4 for all remaining specimens.
6. When you are done placing specimens on the storage rack, close the activity.
Locate a stored specimen
1. Open Specimen Inquiry (By Patient).
2. Search for and select your patient.
3. In Specimen Inquiry, click the link for specimen you want to locate.
4. Review the Specimen Tracking section of the report to find information about the storage status.
a. If the specimen has been placed in storage, you can see the name of the storage rack and the slot
in the Detail column.
b. If you needed to remove the specimen from storage, click the Remove link.
Remove a stored specimen from a rack
Follow these steps to remove a stored specimen from a rack.
1. Use the Epic menu search to open the Container Storage activity.
2. Select and open the shelf, rack, or refrigerator from which you want to remove a specimen.
3. Select the specimen you need to remove and click Remove.
a. The specimen is removed from the rack, and the Specimen Tracking section of Specimen Inquiry is
updated with an action of Removed from Storage.
b. When you remove a specimen, you can add it back to the rack later.

1. Use the Epic menu search to open the Container Storage activity.
2. Select and open the shelf, rack, or refrigerator from which you want to remove a specimen.
3. Scan or select the specimen and click Dispose.

Add tests to an existing specimen
1. Right-click the test on the Outstanding List and select Specimen Update.

 For non-requisition specimens, Order Entry opens.

3. Place and sign the order for the correct test.
4. In Specimen Update, click > Cancel.
5. Unselect the check next to the test you want performed, leaving only the incorrect test selected.
6. Indicate an appropriate reason for cancelling the test and accept the cancellation.

Create a batch
1. Use the Epic menu search to open the Batch Editor.
2. On the window that appears, select Create, select a batch type, and click Accept.
3. In the open batch, click review the list of all specimens that can be added to the batch.

appear in the Batch Queue window.

and click Add Selected.
a. To add multiple specimens at the same time, use Ctrl+click or Shift+click to select the specimens
and then click Add Selected.
Create QC specimens in a batch
In the Batch Editor, place the cursor in an open position and click Quality Control on the activity toolbar.
1. Select the material and the appropriate Lots check box.

Result a batch
1. Open the Batch List.
2. Select the batch that you want to result and click Result Entry to open the Outstanding List.
3. To enter results for an entire batch, click the batch ID on the Outstanding List. Verify that all tests are
selected and bring the batch into Edit Mode.
4. Enter the results.
5. Verify that all tests to which these results apply are selected and click Apply Results.
6. After you’ve entered the results for each test in the batch, click the batch ID on the Outstanding List
and click Verify.
7. Click Confirm Final.

text:
2
Introduction
This document contains instructions on looking up specimen information using an activity called Specimen
Inquiry. Think of Specimen Inquiry as an audit trail for a specimen, as it helps you find the answer to the
following questions:
 Who ordered the collection of a specimen?
 Who collected it, and when?
 Where is the specimen now?
 Have results been entered, and if so, what are they?
 Have any charges been dropped, and if so, which ones?
 and more
Specimen Inquiry supports two distinct approaches to look up a specimen:
 Specimen Inquiry (By Specimen) allows you to look up detailed information for one specimen at a
time.
 Specimen Inquiry (By Patient) allows you to look up a list of all specimens that were collected for a
patient. From the list, you can access detailed specimen information with just one click.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Resulting - Look up Specimen Information.pdf

Look Up a Single Specimen
Follow these steps to look up information for a single specimen at a time:
1. Use the button on your toolbar or the Epic menu search to launch Specimen Inquiry (By Specimen).
2. Enter the specimen ID in the Specimen Lookup window.
 Click Expanded Search to use additional criteria for your search, including patient name, order
number, submitter information, and more.
3. Click Accept.
Instead of searching for the specimen manually, click Specimen Inquiry (By Specimen) and
scan the specimen barcode if you have access to it.

2. Search for and select the patient in the Patient Lookup window.
3. Click Accept.
4. Review the list of specimens, including collection date and time, specimen ID, and test type.
5. Click the ID of a specimen to learn more.

title: Resulting - Quality Control
text:
2
General QC
Create QC specimens manually
Usually in the lab, the system automatically creates QC specimens to be tested at a certain time of day, after a
certain amount of time has passed, or after a certain number of specimens have been processed. The QC
specimens and their results appear on the Outstanding List.
If your testing process changes and you need to add QC specimens, you can do so manually by following these
steps:
1. Use Chart Search to open the Quality Control activity.
2. Add a material.
3. In the Tests field, find and select each test for which you are creating specimens.
4. Select the One test per specimen? checkbox if you want to individually assign tests to specimens.
5. Adjust the Priority, if necessary.
6. Create the specimen.
7. Continue to create new specimens as needed. If you are creating specimens for the same test, you only
need to enter the material and lot information. If you are creating specimens for a different test,
update the test as well.
Distinguish patient specimens from QC specimens
QC specimens appear on the Outstanding List, just like patient specimens. However, the QC specimens look a
bit different.
 Name: They have no associated patient.
 ID: The section code of their specimen IDs is Q.
View a QC graph
1. Use Chart Search to open the QC Report activity. The activity opens to your default report.
2. Review the report’s results and use the options to the right to apply or remove any filters, if applicable.
3. If you need to run a different report, click to review a list of all QC reports available to you.

title: Resulting - Quality Control
text:
3. If you need to run a different report, click to review a list of all QC reports available to you.
4. Click a report name to run it.
5. If you need to review and adjust the report's settings, click .
6. Adjust the report's criteria settings as needed and use the buttons at the bottom of the window to
proceed.

title: Resulting - Quality Control
text:
3
Result QC
Enter QC results
1. On the Outstanding List, select the QC specimen and take it into Edit Mode.
2. Enter the test results.
3. Save the results.
Review if QC results are in range
The system evaluates rules for each component to determine if the QC is in control. The icons you see in the
Result Summary report indicate which rules passed, failed, or caused warnings.
1. Find and select the QC specimen on the Outstanding List.
2. Review QC Details in the Snapshot report on the right.
a. Icons appear for the component-specific QC rules in the report.
 - the result pased all rules.
 - the result is outside of the Warn rule.
 - the result is outside the Reject value.
Accept or reject QC values
QC specimens are processed and resulted just like regular specimens. When the results are out of the control
range, however, the QC doc button appears with an exclamation point ( ). This indicates that you must
complete required documentation for the corrective action before you can verify the QC specimen results.
1. With the QC specimen selected on the Outstanding List, click QC Doc.
2. In the Include? field, select an appropriate value.
 Accept - The system will use this value when evaluating QC rules for this component.
 Exclude - The system will exclude this value and use values obtained prior to this value and after
the last rejected value when evaluating QC rules for this component. This option should not be
used often. It is meant only for user errors that cause erroneous results (for example, running the
wrong material).

title: Resulting - Quality Control
text:
the last rejected value when evaluating QC rules for this component. This option should not be
used often. It is meant only for user errors that cause erroneous results (for example, running the
wrong material).
 Reject - The system will not use this value or any prior values obtained for this component when
evaluating QC rules. This option is used when a specimen is out of control.
3. For any components with a Reject icon , indicate your follow-up action in the Corrective Action
field.
4. Complete the corrective action.
5. Verify the results, if appropriate.

title: Resulting - Quality Control
text:
4
Repeat a component for a QC specimen
You can retest the components of a QC specimen or repeat the entire test.
1. With the QC specimen selected on the Outstanding List, click Repeat Test and select either the
entire test or an individual component to repeat. The repeated component is prefaced with a number
reflecting the number of times it is resulted.
2. Enter the results of the repeated test.
3. If this was part of a corrective action, click QC Doc.
4. Enter the appropriate value in the Corrective Action field.
5. Verify the results, if appropriate.

Identify results that might need to be retested
When various icons appear in the Abnormality (A) and Delta checking (D) columns of the Outstanding List,
your lab might need to rerun tests or components. The chart below explains what the icons in each column
mean.
Icon Name Column Meaning
or Abnormal A The result is outside the reference range, but isn't
severely abnormal.
A indicates the result is above the range; a
indicates the result is below the range.
Abnormal-Critical A The result is significantly outside the reference
range. The physician should be notified
immediately.
Delta D There was a significant change between the
previous and current result.
Linearity L The result is outside the reportable range of the
analyzer.
Reportable R The result must be reported to an external health
agency.
Repeat a component for a test
1. With the test selected on the Outstanding List , click Repeat Test and select either the entire test or
a single component to repeat. The repeated component is prefaced with a number reflecting the
number of times it is resulted.
2. Enter the results of the repeated test.
3. Validate which value to post to the patient's chart, if applicable.
4. Verify the results, if appropriate.
If you re-run a test on a specimen without clicking Repeat Test first, the system will
automatically detect it as a repeated test and preface its result components with a
numerical indicator reflecting the number of times the test was run.

What's available in Chart Review?
The following table includes a brief explanation of some of the most commonly used Chart Review tabs.
Chart Review Tab Type of Information
Encounters Encounter information including the date, type of encounter, department,
and provider
Notes All clinical notes for the patient
Meds Information about current and past medications
Imaging Imaging order information along with associated images
Procedures Procedure notes, orders, and results
Letters Letter information, including the sender, type of letter, associated
encounter date, and the date on which the letter was sent

provider, and associated diagnoses and procedures

Find information in Chart Review
1. Use the button on your toolbar or the Epic menu search to launch Patient Station.
2. Search for and select the patient, and click Accept.
3. Select the Chart Review tab.
a. On the Labs tab, you see a list of the patient's past lab tests.
b. To view details about a specific test, select the test and review the information that appears in the
bottom pane.

title: Resulting - Review Patient Results
text:
3
Apply filters to find information quickly
1. Click Filters on the activity toolbar.
2. Select a filter type, such as Encounter Department.
3. Select the specific criteria by which you want to filter. The results appear in the pane on the right.
Your criteria might match several encounters. Rather than opening each one, click
Review Selected to view one report for all of the filtered encounters.
Review information from several visits at once
1. In Chart Review, go to the Encounters tab and select the visits you want to review.
 If the visits are next to each other in the list, press Shift while selecting the first and last encounter
you want to review.
 If the visits aren't next to each other, press CTRL and select each visit you want to review.
2. Click Review Selected to view a report that includes information from all of the visits you selected.
3. Press CTRL+F to search for a specific phrase or keyword across all of the visits you selected.
4. Enter the words you want to search for in the Find field and press Enter. The word is highlighted each
time it appears in the report.
5. Continue pressing Enter to jump to the next instance of your search term in the report.

Part 2: Accessing Reporting Content
Your reports and other reporting content can be accessed through the Analytics Catalog.
Find and open a dashboard
Dashboards centralize information you need throughout your day and are the primary method of reporting
content distribution. Instead of going to multiple screens to run reports, view your schedule, and access your
In Basket messages, you can see all this information on your collection of dashboards.
Your default favorite dashboard appears when you log in and toggle to the My Dashboards activity. Change
between dashboards depending on the information you need to see.
1. If you're not already on a dashboard, select the My Dashboards workspace.
2. Click the name of the dashboard.
If the dashboard you want is favorited, select it from the list.
If you want to search for additional dashboards, type the name of the dashboard in the search bar or click
Show Catalog to browse the full list.
Favorite dashboards for easy access later. To make a favorited dashboard your default dashboard,
drag it to the top of the list.
Take action from a dashboard component
Your dashboard gives you quick access to all the reports you commonly run. If a report you run frequently isn't
on your dashboard, you can add it.
The Favorite Reports component is populated with the reports that you added to your favorites from the
Catalog. Search for this component in the Catalog, and it will be added to a dashboard specific to your role.

Find and run reports from the Catalog

dashboards. You can quickly access your favorite content and search for new content.

show all content available to you.

Component. Create a new query or load an existing one. Click Create Component and add it to your
dashboard.

Key Report Templates
Report templates can be found by searching the analytics catalog
Report Template Name Description
HB Transaction Report Billing office and clinical department managers can use this report to review any
subset of transactions. Reports display the transactions and provide information
about each transaction. From the report results, managers can investigate the
transactions in Account Summary and click the Tx Actions button to open a list of
transaction and account actions that can be performed on transactions identified by
the report. Managers can also save the results to a file to send to their supervisors
or to an external agency.
HB Executive Summary Billing office managers, financial managers, and financial executives can use reports
built from the Executive Summary report template to monitor charge, payment, and
adjustment transactions to determine why other date-based transaction reports aren't
balancing. Reports from this report template are intended to be run ad hoc to balance
with other reports during issue resolution.
Reports created from the Executive Summary report template show a summary of
active AR, all AR, bad debt, external AR, or bad debt and external AR information.
Managers can run these reports for a specific service area, location, report type, and
date range, and choose groupings for the report data. They can also restrict the
reports by financial class, base class, and bucket type.
HB Account Query Billing office managers can use reports built from the highly flexible HB Account Query
report template to find hospital accounts with specific issues. For example, they might
track high dollar accounts, find and reassign accounts not on workqueues, or identify
accounts missing bed charges.

text:
report template to find hospital accounts with specific issues. For example, they might
track high dollar accounts, find and reassign accounts not on workqueues, or identify
accounts missing bed charges.
Report results appear as a list of accounts that meet the report criteria. The results list
displays basic information about the account (account status, account class, discharge
date, financial class, and account balance). Managers can click on any account to see a
detail view with more account information and account- and bucket-level balances.
Managers can follow up on accounts by performing account activities directly from the
results list. They can also jump to Account Maintenance for more details or transfer the
account to a workqueue for further investigation. Finally, they can export all results to
a spreadsheet for further analysis.
HB Aging Summary Use this template to build the Aging Summary report, which shows accounts receivable
and the length of time that accounts have been outstanding. Billing office managers
and finance managers can run the Aging Summary report weekly to find payers,
financial classes, or locations with high outstanding balances. They can review all of the
outstanding balances in the specified service areas, split by the number of days those
balances have been outstanding.
The report helps identify trends in outstanding accounts receivable, such as whether
particular payers take longer to pay, what kinds of accounts get paid sooner versus
later, and which types of buckets are aging over 90 or 120 days. Billing office
managers can use the report to identify groups of accounts that have been overdue
longer and need to be dealt with more urgently.

text:

managers can use the report to identify groups of accounts that have been overdue
longer and need to be dealt with more urgently.
The report can measure the length of time outstanding from a hospital account's
discharge date, the accepted claim date, or the date of the first external claim.
Discharge Date is the most common setting.
The report columns measure the dollar amount and percentage of money in each
AR Day interval. The In-House and DNB column shows outstanding balances for
open and DNB hospital accounts. Managers can review the dollar amounts and
percentages for each grouper to identify problem areas. For example, if a
particular financial class has high outstanding A/R, insurance follow-up staff should
focus on that financial class.
Revenue Guardian Encounter Report Department and billing managers can use Reporting Workbench template 64010-
Revenue Guardian Encounter Report to help identify missing charges per encounter
or admission. This template was previously called the Enterprise Encounter Charge
Reconciliation Report.

Part 2: Accessing Reporting Content
Your reports and other reporting content can be accessed through the Analytics Catalog.
Find and open a dashboard
Dashboards centralize information you need throughout your day and are the primary method of reporting
content distribution. Instead of going to multiple screens to run reports, view your schedule, and access your
In Basket messages, you can see all this information on your collection of dashboards.
Your default favorite dashboard appears when you log in and toggle to the My Dashboards activity. Change
between dashboards depending on the information you need to see.
1. If you're not already on a dashboard, select the My Dashboards workspace.
2. Click the name of the dashboard.
If the dashboard you want is favorited, select it from the list.
If you want to search for additional dashboards, type the name of the dashboard in the search bar or click
Show Catalog to browse the full list.
Favorite dashboards for easy access later. To make a favorited dashboard your default dashboard,
drag it to the top of the list.
Take action from a dashboard component
Your dashboard gives you quick access to all the reports you commonly run. If a report you run frequently isn't
on your dashboard, you can add it.

Show Catalog to browse the full list.

drag it to the top of the list.

Your dashboard gives you quick access to all the reports you commonly run. If a report you run frequently isn't
on your dashboard, you can add it.
The Favorite Reports component is populated with the reports that you added to your favorites from the
Catalog. Search for this component in the Catalog, and it will be added to a dashboard specific to your role.
When you a run a report from a dashboard component, the results are shown directly in that component. You
can then take additional action on the results.

text:
Encounter Analysis
Reports built from the Encounter Analysis report template show encounter statistics by department. These
reports can be used to help track efficiency by giving you a detailed breakdown of the major events associated
with an encounter, such as appointment check in time, patient wait time, and the time a patient spent in an
exam room.
Clinic managers and clinicians can use reports built from this template to identify sources of inefficiency and
come up with solutions to improve efficiency within their organization. For example, a report built from this
template can help managers identify patients who have a no-show appointment in a given time frame.
Managers can then use this information to follow up with these patients to make sure they know about
upcoming appointments.
Access: Clinical – Management, Clinical.
REFERRAL(AD HOC)
Reports built from this report template can be used to monitor the referrals volume in a given subset of
departments/providers during a specified time period. They are appropriate for use by Referrals Managers.
The search base for reports built from this report template is to run the report for the previous month and not
have any other parameters populated.
Access: Clinical – Management, Clinical.
Workqueue Monitoring
Billing managers and managers in other areas can use workqueue monitoring reports to identify workqueues
that have various issues or just to track work that's tied to workqueues. For example:
• Catch workqueues that are being neglected or otherwise slipping through the cracks. These reports
catch workqueues that need attention based on aging and dollar value criteria.
• Catch workqueues that have no user assigned to them.
• Catch workqueues that have an inactive user assigned to them.

gauge financial performance. Data in the dashboard can be viewed by service area or by lower groupings in
the facility structure, such as locations, departments, bill areas, etc. Supervisors should review the Revenue
Management dashboard daily to identify and address bottlenecks in the revenue cycle.

such as collection ratio, adjustments by category, and monthly activity using the PB Finance Dashboard.

text:
ARPB – Aged Accounts Receivable
Billing office managers, finance managers, and financial executives can use reports built from this template to
review aged AR by a number of groupings and pinpoint opportunities to increase your collections efficiency
and cash flow.
Reports built from this template show AR divided into aging buckets based on the variable aging dates of the
transactions. Aging based on variable aging dates means that this report accounts for circumstances that reset
the aging date for a transaction, for example, when liability transfers from insurance to self-pay responsibility.
Access: Revenue Cycle – Management, Revenue Cycle.
PB Undistributed and Overposted Credits
Credit supervisors can use reports based on the PB Undistributed and Overposted Credit Search report
template to research undistributed and overposted credits to investigate the cause and resolve the credits.
The report detail lists the reason, date, amount, type, and aging buckets for undistributed and overposted
credits, as well as the original invoice number, transaction number, and department. From the report,
supervisors can open Transaction Detail, Transaction Inquiry, and Guarantor Account Maintenanc e to research
the reason for the undistributed or overposted credit and resolve the credit.

Enterprise Encounter Charge Reconciliation Report.

associated charges. Users can track charge their work by marking encounters as reviewed or in review. The
report shows details for charges associated with scheduled Cadence encounters and inpatient admissions to

text:
3
Accessing Reporting Content
Your reports and other reporting content can be accessed through the Analytics Catalog.
Find and open a dashboard
Dashboards centralize information you need throughout your day and are the primary method of reporting
content distribution. Instead of going to multiple screens to run reports, view your schedule, and access your
In Basket messages, you can see all this information on your collection of dashboards.
Your default favorite dashboard appears when you log in and toggle to the My Dashboards activity. Change
between dashboards depending on the information you need to see.
1. If you're not already on a dashboard, select the My Dashboards workspace.
2. Click the name of the dashboard.
If the dashboard you want is favorited, select it from the list.
If you want to search for additional dashboards, type the name of the dashboard in the search bar or click
Show Catalog to browse the full list.
Favorite dashboards for easy access later. To make a favorited dashboard your default dashboard,
drag it to the top of the list.
Take action from a dashboard component
Your dashboard gives you quick access to all the reports you commonly run. If a report you run frequently isn't
on your dashboard, you can add it.
The Favorite Reports component is populated with the reports that you added to your favorites from the
Catalog. Search for this component in the Catalog, and it will be added to a dashboard specific to your role.
When you a run a report from a dashboard component, the results are shown directly in that component. You
can then take additional action on the results.

can then take additional action on the results.
View Report: Jump to the corresponding report in Reporting Workbench.
Component Details: View help text.
Click and select Collapse: Temporarily hide the component.
Find and run reports from the Catalog
The Analytics Catalog is a database of available reports and dashboards that you can access directly from your
dashboards. You can quickly access your favorite content and search for new content.
1. Search for a report by name or topic. You can filter results by favorites, content type, and tags.
• If you prefer to look at the available content without searching or filtering, click Browse. This will
show all content available to you.
2. Apply filters on the left to limit your search results.
• My Favorites: Show content you’ve tagged as a favorite.

text:
ACC Control Center
Scenario: The ACC is busy, and you are concerned about patient throughput at this moment. ACC directors
and providers can use the Control Center to identify and correct patient throughput bottlenecks in real time.
The Control Center has four panels
1. Overall Status
2. Door to Doc
3. Doc to Dispo
4. Dispo to Depart
In this dashboard, users can specify department, date, time, average/median time, and care area. Users can
view historical data as well as department data in real time. This dashboard provides a comprehensive view of
the department status at different points in time and can be used to solve real time issues such as
overcrowding.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/ACC Leadership - Reporting Content Guide.pdf
title: ACC Leadership - Reporting Content Guide
id: file:Shared Documents/ACC Leadership - Reporting Content Guide.pdf#7
text:
1. Overall Status
ACC Census
This section of your dashboard shows the recent ACC census over the past twelve hours and the historical
median for the last eight values for the same hour of the day on the same day of the week.
For example, the 12:00 value on a Tuesday is the median of the last 8 Tuesdays at 12:00.
Waiting Room and Boarders
This section of your dashboard shows the number of patients waiting and the number of boarder patients for
the emergency department.
LWBS/AMA
This section of your dashboard shows how many patients have departed in the recent past with ACC
dispositions of Left Without Being Seen (LWBS) or Against Medical Advice (AMA).
Staff List
This section of your dashboard shows information of the current ACC staff list. Users can also click on a staff
member to be taken to Secure Chat.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/ACC Leadership - Reporting Content Guide.pdf
title: ACC Leadership - Reporting Content Guide
id: file:Shared Documents/ACC Leadership - Reporting Content Guide.pdf#8
text:
2. Door to Doc
In Triage/Waiting for Triage/Room/Provider
This section of your dashboard shows the median amount of time patients have been in triage or waiting to be
triaged/for a room/seen by a provider. If the median time is above a certain threshold, the names of the
patients waiting, their chief complaints, and the number of minutes they've been waiting also appear in the
component.
3. Doc to Dispo
Outstanding Orders
This section of your dashboard shows the number of currently outstanding and overdue radiology, lab, and
consult orders.
Entering ‘Yes’ in the Show Order Subgroups field shows the types of orders outstanding or overdue. Radiology
orders are broken down by procedure category. Lab orders are broken down by specimen type.
In Process
This section of your dashboard shows basic information about in process patients grouped by attending who
has seen the patient. For each in process patient, this section shows:
• Location
• Acuity
• Radiology, lab, and consult order status

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/ACC Leadership - Reporting Content Guide.pdf
title: ACC Leadership - Reporting Content Guide
id: file:Shared Documents/ACC Leadership - Reporting Content Guide.pdf#9
text:
• Length of time in process
4. Dispo to Depart
Likely Admits
This section of your dashboard shows a list of ACC patients likely to be admitted to the hospital. For each
patient the following information appears:
• Bed
• Chief complaint
• Total time in the ACC
• Likelihood of admit score: this metric will be built as an optimization after MSRH go-live.
Ready for Admit/Discharge/Transfer/ Other Statuses
This section of your dashboard shows the median amount of time patients have been at a status of Ready for
Admit/Discharge/Transfer or have other statuses such as Expired, Sent to OR/Cath Lab, Behavioral Health
Hold, Send to L+D, or Boarder. Various information is included depending on the status, such as:
• Inpatient bed is assigned or requested
• Bed number
• Chief complaint
• Admitting provider
• Time in status
• Current location
• After Visit Summary print status
• Location
• Acuity

text:
ACC Dashboard
Scenario: You are interested in learning about the patients in the ACC today, how beds are being utilized,
and whether there is any overcrowding in the ACC.
The ACC Dashboard to monitors information such as wait time trends from the past few hours, patient
statuses, bed utilization, and nursing workflows.
The dashboard has three panels:
1. Current Patients
2. Current Resources
3. Today’s Performance
1. Current Patients
Patients in the ACC
This section of your dashboard shows the number of patients in the emergency department, sorted according
to patient statuses. For each patient status, the component shows:
• Percent of Patients: percent of patients in the ACC with this status
• Total: number of patients who have had that status long enough to be considered overdue
• Average Time: average amount of time these patients have had each status

id: file:Shared Documents/ACC Leadership - Reporting Content Guide.pdf#11
text:
Current Patients by Acuity
This section of your dashboard shows the number of patients who are assigned each acuity level. At each
acuity level, the following components appear:
• Number of patients assigned to the acuity level
• Average amount of time these patients are in the ACC
2. Current Resources
Bed Utilization
This section of your dashboard shows metrics related to bed in care areas, including:
• Percent of beds occupied in each care area
• Number of beds that are open, occupied, held, and blocked in each care area
• Number of overflow beds that are open or occupied in each care area

text:
Nursing Workloads
This section of your dashboard shows the following metrics for each nurse signed into the ACC:
• The number of patients to whom they are currently assigned
• The number of orders that they have not acknowledged
• The number of orders that they have not yet performed
• The number of procedures that they have not yet performed
• The number of medications that have not yet administered
3. Today’s Performance
ACC Overcrowding Score
This section of your dashboard shows the department’s National Emergency Department Overcrowding Score
(NEDOCS). The NEDOCS shown is unique to the department the user is logged into.
Census by Hour
This section of your dashboard shows the ACC’s patient census by hour of the past 24 hours, broken down by
patient status.

text:
Wait Time Trends - Averages
This section of your dashboard shows the average or median amount of time patients have waited between
various events in the emergency department. Wait time trends are calculated using a combination of historical
data and data from currently waiting patients whose wait times exceed the historical average.
