text:
Page 1 of 3
All patients needing a lab draw are required to be scheduled for a lab appointment in the
corresponding lab department. Lab appointments can be made in one of the following ways:
- One-Click Walk-In Lab Appt
- Book It - used for appointments being scheduled in the future
One-Click for Lab Walk-In Appointments
Patients that require labs to be drawn by a phlebotomist in the Lab Draw Department the staff will
utilize the One-Click scheduling functionality from the patients’ appointment desk. Using this
workflow, Epic will schedule and check-in the appointment choosing the preselected visit type and
resource.
From your tool bar click Appts and locate the patient to be scheduled.
Assure that your log-in department is the Lab department that you are wanting to schedule the
appointment into.
Once on the appointment desk, navigate to the Active Request tab and highlight the lab(s) that
need to be scheduled.
From the Appointment Desk menu select the One Click button on the toolbar. Note: This option is
only present when logged into one of the Lab Draw Station departments.

text:
1
Lab Scheduling & Registration - Transcribe
Orders
Transcribe Orders ........................................................................................................................................ 1
Transcribe Orders
Providers working in Epic place orders electronically, so schedulers don't get them on paper. However, you
might need to transcribe orders coming from doctors outside of your organization, or from doctors in your
organization that are not using Epic yet. If you receive incoming paper or fax forms, you need to transcribe the
order into Epic so that the procedure can be scheduled. This will also apply to Beaker Orders (BKR in the
Procedure Name or a Procedure Code that starts with LAB123).
1. Click the button on your toolbar or use the Epic menu search to launch Patient Station.
2. Search for and select the patient, and click Accept.
3. In Patient Station, click Transcribe Orders.
4. Select an existing encounter or create a new one, if applicable.
5. Click Add Order on the Visit Taskbar.
a. The Visit Taskbar appears at the bottom of the screen.
6. Enter the details from the paper order and click Accept.

coverage must be current and

the order.

during the encounter, such as a point-of-care

EHR DOWNTIME/BCA PC RECOVERY PROCEDURE interface
Business Purpose
- To define procedures during computer system downtime and ensure an orderly process for managing business systems, workflow and patient care during planned and unplanned system downtime.
- To establish standards of documentation/information to be entered into the electronic medical record and provide a process for reconciling the electronic medical record post downtime.
- To support the environment of patient care and establish collaboration between ancillary departments by defining the process for business systems, patient registration, ordering of diagnostics, reporting of results, providing treatments and patient services during downtime.
Definitions
- Types of Downtime

title: UTHSA MSRH BCA Policy Final
text:
Definitions
- Types of Downtime
- Scheduled Downtime: Downtimes that are planned and scheduled ahead as needed for software and hardware maintenance and upgrades. Planned downtime allows the departments to be prepared with reports and certain functions performed earlier that would have occurred if the downtime was unplanned.
- Unscheduled Downtime: Unplanned downtime occurs without the normal planning that can take place but is minimized by back-up systems that are in place to cover during these occurrences. Downtime that occurs when there is an unforeseen system failure. (See Disaster Recovery Plan addendum)
- Extended Downtime: When the system does not come back up after a Scheduled Downtime

title: UTHSA MSRH BCA Policy Final
text:
Upon notification of a planned/unplanned Epic downtime, downtime processes will be initiated based on the Downtime Policy and Level notification.
When to Use Downtime Systems
It is expected that clinical personnel will use the Epic downtimes systems in the following scenarios:
Downtime Event
Downtime System
How the System Works
Epic is experiencing an outage (planned or unplanned)
Epic Down 1 SRO
Because Epic Down 1 SRO functions like the Epic Hyperspace interface, it is the most useful downtime system for most users during an Epic outage. When Production Server is down, all patient information contained in Epic system as of last refresh is available on the Shadow Server in a read-only format.
The only difference between Epic Hyperspace and SRO is that SRO is read only.
For Patient Access: use the Epic Down 2 BCA Web system to enter ADT changes to facilitate faster return to normal operations.
Epic and Epic Down 1 SRO are unavailable
Epic Down 2 BCA Web
Epic and SRO could both become unavailable if a hospital loses connectivity to the network.
The central data centers are not available, but the hospital network still works.
Use the BCA Read/Write system to access reports of patient information for the hospital. Patient Access can use it to enter changes to Admission, Discharge and Transfer (ADT) information in preparation for Epic system recovery.
Network outage and/or power outage
Epic Down 3 BCA PC
In the event that the hospital’s computer network fails, or the hospital experiences a power failure, use the Epic Down 3 BCA PC system to view and print reports on the department’s patients.
Each department should have at least one BCA PC with a red keyboard.

title: UTHSA MSRH BCA Policy Final
text:
Each department should have at least one BCA PC with a red keyboard.
Overview of Epic Downtime Systems
University of Texas Health San Antonio (UTHSA) IT has implemented three systems for use during an Epic downtime event. The icons and names are intended to indicate the order in which the systems would be used. These systems are:
Epic Down 1 SRO
- Supports Read Only (SRO) is a read-only copy of the Epic database viewed in by an interface that closely resembles Epic Hyperspace. With SRO, you can view patient records, but you cannot add to them or create new ones.
- The information should be current up to whatever incident caused the switch to SRO.
- SRO is launched from an icon on the desktop of every clinical workstation.
- SRO looks and acts like the regular Epic Hyperspace experience, except that it is read-only.
Epic Down 2 BCA Web
- Business Continuity Access (BCA) Web system (BCA Web server) is a web server that has reports with information for each hospital department.
- For most people, the BCA Web server is located at the hospital. Epic downloads reports to the web server on a regular basis, so that the data is kept current.
- An icon on the desktop of each clinical workstation launches a web browser connection to the reports.
- Patient Access personnel can update the system with ADT data. Other clinical personnel can view the reports but must record new information on paper forms.

title: UTHSA MSRH BCA Policy Final
text:
- Patient Access personnel can update the system with ADT data. Other clinical personnel can view the reports but must record new information on paper forms.
- ADT information that you enter will not be visible to other users of the BCA Web server. However, when Epic returns to function, the ADT data is uploaded automatically to Epic, which supports faster entry of key patient information and a speedy return to normal work processes.
Epic Down 3 BCA PC
- The Business Continuity Access (BCA) PC is intended to be used in the event of a network failure or facility power outage.
- Each clinic and hospital department has a BCA PC located in it.
- The BCA PC consists of a workstation that is directly connected to a printer.
- The workstation and printer power supplies are connected to a red outlet, so they have generator power.
- Epic writes reports to the BCA PC on a regular basis, so the patient information is kept current.
- During a network outage and/or a power outage, department personnel can access the
BCA PC to view and print reports for the department’s patients.
Epic Downtime Forms
Downtime forms will be located on the SharePoint Forms Repository and will be automatically updated to the Downtime BCA PC downtime forms folder.
Downtime forms may be printed directly from the SharePoint site unless network connectivity is lost.
Downtime forms will also be stored in a folder on the BCA PC in case of network outage.
To print downtime forms from the BCA PC in the event of a network outage:
- Double-click the forms icon on the red BCA PC.

title: UTHSA MSRH BCA Policy Final
text:
To print downtime forms from the BCA PC in the event of a network outage:
- Double-click the forms icon on the red BCA PC.
- A Windows interface opens.
- Choose the appropriate forms from the tab structure.
- To print the forms, click the print icon. Forms will print to the designated BCA printer.
Accessing BCA Reports
- To log in to BCA Web (for the Access Department Only):
- Double-click the Epic Down 2 icon on the desktop of any clinical workstation to open the BCA Web interface.
- Enter the same information you use to log in to Hyperspace and press Enter or click Log In.
- To view department-specific information:
- Click Folder List in the toolbar to view a list of departments.
- Click the appropriate link for your department.
- To view and print specific BCA reports
- From the list of reports that appears, click the report that you want to view to open it.
- Check that the printer is set to print to Epic Downtime Printer or BCA Printer and click Print.
- Reports will print to the designated Epic BCA Downtime printer.
To log into BCA PC (available to all staff):
- Double-click the Epic Down 3 icon on the desktop of the department’s designated BCA PC to open the BCA PC interface.
- A list of reports will appear. You may Filter by Tags, or view by Report Type on the lower left. To sort the report columns, click on the column header.
- To preview a report, select the report you want to view and click View.

title: UTHSA MSRH BCA Policy Final
text:
- To preview a report, select the report you want to view and click View.
- To print one or more reports, select the reports and click Print. You may select multiple reports by clicking on them or by using CTRL + Click.
- Check that the printer is set to print to Epic Downtime Printer or BCA Printer, and click Print.
- Reports will print to the designated Epic BCA Downtime printer.
Downtime Management and Communication
- Scheduled Downtimes:
- If possible, the notice of the downtime is communicated to department management by the facility Health IT Department at least 3-4 days prior and by using “Message of the Day” in Epic.
- An upfront message is on the IT Help Desk voice mail when calling:
IT help desk: 210-567-7777
- Detailed status posted on BetterCare SharePoint. This can be accessed by clicking on the Internet Explorer icon. Logging in is not necessary.
- With the availability of the SRO and the BCA Downtime Reports for clinical information, printing needs can be determined by the facility.
- Broadcast Messaging Tool – (Net Support Notify) will be used to communicate alerts for EHR downtimes.
- Unscheduled Downtimes:
- Broadcast Messaging Tool – (Net Support Notify) will be used to communicate alerts for EHR downtimes.
- UT Health Information Technology personnel will time and call all downtimes.
- The help desk will call the facility’s switchboard operator, who will follow facility specific communication procedures.
- For non-hospital UT locations, the Health IT Directors will be notified of the downtimes/outages and will follow their communication process.
- An up-front message on the IT Help Desk voice mail when calling:

title: UTHSA MSRH BCA Policy Final
text:
- For non-hospital UT locations, the Health IT Directors will be notified of the downtimes/outages and will follow their communication process.
- An up-front message on the IT Help Desk voice mail when calling:
IT help desk 210-567-7777
- Detailed status posted on the UT Health Intranet. This can be accessed by clicking on the Internet Explorer icon. Logging in is not necessary.
- Ongoing notifications will be updated via UT Health Intranet messages along with pop up notifications available. Ongoing updates will occur during the daily Hospital Safety Huddle with key leadership to report back to the units.
- Management/Communication when system is restored:
- Broadcast Messaging Tool – (Vocera/Rover) will be used to communicate alerts for EHR downtimes and recovery.
- The helpdesk will call the facility’s switchboard operator, who will follow facility specific communication procedures.
- For non-hospital UT Health locations, the Health IT Directors will be notified of the downtimes/outages and will follow their communication process.
- An up-front message on the IT Help Desk voice mail when calling 210-567-7777
- Detailed status posted on the UT Health Intranet. This can be accessed by clicking on the Internet Explorer icon. Logging in is not necessary.
Application Specific Downtime Procedures
Registration (ADT) Downtime Procedure
- When the registration module is not available, appropriate designated Patient Access personnel will contact Information Technology Help Desk to report that the system is down and ascertain from Information Technology, how long the system will not be available. The Patient Access Staff will:
- Communicate this information to all registration associates.
- Notify registration management.

title: UTHSA MSRH BCA Policy Final
text:
- Communicate this information to all registration associates.
- Notify registration management.
- Patient Access will acquire pre-printed downtime forms (blank Patient registration summary PRS) from the BCA PC. Electronic versions of the face sheet are stored on SharePoint and the BCA downtime computer under Patient Access folder.
To Register a Patient During Downtime (With Internet Access)
- Use SRO to check for previous existing medical record number.
- A downtime CSN number will always need to be issued. Refer to the downtime CSN numbers and CSN number log sheet. A minimum of 1,000 downtime numbers should always be available.

title: UTHSA MSRH BCA Policy Final
text:
It will be the responsibility of the Laboratory Director/Charge person or the Information Services staff to perform initial checks on the system to determine the problem, if possible and if the problem is EHR or a middleware product.
- Check to see if all terminals in the laboratory are unresponsive. If yes, there may be a bigger problem than expected. If not, the system is not down and there may be a hardware or communications problem within the laboratory.
- Check to determine if other laboratories are down also. Ask the user at each site whether they are able to get any response from their EHR terminals
- Contact the HELP DESK: 210-567-7777
- The exact downtime protocol to be followed will be worked out by the Laboratory Director/Charge person on site with consultation from the IT staff. Consideration should be given to the staffing and workload levels. With guidance from Information Technology, they will make a judgment concerning the cause of the problem and project a possible downtime/recovery time.
- Laboratory Director or Charge Person responsibilities include:
- Establish a Command Center or location in the laboratory to coordinate downtime functions.
- Perform an initial Assessment of Laboratory needs for the downtime: In collaboration with pathologists, supervisors, charge staff, determine staffing needs and extent of the initiation of call back protocols to get additional staff into the departments as needed. Laboratory staff on duty at the time will not be allowed to leave their work assignments until directed to do so by Laboratory director or Charge Person.

- The laboratory director will communicate additional staffing/support needs to administration.
- Laboratory director and supervisory staff will communicate changes of staffing needs as the event continues.
- The command center will remain in effect until the EHR system is restored and a recovery plan is implemented. Additional staffing needs will be extended throughout the recovery process.

Pharmacy (Willow) Downtime Procedure
Scheduled Downtime Prep
- Pharmacy will print the 3-Day MAR they currently print for downtime after 4 hours have elapsed.
- Prior to an extended scheduled downtime, “3-Day MARs” will be printed by the Nursing units once all medications in pharmacy queue are verified. Nursing can use BCA to view the e-MAR.
- Pharmacy will print the following prior to downtime:
- Patient Hospital Census Report
- 2 sets of 24-hour window of IV labels – both IVPB and large volume labels
- Print copy of 3-day MAR for Pharmacy use as a patient profile.
- Print the next “Patient Specific” label run if necessary.
- Convert All Dispensing Machines (DM) to “Critical Override”. Pharmacy will also turn on “high risk Override group” which prompts nursing for a co-signature when a high-risk drug is overridden from the dispensing machine.
- Communications
- Pharmacy will have access to census reports in BCA Web.
- Pharmacy to call lab for pertinent labs.
- System generated in Medication Dispensing System will be in Capital Letters. Manual entry will be in all lowercase.
Unscheduled Downtime
- Pharmacy will print MAR as soon as unscheduled downtime has been confirmed.

title: UTHSA MSRH BCA Policy Final
headingPath: Scheduled/Unscheduled Downtime Printing and Access to the EHR
text:
- System generated in Medication Dispensing System will be in Capital Letters. Manual entry will be in all lowercase.
Unscheduled Downtime
- Pharmacy will print MAR as soon as unscheduled downtime has been confirmed.
- Downtime MARs and unverified medications report can be up to 1 hour behind of real time ordering. Broadcast messages should be sent to providers to instruct them to notify nursing of any orders entered in the last hour to ensure no delay or omission of orders. Nursing to follow-up on any missing medications with a call to provider. Nursing will update their MAR and will call Pharmacy to update MAR for missing medications.
- Convert ALL Dispensing Machines to “Critical Override”. Pharmacy will also turn on “high risk Override group” which prompts nursing for a co-signature when a high-risk drug is overridden from the DM.
- Communications
- Pharmacy will have access to census reports in BCA Web.
- Request a copy of the current patient census report from Bed Control.
- Pharmacy to call lab for pertinent labs.
- System generated in Medication Dispensing System will be in Capital Letters. Manual entry will be in all lowercase.
Oversight of Medication Use Process during Downtime
- Pharmacy will use the Epic downtime system for review of necessary medical information in a downtime for existing patients. Nursing will send height, weight, allergies for new patients or changes in existing patients.
- Nursing will call Pharmacy and send all physician orders via courier or tube.

title: UTHSA MSRH BCA Policy Final
headingPath: Scheduled/Unscheduled Downtime Printing and Access to the EHR
text:
- Nursing will call Pharmacy and send all physician orders via courier or tube.
- Orders will be reviewed and verified by a pharmacist for appropriateness, dosing, allergy/interaction checking, etc. Orders needing to be dispensed by pharmacy will be labeled, dispensed, and will be documented per Pharmacy standard process. This documentation will become part of the patient’s MAR in the Pharmacy.
- Pharmacy will use the printed MARs as a “Patient Profile” to review meds before dispensing, tracking new orders, discontinued meds, allergy checking, etc.
- If a clinical question is identified upon pharmacist review, pharmacist will contact the ordering provider to resolve the issue.
- Pharmacy will document new IV starts including IVPBs.
- Manual MARs will be started, in each area, on all newly admitted patients by both Pharmacy and Nursing.
- STAT orders will be communicated by phone with written orders courier or tubed ASAP.
- Pharmacy will keep a manual record of dispensed bulk items as well as other pharmacy dispensed medications during the downtime for subsequent billing recovery.
- In downtime greater than 24 hours, there should be an attempt to periodically reconcile the pharmacy MAR records with nursing MARs to assure that they match. This reconciliation should be done as complete as possible with special emphasis in the critical care and pediatrics patient care areas.
Recovery
- Pharmacy notified by patient access when cleared to enter orders on all patients.
- A Pharmacist will enter orders and have a 2nd Pharmacist verify all orders from patient orders from the downtime orders.
- Nursing units are notified as soon as order entry is completed for their unit. Pharmacists will call the unit.

title: UTHSA MSRH BCA Policy Final
headingPath: Scheduled/Unscheduled Downtime Printing and Access to the EHR
text:
- Nursing units are notified as soon as order entry is completed for their unit. Pharmacists will call the unit.
- Dispensing Machine “Critical Override” manually turned off by pharmacy.
- Conduct review of billing reports to determine if charges were processed correctly.
- Also run “Charges and Credit Report” Dispensing Machine reports to determine all medications that need to be charged: new patients added at the Dispensing Machine, items taken out on profiled patients, and non-profiled areas such as perioperative and procedural areas.
Quality Risk Management
During any down time (scheduled or unscheduled) staff will still document patient and non-patient safety events in the Press Ganey High Reliability Platform (HRP) online application. In the event HRP is also down, use the downtime safety event reporting form, available in the downtime forms folder on the BCA PC.
Completed downtime safety event reports on paper will be forwarded by the staff member to their appropriate manager/supervisor. The manager/supervisor will review the event, take the appropriate action.
Safety events will be classified according to the following algorithm:
The manager/supervisor will forward the paper-based safety event report to the Quality & Patient Safety Department. The Quality & Patient Safety Department will then enter the completed report into HRP for aggregation, tracking and trending, and follow-up.
CAUTION: All Serious Safety Events and all Precursor Safety Events resulting in permanent or temporary harm require an immediate phone call to the Director of Patient Safety or the Administrator on Call (after hours).
Disaster Recovery Strategy

title: UTHSA MSRH BCA Policy Final
headingPath: Scheduled/Unscheduled Downtime Printing and Access to the EHR
text:
CAUTION: All Serious Safety Events and all Precursor Safety Events resulting in permanent or temporary harm require an immediate phone call to the Director of Patient Safety or the Administrator on Call (after hours).
Disaster Recovery Strategy
A disaster is a disruption to normal data center operations where the expected time for returning to normal operations significantly exceeds the recovery time objective (RTO) for the system. For the Epic system, the target RTO is 1 hour. Disaster recovery plans are implemented when hardware, software, or the network becomes critically dysfunctional with no apparent short-term resolution. The options available for recovery depend on the strategies implemented for disaster recovery in the system’s technical infrastructure.
The primary disaster recovery strategy implemented for Epic is redundancy. When one serves as the production data center, the other is the secondary data center, fully capable of taking on the role of production data center.
Data Protection and Replication Strategy
UT Health’s data protection and replication strategy is based on maintaining copies and backups of Epic production data.
Contact the IT security help desk for further need to know information and policy on Disaster Recovery, Data Protection and Replication Strategy.

CONCISE VS. COMPREHENSIVE

The patient, with a history of diabetes and recent vision loss, presents for follow-up. They report no nausea
with weekly Trulicity injections and are familiar with the pen. They have not experienced the common side
effect of weight loss with Trulicity, and attribute their recent weight gain to decreased mobility due to vision
loss. They underwent an operation for their vision last week, but report no improvement and are unable to
drive. They continue to work, with transportation provided by their husband.
They are also taking metformin and insulin, but no Farxiga. They administer 20-25 units of insulin at bedtime
and report no hypoglycemic episodes. Their morning blood sugars are around 140. They recall a previous
medication, possibly an injectable, that maintained their blood sugars in the 90s, but cannot remember the
name. They have one more box of insulin vials left from a previous prescription.
In addition to their diabetes and vision loss, they have been dealing with the stress of decreased
independence and increased reliance on their husband for transportation.
The patient, with a history of diabetes, has been managing their condition with Trulicity, metformin, and
insulin. They have not experienced any side effects such as nausea or pancreatitis from the Trulicity. However,
they have not noticed any weight loss, a common side effect of the medication. They have been taking
insulin at a dosage of between 20 and 25 units, with no episodes of hypoglycemia. Their blood sugar control
has been satisfactory, with an A1c close to 7, but there is a desire to lower it further due to their eye problems.

RECORDING TIPS
Record using a high-speed Wi-Fi connection for the fastest note-generation and smooth uploads.
Abridge needs your phone’s microphone. Make sure that you're not using other apps that
are using your device’s microphone at the same time as recording with Abridge.
Place your phone in between you and your patient without any obstructions.
Never log out of or delete the app. If you’re experiencing an issue with recording or uploading,
reach out to our Support team at help@abridge.com.
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY

Converse instead of dictate. Abridge processes natural clinician-patient conversation, so
talk to your patient like you normally would.

text:
RECORDING TIPS
Verbally share findings and plans throughout the visit, including during the physical
exam. Be sure to vocalize non-verbal cues such as shrugs and nods.
Use the pause and resume functionality to include medical terminology before or after
a visit. The more details you can provide, the higher quality note will be produced.
If you answer a phone call while recording, Abridge will automatically pause the recording.
After you end the call, we recommend that you tap on the Abridge app to bring it back
into the foreground, where you should see the recording resume.
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY
Don’t use headphones. For telehealth visits, your phone needs to pick up
the audio from your computer's speakers to capture the visit.

CONCISE VS. COMPREHENSIVE
GET STARTED
CONCISE COMPREHENSIVE
The patient, with a history of diabetes and recent vision loss, presents for follow-up. They report no nausea
with weekly Trulicity injections and are familiar with the pen. They have not experienced the common side
effect of weight loss with Trulicity, and attribute their recent weight gain to decreased mobility due to vision
loss. They underwent an operation for their vision last week, but report no improvement and are unable to
drive. They continue to work, with transportation provided by their husband.
They are also taking metformin and insulin, but no Farxiga. They administer 20-25 units of insulin at bedtime
and report no hypoglycemic episodes. Their morning blood sugars are around 140. They recall a previous
medication, possibly an injectable, that maintained their blood sugars in the 90s, but cannot remember the
name. They have one more box of insulin vials left from a previous prescription.
In addition to their diabetes and vision loss, they have been dealing with the stress of decreased
independence and increased reliance on their husband for transportation.
The patient, with a history of diabetes, has been managing their condition with Trulicity, metformin, and
insulin. They have not experienced any side effects such as nausea or pancreatitis from the Trulicity. However,
they have not noticed any weight loss, a common side effect of the medication. They have been taking
insulin at a dosage of between 20 and 25 units, with no episodes of hypoglycemia. Their blood sugar control
has been satisfactory, with an A1c close to 7, but there is a desire to lower it further due to their eye problems.

RECORDING TIPS
Record using a high-speed Wi-Fi connection for the fastest note-generation and smooth uploads.
Abridge needs your phone’s microphone. Make sure that you're not using other apps that
are using your device’s microphone at the same time as recording with Abridge.
Place your phone in between you and your patient without any obstructions.
Converse instead of dictate. Abridge processes natural clinician-patient conversation, so talk to
your patient like you normally would.

text:
RECORDING TIPS
Verbally share findings and plans throughout the visit, including during the physical
exam. Be sure to vocalize non-verbal cues such as shrugs and nods.
Use the pause and resume functionality to include medical terminology before or after
a visit. The more details you can provide, the higher quality note will be produced.
If you answer a phone call while recording, Abridge will automatically pause the recording.
After you end the call, tap on the Haiku app to bring it back into the foreground, where you
will need to tap the play button to resume the recording.
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY
Don’t use headphones. For telehealth visits, your phone needs to pick up
the audio from your computer's speakers to capture the visit.

Taking a listen.

title: Epic Transition from Citrix
text:
Notice to UT Health Epic Users
Retirement of CITRIX.UTMSA.COM URL and UT Health Citrix Storefront
Effective Date: March 2, 2025, at 12:30 AM
What to Expect:
• On Campus/On Network UT Provided Work Stations: Users accessing Epic on campus and on
UT Network computers will experience no changes.
• UT Workstations using Global Protect and Citrix WorkSpace Application: Users accessing
Epic using Global Protect and Citrix Workspace Application should reboot their workstations on
March 3, 2025.
• Non-UT Workstations: Users with non-UT workstations will need to use the new URL:
https://windows.cloud.microsoft/
Select the APPS tab from the webpage.
• Non-UT Network Users: Users not on the UT Network and not using Global Protect will need to
use the new URL:
https://windows.cloud.microsoft/
Select the APPS tab from the webpage.
What You Need to Do:
• On Campus and UT Network Computers: No action required.
• Global Protect and Citrix Workspace Application Users: Reboot their workstations on March
3, 2025.
If any issues occur, you can use this link:
https://epic-storefront.et0582.epichosted.com/Citrix/EpicWeb
• Non-UT Workstations: Start using the new URL:
https://windows.cloud.microsoft/
Select the APPS tab from the webpage.
Non-UT Network and Non-Global Protect Users: Start using the new URL:
https://windows.cloud.microsoft/
Select the APPS tab from the webpage.
Additional Information:
If you are unsure of how to proceed, please contact the IMS Service Desk at 210-450-4800 option 2 or
(0-4800) for assistance in updating your device.

This is applicable to the Inside-only workflow at this time.

Haiku users will now see a gear icon within the Abridge

© 2025 Epic Systems Corporation. Confidential.
Charge Review: Error vs Warning
What is the difference between an (hard stop) vs a (soft stop) messages? On the right-
side of the WQ activity, the Error report provides help information on how to review and correct sessions, if
needed. If you do not see the bar, click on the arrow to the right side of the screen. If you need to correct the
information, you can open the Charge Review session.
need to be corrected before moving on.
need to be reviewed. These are items that need someone to review and verify this is correct to
keep going, or we need to correct this item before we move on.
When you review a Warning such as UTD Reg Dental Charge and Dental Coverage Mismatch, be
sure to read the accompanying information. The Warning below states the Error, the Rule number, and the
information on how to manage the warning.
For example, this Warning is telling us, this patient has a Dental procedure code D1110, but the patient has a
medical coverage.
• Use the pencil icon next to the coverage field to remove the medical coverage and use a dental
coverage if it should be billed to a dental insurance.
• If a coverage update is not needed and the information provided is correct - you will accept the
session, and add a note of ‘Coverage is correct, Coverage has been updated to I.e. Cigna PPO’. Then,
Resubmit the session. Once resubmitted, the session will fall off the current workqueue.

text:
Continued on next page. © 2025 Epic Systems Corporation. Confidential.
Another example is a Warning in the UTD Reg_Self Pay Review. The warning message tells you that the
session needs to be reviewed to confirm there is no insurance coverage. No insurance was added to the
patient registration.
• If the patient HAS insurance, you will need to go back to Registation and add the insurance to the
patient’s account.
o Once added, go back to the Charge Review session, click the Pencil icon in Coverages, Add the
insurance to the Visit, using the Green Plus sign, and Accept.
o You can then Test the session at the bottom and this should clear the warning. You can then
accept, add a note I.e. Insurance added to patient and Resubmit. Once resubmitted the session
will fall off the current Workqueue.
• If this patient is truly NO insurance, we can accept the session, add a note, I.e.Patient is true self-pay,
and resubmit. Once resubmitted the session will fall off the current workqueue.

title: Chage Review Error vs Warning
id: file:Shared Documents/Wisdom/Front End/Chage Review Error vs Warning.pdf#2
text:
Continued on next page. © 2025 Epic Systems Corporation. Confidential.
One more example of a Warning is in the UTD Reg PB Dental Charge Requires Authorization. First
read the message that comes with the warning. In this case, the dental procedure identified requires an
authorization number.
• If an authorization is required, message instructs you to click “Show all fields” in the Session section,
and use the Dental Billing Plan field to attach a DTP record to the session that contains the
appropriate authorization information. Once added, you can Accept the session and Resubmit.
Resubmitting the session causes the session to fall out of the workqueue.
• If an authorization is not required, you can accept, add your note, I.e. Authorization not needed for
insurance, and resubmit.

text:
Continued on next page. © 2025 Epic Systems Corporation. Confidential.
Errors MUST be fixed before you can move on.
For the following Error in the UTD Reg-Coverage Generic Missing Req’d Info, we first review the
message. The Generic Coverage loaded critical information is missing for claims. For this one, go back to
Registration and add all of the required information. The system is asking for Address, City, Zip and Phone.
We do NOT want to Force these errors, Forcing will cause these to try to go out. They will error again for
missing information, the system does not know where to send this claim. Once this information has been
added, resubmit the claim. Then add a note, I.e. Insurance information has been updated, when the window
appears.
Once resubmitted this will allow the session to fall off this workqueue.

Another example of an Error is in the Reg Subscriber Name-Invalid Format. This message this tells us
the format for the name is invalid.
Go to the Patient’s Registration, and then Subscriber Information. When it comes to names, there could be
numerous reasons for the error. Make sure to compare the name to what is on the insurance card. Once
corrected, go back to the session and Test. If it clears the error, you can then resubmit. Once resumbitted it
will fall off the workqueue. If the error does not clear, review the name again.
A few examples of name errors:
Doe,JaneM

no space in between names

PRO TIP:
When you see Errors in Other Workqueues, this means the error needs to be fixed in the other workqueue
and does not affect the current workqueue you are in.

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Wisdom/Front End/Cash Drawer Tip Sheet - UTD.pdf
title: Cash Drawer Tip Sheet - UTD
id: file:Shared Documents/Wisdom/Front End/Cash Drawer Tip Sheet - UTD.pdf#0
text:
1
Closing your Cash Drawer
Record your cash drawer contents
1. Click Billing Activities and then select Cash Drawer. Or chart search “Cash Drawer” and find your
cash drawer (should be the same as your username).
2. In the Cash table, enter the number of bills and coins that are in your physical drawer. For example, if
you have 4 one-dollar bills, you would enter "4" in the Quantity field for the 1.00 line.
3. In the Other table, enter any check payments using one line for each separate payment. Specify the
type of each payment in the Source field and enter the amount paid in the Amount field.
Match cash drawer contents to posted payments
1. Click Select All to select all of the payments in the Match Drawer Contents to Posted Payments section.

Last updated 1/28/25
PRIOR AUTH WORKQUEUES: APPT REQUEST & PATIENT
Prior authorization may be required when a dentist orders a treatment plan for a patient. To ensure authorization is obtained
prior to the patient arriving for their appointment, the patient is routed to a workqueue once the treatment plan has been
placed so that the clinic staff can quickly identify the patients that need authorization obtained. The patient will route to one
of two workqueues depending on whether they already have the procedure scheduled or if the procedure is still needing to
be scheduled.
• Patient Prior Auth Workqueue: displays patients without an authorization status for a pending treatment plan with a
scheduled appointment.
• Appt Request Prior Auth Workqueue: displays patients without an authorization status for a pending treatment plan
without a scheduled appointment.
The authorization process can be initiated and tracked the same way from either workqueue. The following steps walk
through the Prior Auth workflow that will be completed within Epic; the workflow of actually obtaining authorization is not an
Epic workflow, and training for that piece should be discussed with your department’s leadership.

Subsections Since the Patient Prior Auth and Patient Prior auth workqueues exisit for different purposes,

Subsection 1: Patient Workqueues
Complete the steps in this subsection to learn how to defer a patient on a workqueue, which
is a workflow utilized from the Patient Workqueue to remove a patinet from your Active
worklist until an overnight query runs to remove all patinets with a complete authorizations
station.
Subsection 2: Appt Request Workqueues
Compelte the steps in this section to learn how to schedule a patient from the Appt Request
Schedule Workqueue once authorization has been obtained.
Subsection 1: Patient Workqueues
Every night a query runs and removes all patients from the workqueue with an appropriate authorization status documented.
To avoid confusion regarding what patients should still be active on the workqueue, you should defer the patient to remove
them from your Active tab in the workqueue. Deferring a patient will place them on the Deferred tab in the workqueue, which
is where they will remain until the overnight query is complete.

title: MSPQ Completion
text:
© 2025 Epic Systems Corporation. Confidential.
MSPQ Completion
For visits with Medicare coverage, you need to ask the patient a series of questions known as the Medicare
Secondary Payor Questionnaire, or MSPQ. Some of the information entered may have the system
automatically switch the filing order of the payer based on the circumstance, and type of visit.
When checking in a patient with Medicare coverage, the MSPQ (Medicare Secondary Payer Questionnaire) will
automatically pop up as part of the workflow. Follow these steps to complete the questionnaire:
• Ask the patient each question listed
in the questionnaire. Ensure their
responses are clear and accurate.
• Select the correct answer for each
question based on the patient’s
responses.
Depending on the patient's answers to certain questions, you may be prompted to enter additional
information. Examples may include:
• Details about other insurance
coverage.
• Employment status or details about
the employer.
• Accident or injury-related information.
• Ensure all required fields are completed accurately before proceeding.
Once the MSPQ is completed, it remains valid for 90 days for outpatient care and 30 days for inpatient care.

text:
Continued on next page.
Setting Up Orthodontics Dental Billing Plans
Many patients will have in-progress orthodontia treatment that has a payment plan set up for self-pay and/or
insurance charges in axiUm. We need to cancel these payment plans in axiUm and create orthodontics dental
billing plans for charging in Epic.
Similarly, for treatments taking place entirely in Epic, we don’t want to rely on clinical treatment plans to
generate orthodontics charges, as they could be missing the right timing or pricing. Instead, we will use a
workqueue to catch clinical charges and replace them with our own orthodontics billing plans.
Transferring from axiUm orthodontics payment plans in progress
1. To prepare to transfer a plan from axiUm to Epic, review the conditions of the patient’s orthodontics
payment plan in axiUm. You will need the following information to set up their orthodontics dental
billing plan in Epic (tip sheet examples used in blue):
a. Patient/guarantor information (so you can look them up in Epic)
i. e.g. Orthodontics, Savannah [60000975]
b. Insurance information (if insurance is paying for any of their orthodontics treatment)
i. e.g. Delta TX
c. Authorization information (e.g. auth number, auth date, authorized amount)

text:
© 2018 Epic Systems Corporation. Confidential.
FAQs
What if I need to change my charging plan after it has been created?
You can change the name, guarantor, coverage, department, and billing provider on a dental billing plan using the
“edit” button in the activity without having to terminate the plan and create a new one. To edit the charge frequency,
amount, date, or code, you’ll have to terminate and recreate the ortho charging plan by selecting
within the orthodontic charging plan. Doing so will void all previous charges created by the old orthodontic charging
plan.
What if the guarantor or payer has an overdue orthodontics balance in axiUm?
When transferring from axiUm to an orthodontic charging plan in Epic, you want to leave any outstanding self-pay
balances in axiUm. When you enter the “plan amount” in the charging plan fields, you should think of it as the amount
left to be charged, not the amount due.
What if the guarantor has already been fully charged out and completely paid off their
orthodontics balance but still have treatments, and I am getting clinical charges from treatment
completion in my workqueue?
You should delete these sessions using the “Delete” button in your charge review workqueue. Clinicians can now track
these visits for student credit without needing $0 charges posted to the account.
What if a guarantor wants to pay more of their treatment plan up front than agreed upon?
By design, the orthodontic charging plan will generate monthly charges whether the guarantor has paid off their balance
or not. If a patient pays off some or most of their balance in full, that credit on their account will match to charges as

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/Wisdom/Front End/UTHSA Orthdontia Charging Dental Billing Plans - Tip Sheet.pdf
title: UTHSA Orthdontia Charging Dental Billing Plans - Tip Sheet

meta.file: UTHSA Orthdontia Charging Dental Billing Plans - Tip Sheet.pdf

id: file:Shared Documents/Wisdom/Front End/UTHSA Orthdontia Charging Dental Billing Plans - Tip Sheet.pdf#11
text:
or not. If a patient pays off some or most of their balance in full, that credit on their account will match to charges as
they are generated monthly. This means that, for example, if a patient has 4 months of $100 charges left on their
ortho charging plan in January of 2024 and they pay a lump sum of $300 in January instead, the $300 payment will
match to the $100 automatic charges in January, February, and March. Then, in April, the patient will be charged the
last $100 they have remaining to pay. This can be frustrating for patients who just want to pay off their balance sooner
and not wait several months to be charged again, so often the best option is to start a new charging plan and update
the charging schedule in alignment with the guarantor’s plan for payment.
What if the patient qualifies for a sliding scale discount? Will this be applied to their ortho
charges?
Sliding scale financial assistance discounts will be applied to ortho charges the same way they are applied to other
charges. Patients need to qualify and be within the financial assistance approval timeframe for discounts to post
automatically.

Welcome to UT Health!

Learns.

1. Open Google Chrome and navigate to UTHSCSA.edu
2. Select Search/Quicklinks and select UT Health Learns from the Login section.

text:
Dentist, Dental Faculty and Resident Information Sheet
1
Welcome to UT Health!
To gain Epic Wisdom, you are required to complete the following courses:
 Epic Wisdom Dentistry [WBT]
 Epic Wisdom Dentistry [BLT]
You may be required to complete additional courses as well. To determine which trainings are required
for your job role, complete the following steps:
1. Open Google Chrome and navigate to uthscsa.sharepoint.com/teams/UTHealth-EpicCare
2. Click Job Role & Related Access
3. Locate your Job Role and complete the appropriate courses.
 Courses must be completed in the order listed on the SharePoint site.
 If there is a section with two courses listed (WBT and BLT/ILT), that means the [WBT]
is a prerequisite that must be completed to register for the [BLT/ILT] course.
Please read the following carefully:
1. You must complete the web-based training [WBT] before attending instructor-led training [BLT
or ILT].
2. Once you complete the [WBT] training, users will need to enroll for all required in person [BLT or
ILT] training. Enrollment is complete once you have selected which class date you would like to
attend.
3. You must register to attend the in-person training [BLT or ILT] no later than 3:00pm one
business day before class to ensure that training materials will be prepared.
Use the following steps to complete the web-based training:
1. Open Google Chrome and navigate to UTHSCSA.edu.
2. Select Search/Quicklinks and select UT Health Learns from the Login section.
3. Log in with your UTHSCSA credentials.
4. Click the UT Health Learns icon.
5. The Current Learning folder opens. Click Search along the bottom of the screen.

UTD Price Inquiry & Dental Fee Report
It is important to utilize Epic fee and pricing tools as the source of truth for pricing and fee information as operationally
approved price changes went into effect October 1, 2024, prior to UTD Go Live. Prices are reflective of current
organizational costs and set by UTD Financial Operations based on many factors and subject to change at any time. It is
discouraged to print pricing or fee data as these values could change at any time.
Price Inquiry and reports within the Analytics Catalog are available based on staff security to review fees/prices in
real time in Epic and should be utilized when possible.

Staff with the appropriate security can access and utilize Price Inquiry with the following steps:
1. To open, click the Epic button and search for Price Inquiry. There are two tools within Price Inquiry: Price
Lookup and Fee Schedule Viewer.

calculating patient estimates, as the prices it generates do not include insurance benefits or self-pay discounts.
To find if a code is available and priced in Epic, enter the procedure, applicable modifiers and the appropriate
quantity; select the Simple Pricing option and appropriate fee schedule, then click the +Add Procedure button.
The fee will appear in the right side of the screen with the current price assigned to the selected fee schedule.
3. Use the Fee Schedule Viewer tab to investigate procedure information stored in a fee schedule. You can enter a

UTD Dental Fees and RVUs Report
Within the Analytics Catalog a Workbench Report was added as a tool for fee review as well for those with
appropriate security to access. To open the catalog, click the Epic button and search for Analytics Catalog.
1. The catalog opens with the My Catalog checkbox selected. This view shows you your favorite reporting tools.
To search for a report not already marked as a favorite, uncheck this box.
2. Enter keywords, such as "fee" in the search field to search for this reporting content.
3. Use filters to narrow your search results. For this report, select WorkBench Reports to search only for
Workbench Reports available to you.
4. Before running the report, you can mark a record you found as a favorite by clicking the star icon that appears
when you hover over a card.
5. Click the purple arrow to view the report.
6. The report is set up to show the UTD GENERAL DENTIST FACULTY [88] fee schedule data. You can expand
the filter to include other fee schedules by clicking the blue Fee Schedule link and adding the other fee schedule
you wish to see.
7. You can add additional filters for the columns within the report by clicking the plus button in the filter selection
toolbar or the +Add another Filter link.
8. The Explore tab will pop you into SlicerDicer for further exploration.

© 2025 Epic Systems Corporation. Confidential.
Key Terms
Fee - the unit charge of a chargeable procedure representative of the dollar amount or price of a patient service billed
to insurance and/or guarantors responsible for accounts. Also referred to as “price” or “charge” for a chargeable
procedure.
Fee Schedule (FSC) – used to associate fee/prices with chargeable procedures. For UTD, fee schedules with pricing
revisions approved by UTD Finance Operations went into effect October 1, 2024. Prices in Epic are different from
Axium with these revisions and reflective of organizational cost increases. There are three fee schedules used for UTD:
• UTD General Dentist Faculty [88]: this is the default fee schedule used where all available chargeable
procedures are priced for UTD and used as the main source of pricing if a price is not found in other fee
schedules.
• UTD Grad Resident [90]: this fee schedule is used when the provider performing the service (service provider) is
a dental resident to provide an alternate price for a procedure different from the default fee schedule.
• UTD PreDoc Student [91]: fee scheduled used when the provider performing the service (service provider) is a
dental student or hygienist student to provide an alternate price for a procedure different from the default fee
schedule.
Procedures (EAP) - For Epic's billing applications, chargeable procedure (EAP) records represent types of charges,
payments, and adjustments. For example, you'll have procedure records for an insurance payment, a contractual
adjustment, charges for various office visits, and many more. Clinical orderable or performable procedures used to
define care for patients are representative of CPT, ADA (CDT) and HCPCS codes and are typically linked to chargeable

define care for patients are representative of CPT, ADA (CDT) and HCPCS codes and are typically linked to chargeable
billing procedures for claims and billing purposes. Some custom codes, also called “pseudo”, “step”, “i” or “dot” codes
at UTD are also available but limited due to the extensive maintenance required and typically unnecessary for most
scenarios.
• Some of these codes that were once available in Axium are available in Epic, but this list has been limited
since most variations could be captured other ways with Epic tools.
Guarantor – this is the person financially responsible for a given set of professional charges for a patient, specific to
each service area.
Guarantor Account – created by front desk staff to assign patient financial responsibility where the charges,
adjustments, payments and financial details are stored. Registration staff collect or update demographic information
about the guarantor that billing staff can later use to send bills for charges not covered by insurance.
Account Maintenance – module that allows billers and staff with the appropriate security to see financial activity for a
guarantor account
Price Inquiry – Hyperspace module from which users with appropriate security can view procedure fees/prices that
are stored in UTD fee schedules. Price Inquiry consists of two tools: price lookup and fee schedule viewer.
Analytics Catalog – Epic’s one-stop shop for reporting content, including reports, dashboards, and SlicerDicer
sessions.

text:
Continued on next page.
More Robust Orthodontic Estimates
You now have more options for managing estimates for orthodontic services.
This tip sheet refers to Financial Arrangements. Your organization might
label these as Estimates or Patient Estimates depending on your setup.
Create an Estimate from a SmartSet
Typically, a single estimate is created for an orthodontic episode at the beginning of the treatment. However,
there are some cases where additional charges might be needed during the course of treatment. In these
cases, you can create an estimate for the additional charges from the SmartSet.
1. In the Orthodontics activity, open the SmartSet for the additional charge.
2. To create an estimate for the additional charge, click Financial Arrangement.
3. Sign the SmartSet.
Create an Estimate to Illustrate an Alternative Option
By default, orthodontic estimates look at the treatment plan to determine which services should be included.
However, there might be times when you want to create an estimate to illustrate a treatment option that is
different from the current treatment plan. In these cases, you can select a template to use in the estimate,
which overrides the treatment plan.
1. In the Billing section of the Orthodontic Treatment activity, click the next to Create in the
Financial Arrangements section and select Create & Build.
2. Enter a name for the estimate in the Name field.
3. In the Orthodontic Template section, select the template that represents the alternative treatment in
the Template field.

provider name is in note text.
Scanned Documents 5 years* of Pathology and Radiology Reports scans
Allergies
Outpatient Medications Abstract = Review axiUm and enter data into Epic

Staff Function

Staff Function
Insurance Coverages Coverages for all patients seen in the year 2024
*5 years goes back to Dec 1, 2019
Between December 10th and 13th, the Encounters, Notes, and Scanned Documents you see in Epic will only be
current as of December 2, 2024. After December 13, the converted axiUm data will be caught up through Go-
Live. Any new axiUm data we import after Go-Live will not overwrite data that was manually entered into Epic.

data into the patients' Epic chart. Dental users will have Read Only access to axiUm after Go-Live.

text:
Rooming (EPR and Vitals)
Click on Rooming and fill out the pages as needed for your NPE, limited exam, or case
reassessment.
- You will be asked to designate a co-signer upon first edit of Rooming. Name your
attending faculty
- NOTE: The WIS Note Templates automatically pull information from the Rooming tab
so be sure to fill this tab out properly
- Visit Info for the CC and HPI
- Dental Vitals for vitals
- Allergies for allergies (crazy right)
- Medication Review for medications
- History to update medical history (past and present illnesses, review of systems, family
history, social history, etc.)
- Dental Health AND Caries Risk Assessment if you need to complete D0420.1 (risk
assessment) for an NPE
- Implants for information about implants
Continue through the main tabs left to right (detailed explanation next section):
- Soft Tissue for extraoral and intraoral exam
- Tooth Chart for pertinent hard tissue findings (i.e. caries, fractures, missing
teeth, existing restorations, etc.)
- TIP: In the Tooth Chart on the top right, there is a Auto-Plan
Procedures button which will automatically plan your restorations and
properly link them to their corresponding clinical findings
- This feature will attempt to put resin composite restorations for all
caries and fractures. So if you need to plan a crown, do so
manually BEFORE clicking Auto-Plan Procedures
- Periodontal Chart section of the Tooth Chart for periodontal findings

Clinical findings are recorded under Tooth Chart.
- Clinical Findings (caries, fractures, root tips, etc.) are recorded in RED
- Existing Restorations (fillings, crowns, RCT, etc.) are recorded in BLUE
- Planned Procedures are recorded in GREEN
- Completed Procedures are recorded in PURPLE
Periodontal findings are recorded under the Periodontal page of Tooth Chart

Once you have completed your clinical findings and periodontal chart, faculty must clinically
confirm them and then officially approve them on Epic. This is intended to be done chairside on
your personal device. As such, please enter all findings into the patients Tooth Chart
BEFORE calling faculty over to confirm them. Once your faculty has approved your findings,
click the Approve button at the bottom of the Tooth Chart. Faculty will then use their login
credentials to approve
Alternatively, faculty can approve your findings at the faculty station by going to your
patient’s chart on their personal Snapboard or Schedule, opening up the patient’s Tooth
Chart, and clicking Approve at the bottom of both the Hard Tissue and Periodontal
pages.
Treatment Planning
To quickly plan procedures based on the findings in your Tooth Chart, click the Auto-Plan
Procedures button on the Tooth Chart as shown below.
Please note: This button will attempt to address all issues with Resin Composite Direct
Restorations. Thus, if a tooth needs some other procedure (EXT, crown, RCT, etc.), these
procedures will have to be manually added BEFORE clicking this button. This button will
also not auto-plan advanced procedures such as dentures or bridges.

Outstanding

text:
You can write your note from scratch, copy and paste an existing template, or use a WIS
Template for your note.
That said, try to use the WIS Templates to write your notes. These WIS Templates will
automatically pull information from the patient’s rooming tab, chart, and treatment plan.
POV: You have finished your note, finalized findings, completed all referrals, etc.
To conclude your appointment, click Sign Visit/Encounter in the bottom right; this is your way
of saying that you’re done for the day, you’ve completed your appointment, and there are
no more changes you would like to make to the patient’s chart.

text:
Common hard stops include:
- Unsigned orders
- No named co-signer
- Patient requires excuse note for work or school
These must be addressed before you can click Sign Encounter/Visit.
Once you have successfully clicked Sign Encounter/Visit, the faculty you named as co-signer
will receive a notification in their In Basket, allowing them to co-sign both the visit and any
outstanding items they have yet to co-sign.

Glossary
Hard stop. The item associated with this symbol cannot be finalized without
the hard stop being addressed.
Approval Faculty agreement on components of the patient’s chart (findings, perio
chart, planned treatments)
Co-sign Faculty approval of a non-procedure item. Required after student signs
(see “Signing” below). Anything that must be signed must be co-signed
afterwards.
Co-signer Your attending faculty
Completed
Codes
Codes which have been completed (final prosthesis delivered, restoration
complete, etc. Completing a code does not need faculty approval;
completed codes are approved when faculty co-sign the visit.
i-codes In Process. i-codes are assigned to multi-appointment procedures before
completion. The proper code should only be completed at final delivery.
Example: Crowns (D2740) take multiple appointments. For each appointment leading up to
final delivery (prep, master impression, provisional remake, etc.), the code D2740I should
be assigned to your appointments. The D2740 code should only be used following final
crown delivery. The same goes for complete dentures, RPDs, etc. These need to be
approved just like any other code
In Basket List of items on your to-do list and updates about items from your to-do list.
Please always try to keep your in basket clear.
Orders Communications with anyone not on the pre-doc floor. Includes radio
requests, referrals, and consults.
Outstanding
Codes
Codes which are in a patient’s chart but not assigned to a specific
treatment plan
Pending Codes Codes which are in a treatment plan but not assigned to a specific visit

1. Introduction
The MiPACS HTML5 Web Viewer enables users to view and manipulate a wide variety of medical images. MiPACS HTML5 Web Viewer requires no
installation on the client’s behalf and is compatible with any HTML5-compliant web browser (including Google Chrome, Microsoft Internet Explorer 9
and up, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, MacOS Safari, iPad, iPhone, Android, and more). Digital Images from a variety of different sources (including
CT, MRI, Ultrasound Units, imaging sources etc.) can be analyzed, displayed, manipulated, stored, and sent across different networks by using
MiPACS HTML5 Web Viewer. There are several different functions that users can use when they are viewing images. Some of these functions include
annotation and measurement of regions of the image, image stacking, window width and level manipulation. MiPACS Web Viewer also has the ability
to display and render 3D images. The user will be able to see image sets rendered through VRT, MIP, SSD and MPR functions.

12.1.6 Curve
The Curve tool used to draw a line that will have a curve in it.
To use this tool, select the Curve button or the drop-down menu button next to the Select/Point/Arrow/Rectangle/Ellipse/Line/Freehand/Polyline
/Polygon/Text/Note/Highlight/Text Pointer button and then select the Rectangle tool button. Then click on the image and draw a line that is desired.
The next click will then make the line curve. This creates a start point, apex, and end point.
Steps to use the Curve Tool
Click the Curve button.
Click and drag the cursor to create a line.
Click on another part of the image to create the curve.
Next, click on another part of the image to continue making a curved line or double click to set the line.
Manipulate the curve by moving the boxes or manipulate the two green circles.
Click on the curve to reset it on the image.

13.2.4 Calibrate Ruler
The Calibrate Ruler tool used to measure an object of known size and then used to manually put in the length of the of the object. This will calibrate
the other Ruler functions (Ruler, Poly Ruler) to then use the measurement form the Calibration Ruler as the standard for anything measured after that.
To use this tool, select the Ruler tool button and measure the object with the known measurement. Then click the drop-down menu next to the Ruler
button and click the Calibrate Ruler button. The length of the known object and the unit of measure that the object is in can then be inputted. There is
also a small button on the screen that says Apply to all Images. The Apply to all Images box will need to be selected before clicking OK, in order for
the Ruler and Poly Ruler to measure in the calibrated measurement for all measurements on the image.
Steps to Calibrate Ruler
Select one of the Rulers/Poly Rulers on the image.
Click the Calibrate Ruler button.
Change the Length, the Ruler Unit, and check/uncheck the Apply to all images.
Click OK.

14. 3D Imaging Tools
The 3D Imaging Tools can be found on the top of the Viewer Tab by selecting the 3D Imaging Tools. These tools can be used to increase the
diagnostic quality of the image. All effects that are placed on the image using these tools can be done without losing the original image.
14.1 3D Tools
14.1.1 Cross Hair
The Cross-Hair tool is used to help navigate the 3D Image. The Cross-Hair tool provides a yellow cross hair on the Axial, Coronal, and Sagittal planes
that move in sync with each other providing the same location. The reason there is symmetry between the cross hairs is due to the orthogonal
projections being generated from the axial stack which the MPR generation of the three planes.
To use this tool, click on the Cross-Hair button. Then click any of the three plane windows. The cross hair will formulate on the window that is selected,
then select one of the other two windows to get the other windows to produce the cross hair.
Steps to use the Cross Hair Tool
Click on the 3D rendered image. (This will allow the user to use the dropdown menu next to the 3D settings button)
Click the Cross Hair button to toggle the button on and off.

14.1.5 Dental Panoramic
The Dental Panoramic Tool is used to create a panoramic image from a head CT.
To use the Dental Panoramic Tool click on the axial image of a CBCT image. Scroll through the stack of images until the lower teeth are visible. Then
select the Dental Panoramic Tool. Click on the rear molar on either side to start. A yellow dot will appear that is surrounded by a shaded outer layer.
When consecutive yellow dots are constructed a solid yellow line will connect the yellow dots. For the best image make sure that the solid yellow line
is in the center of the features that are desired to be seen in the panoramic view. From there click in small sections around the mouth until the other
back molar is reached. Double click to end the panoramic. This will produce a panoramic image off to the right of the 3D rendered image.
Steps to use the Dental Panoramic Tool
Click the axial window

19. Tablet Functions
The MiPACS HTML5 Web Viewer can be accessed from a number of devices as long as there is internet. For diagnostic purposes we suggest using a
screen that is 7” in length or greater. Tablets will function the same way using a tablet or desktop/laptop, with the only difference being fingers are
used to navigate the application compared to the standard keyboard and mouse.
19.1 Zoom
Zooming in and out can be achieved by touching the screen with two fingers. To zoom out of the web viewer take two fingers and expand them away
from each other. To zoom in on the web viewer take two fingers and bring them together.
19.2 Ending a Ruler Measurement/Annotation Tool
There are tools that can be ended with a double left click. To achieve a finished ruler measurement and annotations, simply double tap the screen at
the desired position to end the measurement/annotations.

The MiPACS HTML5 Web Viewer User Guide goes over the end User side of the MiPACS HTML3 Web Viewer. Request our MiPACS HTML5 Web
Viewer Admin Guide to get a better understanding of the web viewer from an Administrative perspective. For any comments, questions, or concerns,

UT Operations
Dashboard & Metrics
Business Intelligence & Data Analytics Team
Epic Reporting Content Guide
Objective
The UT Operations Dashboard serves as a tool for operational leadership to access key performance metrics,
especially those pertaining patient access. For additional information on reporting content, updated training
materials, and further support, please visit our internal SharePoint page: UT Analytics Center of Excellence.
Accessing the Dashboard
Your reports and other reporting content can be accessed through the Analytics Catalog.
Find and open the dashboard
The dashboard to search for is named UT Operations Dashboard. If you would like to access the dashboard
through a browser, ensure you are logged into the UT network (or Global Protect VPN if accessing remotely)
and go to this link: UT Operations Dashboard
Dashboards centralize information you need throughout your day and are the primary method of reporting
content distribution. Instead of going to multiple screens to run reports and view key metrics, you can see all
this information on your collection of dashboards.
Your default favorite dashboard appears when you log in and toggle to the My Dashboards activity. Change
between dashboards depending on the information you need to see.
1. If you're not already on a dashboard, select the My Dashboards workspace.
2. Click the name of the dashboard.
If the dashboard you want is favorited, select it from the list.
If you want to search for additional dashboards, type the name of the dashboard in the search bar or click
Show Catalog to browse the full list.
Favorite dashboards for easy access later. To make a favorited dashboard your default dashboard,
drag it to the top of the list.

2
Take action from a dashboard component
Your dashboard gives you quick access to all the reports you commonly run. If a report you run frequently isn't
on your dashboard, you can add it.
The Favorite Reports component is populated with the reports that you added to your favorites from the
Catalog. Search for this component in the Catalog, and it will be added to a dashboard specific to your role.
When you a run a report from a dashboard component, the results are shown directly in that component. You
can then take additional action on the results.
View Report: Jump to the corresponding report in Reporting Workbench.
View Session: Jump to the corresponding session in SlicerDicer.
Component Details: View help text.
Click and select Collapse: Temporarily hide the component.
Use dashboard parameters to update focus of metrics
Most of the metrics on this dashboard are controlled by the parameters at the top of the dashboard. You will
be able to tell which components will be affected by hovering over one of the parameters and seeing which
section’s borders on the dashboard becomes blue.
There are three main parameters to consider updating:
• Summary Level – narrows down the metrics to a service area, revenue location, department, or
provider level
• Summary Target – after selecting a Summary Level, users can select which target(s) to focus on
• Date Range – determines if the values should be shown yearly, quarterly, monthly, weekly, or daily.
This options also allows to select the number of periods for these intervals.
These parameters can be saved in a personal “view” for ease of coming back to this set combination of

text:
4
Metric Definitions
The metrics on the dashboard are a mix of Epic-recommended and custom metrics built by the BI Team.
Definitions for each of these metrics are listed below.
Metric Name Epic/Custom? Description
New Patient
Appointment Rate
Epic This metric displays the percentage of completed appointments
that are flagged as new to the service area.
Numerator: Total number of completed appointments
Denominator: Total number of appointments that are marked as
new visits.
New Patient Visits Epic This metric displays the count of visits that are considered new to
the department of the visit.
Completed Visits Custom This metric shows the count of visits with a Completed or Arrived
status, sliced by whether the visit is considered a Video Visit or a
Physical Visit.
Provider Utilization Epic Provider utilization is calculated by dividing the time in completed
or arrived appointments and dividing it by the amount of time in
regular available openings on the schedule.
Numerator: The total amount of appointment time in a completed
or arrived status.
Denominator: The total amount of time in regular openings.
Exclusions: A scheduled task determines which
provider/department combinations should be excluded from the
metric. Exclusion is met if one of the following conditions occur:
• The provider is “generic”, meaning a provider record used
for scheduling appointments or cases before the actual
provider is known.
• The provider’s template for the department is an OpTime
template
• The provider’s schedule utilization for the department is
below 35% or above 200%

sourceId: file:Shared Documents/UT Operations Reporting Content Guide.pdf
title: UT Operations Reporting Content Guide
id: file:Shared Documents/UT Operations Reporting Content Guide.pdf#5
text:
5
Schedule Utilization Epic Schedule utilization is calculated by taking the total amount of
booked time on the schedule, plus any openings that went unused
due to a late patient-initiated cancellation, and dividing it by the
amount of time in regular available openings.
Numerator: The total amount of booked time, plus any unused
time in regular openings due to late patient-initiated cancellations.
Denominator: The total amount of available time in regular
openings.
Exclusions: A scheduled task determines which
provider/department combinations should be excluded from the
metric. Exclusion is met if one of the following conditions occur:
• The provider is “generic”, meaning a provider record used
for scheduling appointments or cases before the actual
provider is known.
• The provider’s template for the department is an OpTime
template
The provider’s schedule utilization for the department is below 35%
or above 200%
Resource Utilization Epic Resource utilization is calculated by dividing the time in completed

DEMO SCRIPT
1-liner: Patient is here for management of hypertension, type 2
diabetes mellitus. Type 2 diabetes mellitus is not optimally
controlled, based on A1c from June 2020.
HPI: Patient denies chest pain, palpitations, shortness of breath,
vomiting, change in bowel habits.
Imaging: Chest x-ray: on my independent review and interpretation,
negative for pneumonia
PE: On exam the rash looks most consistent with a viral exanthem and
not a cellulitis or sjogrens syndrome or a more dangerous condition.
A/P: Bilateral erythematous and bulging tympanic membranes
without rupture. Febrile to 38°C. Likely secondary to a viral illness. No
signs of bacterial meningitis or pneumonia. Well-appearing and
vaccinated, making a lumbar puncture unnecessary. Chest x-ray
negative for pneumonia. Discussed that amoxicillin is the preferred
treatment due to its effectiveness in children under X months.
Anticipated outcome is resolution of symptoms within 10 days with
proper adherence to medication.
The patient was identified in the holding area, taken to the operating room
and placed on the table in supine position and general anesthesia was
induced. Both arms were left out and protected with Kerlix rolls, a footboard
was placed at the foot of the bed. The patient's abdomen was then prepped
and draped in sterile fashion, and after an appropriate perioperative timeout
a Veress needle was inserted in the left upper quadrant at Palmer's point.
Pneumoperitoneum was established with CO2 insufflation. The patient's
abdomen was measured and marked for appropriate trocar placement,
including marking for the Titan stapler trocar.

axillary line, and another 5mm port in the right upper quadrant. A Diagnostic

title: Verbatim Mode Guide
text:
VERBATIM FAQS
What version of the Abridge mobile app is required to use
Verbatim Mode?
We recommend using the Abridge Clinician App version
3.6 or later.
What languages will Verbatim Mode work for?
At this time, Verbatim Mode only detects and
transcribes English.
Can I edit verbatim content?
Verbatim content can be edited as normal text on
notes.abridge.com. It cannot be edited on the mobile app.
Can I delete a verbatim snippet after recording?
Yes, you can select the three-dot menu on the upper right
in Verbatim Mode. Or, rather than assigning the snippet to
a section, you may select the back arrow and be
prompted to confirm deletion.
FAQS
Need help? Contact help@abridge.com
Why are complex terms and medications misspelled in the real-
time transcription but correctly in the note?
The real-time transcription shows an estimate of your spoken
words. When the recording is submitted for note generation,
Abridge polishes the output to catch errors when possible.
What happens if my device loses network or WiFi connection
while recording in Verbatim Mode?
Verbatim Mode will stop working until the connection is restored.
If the network is interrupted or offline, the preview will stop
transcribing.
Is Verbatim Mode available via Web Recording?
At this time, Verbatim Mode is a mobile-only feature.12

This is a mobile-only release; Web Recording is TBD
It's not dictation or voice-to-text… it's even better. Verbatim content is run through our
ASR during note generation, ensuring clinical accuracy.
Feature/Solution
Verbatim Mode allows clinicians to switch into word-for-word capture, for either a
snippet or for the entire note. This may be used alongside an ambient recording.
Verbatim Mode also allows clinicians to add more Verbatim content after the note is
generated in the mobile preview.
Verbatim Note: Generates a standalone note as an alternative to producing a
summarized note from an ambient recording.

precision is a priority over summarization.

Diagnostic rationale: "Given the patient's history…"
Augmentation: Clinicians have expressed the desire to add verbal content after
note generation.

RELEASE #25.03 – MARCH 25TH, 2025

We're aiming to reduce touchpoints from capture to send for most notes.

notes.abridge.com

Abridge Integrated users will now be able to review and send their generated note, right
from the Abridge mobile app.

text:
EpicUUID: 03AAD6C2-6EB6-4152-AD88-0756AD63A31C
Epic-Led Thrive Training for Physicians
A Personalized Epic Experience
Happy, efficient providers are better at helping patients get healthy and stay healthy. After going live
with a new EHR, many physicians can benefit from extra support to help take advantage of all the new
features, maximizing their productivity and allowing them to spend more time with patients. Epic’s
post-live training program, Thrive, helps providers improve their mastery of the system by focusing on
efficiency tips and customization.
Thrive is a hands-on, workshop-style class taught by Epic trainers. During class, attendees learn to
complete common workflows more efficiently and update key user settings to suit them. Working with
small classes, trainers can address individual questions and ensure that physicians leave Thrive with
personalization settings updated in their live environment. Just two hours in Thrive can help providers
save time daily by making Epic better serve their needs, giving them back time with patients.
Program Details
Interested? Start the discussion with your BFF.
© 2023 Epic Systems Corporation
Audience
Physicians who use EpicCare Ambulatory, EpicCare Inpatient, or ASAP. Some
organizations choose to send a subset of super users, but we recommend Thrive for
all providers who use these applications.
Cost
On-Site: $2000 per trainer per day
Virtual: $100 per provider track
Class Format
Each Thrive training track consists of two 1–2-hour classes with no more than 15
students at a time. Epic trainers lead class to ensure that your providers get the
latest recommendations.
While we strongly recommend an onsite initial trip to build excitement and get
buy-in for the program, the classes area available in person or live via video call.
Registration & Reporting
