Use Case 9: Generate a callback script for a difficult conversation
Need to call a patient about a missed referral, declined coverage, or scheduling conflict? Get a script
first.
"I need to call a patient to let them know their imaging order needs additional pre-auth, which
means a 1-week delay. Draft a 60-second call script: empathetic opening, clear explanation,
what we're doing about it, ask if they have questions."
Use Case 10: Document a workflow or SOP for your team
Asked to write up how you handle a recurring scenario? Outline it with Chat in 5 minutes.
"Draft a one-page SOP for how our front-desk team handles a walk-in who has insurance we
don't accept. Cover: greeting, options to offer (cash pay, financial counseling, referral out), what
to document, when to escalate to the office manager."
Quick-start prompts to save
• "Translate this into plain English for the patient. 6th-grade reading level."
• "Draft a [type of message] to a patient about [situation]. Friendly, professional tone, under
[length]."
• "Give me 3 opening lines for a [type of call]. Empathetic, not defensive."
• "Now respond as the patient — what might they say back?"
Your one-week challenge
Pick 2 of the 10 use cases above. Try them this week on real work (de-identified). Save the
prompts that worked. Those saved prompts become your team's first Assistants when UTHSA
opens Assistant Builder org-wide.

title: Qualified Chat for Physicians and APPs UTHSA Training Module
text:
QUALIFIED HEALTH × UTHSA
Qualified Chat for Physicians & APPs — UTHSA Training Module · Page 1
Qualified Chat for Physicians & APPs
Practical AI use cases for UTHSA physicians and advanced practice providers.
Why this matters
Qualified Chat is HIPAA-compliant AI made for clinicians — your version of ChatGPT, but safe
to paste de-identified clinical detail into. Most physicians at peer institutions save 30–60 minutes
a day on documentation, patient education, and the email overhead that eats clinic time. This
guide shows you how to use Chat well, when to build a reusable Assistant, and 10 high-
leverage use cases.
Part 1 — How to use Qualified Chat (and when to build an Assistant)
Getting started in 60 seconds
• Log in: chat.qualifiedhealthai.com using your UTHSA email.
• Type your clinical question or paste de-identified info. Be specific about role and audience.
• Save your best prompts — the second use is 10x faster than the first.
PHI guardrails (because you'll ask)
Qualified Chat is HIPAA-compliant — you can paste de-identified clinical scenarios safely. Best
practice: strip identifiers (name, MRN, DOB) before pasting, and use placeholders like "72 y/o
female, day 4 post-op CABG, on amiodarone." Never paste full identifiers into any other AI tool
(ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot) — only Qualified Chat is sanctioned at UTHSA for PHI-adjacent
work.
Chat vs. Assistant — when to build a reusable one
A Chat is a one-off. An Assistant is a tuned mini-app — same setup, same knowledge base,
every time. If you keep asking variations of the same question (e.g., "give me a one-page
patient handout on X at 6th-grade level"), build an Assistant once and skip the setup forever.

Use Case 2: Differential diagnosis brainstorm
Stuck on a vague presentation? Ask Chat to walk through differentials with you — then push back to

"Walk through the differential for a 55 y/o male with 2 weeks of post-prandial epigastric pain,

Pro tip: Always add "think step-by-step" — accuracy on clinical reasoning goes up meaningfully.
Use Case 3: Draft a referral letter or insurance prior-auth justification
Paste the relevant clinical context (de-identified) and ask Chat to write the letter.
"Draft a prior-auth justification letter to insurance for an MRI of the cervical spine for a 48 y/o
with 6 weeks of radicular arm pain unresponsive to conservative management. Reference
standard imaging criteria. Tone: professional, clinical, persuasive."
Use Case 4: Summarize a long research article into a clinical TL;DR
Paste the abstract (or upload the PDF), get back a 3-bullet TL;DR plus a 2-bullet "would this change
my practice" judgment.
"TL;DR this NEJM article in 3 bullets. Then 2 bullets on methodology I should know. Then 1
bullet: would this change how I manage [my patient population]?"

follow up."

Need a fast clinical reference? Ask Chat — and demand it think step-by-step on anything involving
math or interactions.
"What's the recommended dose adjustment for apixaban in a patient with CrCl 28? Walk

Use Case 8: Draft a FMLA, school, or work-excuse letter
Recurring admin task that takes 10 minutes? Make it 60 seconds.
"Draft a return-to-work letter for a 42 y/o who had a knee scope 2 weeks ago. Cleared for desk
work, no prolonged standing for 4 more weeks. Address to employer, professional tone."
Use Case 9: Brainstorm a difficult conversation
End-of-life, addiction, weight loss, treatment refusal — ask Chat to suggest an opening that's
compassionate and direct. Then refine to your voice.
"I need to have a goals-of-care conversation with the family of a patient with end-stage HF.
Suggest a 3-sentence opening that invites them to share what they understand. Then suggest 3
follow-up questions to ask."
Pro tip: Roleplay with Chat as the family member to anticipate hard responses.
Use Case 10: Polish your own writing — abstracts, grants, presentations
Drafting a poster, abstract, conference talk, or grant aim? Use Chat as a tireless editor.
"Tighten this abstract for a clinical research conference. Keep under 250 words. Make the
methods crisper and the conclusion more specific. Active voice. Don't change the data."

QUALIFIED HEALTH × UTHSA
Qualified Chat for Nurses — UTHSA Training Module · Page 1
Qualified Chat for Nurses
Practical AI use cases for the UTHSA nursing team — built around your real workflows.
Why this matters
Qualified Chat is HIPAA-compliant AI made for your day-to-day. It can save 30–60 minutes a
shift on the tasks that take time but don't take skill — patient education, handoff prep, charting
polish, family questions. This guide shows nurses how to use Chat well, when to build a
reusable assistant, and 10 concrete use cases you can try this week.
Part 1 — How to use Qualified Chat (and when to build an Assistant)
Getting started in 60 seconds
• Log in: chat.qualifiedhealthai.com using your UTHSA email.
• Click "New conversation," type your question, hit enter.
• Pin your most-used chats so they stay at the top of your sidebar.
Stay safe with PHI
Qualified Chat is HIPAA-compliant — you can paste de-identified clinical info safely. Never
paste full identifiers (name, MRN, DOB together). When in doubt, swap details for placeholders:
"a 72 y/o post-op female on day 2 of warfarin" works just as well as the real chart.
Chat vs. Assistant — when to use which
A regular Chat is great for one-off questions. An Assistant is a mini-chatbot tuned to one
repeated job — same instructions, same knowledge base, every time. If you find yourself typing
the same setup prompt 3+ times a week, that's the signal to build an Assistant.
• Use Chat for: one-time questions, ad-hoc summarization, quick lookups.
• Use an Assistant for: discharge instruction drafts, patient education in plain English, shift
handoff templates, common family-question scripts.

• Use an Assistant for: discharge instruction drafts, patient education in plain English, shift

Assistants coming soon to your team
UTHSA is rolling Assistants out org-wide after the June Build-a-Thon. You'll be among the first
to build one for your unit. Until then, get fluent in Chat — every prompt you save now becomes
the starter for your first Assistant.
Two example Assistants nurses should build first
• "Plain-English Patient Educator" — paste any discharge instruction or med info, get back a
6th-grade reading level version.
• "Shift Handoff Helper" — paste your SBAR notes, get back a tight, structured handoff your
colleague can scan in 30 seconds.
Part 2 — Ten Use Cases You Can Try This Week
Use Case 1: Translate discharge instructions to plain language
Paste the discharge instructions and ask Chat to rewrite at a 6th-grade reading level. Cuts patient
confusion and reduces "why am I taking this?" callbacks.
"Rewrite these discharge instructions at a 6th-grade reading level. Use short sentences. Keep
all warnings and red-flag symptoms. End with a one-line summary of when to call us."
Pro tip: Add "in Spanish" at the end and you've got a translated version too.

Qualified Chat for Nurses — UTHSA Training Module · Page 2
Use Case 2: Draft a SOAP note from messy shift notes
Dictate or paste your shift notes (de-identified) and ask Chat to structure them into a clean SOAP
format.
"Organize the following clinical notes into a SOAP note. Keep the language clinical but concise.
Flag anything that looks incomplete."
Use Case 3: Explain a medication to a worried family member
Family member doesn't understand why their parent is on a new med? Drop the med name and ask
Chat to write a 100-word explanation in plain English.
"Explain metoprolol to a family member with no medical background. Why we use it, common
side effects in plain language, and when to call the nurse. Under 100 words."
Use Case 4: Build a quick shift handoff summary
Paste your patient list and notes for the shift, ask Chat to organize into a clean handoff.
"Take these 6 patient notes and turn them into a structured shift handoff: room, name (use
placeholders), one-line status, key changes this shift, action items for next shift."
Pro tip: Save this prompt — it's your first Assistant in the making.
Use Case 5: Look up a clinical guideline fast
Need a quick refresher on a protocol? Ask Chat — and follow up with "how would I apply this to a
72-year-old with renal impairment?"
"Summarize the SCD prevention guideline for post-op patients. Then tell me what would
change for a patient with active GI bleed."
Pro tip: Always verify against your unit's protocol before acting — AI is a great first-pass reference, not a
substitute for the policy doc.

Use Case 6: Polish a difficult email or message to a provider
Need to send a tactful note to an attending about a missed order? Draft it rough, paste it in, ask Chat
to soften the tone while keeping the urgency.
"Rewrite this email to a physician about a missed order. Keep it professional and concise. Make
the ask clear but the tone collegial — not accusatory."
Use Case 7: Generate patient education on a new diagnosis
Patient was just diagnosed with afib and is overwhelmed. Generate a one-page handout they can
take home.
"Write a one-page patient handout on atrial fibrillation. 6th-grade reading level. Cover: what it is,
why we treat it, what they should watch for, when to call us. Use simple bullet points and a
friendly tone."
Use Case 8: Brainstorm how to approach a tough family conversation
End-of-life conversation coming up? Ask Chat to suggest a 3-minute opening that's compassionate
and honest. Then refine.
"I need to start a goals-of-care conversation with the family of a patient with end-stage CHF.
Give me a 3-sentence opening that's warm, honest, and invites them to share what they

Pro tip: Roleplay with Chat: "Now respond as a grieving spouse — what might they say back?"
Use Case 9: Summarize a long chart you're inheriting
Just got a new patient mid-shift with a 30-page chart? Paste the relevant sections (de-identified) and
ask for a 60-second briefing.
"Summarize this chart for me in 5 bullets: active issues, current meds, recent labs/imaging
worth knowing, anything pending, and what I should hand off at end of shift."
Use Case 10: Draft a quick policy or huddle script
Charge nurse asked you to lead morning huddle on a new fall-prevention protocol? Ask Chat to draft
a 3-minute script.
"Draft a 3-minute morning huddle script introducing our new fall-prevention protocol. Friendly
tone, end with one specific thing each nurse should do today."
Quick-start prompts to save
• "Rewrite this for a [audience] in plain English under [length]."
• "Summarize this in 5 bullets — what changed, what's pending, what I should hand off."
• "Walk through your reasoning step-by-step before giving your answer."
• "You are a [role]. Help me with [task] for [audience]."
Your one-week challenge
Pick 2 of the 10 use cases above. Try them this week with real (de-identified) work. Save the
prompts that worked best — those become your starter Assistants when UTHSA opens
Assistant Builder org-wide.

title: Abridge Support Tip Sheet
text:
Providers can quickly determine the appropriate support team to contact when issues arise within Abridge. Understanding which help desk to contact can reduce delays, improve issue resolution times, and ensure Providers receive the correct support as efficiently as possible.
Providers should contact the Abridge Help Desk for issues directly related to Abridge functionality, such as note generation concerns, microphone or recording issues within the Abridge application, missing transcripts, or problems with AI-generated documentation.
Click on Support under the Abridge Tab in Hyperspace to directly contact the Abridge Help Desk.
The UT Health Epic Support Help Desk should be contacted for Epic-related concerns, including login issues, workflow problems within Epic, or technical issues affecting the Epic environment.
To contact UT Health Epic Support, Press F1 to Submit a Ticket or contact at (210) 450-4800 opt.1
By using this tip sheet as a guide, you can streamline the support process, minimize downtime, and help maintain efficient clinical workflows.

text:
CONFIDENTIAL & PROPRIETARY
INPATIENT USE GUIDANCE
Leverage Abridge when performing back-to-back admissions, reducing the cognitive
burden of remembering details from multiple encounters and improving note accuracy.
Use Abridge for the History and Physical (H&P) and initial Consultation notes.
Use the “comprehensive” setting for the HPI and the “bulleted” version of the A/P.
H&P/ADMISSION NOTE, INITIAL CONSULT NOTE
Pre-chart with Abridge by capturing interval history from morning rounds
or discussions with other staff to add additional context for progress
notes.
Use Abridge for the “Subjective” and “Physical Exam”.
The A/P may be helpful for progress notes; however, we know most
users typically refer to the A/P from the previous day’s note.
PROGRESS NOTE
Ensure all recordings are completed within 24 hours of beginning.
For the most robust note possible, monologue key details about the patient before or after the visit, including
interval history, or additional medical decision making.
KEY TIPS33

title: UTHSCSA Prompt Editing One-Pager
text:
Prompt Editing
No more manual edits — tell Abridge exactly what you want your note to look like, in plain language.
WHAT IS PROMPT EDITING?
Prompt editing lets you revise a clinical note using
plain-language instructions instead of manual edits.
Type what you want changed, and Abridge AI
interprets the request and suggests a revision — you
review it and accept or reject the change.
WHERE TO FIND IT
Prompt editing lives in the Abridge AI tab next to
your note — available anywhere Abridge AI is
enabled, including notes.abridge.com, Inside, and
mobile. The same tab also offers clinical decision
support and note preferences.
HOW TO USE IT
1. Record and generate a note in Abridge.
2. Open the note and select the Abridge AI tab.
3. Type a prompt describing the change you want
(e.g., "make note more concise").
4. Review the suggested edits. Accept or reject each
change, and keep refining with additional prompts
as needed.
5. Save prompts you use often by selecting the
bookmark icon — access them anytime from the
bookmark icon in the prompt editor.
PROMPT VS. PREFERENCE — WHICH SHOULD I
USE?
USE A PROMPT
For a one-time change to
this note only. Type it,
review the result, done.
USE A PREFERENCE
When you catch yourself
typing the same
instruction note after
note. Save it once, and
Abridge applies it
automatically to every
future note.
Turn any accepted prompt into a preference with one
click, or save one directly from the bookmarks panel.
Preferences can be viewed, edited, or removed at any
time.
HOW TO WRITE AN EFFECTIVE PROMPT
Good prompts are specific — name the section, and

HOW TO WRITE AN EFFECTIVE PROMPT
Good prompts are specific — name the section, and
describe exactly what you want. Four things you can
ask for:
Add "Include a family history section in my HPI,
using everything discussed."
Replace "Replace ‘Zoloft’ with sertraline in the HPI
and A&P."
Reorganize "Make my assessment and plan
system-based."
Adjust Style "Make the HPI more concise without
removing clinical meaning."
Tip: Start simple, then get more specific. You can
always send another prompt to further refine the
result.
SIMPLE TO COMPLEX: EXAMPLE PROMPTS
SIMPLE
"Make my HPI more concise."
INTERMEDIATE
"Add a two-sentence summary at the
beginning of my note."
COMPLEX
"Format my HPI as follows, filling in each
section from the relevant conversation. If not
discussed, write ‘not discussed’: Last ADHD
addressed / Current medications / School
performance / Behavior."

title: AI-Text-Assistant-One-Sheet
text:
EPI C AI T EXT AS S IS TANT — CUS TO M I NS T RUC TIO NS
It is not just a reformatter.
The built-in prompts clean up text. Custom instructions let you specify voice, reading level, structure, and constraints —
which turns the same button into a compression engine, a note converter, a pre-signature safety check, and a teaching tool.
SIX THINGS MOST PEOPLE NEVER TRY
1. Compress a wall of text to only what matters
Turn tens of pages of imaging in a discharge summary into
study name, date, and impression — radiologist's wording
untouched. Also works for abnormal labs only, consult
recommendations only, med changes only.
2. Rewrite for the family, in your voice
Not generic "patient-friendly." You control person (first, not
third), reading level, jargon substitution, whether it reads as a
letter, and numbered next steps with a stated callback
window.
3. Convert one note type into another
A resident's daily progress note into a draft attending
attestation — attestation statement, interval events, exam,
numbered A&P. Output has sections the input never had.
4. Read your note back to you before you sign
Flags contradictions, med/allergy conflicts, unaddressed
abnormals, copied-forward text, and framing that calls a
patient stable when the data disagree. Capped at five bullets.
5. Generate a teaching point from the case
A 20-word clinical pearl plus a Socratic question for the
resident. Never goes in the chart — read it, use it, delete it.
6. Write your interval history for you
Select the copied-forward or ambient content and get a short
"In the last visit…" paragraph in past tense, plus the treatment

title: AI-Text-Assistant-One-Sheet
text:
6. Write your interval history for you
Select the copied-forward or ambient content and get a short
"In the last visit…" paragraph in past tense, plus the treatment
plan stated in definitive terms — was started, was increased,
was referred — never softened into "discussed" unless it truly
was.
WHAT SEPARATES A PROMPT THAT WORKS
Assign a role. "You are an attending physician" anchors
vocabulary and register.
Say whose voice it is. Third-person drift is the most
common failure.
Write the negatives. "Do not add, remove, or infer." It
pads unless told not to.
Name a reading level. "Sixth-grade, especially for
anatomical terms" beats "make it simple."
Bound the output. Max bullets, one sentence each,
"include no other sections."
Define the fallback. "If nothing qualifies, do X instead"
stops it inventing findings to fill your format.
TWO PROMPTS TO TRY TODAY
Radiology impressions only
Highest-ROI prompt here. Select the imaging block in a discharge
summary.
The selected text contains radiology imaging reports. Keep
only the study name, the study date, and any section
labeled Impression or Conclusion. Delete everything else.
Do not alter the wording of the impression or conclusion.
Format each entry as the study name followed by the date in
parentheses, in bold, on its own line. Place the impression
on the next line with no blank line between them, and do
not bold or italicize it. Remove any line beginning with
"Report Verified by" or "Approved by".
Highest-priority fixes before signing
Read the output, then undo. Do not accept it. See the warning
below.
Review the selected note for documentation quality,
internal consistency, clinical framing, and patient safety
problems. Look for contradictions, mismatches between

title: AI-Text-Assistant-One-Sheet
text:
Highest-priority fixes before signing
Read the output, then undo. Do not accept it. See the warning
below.
Review the selected note for documentation quality,
internal consistency, clinical framing, and patient safety
problems. Look for contradictions, mismatches between
framing and documented data, medication or allergy
conflicts, unaddressed abnormal findings, diagnoses or
plans unsupported by the note, copied-forward or outdated
text, timeline or anatomic errors, and unclear follow-up
ownership. Pay particular attention to any place the
patient is described as stable, well-controlled, low-risk,
routine, or asymptomatic when the documented data suggest
otherwise.
Do not assume any fact not explicitly stated in the note.
Do not offer medical advice.
Output only a section titled "Highest priority fixes before
signing." Maximum five bullets, one sentence each. Include
only genuine safety risks or major contradictions, with no
explanations. If no high-priority issues exist, title the
section "For your consideration" and list the top three
lower-priority fixes instead. Assume the reader has thirty
seconds. Include no other sections.
Four things to know before you start
The output replaces your selected text. On any
review or teaching prompt, read it and undo (Ctrl+Z).
Do not click accept out of habit.
Getting error C1001? Add the line "Do not offer
medical advice" to your prompt. It usually clears
the guardrail.
SmartBlocks cannot be selected. If your A&P is
dynamic, the Assistant will not run on it.
Spell out abbreviations. Requests have failed on
terms like MDM, and on text containing both English
and a translation.

- Update:

- July 9 course stats, 22 participated / 9 submitted survey:
- (9) Overall: 6-Excellent, 2-Good, 1-Fair
- (5) Relevancy: 3-Strong agree, 2-Agree
- (8) Save Time: 1-Strongly agree, 3-Agree, 2-Neutral, 2-Disagree
- (5) Recommend: 4-Yes, 1-No*
- (4) Testimonials:
- Learned ways to automate order entry, particularly meds
- Very good course
- It really gave me a better understanding about navigating through EPIC and using Templates
- Was able to clean up rarely used buttons, create "favorite" orders for more efficiency and a smartlink also for more note taking efficiency, less typing
- * First, thank you for investing in EPIC training and providing these learning opportunities. I appreciate the effort that went into developing and delivering the session.
One observation I had is that the content seemed geared toward users who are relatively new to EPIC. While that foundational information is certainly valuable, I wonder if there may be an opportunity to offer a more advanced track for experienced clinicians.
Given the significant time commitment of a three-hour session for busy clinical faculty, I believe the training could be even more impactful if it included more advanced functionality and workflow optimization strategies. For example, I was hoping to learn more about topics such as SmartSets, customization options, and approaches to improving team workflows. These areas were touched on only briefly, and additional depth would have been very valuable.

title: Epic Provider Training Requirements
text:
Register For Your Epic Learning
Page 1
Epic Training for New and Existing Providers
To ensure you have the appropriate Epic access for your role, you may be required to complete
additional Epic training if you are:
A new provider joining UT Health, or
Current UT Health Employee Requiring Additional Access
Examples: new MSRH privileges, KSP ASC privileges, or other expanded clinical access.
Please refer to page 3 to determine which Epic training courses are required for your role and practice
location.
Please read the following carefully:
It is recommended that the web-based training [WBT] is completed before attending
instructor-led training [BLT or ILT].
You must register to attend the in-person training [BLT or ILT] no later than 3:00pm one
business day before class to ensure that training materials will be prepared.
At the end of this document is a repository of provider onboarding education by
specialty. It includes direct links to learning enrollments to save time in searching.
Use the following steps to enroll/complete your WBT Epic learning:
1. Open Google Chrome and navigate to UTHSCSA.edu.
2. Select Search/Quicklinks and select UT Health Learns from the Login section.
3. Sign in with UTHSCSA-Azure to log in with your UTHSCSA credentials.
4. Click the UT Health Learns icon.
5. The My Learning folder opens. Click Learning Catalog along the bottom of the screen.
6. Search for the course that matches the specific specialty.
7. Click Enroll.
8. Click Launch next to each required module until all modules are complete.
You may need to click the expand arrows to the right of the module title to see the Launch
button.
Use the following steps to complete the BLT scheduled classroom training:

title: Epic Provider Training Requirements
text:
You may need to click the expand arrows to the right of the module title to see the Launch
button.
Use the following steps to complete the BLT scheduled classroom training:
1. Open Google Chrome and navigate to UTHSCSA.edu
2. Select Search/Quicklinks and select UT Health Learns from the Login section.
3. Sign in with UTHSCSA-Azure to log in with your UTHSCSA credentials.

title: Epic Provider Training Requirements
text:
Register For Your Epic Learning
Page 2
4. Log in with your UTHSCSA credentials.
5. Click the UT Health Learns icon.
6. The My Learning folder opens. Click Learning Catalog along the bottom of the screen.
7. Completion match in the Search for learning field for the course you are looking for.
8. Available Offerings appear for you to select a date to attend. Click Enroll to complete registration.
The date listed in the TITLE of the offering is when the class occurs.
9. The page will update and the class you enrolled in appears. You will not be able to complete this
section until the day of training.
10. You will receive an email from the class instructor one business day before the scheduled training.
Read the email carefully as it will include important classroom logistics.
Providers will not receive Epic access until the credentialing process is complete. It is highly
recommended that you attend training no more than two weeks before your first day of clinic.
Please reach out to the Epic Training Team with any questions at epiccaretrainingteam@uthscsa.edu or
210-450-4800 option 1. Thanks!
ATTENTION PREVIOUS EPIC USERS AND UHS EPIC USERS:
You may be exempt from completing the web-based training and/or instructor-led training. Send
an email to EpicCareTrainingTeam@uthscsa.edu for instructions to complete the Ambulatory
Provider Previous User Simulation and Assessment.
Please note that this option is only available to ambulatory providers. Basic Epic provider access
will be granted with a successful completion of the course; some specialties (such as
Oncology/Beacon, Orthopaedics/Bones, etc.), may require additional in-person, virtual, or web-
based training.

Year in Review
UT Health San Antonio
Epic 2024
- **You**: 260,000 care gaps closed with external data reducing duplicative care & helping your patients stay healthier, longer.
**Epic community**: 475 million care gaps
- **You**: 1,400 hours of clinician time were saved processing medication refills with protocols that automatically present relevant criteria to the clinician.
**Epic community**: 7.3 million hours
- **You**: 4,000 appointments filled using Fast Pass, generating $250,000 in additional revenue.
**Epic community**: Patients were seen an average of 29 days sooner with Fast Pass.
- **You**: 4,100 hours saved with revenue cycle automation helping your system run efficiently and freeing up staff to focus on more complex work.
**Epic community**: 20.6 million hours
- **You**: Patients checked in online for 25% of appointments. At 3.5 minutes of staff time per appointment, that is 14,000 hours. This saved front desk staff an estimated $270,000.
**Epic community**: $296 million
- **21,000** notes were generated using ambient voice recognition integration into Epic, reducing time spent writing notes and improving provider satisfaction.
- Patients took action **14,000** times as a result of your campaigns improving preventive care and **engagement with your organization**.

Satisfaction remains high, with nearly 7 out of 10 respondents agreeing or strongly agreeing, and very few expressing dissatisfaction.
**EPIC IS RELIABLE**

Most users consider Epic reliable, with over two-thirds expressing agreement and only a small percentage reporting dissatisfaction.
**Dec. 2025**
Satisfaction with Epic's reliability is very high, with over 7 in 10 respondents agreeing or strongly agreeing, and only a small percentage expressing dissatisfaction.
**EPIC IS EASY TO USE**
**July 2025**
While most users find Epic easy to use, this category has the highest proportion of negative responses compared to others, indicating room for improvement in usability.
**Dec. 2025**
While most users find Epic easy to use, this category still has the highest proportion of negative responses compared to other areas, indicating usability improvements could make a difference.

- Neutral slightly up.

text:
Image: Abridge Quick start guide page 2
Folder: Images1
File name: Abridge Quick start guide page 2.jpg
FAQ infographic answering common provider questions about using Abridge with Epic, Haiku and Canto, plus support contacts.
ABRIDGE FAQs
Answers to your most common questions
How do I get started?
Download Haiku (mobile/tablet) or Canto (iPad), register your device, then launch Abridge from a scheduled patient.
How do I access the Abridge tab in Epic?
Click on a patient encounter on a desktop version of Epic. Click the More icon to access More Activities. Pin the "Abridge" option.
How do I pull the Abridge note into my report?
- .HPISEC — History of Present Illness
- .RESULTSEC — Results
- .PESSEC — Physical Exam
- .APSEC — Assessment & Plan
You can also add these SmartPhrases into your existing note templates using SmartPhrase Manager.
Can I customize my notes?
Yes. Click on the Abridge Tab in Epic and use the Prompting feature to personalize note structure, content, and formatting. Your preferences can be saved for future notes.
How do specialty note templates work?
Abridge automatically assigns a specialty template based on your department. You can view or adjust your specialty settings in the Settings menu.
Can more than one provider use Abridge for the same encounter?
Only one provider can record a note for a single encounter. An attending may record a resident's presentation. Patient providers may each create their own individual notes.
Can Abridge generate a Patient Visit Summary?
Yes! Use the SmartPhrase ASPES to generate an easy-to-read, plain-language summary for patients.
Why don't I see the Abridge icon in Haiku?

FAQ infographic answering common questions about using the Abridge ambient documentation tool in Epic, Haiku and Canto, with support contacts.
**ABRIDGE FAQs**
Answers to your most common questions
**How do I get started?**
Download Haiku (mobile/tablet) or Canto (iPad), register your device, then launch Abridge from a scheduled patient.
**How do I access the Abridge tab in Epic?**
Click on a patient encounter on a desktop version of Epic. Click the More icon to access More Activities. Pin the "Abridge" option.
**How do I pull the Abridge note into my report?**
- .HPISEC — History of Present Illness
- .RESULTSEC — Results
- .PESEC — Physical Exam
- .APSEC — Assessment & Plan
You can also add these SmartPhrases into your existing note templates using SmartPhrase Manager.
**Can I customize my notes?**
Yes. Click on the Abridge Tab in Epic and use the Prompting feature to personalize note structure, content, and formatting. Your preferences can be saved for future notes.
**How do specialty note templates work?**
Abridge automatically assigns a specialty template based on your department. You can view or adjust your specialty settings in the Settings menu.
**Can more than one provider use Abridge for the same encounter?**
Only one provider can record a note for a single encounter. An attending may record a resident's presentation. Patient providers may each create their own individual notes.
**Can Abridge generate a Patient Visit Summary?**
Yes! Use the SmartPhrase .PVSSEC to generate an easy-to-read, plain-language summary for patients.

text:
Single Billing Office (SBO)
New Feature
UT Health can use Resolute Hospital Billing and Resolute Professional Billing together to send a single patient statement that includes balances from both systems.
Patients can send one check and set up one payment plan for both balances.
If a patient is confused about their bill, they can talk to a customer service representative who can answer questions about both balances.
SBO addresses the patient billing needs of a combined billing office. It focuses only on the self-pay aspects and is not designed to affect insurance workflows.

We have enhanced our proxy access process for individuals under the age of 18 to provide a more seamless and user-friendly experience. Here's a detailed overview:
Parents or guardians can conveniently access the Under 18 Proxy Form in two ways: directly from the prominent link on the main MyChart page or through the MyChart account menu. This ensures accessibility for all users within the platform.
Upon selecting the Under 18 Proxy Form, parents or guardians will be guided through a straightforward process to provide necessary information and permissions. The form is designed to be user-friendly and efficient.
Once the form is completed, it is automatically routed to the HIM’s department in-basket. HIM reviews and processes the proxy access request, prioritizing security and compliance. Awareness
Users
Type and % of User Base
Access Summary
1- Analytics End Users

SlicerDicer is one of Epic’s self-service reporting tool that allows users to easily adjust and improve queries and handle large data sets. Adoption of this feature has the potential to decrease report requests and will allow users to get the information they need more quickly.
Tier based analytics security structure, approved by the Analytics Council leadership, will be enabled in April 2024. Based on tier assignments, 90% of UTH Epic users will have access to SlicerDicer functionality and will be able to access 25 out of 33 core data models.

New and Seasoned providers are typically taught efficiency tips and tricks by their colleagues rather than through formal training after onboarding. This can result in a deviation of best practices leading to inefficiency instead of efficiency. End User Settings Labs and Thrive curriculum educate physicians what tips and tricks to implement today.

title: Refuel Phase 2 - April 10 Go-Live (3.18 Updates)
text:
Pharmacy Dispense Unit Update
As of December 2021, Surescripts stopped accepting several potency unit codes including quantity of dispense units to outside pharmacies (such as bottle, pen, device, inhaler, puff, tube, mg, vial, syringe, package, bag , units, drops, ampule, bar, device, etc.) Because of this change, the commonly ordered medication records have been updated with allowable dispense units to ensure that Surescripts can accept what Epic sends. Epic will alert ordering providers at signing if an order is prescribed with a retired unit with a hard stop. For example, a disallowed dispense unit of “pen” will trigger an Order Validation warning to ensure the medication is ordered with an allowed dispense unit.

headingPath: Slide 6: Care Path For Childhood Obesity
text:
Care Path For Childhood Obesity
New Feature
Care Paths help tell the story of a patient's course of treatment for a symptom or diagnosis, making it easier to see what treatments and interventions a patient has already tried, and what the possible next steps might be. The Childhood Obesity Care Path suggests treatments plan via OurPractice Advisories based on the patient’s BMI. During subsequent visits, next steps will be based on lab results and whether the patient’s goals are being met. Giving providers access to this Foundation System tool will allow them to track and determine treatments for childhood obesity patients more easily.
Vitals will be entered for patient and if BMI criteria is met, the Childhood Obesity Care Path will appear under Care Path activity.
User will then be able to navigate to Best Practice section of patient Rooming Tab and select Modify Care Path to make the appropriate treatment plans. Care Path and next steps for patient be based upon goals being met. User can Resolve the Care Path when appropriate.

title: Phase 3 Manage Consent
text:
New Workflow
Amendments: Manage Consents and Treatment Plans
When a study is amended, study coordinators can keep consents and treatment plans up-to-date for patients. For a given amendment, they can indicate whether patients need to be re-consented and whether any updates are needed to their treatment plans.
Doing so helps research coordinators identify patients who are affected by the changes and ensure that they sign updated consent documents and receive modified treatment plans as appropriate.

title: Phase 3 Care Path
text:
Care Path For Childhood Obesity
New Feature
Care Paths help tell the story of a patient's course of treatment for a symptom or diagnosis, making it easier to see what treatments and interventions a patient has already tried, and
what the possible next steps might be. The Childhood Obesity Care Path suggests treatments plan via OurPractice Advisories based on the patient’s BMI. During subsequent visits, next
steps will be based on lab results and whether the patient’s goals are being met. Giving providers access to this Foundation System tool will allow them to track and determine
treatments for childhood obesity patients more easily.
Vitals will be entered for patient and if BMI criteria is met, the Childhood Obesity Care Path will appear
under Care Path activity.
User will then be able to navigate to Best Practice section of patient Rooming Tab and select Modify
Care Path to make the appropriate treatment plans. Care Path and next steps for patient be based
upon goals being met. User can Resolve the Care Path when appropriate.

title: Phase 3 Contraindicated Medication
text:
Contraindicated Medication Warnings for Research
When a patient is enrolled in a research study, the ordering provider will receive a notification if the patient is at risk of
taking a medication that could potential result in an harmful reaction or jeopardize their participation in the study. If you
see this warning, check the storyboard to identify the study the patient is in.
These warnings appear in the same locations and workflows as other medication warnings. If you feel the medication you
are ordering is necessary, please reach out to the principal investigator of the study for further discussion.
Note: This functionality is available on study-to-study basis.

The patient indicates whether he or she is interested in participating, and
an In Basket message is sent to the study team to follow up.

denials and quicker reimbursements. This means more reliable billing
and support for high-quality patient care.

text:
Ask Questions About Appointment Requests
When you have a question about an appointment request that's preventing you from scheduling the request,
you can get answers by sending an In Basket message to a clinician directly from an appointment request
workqueue. The In Basket message is linked to the appointment request, so you no longer need to add
request and patient information to your message.
This tip sheet shows you how to send a message from an appointment request workqueue. You can also send
messages from the following places:
 Active Requests tab on the Appointment Desk
 Appointment Request activity toolbar
 Requests toolbar in the Front Desk activity
 Shortcut menu in the Snapboard request depot
Send a Message
1. Select a request in an appointment request workqueue and click In Basket Msg to open the
Appointment Request message form.
2. The default message priority is Routine. Click High or Low to change the priority if needed.
3. Use the quick buttons to select the ordering user, authorizing provider, or referred by provider as a
recipient, or manually enter a recipient in the To field.
4. By default, responses are sent to you. To send responses to a pool instead, enter the pool in the Pool
for Responses field.
5. Enter a subject and your message.
6. Click Send.
In the Dates section, there are optional settings to delay sending the
message, set a due date for the recipient, and set an expiration date for
the message.
Continued on next page.

Check Responses to Messages
When a clinician responds to your message, a notification appears in the upper right corner of Hyperspace.
Click the notification to open the message in In Basket.
If you now have the information you need to schedule the request, return to the Depot to schedule it. You can
also click Schedule to open the request in Book It, if needed.
Continued on next page.

slide 1

Billing Letters
Overview
Utilizing additional billing letters, to improve the billing office processes.
Benefits
• Billing office staff need to contact patients, guarantors, providers, and insurance companies at
many points during the revenue cycle, and letters play an important role in this process.
• End users are able to edit any of the letters directly in Epic.
• Users can print letters immediately as part of their workflows but the letters can also be scheduled
to print using a batch job.
• The billing letters appear in MyChart
Operational Note
The additional billing letters don't change user workflows, so training is not needed.

title: Phase 3 Billing Statement
text:

Enhancements to Billing Statements
Overview
Utilizing updated billing statement enhancements allows us to design statements and detail bills.
This gives us increased control over how billing information is presented to guarantors.
Benefits
• Improve customer service by offering users and patients three ways to view the same statement.
• MyChart Statements
• Paper Statements
• Statements in Account Maintenance
• Design payment-related information to fit organizational needs.
• Exercise more control over statement and detail bill templates.
• Improve the quality of paperless statements guarantors view online.
• Enhance paperless billing integration with MyChart.
Operational Note
Billing Statements enhancements won't change user workflows, so training is not needed.

The rules within the Patient Workqueues have been changed to be consistent across the institution.
Patients with missing registration items or incomplete registration will now fall into the workqueue 14 days
prior to their appointment and stay in the workqueue 7 days after their scheduled appointment date.

title: Phase 3 CRM
text:
– slide 1
New Workflow
Call Management (CRM)
Call Management is Epic's application to help UT Health Access Center manage calls
and workload, both at the individual level and for the entire Access Center.
• Support a two-tier triage workflow. Front desk staff can
use the Call Hub and Phone Book activities to take
patient messages and route those messages to the
appropriate clinicians.
• Support calls regarding multiple family members. With
Family Switch, users taking a call for one patient can
quickly open a new triage call for a second family
member. This can be useful, for example, if a parent calls
on behalf of two sick children.
• Use a Computer Telephony Integration (CTI) service to
place and receive calls from their computer screens.

title: Phase 3 CRM
text:
– slide 2
New Workflow
Call Management (CRM)
The new Call Management System (CRM) is designed to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of our UT
Health Access Center personnel. This system will streamline call handling, enabling staff to manage a variety
of scenarios with ease, from scheduling appointments to addressing patient inquiries.
Schedule and Reschedule: Staff can
schedule new appointments and
reschedule existing ones while
documenting all relevant notes
pertaining to the call.
Updating Information: Staff can manage
general questions, such as updating patient
demographics and processing new Primary
Care Provider (PCP) requests.
Complaint Management: Staff can document
complaints and route them to the appropriate
department or individual for resolution.
Refills and New Requests: Staff can
handle medication refill requests, new
medication requests, and any
medication-related questions, routing
them through the in-basket for
processing.
Status Updates: Staff can assist
patients with questions about the
status of a referral by routing these
inquiries to the appropriate staff via
the in-basket.
Patient Enrollment: Staff can sign up
patients for MyChart, initiate proxy
access, and address any issues or
questions related to MyChart

title: Phase 3 CRM
text:
– slide 3
New Workflow
Call Management (CRM)
Training Plan
To ensure that all staff are fully prepared to utilize the new CRM system effectively,
the following training plan has been developed:
Lunch-and-Learn Sessions
Demonstrations and Q&A: Multiple sessions will be held to demonstrate the CRM
workflows and provide an opportunity for staff to ask questions.
Hands-on Practice
Simulations will be created for each workflow, allowing staff to practice and gain
confidence in using the system.
Tip Sheets and Quick Guides

text:
Charge Capture Navigator System
As UT Health San Antonio moves towards an integrated healthcare delivery
system, we are standardizing charging to ensure accurate revenue capture across
our Epic system at the appropriate points in a patient's care. The Charge Capture
Navigator streamlines this process by allowing charges for supplies, DME, clinic
procedures, and more to be captured consistently and efficiently within our
Ambulatory clinics. This eliminates the need to enter separate charge orders for
each item or procedure, while keeping clinical orders—such as those for labs,
imaging, medications, and procedures—focused on patient care and treatment
tracking.

text:
Dig Deeper into Supply and Demand
Track your past demand, KPIs, and trends using new components on the Outpatient Specialty Supply and
Demand dashboard, which was previously titled "Outpatient Supply and Demand - Next 7 Days."
Try It Out
From the My Dashboards activity, search for the Outpatient Specialty Supply and Demand dashboard. Refer to
the sections below for details about each new or updated component on the dashboard.
Past Demand
The Demand section is now labeled "Past Demand."
In the Appointment Demand component, you can see the average number of same-day appointments to help
you determine how you will reach full utilization by the end of the day. For example, if you see that you have
10 openings today and you average 10 same-day appointments, you can expect that same-day appointments
will fill those openings. If you don't average enough same-day appointments to fill all of your openings, you
can reach out to patients who are on the wait list or who have outstanding appointment requests.
The new Online Scheduling Summary component shows how many appointments were scheduled online and
how many of your scheduled appointments could have been scheduled online.
Appointment KPIs
In the Appointment KPIs section, appointment lead time now appears in separate components for returning
patients and new patients. The Cancellation Rates in 10 Day Window component has been replaced by the

 Appointments from Requests. Shows the percentage of appointments that are linked to a request. Use
this metric to give context to the other request-related metrics on the dashboard.
 MyChart Active No-Show Rate. Shows the no-show rate for patients who have an active MyChart

 Fast Pass Offers Scheduled. Shows the number of appointments that were scheduled when patients on

Workqueue Volume." Instead of a breakdown of appointment requests by status, you can now see the
number of overdue appointment requests and the number of appointment requests that are due soon for a
given workqueue. You can follow the links to each workqueue and look for requests to schedule if you need to
fill some openings.

text:
A Consolidated View of Arrival and Registration
Status
The front desk is the mission control center for keeping track of whether patients have arrived for their
appointments and are checked in. There are two new columns on the Department Appointments report for
front desk staff that consolidate all of the ways that patients can arrive and complete registration for their
appointments.
 The new Arrival Status column helps you tell where a patient is on their journey between getting their
appointment scheduled and arriving at the clinic. For example, the column shows if a patient's
appointment hasn't been confirmed or if they're currently checking in at a kiosk. If your organization
uses Hello Patient for self-arrival and the patient indicated when they will arrive, the patient's
estimated time of arrival appears in the column.
 The new Registration Status column shows an icon so you can quickly identify whether you will need
to complete registration for a patient's appointment. Possible statuses include whether there are
registration errors that need to be resolved, or whether the patient is currently checking themselves in
or is being checked in by another staff member.
Refer to the Try It Out section for information about all of the possible icons and text that can appear in these
new columns.

columns.

The Template Advisor sidebar appears on the right side of the screen in the Edit Template activity. The sidebar
contains two sections: the Overview and the Recommendations sections. The Overview section contains the
schedule utilization rings and the block outcomes bars. The Recommendations section contains the block issue
cards. Read on to learn about these sections.
The Schedule Utilization Rings
At the top of the sidebar, the schedule utilization rings display a percentage value for three measures of
template performance:
 The ring on the left is Past Schedulable No Warnings, which measures the percentage of templated
time that could be scheduled into without needing to override warnings.
 The middle ring is Past Schedule Utilization, which looks back at the template's utilization leading up to
today's calendar date. Any time that was scheduled into in the template is compared with the amount
of templated time to calculate this measure’s utilization percentage.
 The ring on the right is Future Schedule Utilization, which looks at the provider's utilization for
upcoming days in the specified date range. Appointment time scheduled into the provider's upcoming
template is compared with the amount of templated time available.
The Block Outcomes Bars
To help clinic managers and template builders understand how specific blocks on the template are
contributing to or hampering schedule utilization, the Block Outcomes bars break down how individual blocks

text:
Block usage is broken down into four outcomes:
 Used (dark green) represents appointment time scheduled into with a visit type associated with the
block on the slot.
 Alternative (light green) represents appointment time scheduled into through an alternative to the visit
type associated with the block without overruling the block. Alternative outcomes include:
• Time scheduled using another block on the same slot
• Time scheduled after the block released to another block
• Time scheduled after the block released to an unblocked slot
 Overruled (orange) represents appointment time scheduled into by overruling a block warning.
 Unused (red) represents appointment time for the block that was not scheduled into. This is unused
time on the schedule that is occupied by the block.
If the blocks that appear in the Block Outcomes section have release settings, you can view these settings by
clicking the More Info button in the section. The Template Advisor can identify whether the block releases to
another block, which block it releases to, how many days in advance, and whether the release settings are
configured at the provider or department-level, which is indicated by the provider icon or the department
icon.
The Issue Cards
Issue cards identify issues with template build for providers, such as blocks without associated visit types,
provider or department-level restrictions, mismatched visit type lengths, and visit type modifiers that don't
match the provider's slot lengths. The issue cards also flag upcoming held time that might require you to
update the provider’s template so no time goes unused unintentionally. Click the down arrows on the issue
cards to see affected slots, visit types, and advice for resolving the issue.

text:
There are three types of issues that the Template Advisor identifies in issue cards in the Recommendations
section:
 Unusable Block. This issue occurs when a block is on a provider’s template but cannot be scheduled
with that provider, for instance if there are scheduling restrictions set for that provider.
 Slot Length Mismatch. This issue occurs when the length of a slot does not evenly divide the default
visit length of the visit types associated with the block on that slot.
 Upcoming Unused Held Time. If there is held time on the provider’s template in the next 14 days, the
Template Advisor identifies the held time and recommends either marking it as unavailable or
removing the held time from the template, depending on the status of the held time. This issue type
helps you keep track of held time that might need to be re-evaluated as the day approaches.
On-the-Fly Settings
Click the gears icon in the top right corner of the sidebar to open the on-the-fly settings for the Template
Adivsor sidebar. The Template Advisor sidebar has two sections: the Overview, containing the Schedule
Utilization rings and Block Outcomes bars, and the Recommendations section, containing the issue cards. In
these on-the-fly settings, you can configure which of the two sections appear and whether to show the legend
for the Block Outcomes section. You can configure the date range for the Schedule Utilization rings in the
Overview section by setting the Overview Date Range option to either 7, 14, or 30 days.
Continued on next page.

text:
Example Workflow
You hear from a scheduler that one provider always seems to need a block override to be scheduled with. You
open the provider’s template in the Edit Template activity to investigate. You see in the Template Advisor
sidebar that the provider has a low value for the Past Schedulable No Warnings ring in the Schedule Utilization
rings section. Then, in the Recommendations section, you see that the New Patient block has a Slot Length
Mismatch issue card.
You look at the default length of the visit type listed in the issue card and see that it has a forty-minute default
length, while the slots for that block on the provider’s template are fifteen-minute slots. You adjust the slot
lengths for that block to twenty-minutes and apply the changes to the template. After the change is filed, you
see the Slot Length Mismatch issue card disappear. You return to the Edit Template activity a week later to see
the block outcomes bar for the New Patient block is all green.

text:
Ask Questions About Appointment Requests
When you have a question about an appointment request that's preventing you from scheduling the request,
you can get answers by sending an In Basket message to a clinician directly from an appointment request
workqueue. The In Basket message is linked to the appointment request, so you no longer need to add
request and patient information to your message.
This tip sheet shows you how to send a message from an appointment request workqueue. You can also send
messages from the following places:
 Active Requests tab on the Appointment Desk
 Appointment Request activity toolbar
 Requests toolbar in the Front Desk activity
 Shortcut menu in the Snapboard request depot
Send a Message
1. Select a request in an appointment request workqueue and click In Basket Msg to open the
Appointment Request message form.
2. The default message priority is Routine. Click High or Low to change the priority if needed.
3. Use the quick buttons to select the ordering user, authorizing provider, or referred by provider as a
recipient, or manually enter a recipient in the To field.
4. By default, responses are sent to you. To send responses to a pool instead, enter the pool in the Pool
for Responses field.
5. Enter a subject and your message.
6. Click Send.
In the Dates section, there are optional settings to delay sending the
message, set a due date for the recipient, and set an expiration date for
the message.
Continued on next page.

Follow Up on Incorrect Phone Numbers
To help ensure that guarantors can get billing notifications and other communication as needed, the system
flags incorrect phone numbers that need to be updated. The number might be incorrect because it's not a
valid phone number, it is disconnected, or it is the wrong type for the field.
Try It Out
Icons call attention to issues with phone numbers:
 The icon indicates that the phone number status query is currently processing.
 The icon indicates that the phone number entered is invalid. Remove this number and collect a
more up-to-date number if possible.
 The icon indicates that the number entered is the wrong type. For example, a landline phone
number is entered in a mobile field, or vice versa. Move the number to the correct field.
 The indicates that the phone number could not be verified.

text:
Customize Nurse Auto Assignment for Infusion
Visits
Adjust how nurses are automatically assigned to visits by the Visit Assignment Wizard.
Try It Out
1. In the Visit Assignment Wizard, select the drop-down menu next to the Auto Assign button.
2. Select Customize.
3. In the window that appears, drag the metrics into the order that matters most for your infusion center.
The metrics are evaluated from top to bottom. For example, if you want to assign visits first to the nurse
with the least total workload, drag the Lowest total workload metric to the top of the list.
 Lowest number of assignments. This metric prioritizes the nurse with the fewest total appointments.
 Lowest total workload. This metric prioritizes the nurse whose appointments have the least total
workload.
 Lowest number of concurrent appointments. This metric prioritizes the nurse with the fewest
overlapping appointments at the time of the appointment being assigned.
 Lowest total appointment length. This metric prioritizes the nurse with the fewest total minutes of
assigned appointment time.
4. Click Accept to save the order for the next time you use the Auto Assignment feature.

text:
Infusion Operational Overview Dashboard
When it comes to infusion scheduling, there are many factors that consider when determining how well your
infusion center is performing in terms of scheduling efficiency and visit volume. Success isn't defined solely by
having high schedule utilization. You also need to consider nursing workloads, delays caused by providers or
inaccurate infusion durations, scheduler productivity, and appointment lead times.
The Infusion Operational Overview dashboard shows data for all of these areas to help tell your infusion
center's scheduling story. For example, if you recently implemented the Infusion Scheduling Template
Generator activity or are planning to do so soon, you can use the dashboard to identify whether that effort is
helping to increase utilization, lower patient wait times, and even out nursing workloads.
To access the dashboard, search for "Infusion Operational Overview" in the My Dashboards activity.
Try It Out
The components on the dashboard are divided into the following groups.
Continued on next page.

sourceId: file:RefuelUpgrade/Refuel Phase 3/Beacon Upgrade Training Slides - Feb + May 2024.pdf
title: Beacon Upgrade Training Slides - Feb + May 2024

meta.file: Beacon Upgrade Training Slides - Feb + May 2024.pdf

id: file:RefuelUpgrade/Refuel Phase 3/Beacon Upgrade Training Slides - Feb + May 2024.pdf#24
text:
Utilization
How full is your schedule, how full are your nursing workloads, and how are add-ons, no-shows and late
cancellations contributing to your utilization metrics?
Chair Utilization
The Chair Utilization component shows total resource utilization. Utilization in this context is calculated by
dividing the total time of completed and arrived appointments by the total time of regular openings on the
schedule. The current month to date's utilization is included as a badge at the top of the component. Only
resource type providers are included. Resources marked as excluded from utilization reports are not included.
If your utilization rate is low and the lead time shown in the Access to First Treatment component is long, use
the Resource Time Lost or Gained component to determine whether the unused time in your schedules is
caused by no-shows and late cancellations.
Infusion Stats Per Nurse Hour
The Infusion Stats Per Nurse Hour component shows the total infusion hours and workload score per nurse
hour on a monthly basis. This component can help you understand whether the nursing workload has changed
over time. If it has, you can use other components on the dashboard to dig into why that's the case.
The workload score metric is calculated only if your organization has set up an outpatient workload scoring
system.
Add-Ons, No-Shows, and Late Cancels
The Add-Ons, No-Shows, and Late Cancels component shows the amount of schedulable time that was lost
due to late cancellations and no-show appointments, as well as the amount of time gained from add-on
appointments.
By default, a late cancellation is defined as a cancellation less than 24 hours before the scheduled

sourceId: file:RefuelUpgrade/Refuel Phase 3/Beacon Upgrade Training Slides - Feb + May 2024.pdf
title: Beacon Upgrade Training Slides - Feb + May 2024

meta.file: Beacon Upgrade Training Slides - Feb + May 2024.pdf

id: file:RefuelUpgrade/Refuel Phase 3/Beacon Upgrade Training Slides - Feb + May 2024.pdf#25
text:
due to late cancellations and no-show appointments, as well as the amount of time gained from add-on
appointments.
By default, a late cancellation is defined as a cancellation less than 24 hours before the scheduled
appointment time that wasn't filled by another appointment. Your organization might have configured a
different threshold.
An add-on appointment is defined as a completed appointment that was scheduled on the same day that it
took place.
If you're losing time to no-shows or late cancels,, ask your Epic project team about strategies you can use to
reduce your no-show rate.
Delays
Are infusions starting late or ending after the department has closed for the day? Are they being delayed
because a previous appointment ran long? Do patients with multiple appointments have long waits between
their appointments?
Infusion Start Time Delays
The Infusion Start Time Delays component shows the average time between when completed infusion visits
were scheduled to begin and when they actually began. The component shows a separate line for the average
wait times of only the visits that were scheduled during peak hours, as configured in the Infusion Scheduling
Continued on next page.

sourceId: file:RefuelUpgrade/Refuel Phase 3/Beacon Upgrade Training Slides - Feb + May 2024.pdf
title: Beacon Upgrade Training Slides - Feb + May 2024

meta.file: Beacon Upgrade Training Slides - Feb + May 2024.pdf

id: file:RefuelUpgrade/Refuel Phase 3/Beacon Upgrade Training Slides - Feb + May 2024.pdf#26
text:
Template Generator activity. If an appointment was checked in after the appointment's scheduled start time,
the check in time is used to calculate the wait time instead of the appointment start time.
If your wait times are high, review your staffing assignments to determine whether there are some nurses
who have higher workloads than others. There could be an opportunity to better balance workloads across
your nursing staff.
Provider-Caused Delays
The Provider-Caused Delays component shows the percentage of infusion visits that were delayed because the
patient had a prior appointment with a provider that ran longer than expected, and the delay isn't attributed
to the patient. Any infusion visit that doesn't meet one of the following conditions is considered to have
started late because of a provider delay for a prior appointment:
 The patient checked in for their infusion visit before the scheduled start time, so there is no delay.
 The patient checked in late for their first appointment of the day, so the delay is attributed to the
patient.
 The patient had a prior appointment that ended with enough time for them to get to their infusion visit
on time, but the patient checked in late for their infusion visit, so the delay is attributed to the patient.
Travel time and patient prep and recovery time are considered when determining whether a patient
had enough time between when the prior appointment ended according to End Visit event and the
scheduled start time of their infusion visit.
Use the drilldown report to identify specific providers to follow up with and determine why their
appointments are running long.
After Closure Finishes

sourceId: file:RefuelUpgrade/Refuel Phase 3/Beacon Upgrade Training Slides - Feb + May 2024.pdf

id: file:RefuelUpgrade/Refuel Phase 3/Beacon Upgrade Training Slides - Feb + May 2024.pdf#27
text:
scheduled start time of their infusion visit.
Use the drilldown report to identify specific providers to follow up with and determine why their
appointments are running long.
After Closure Finishes
The After Closure Finishes component shows the number of infusion visits that lasted beyond the
department's close time. The department close time is determined by the following:
 The latest end time for nursing staff that's defined in the Infusion Scheduling Template Generator
activity.
 If no shift times are defined in the Infusion Scheduling Template Generator activity, then the closing
time defined in the Hours of Operation activity is used.
 If a closing time isn't specified in the Hours of Operation activity, then the latest end time for schedule
templates in the department is used.
Use the drilldown reports to view appointment details so you can follow up to find out why the appointment
didn't finish on time. Likely reasons are that the visit started late or the scheduled infusion duration wasn't
accurate, so you can use this component in conjunction with the Infusion Start Time Delays, Provider-Caused
Delays, and Duration Accuracy components to get the full picture.
Patient Layovers
The Patient Layovers component shows the average layover length, or time between appointments for
patients who have multiple appointments. Patient layover time is the total time between the end of one
appointment and the start of the next appointment.
Continued on next page.

sourceId: file:RefuelUpgrade/Refuel Phase 3/Beacon Upgrade Training Slides - Feb + May 2024.pdf

text:
Volumes
Are your visit volumes and revenue trending up or down? Do certain days of the week have more visits than
others?
Patients Per Day
The Patients Per Day component shows the number of unique patients with appointments by day of week.
Data for time periods longer than one week are averaged. Only patients with at least one completed
appointment on that date are included.
If you find that you are scheduling more appointments on certain days than others, you might need to adjust
your staffing on those days, or you might want to adjust your scheduling templates to even out the number of
patients seen each day.
Visit Volumes and Charges
The Visit Volume and Charges component shows trends for the number of visits, hours of infusions, and total
appointment-related charges. Visit volume includes completed appointments scheduled with at least one
resource type provider. Charges include all hospital and professional charges related to an appointment
scheduled with at least one resource type provider.
Scheduling
Did an infusion take longer than what it was scheduled for? What tools are your schedulers using to make
appointments? How long does it take them to schedule an appointment?
Duration Accuracy
The Duration Accuracy component groups infusion visits by appointment length and calculates the median
actual duration of the visit and total volume. Click the links for each appointment length to view a drilldown
report for specific appointment details.
If the average difference is a multiple of your minimum slot length, you might need to update your visit type
lengths, decision tree logic, or visit type modifiers so that you're scheduling more accurate visit lengths.
Mode and Time to Schedule

sourceId: file:RefuelUpgrade/Refuel Phase 3/Beacon Upgrade Training Slides - Feb + May 2024.pdf
title: Beacon Upgrade Training Slides - Feb + May 2024

id: file:RefuelUpgrade/Refuel Phase 3/Beacon Upgrade Training Slides - Feb + May 2024.pdf#29
text:
lengths, decision tree logic, or visit type modifiers so that you're scheduling more accurate visit lengths.
Mode and Time to Schedule
The Mode and Time to Schedule component shows the percentage of appointments that were scheduled
using different scheduling activities and the average amount of time users spent scheduling those
appointments.
If you're using the Infusion Scheduling Template Generator activity, most of your infusion visits should be
scheduled using the Solutions view and the average time to schedule an appointment should trend
downward. Follow up with scheduling staff if you notice an upward trend in the time spent scheduling or in
usage for scheduling modes that you're not expecting.
Hot Spots
Are there certain days of the week or hours of the day that have a higher volume of visits?
Continued on next page.

sourceId: file:RefuelUpgrade/Refuel Phase 3/Beacon Upgrade Training Slides - Feb + May 2024.pdf

id: file:RefuelUpgrade/Refuel Phase 3/Beacon Upgrade Training Slides - Feb + May 2024.pdf#30
text:
Visit Volume
The Visit Volume component shows a heat map of visit volume by day of week and time of day. An
appointment's start time is used to determine the hour of the day it is counted under. Visit volume includes
completed appointments scheduled with at least one resource type provider.
Use this component to identify hot spots where you might need to make staffing adjustments in the short or
long term, or make scheduling adjustments to even things out in the long term.
Access
How long does it take for a patient's infusion visit to get scheduled after it's been signed by a clinician? And
how far out is the appointment?
Access to First Treatment
The Access to First Treatment component shows the lead time and scheduling turnaround time for patients'
first treatments in treatment plans. Only appointments that are linked to a treatment plan are included in
either metric.
If your lead time is long and the utilization rate shown in the Chair Utilization component is low, use the Add-
Ons, No-Shows, and Late Cancels component to determine whether the unused time in your schedules is
caused by no-shows and late cancellations.

text:
New Feature
Complete More Medication Management from
Mobile
Use the Orders activity on an iOS device to document
medication adherence and status, add an order note, and more
for outpatient visits.
• Quickly document a patient's medication adherence by
tapping Taking, Not Taking, or Taking Differently on the
medication list.
• Take action on all medications with the 3-dot menu.
• Tap a medication to see additional action options. You can
view more details about a medication and toggle medication
statuses like taking, long-term, and hidden from MyChart
proxy. You can also add or review the order note or view
reference links for the medication.
• See allergy details for a patient by tapping on the patient
header. A separate Allergies banner no longer appears in the
Orders activity to minimize scrolling in the medication list.
Key Changes

text:
New Feature
Get a Patient Preview from the Schedule
Tapping once on a patient's visit in
the Schedule on Canto now opens
a preview report about the patient
without opening that patient's
chart. Use this report to prepare
for upcoming visits or get a quick
overview of your day before you
start work. Double tap to open the
patient's chart when you're ready
to start your documentation or dig
into more detailed information. If
there isn't enough space on your
screen for a side-by-side view, you
can still open the preview by
tapping the three-dot menu.
Key Changes

text:
New Workflow
Focus on Notification Without Lifting a Finger
When a notification appears in Hyperspace and you want to focus or click on it, use the keystrokes
Ctrl+Alt+Shift+K.
After you focus on a notification you can use Tab to focus on the next action you’d like to take, like closing the
notification. Pressing the Spacebar completes the action. If you want to move it around the screen, press
Ctrl+Alt+Shift+P/L to move it to a new location.
Additional Changes

sourceId: file:RefuelUpgrade/Refuel Phase 3/Radiant Upgrade Training Slides - May 2024 FINAL.pdf

text:
New Look
Assistant Bar: Spotlight Cards in the Dropdown
To help you quickly find information and navigate to the right place in the chart, search is moved to a more
prominent location at the top-center of Hyperdrive and is now called the Assistant Bar. Regardless of what you’re
doing in Hyperspace, search is always available in a single location.
Click the new Assistant Bar or press Ctrl+Space to start searching.
Note that to provide more room for patient information, a search field no longer appears in Storyboard.
Key Changes

New Reports to Monitor Patients with C. diff
Two new reports show patients with suspected or confirmed C. diff
infections:
• Infection preventionists can use the report C. diff - Suspected
and Confirmed C. diff Patient Monitoring (Login Hospital)
to monitor the care of patients with suspected or confirmed C.
diff infections at their hospital.
• Nurse managers and charge nurses can use the report C. diff -
Suspected and Confirmed C. diff - Patient Monitoring
(Login Department) to monitor the care of patients with
suspected or confirmed C. diff infections in their department.
Key Changes
New Feature

text:
One-Click Reorder in Results Review
Re-order Tests from Results Review
If a patient has an
abnormal result that
needs retesting or a
procedure that they
need repeated, right-
click the result in
Results Review and
select Reorder to send
the order to the Orders
cart.
-You can reorder lab tests
or procedures from the
patient’s current outpatient
visit. You can’t reorder an
order that has external
results.
New Feature
Reorder lab tests or procedures
from the patient’s lab results under
Labs tab in Chart Review will also
be available by right clicking the
order.
You will not be able to reorder an
order that has external results.
