text:
Get More Complete Specimen Documentation by
Requiring Collection Items in Order Inquiry Collection
To ensure that phlebotomists complete all the specimen documentation that the lab needs, required items are
now enforced in the Collection activity when users open it from Order Inquiry. When the collecting user scans or
clicks to document the collection of the specimen, the user must fill out all fields that have been defined as
required before completing collection. Previously, item requirements were only respected for tasks launched
from work lists.
Additional Changes: Cross-Role
Updates
New Look

sourceId: file:RefuelUpgrade/Upgrade vAugust2024/Beaker Upgrade Training Slides - August 2024.pdf
title: Beaker Upgrade Training Slides - August 2024
id: file:RefuelUpgrade/Upgrade vAugust2024/Beaker Upgrade Training Slides - August 2024.pdf#10
text:
Get More Complete Specimen Documentation by
Requiring Collection Items in Order Inquiry Collection
The Label Printer field now appears in the Collection activity accessed from Order Inquiry the same way it does
for Nurse Task Collection, enabling greater flexibility for selecting printers. The settings to allow or require
printer selection now also apply to phlebotomy collections. If you have nursing tasks that are shared with
phlebotomy, you need to assess whether the tasks can continue to be shared with these settings.
Additional Changes: Cross-Role
Updates
New Look

sourceId: file:RefuelUpgrade/Upgrade vAugust2024/Beaker Upgrade Training Slides - August 2024.pdf

id: file:RefuelUpgrade/Upgrade vAugust2024/Beaker Upgrade Training Slides - August 2024.pdf#11
text:
A Cleaner View of Results
Results stand out more clearly in In Basket and Chart Review now that reference ranges are visible in a hover
bubble instead of next to the result values. To add them back, open your personalization settings and select
Show Ref Range on hover.
Additional Changes: Cross-Role
Updates
New Look

sourceId: file:RefuelUpgrade/Upgrade vAugust2024/Beaker Upgrade Training Slides - August 2024.pdf

id: file:RefuelUpgrade/Upgrade vAugust2024/Beaker Upgrade Training Slides - August 2024.pdf#12
text:
Spot Trends for Past Organisms and Sensitivities from
the Outstanding List
You can view a history of a patient's recorded organisms and corresponding sensitivities over time for all
specimen types and sources in Related Results review, making it easier to plan treatment based on the results,
monitor antibiotic resistance, and implement infection control measures.
Key Changes: Cross-Role Updates
Time Saver

text:
Dig Into DRG Impacts on Accounts
Use MS-DRG or APR-DRG dashboards to monitor the
impacts of your CDI specialists on accounts, helping
you gauge the success of your CDI program and
identify areas for improvement.
Track how your department is doing and identify areas
where specialist education is needed by drilling down
into time periods in the Impact Monthly section or
Major Diagnostic Categories (MDC) in the Impact
Matrix section. If you notice that the Diseases and
Disorders of the Nervous System MDC is receiving
fewer queries this month, drilling down by user helps
you know when to educate users on accurately
reviewing and querying accounts.
Key Changes
New Feature

id: file:RefuelUpgrade/Upgrade vAugust2024/HIM and Identity Upgrade Training Slides - August 2024.pdf#5
text:
Drill Into CDI Query Utilization and Effectiveness
You can see how often and how quickly providers
respond to CDI queries, as well as the impacts of those
queries, on the CDI Queries dashboard, helping you
understand the effectiveness of your CDI program.
The dashboard is based on data from SlicerDicer,
making it easy for you to dig deeper. Slice by query
senders, recipients, or types to track how your CDI
program is doing and identify areas where specialist or
provider education is needed. For example, if you
notice that a particular provider's average query
response time has risen this month, slice by query type
to evaluate whether the increase in delays is related to
a specific query type for which provider education
materials are available.
Key Changes
New Look

Send Releases Electronically for Recipients with or
without MyChart
Rather than print a paper release for a recipient without a MyChart account, you can now send a link to securely
download the release using the Electronic Delivery option. A green leaf icon shows when a recipient can receive
a release electronically. This option replaces the Release to MyChart option, so use it for MyChart releases as
well.

include professional coding queries as well, so make sure to use
the Query Workflow criterion to select the type of queries you
want to see.

The Document Indexing Automation dashboard shows you the accuracy of auto-indexing features, such as
Directory Sweep or barcode scanning, so that you can start saving indexers time by changing documents to not
require review anymore if auto-indexing is generally accurate.

Review All Auto-Indexed Documents the Same Way
If you review auto-populated information
on documents coming into your system,
know that review for documents coming in
from Directory Sweep now works like
review for barcode scanned documents.
You'll see icons indicating which fields were
auto-populated, meaning you either need
to update those fields or confirm the
information is accurate before processing.

Get Ready for Patient Loads in Hyperspace
A Hyperspace-based workflow replaces the spreadsheets and text-based utilities that you and your Epic
representative used to use to import patient records. Use these new tools to ensure that patient records loaded
into Epic from another system are formatted correctly, don't duplicate existing records, and have the correct
information from the legacy system.

With appropriate security, you can now reopen a closed chart correction case, like if you need to complete
additional tasks or add new information, if the patient requested the case reopened, or if the case was
mistakenly closed.

New Workflow

text:
Reach Out When a Patient Is Interested in SDOH
Assistance
Now that patients can indicate when they want assistance
addressing SDOH, look for the hands heart icon to know when you
should talk with them about resources.
When a domain's risk color goes all the way to the center (A), a
patient has said they want assistance for that domain. For this
patient, those domains are Alcohol Use and Social Connections.
When you hover over a domain (B), the icon appears in the upper
right corner and indicates whether assistance was requested or
declined.
Key Changes: Cross-Role Updates
New Feature

sourceId: file:RefuelUpgrade/Upgrade vAugust2024/Healthy Planet Upgrade Training Slides - August 2024.pdf
title: Healthy Planet Upgrade Training Slides - August 2024

meta.file: Healthy Planet Upgrade Training Slides - August 2024.pdf

id: file:RefuelUpgrade/Upgrade vAugust2024/Healthy Planet Upgrade Training Slides - August 2024.pdf#4
text:
Identify Patients Who Want SDOH Assistance
Drive outreach for and prioritize patients who requested help with
SDOH needs using three filters in either of the following
SlicerDicer data models:
• The Patients data model shows only an overall picture of a
patient's SDOH information and does not include details about
specific entries or domains. Using the assistance filters shows
whether generally, at some point, the patient wanted assistance
with any domain.
• The SDOH Current Risk Levels data model shows a patient's
current risk level for an SDOH domain, where each row is a
domain per patient. Using the assistance filters shows whether
the patient wanted assistance the last time they were screened
for each domain.
Key Changes: Cross-Role Updates
New Feature

Review Preventive Care Attestations
Patients can now use MyChart to let you know about screenings they've received elsewhere, the same way they
can for immunizations, so you can verify supporting documentation and update the chart in Health
Maintenance.

New Workflow

When you file flowsheet documentation for your patient, that documentation now automatically completes
related checklist tasks, just like lab results and notes already do.

Time Saver

More easily find the checklist tasks you're looking for by
expanding or collapsing groups of tasks like consults,
documentation, imaging, labs, and letters.

Track trends in the medication therapy problems documented across your organization with the Completed
Medication Therapy Problems Overview dashboard and dig into details in SlicerDicer.

Track More Care Companion Escalations with New
Categories
Gauge how many Care Companion escalations resulted in a
patient action, how many resulted in a clinical follow-up, and how
many resulted in both with updates to the Care Companion
Overview Dashboard. If you notice an uptick in clinical escalations,
for example, you might want to check on how clinicians are
managing their workload.

SDOH Specifics from Anywhere in the Chart
Hover over a social driver of health in Storyboard to see specifics
for that domain, just like what you see when you hover over a
domain in the SDOH Wheel. Recent concerns and assistance
requested both show only the relevant domains. Hover over Social
Drivers to see the familiar bird’s eye view of all domains.

Keep an Eye on In-Progress Care Gaps
The clipboard you see when patients have an in-progress order for a Health Maintenance topic now indicates
whether the topic is overdue or due soon, so you can follow up with patients to make sure they're receiving the
necessary care.

Interventions
If you’re adding a care plan goal or intervention with a general default discipline, such as Interdisciplinary, and
your organization’s policy requires that you update it with the specific discipline of the clinician who’ll work with
the patient, you can now add or change values in the Disciplines field.

text:
Repeat Cycles to Save Clicks When You Extend a Plan
When you extend treatment plans, use an existing cycle as a template for future cycles so you don't copy
forward unique changes you made to past cycles. A new Repeating Cycles section appears (A), repeating cycle
medications appear in purple (B), and repeating cycle days are dashed (C).

text:
Add American Cancer Society Educational Materials
to the AVS
Send patients home with reference materials approved by the American Cancer Society (ACS) in their After Visit
Summary in their primary language to help them understand their cancer diagnosis and navigate their
treatment journey. References are available in English, French, Haitian Creole, Korean, Polish, Portuguese,
Russian, Simplified Chinese, Spanish, Tagalog, Ukrainian, and Vietnamese.
Key Changes
New Feature

sourceId: file:RefuelUpgrade/Upgrade vAugust2024/Beacon Upgrade Training Slides - August 2024.pdf

Reactivate Discontinued Treatment Plans
If a treatment plan that is still needed is mistakenly discontinued, you can now reactivate it, retaining previously
completed days and released medications.
Additional Changes
New Workflow

text:
UT HEALTH SAN ANTONIO
Overview of New Epic Features
August 13, 2025 upgrade to Epic vFebruary25 Happy Patients
Upgrade Commitment
We are committed to making lives better for both our
patients, clinicians, and supporting end users. Together with
our Epic partner, we are upgrading quarterly to take
advantage of clinical features and automation, streamlined
workflows, improved access to patient health information and
elevated patient health care experience.
Drivers of Success
Clinical Efficiency
Opportunities to save clicks, mouse movement,
and keyboard strokes add to clinical happiness.
Look to learn what's new that could save you!
Patient Centered
Involvement in their healthcare creates happy
and grateful patients. Updated technologies that
support patient health and safety put us as a
leader in healthcare
Revenue Leading
Complete and accurate charting along with
proactive determinants of health needs drive
strong organizational revenue.
Do not miss in this
upgrade...
New Features
• New Lab Status Tracker in Chart Review
• Reporting on Social Determinates of Health
• Secure Chat Treatment Plans
• Anesthesia Post Procedure Notes in Mobile apps
• Generative AI and SideKick in SlicerDicer
Quick Wins
• Recognizing Veteran Status in Storyboard
• Video Library now available in mobile apps
• Collection Instructions in Specimen Navigator
• See Why Charges Split on Different Claims
New Workflows
• Dental Lab Status updates in the Storyboard
• Rover Nurse Brain Documentation Features
• HIM act on Potential Conditions from Doc Review
• Discharge Planning now available on the sidebar
Time Savers
• Edit PDFs in Gallery during Indexing
• Submit Replacement Claims Easier
• Easier Search for Data Models in SlicerDicer
• ED Trackboard To Do even faster

conclusions about related test results,

Nurses and other inpatient users can now take action on more

actionable from the Brain in Rover.

rows you need to complete based on your selections, like in other places where you document flowsheets. In
this example task, after you click Doc, you see the first flowsheet row you use to indicate the pain assessment.
After making a selection, you see the additional rows specific to that assessment.

text:
Key Highlights to Know
Quick Win
Make Workqueue Entries Stand
Out with Conditional Formatting
To help workqueue users better prioritize their work, you can make workqueue entries stand out by setting
conditional formatting. This allows you to highlight data in workqueue columns that you think is important
for users to know about and act upon.
Conditional formatting is available in all workqueue types, allowing for a wide variety of uses. For example,
you can highlight insurance follow-up records that are approaching timely filing, accounts with high dollar
amounts, urgent referrals, or payers that require special attention.

from the Dashboard
Dashboard Insights uses Generative AI to allow users to condense the data shown on a dashboard into a text
summary, helping them quickly identify the most important information. When a user requests a summary from
a button on the dashboard, any graph, table, and badge components are summarized using a prompt.

text:
Confirm Patient Identity Before Changing
Demographics
To help you avoid changing
information on the wrong patient's
chart, you'll need to confirm two
pieces of identifying information - like
a phone number, email address, or
street address - before you can save
significant changes to a patient's
demographics (Patient Name, Date of
Birth, Sex, SSN).

text:
Schedule Requests for Follow-Up Visits
Because it's now easier for clinicians to create schedulable follow-ups, you might start seeing more appointment
requests to schedule for patients' follow-up visits. As part of this change, clinicians can indicate when a follow-
up should be scheduled only as needed (PRN). If a patient calls to schedule a PRN follow-up, you can quickly
find it on the Active Requests tab of the Appointment Desk.
New Look

Text a link to guarantors to make it easier for them to
add a new card or bank account so you don’t need
to collect payment information over the phone and
enter it in a credit card device.

text:
Send ABNs to Patients in My Chart
When you discuss an ABN with a patient, send it to them in MyChart so they can sign it conveniently
without a paper form. If they don't have a MyChart account, you can use the same workflow to send them
an email or text message with a link where they can sign their ABN securely.
Quick Win

text:
CC Results to Providers Outside Your Organization
When you cc results to keep other
providers in the loop, you can now
search for and include providers
who work outside your
organization—it works the same
way as sending letters in the
Communications activity.
Key Upgrade Highlight
New Feature

sourceId: file:RefuelUpgrade/Upgrade vMay2025/Key vMay25 Highlights to Know.pdf
title: Key vMay25 Highlights to Know
id: file:RefuelUpgrade/Upgrade vMay2025/Key vMay25 Highlights to Know.pdf#15
text:
Send Direct Links to Help Patients Finish
Questionnaires
If a patient has unfinished questionnaires at the time of their visit,
send them a direct link to complete them in MyChart while they're
in the exam room. If the patient can't complete the questionnaire
themselves, say if they don't have a smartphone, use the Answer
Questionnaires section to respond on behalf of the patient while
you discuss the questions, now that the option to have patients fill
out the questionnaire themselves on the exam room computer is
removed.
To send a direct link:
• Hover over the Unanswered questionnaires? column in the
schedule and then click Send Questionnaires Link.
• Click Send Direct Link in the Questionnaire Assignment activity
or navigator section.
• Choose Send Link Via Text or Send Link Via Email in the Send
Questionnaires Link activity.
Key Upgrade Highlight
New Workflow

sourceId: file:RefuelUpgrade/Upgrade vMay2025/Key vMay25 Highlights to Know.pdf
title: Key vMay25 Highlights to Know
id: file:RefuelUpgrade/Upgrade vMay2025/Key vMay25 Highlights to Know.pdf#16
text:
Review Meds Faster by Applying Recent Responses
If a patient had a visit during the last
seven days and reported how they
were taking their medications, those
recent responses are pre-selected in
the Medication Review section, so you
can click Copy Forward to apply them
all with a single click.
Key Upgrade Highlight
Quick Win

sourceId: file:RefuelUpgrade/Upgrade vMay2025/Key vMay25 Highlights to Know.pdf
title: Key vMay25 Highlights to Know
id: file:RefuelUpgrade/Upgrade vMay2025/Key vMay25 Highlights to Know.pdf#17
text:
Add Problems to Your Diagnosis-Aware Note
For users that use problem-oriented
assessment and plan notes you can now
include and remove patient problems
using .DIAGPOC smartlink. This both adds
the problem to your current diagnosis-
aware note and marks it as a hospital
problem, visit diagnosis, or clinical
impression so that it’s included
automatically in the future.
Key Upgrade Highlight
New Feature

sourceId: file:RefuelUpgrade/Upgrade vMay2025/Key vMay25 Highlights to Know.pdf
title: Key vMay25 Highlights to Know
id: file:RefuelUpgrade/Upgrade vMay2025/Key vMay25 Highlights to Know.pdf#18
text:
Better-Informed Decisions About Urine Culture Orders
When you place a urine culture
order from the NEW urinalysis
order panel, the system
prompts you for an appropriate
indication for the order and
shows you a report of recent
urinary symptoms and results.
The order panel reminds you of
the appropriate situations for
ordering urine cultures (A). As
you select an indication (B),
refer to the report that appears
right in the Order Composer
with information about recent
symptoms (C) and results (D).
Key Upgrade Highlight
New Feature

Click Spotlight to see the most

their details (C).

Score
Get an assist when determining a patient’s ASA score with a system-calculated suggested minimum ASA
score, which can be seen in the Anesthesia Storyboard and preprocedure evaluation (shown below).

Request Support for Anesthesia Emergencies
To quickly reach out for help during an
emergency situation, use the
Emergency Call button to notify
relevant staff, like supervising
anesthesiologists and your
organization's emergency response
team. From the Intraprocedure activity,
you can request help (A) and monitor
existing requests for help from the
Emergency Notifications Status
banner (B).

Previously after logging into hyperspace a user will have to separately Sign in (Left). Now Sign in more
efficiently at the start of your shift at the point of initial log in (Right). Much of your defaults will also save and
be there for you in future shifts as well.

Use Track Board views with filters to quickly
see the set of patients you're looking for,
instead of switching between views to see
patients in different care areas or statuses.
In this example, you can select and clear
checkboxes to adjust which care areas to
include in the view (A). Patients are
grouped by those selected care areas on
the ED Track Board (B).

Quick Win

text:
Automatic Beyond-Use-Date Calculation
The system now automatically calculates a
beyond-use date (BUD) for compounded
sterile preparations, based on the
preparation environment, sterility of the
ingredients, and storage—the new Beyond
Use Date activity lets you change the
storage type to recalculate the BUD and
review the information used in the
calculation.
Tip Sheet: Review or Recalculate a Preparation's BUD (Pharmacist)
Tip Sheet: Automatically Calculate the BUD for Your Preparations (Pharmacy Technician)
New Feature

Repackaging

Compounding and Repackaging Check activities.

text:
Monitor HAIs from New Dashboards
Keep an eye on healthcare-associated
infection data and explore trends using
these dashboards that show numbers of
cases and standardized infection ratios
(SIRs) for several common infections,
including HAIs, C. diff, CAUTI, CLABSI,
MRSA, SSIs, and VAEs.
Click any component on these
dashboards to open SlicerDicer and
explore in more detail.

You might notice the workqueue you use to process external mortality reports now includes reports received
from another organization through Care Everywhere. You can handle these reports the same way you do other

You can now track claim rejections in follow-up records, similar to how you track denied claims. Also, new billing
activities help you work those rejections and resubmit claims.
Tip Sheet: Track Payer RejectionsKey Upgrade Highlight

Use the Browse Related Procedures
option in the Potential Procedure
Codes and Level of Service sections of

find and select procedures that are
related to a charge, making it easier to
replace a charge with one that is more
accurate.

Use Provider Finder in Charge Entry and Review
Provider Finder has come to charge entry and review, making it easier for you to find the right service and
billing providers for charges. Provider Finder lets you search for providers by name, location, specialty,
department, and other criteria, so you can narrow down the list of providers to find the one you need.

workqueues and the Clinical Coding Quality Review report, while new filters make it easier to compare original

title: Key vAugust25 Highlights to Know
text:
Track Insurance AR to Resolution
New Payer Billing Threads data models in SlicerDicer help
you track insurance AR from the initial claim through the
final outcome with that payer, even when there were
denials and resubmissions along the way.
What are "payer billing threads"?
A payer billing thread represents everything that
happened to charges assigned to a payer, from the initial
claim through the final resolution with that payer. While
corrections, denials, rebills, and replacement claims can
cause charges to have multiple buckets (for HB) or
insurance follow-up records (for PB), a single payer billing
thread draws all of those events and records together to
reflect the history and outcome for the charges. Built-in
filters and measures in SlicerDicer support outcome-
focused reporting, such as days to resolution, payment
trends, and resolution breakdowns.
Upgrade Highlights to Know
New Workflow
Use the Payer Billing Threads data model
to identify payers that take longer to
respond.
Use the Payer Billing Threads data model to
analyze outcomes by payer.

Label Content
When pharmacy users reprint medication labels, the content

ensure that the reprinted label contains the information the
pharmacy technician saw when preparing the dispense.
Any subsequent changes to the order or to label
configuration are not reflected in the reprinted label.
Optionally, you can change this behavior to always
regenerate the label data based on current order details, or
you can let users choose whether to reprint the original or

If you’re using the Patients, Patient Portal

can send a message to all selected
patients at the same time.
How might I use this?
Filter your SlicerDicer results to all
MyChart-active patients with diabetes or
a particular type of cancer. Then, right-
click and select Send Patients Message to
send dietary education materials to those
patients.

title: Key vAugust25 Highlights to Know
text:
Show Rounded Numbers in SlicerDicer Reports
The Rounding slider lets you adjust the decimal
precision of measures so you can make better
visual comparisons. You can also now choose to
trim the trailing zeroes from results.
How do I do it?
To adjust the number of digits or decimal places
displayed for a given measure, use the Rounding
slider when configuring the measure.
To remove trailing zeroes from your results in
detail table, crosstab, or horizontal bar graph
views, go to the Visual Options card and click
Trim under Trailing Zeroes.
Upgrade Highlights to Know
New Feature
Here, trailing zeroes are
trimmed, and total
amounts are rounded to
four digits for easier
comparison.
You might keep trailing zeroes in
a detail table view, so all values
line up or trim them to reduce
visual clutter in a horizontal bar
graph.

title: Key vAugust25 Highlights to Know
text:

After you've narrowed down your
SlicerDicer query to a list of visits
or infusion visits you want to
investigate further, you can open
individual encounters in the chart
directly from your detail list—just
select a row, right-click, and
choose Open Encounter.
Upgrade Highlights to Know
New Feature

title: Key vAugust25 Highlights to Know
text:
Report Medicare CQMs for Your MSSP ACO
Starting in reporting year 2025, MSSP ACOs can no longer report CMS Web Interface measures.
Instead, ACOs must report four measures using one of the following collection types: eCQMs, Medicare Clinical
Quality Measures (Medicare CQMs), or MIPS Clinical Quality Measures (MIPS CQMs).
You can now use Epic-released tools to help collect data for Medicare CQMs and to generate files in the required
format for submission at the end of the year. Use the Tipsheet in the dashboard for more information.
Upgrade Highlights to Know
New Feature

text:
Capture Clinical Videos in Haiku on Android Devices
Ambulatory clinicians can capture clinical videos for patient documentation in Haiku
on Android devices. For example, a clinician might use a video to show a patient's gait
or range of motion. By default, the maximum video length is 60 seconds.
After recording, users can preview the video, select a document type, enter a
description, retake the video, or add more media, just as they can for an image.
Unlike images, a video preview cannot be rotated.
Recorded videos are temporarily cached on the device. Videos are deleted from the
device to free space and comply with privacy regulations when:
• They are saved.
• The clinician discards them without saving.
• The app times out before saving occurs.
• The clinician closes the app before saving occurs.
• The recording is interrupted by a process, such as backgrounding the app.
Upgrade Highlights to Know

text:
More Flexibility for Fully Covered Procedures in
Estimates
Quick Win
There are some scenarios where payers fully cover the cost of a procedure. If accurately identifying procedures
as fully covered has been difficult, you can now use a rule-based setting to simplify estimates for procedures
that are fully covered by insurance.
What is the Benefit?
• Simplify benefit filing, discount rules, and service type configuration.
• Reduce the amount of ongoing maintenance.
• More easily identify procedures as fully covered.
For example, a payer might require a patient to pay for a portion of a mammogram that is considered
diagnostic, but the payer might cover the entire cost of the mammogram if it is considered preventative. You
now have a flexible option to apply fully covered logic to specific procedures in estimates. If a procedure line
on an estimate satisfies a rule that you define, the procedure is considered fully covered by insurance. No
benefits are applied, and the patient responsibility for the procedure is reflected as $0 in the estimate. Since
benefits are not applied, benefit accumulation is not affected by these procedures.

Spend less time typing by using autocompletion
suggestions in large text fields in Hyperspace, such as
notes, letters, In Basket messages, and secure chat
messages.
Be aware that autocompletion simply attempts to
predict the next word or phrase and does not have
access to the patient's chart; therefore, it should not be
interpreted as clinical guidance or decision support.
Can I turn it off?
If you find autocompletion distracting, you can turn it
off by doing the following:
1. Search SmartTools to open the SmartTools tab in
My Settings.
2. In the User Interface section, clear the Show
autocomplete suggestions while typing checkbox.

from any narrator you happen to be
working in—just click the RSI button to
pull in pre-treatment documentation,
medications, and airway placement
events, all grouped together and
arranged in the order you need them.

Upgrade Highlights to Know
Quick Win
Verbal and per protocol orders you use
regularly now have a place in the
narrator toolbox, so you can place them
without switching to the Orders tab or
opening the Manage Orders activity.
Which orders can I place, and where
will they appear?
Any narrator, including the ED Narrator,
Procedural Narrator, and specialty
narrators like the Trauma Narrator, can
include an orders section in the toolbox.
If you need to place orders that don't
appear in the narrator toolbox, you can
continue to find and place those orders
the way you do today.
Click a protocol order from the
toolbox (1) and enter details about
the order in the Event Log (2).
When you place a point of care
test (1), you can enter order
details (2) and results (3) at the
same time. Clicking Accept
places the order and files the
results. Click Result Later if you
aren't ready to enter results
now.

patient you saw earlier in your shift, you
can find them without leaving the Track
Board by hovering over a new My Patients
This Shift metric at the bottom of the
screen.
Why don't I see the metric?
If you didn't see any metrics at the bottom
of the Track Board previously, you might
not see the new metric either, depending
on how your organization chooses to set
up your Track Board views.
Upgrade Highlights to Know
Quick Win
You can see all of the patients you've been assigned to during your current
or most recent shift. This includes patients who have left the ED already,
which helps if you need to review their charts but can't recall their names.

Care Journeys (Slide 1 of 2)

As you review upcoming outreach tasks in reports or in the Outreach Management navigator section, make
sure the Planned For date is accurate so patients know when to expect a call, or clear the Show in MyChart
checkbox to remove the event from their timeline.
Where does it appear in MyChart?
Planned outreach tasks appear in the care journey timeline, which also shows upcoming and past visits.
Other information about the care management program appears in the care journey such as:
• An overview of the program.
• Who’s on their case team.
• Related documents like After Visit Summaries and decision letters.
• Care Companion educational content, tasks, and questionnaires.

Discrete Details from Free-Text Sigs
To help clinicians more quickly act on
medications that have free-text sigs,
generative AI now helps translate those
sigs to discrete values for dose, route,
frequency, PRN reasons, and
administration instructions.

Changes with AI
To help clinicians understand the story behind a patient's medications—what was tried, what worked, what
didn’t, and why—Synopsis uses generative AI to surface relevant text from clinical notes. Clinicians can hover
over a medication to view Note Insights, which are excerpts from notes that mention medication changes with
links to full notes for deeper review.

Understand Imaging Results
Patients can use AI to see a patient-
friendly summary of their imaging test
results in MyChart, which can help them
understand their results and reduce
confusion while waiting for provider
comments.
This feature respects all our existing
patient sensitivity settings for hiding and
sharing results in MyChart. The AI model
can only read patient information from
results after it is released to the patient.

To save time documenting visits with
back-office imaging, add .IMGDOC
to your note to review images and
add results or comments without
leaving your note. Clinical support
staff can enter a preliminary result if
needed, while physicians can enter a
final result.

You’re Adding Problems and Goals
After you add a problem or goal to a care plan, you can add associated goals or interventions right from the
same window instead of adding each one separately. You can also favorite elements that you use frequently so
you can select them from the window rather than searching.

One Spot

information in a single place instead of piecing it together from documentation throughout the chart. You can
add events to the history when needed, and you can type .PSYCHTXHIST in a note to pull in the patient’s
psychiatric history.

title: Imprivata-Request-Form-Guide
text:
This form is to request Imprivata Single Sign-on Access and Provider Electronic Prescription for Controlled Substance (EPCS) Access.
- To start click on the following link: http://prwinvob001.utmsa.local/appnet_html/imprivataform.html
You will find a webpage with the following two options.
- Enter Request will take you to the request form.
- New Department Template is an Excel spreadsheet that is only needed when a Department is starting the Electronic Prescription for Controlled Substances.
- Enter Request
This is what you will see when you select “Enter Request”
Enter Request Cont’d
You will notice that some information is prefilled. You will just need to enter your Phone Number and select if the department is NEW to Electronic Prescription for Controlled Substances (EPCS) or select EXISTING if the depart has gone through the onboarding process already.
If you select NEW you will need the Excel Spreadsheet from NEW DEPARTMENT TEMPLATE mentioned in 1.B. Once spreadsheet is filled out with all participating provider information you will need to attach it.
If you select EXISTING, you will see an additional drop down appear, EMPLOYEE TYPE.
Employee Type will have the following options:
Employee Type Cont’d
When PROVIDER is selected additional field will appear below in order to fill.
Once all fields are filled please Submit.
NURSING STAFF is only selected when an employee needs to be granted Imprivata Single Sign-on Access (badge access).
Fill fields and click submit.

Inpatient Insights | {"fileName":"Reserved_ImageAttachment_[6]_[Image0][32]_[350ae9dc6698490aa17b25bd5e511f63][1]_[1].jpg","originalImageName":"Inpatient Insights"} | Rounding clinicians see a complex mix of patients, ranging from those they've been checking in with every day to those they've never met before. To help them quickly prepare for each of those patients, they can use generative AI to create three types of insights to fit the type of information and level of detail that would be most helpful:
- Patient Story insights are designed to familiarize clinicians with a patient they have not previously encountered. These summaries include history from notes and chart data, recent events, and other details related to the current admission, helping them prioritize and plan their care efficiently. Patient Story summaries are organized into three sections: history, events during admission, and recent events. The recent events section includes similar information to the freestanding Recent Events summary described below.
- Notes summaries focus on summarizing relevant details from recent notes on the patient, helping clinicians quickly get up to speed on recent observations and developments or see highlights from the rest of the treatment team.
- Recent Events summaries provide an overview of recently documented information on the patient, including intake/output, medications, results, orders, the problem list, notes, vitals, nursing assessments, and code events, ensuring that clinicians are aware of significant recent changes in a patient's condition since the last time they rounded. | Gen AI - Clinicians | Provider | Item | sites/AITech/Lists/GenAIClinician

These insights provide references to the notes where specific details were discussed. To help the system focus on the right thing, clinicians can choose specific notes to summarize or request the summary to focus on a specific topic. | Gen AI - Clinicians | Provider | Item | sites/AITech/Lists/GenAIClinician
PB Coding Assistant | {"fileName":"Reserved_ImageAttachment_[6]_[Image0][32]_[1859758c4f8943f1bfd6253fad161352][1]_[1].jpg","originalImageName":"PB Coding assts"} | Save coders time so they can process more sessions and focus on those that require more expertise, helping maximize reimbursements. The Coding Assistant shows coders a list of potential diagnosis and procedure codes they might want to add based on notes that are relevant to a particular charge session, helping them review charge sessions efficiently and avoid jumping between many activities in search of relevant information.
Qualifying notes are automatically processed behind the scenes before a coder reviews the session, and they can jump to the source of supporting documentation when they need additional context. Cited text is highlighted in the note so they can decide whether the suggestion makes sense, all without needing to access Chart Review. When they decide to use a potential code, they can quickly add, swap, or remove codes from the charge session directly. | Gen AI - Patients | Support Staff | Item | sites/AITech/Lists/GenAIClinician
